TO BOTH MACARTHUR AND WILLOUGHBY, TODAY'S BATTLE IS AN OLD 
CONFLICT IN MODERN DRESS. THE TALL? SCHOLARLY INTELLIGENCE OFFICER 
HAS SERVED WITH MACARTHUR FOR OVER TEN YEARS--THE DECADE EMBRACING 
THE FIRST DISMAL DEFEAT, THEN THE THUNDEROUS TRIUMPH IN THE PHILIP- 

THE CONDITIONS ARE SOMEWHAT THE SAME. IN 1941 THE FILIPINOS. TOO 
LACKED EFFECTIVE ARMS AND ADEQUATE TRAINING. THEY, TOO. WERE STUNNED 
3Y A SURPRISE ATTACK THAT GAVE JAPANESE TROOPS A TREMENDOUS ADVANTAGE. 

MACARTHUR'S BIGGEST JOB THEN WAS TO RESTORE SHATTERED MORALE. 
IT TOOK HIM ALMOST FOUR YEARS TO DO IT, WITH A SLOWLY GROWING 
FORCE AGAINST A FIRMLY EMBEDDED ENEMY. 

HIS FIRST MOVE FOR MORALE THIS TIME WAS HIS DRAMATIC FLIGHT TO 
THE WAR ZONE LAST THURSDAY. IT WAS DANGEROUS ENOUGH TO CIVE ULCERS TO 
HIS SECURITY OFFICERS. ENEMY AIR FORCES WERE ACTIVE. FOR A 70-YEAR- 
OLD VETERAN -- AND FOR MUCH YOUNGER MEN -- IT ALSO WAS AN ARDUOUS 


TRIPe 

IN A DAY OF CEASELESS ACTIVITY MACARTHUR HAD ONE MEAL. BECAUSE 
HE WANTED TO DRIVE TO THE FRONT, HIS LUNCH WAS A CANDY BAR. 

THERE'S ONE MAJOR DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE BATTLE TODAY AND THE ONE 
NINE YEARS AGOe MACARTHUR NOW HAS A POWERFUL AIR FORCE, A WELL 
TRAINED ARMY STRONG NAVAL UNITS, AND INTERNATIONAL SUPPORT. 

HE HAS BEGUN TO USE THESE WITH THE SKILL AND SPEED THAT MARKS ALL 
HIS STRATEGY. 

HE IS RACING AGAINST TIME. 


HE HAS JUST BEGUN TO FIGHT.

HAS BEEN THE ATTITUDE OF THE INDIAN GOVERNMENT. TRADITIONALLY PRIME

AP)-AN EXPERIENCED STAFF OF CORRESPONDENTS 
THE WAR IN KOREA FOR THE ASSOCIATED PRESS-e 

IT'S A TOUGH ASSIGNMENT. COMMUNICATIONS ARE SLOW, UNCERTAIN. 
LIVING CONDITIONS IN THE FIELD ARE PRIMITIVE. AND THERE IS THE EVER@ 
PRESENT DANGER IN THE MIDDLE OF A SHOOTING SCRAP. 

BUT NEARLY ALL OF THE AP CORRESPONDENTS HAVE BEEN SEASONED BY 
SERVICE IN WORLD WAR II. AND IN THE CASE OF RUSSELL BRINES, CHIEF OF 
THE ASSOCIATED PRESS BUREAU AT TOKYO, BIG NEWS--AND BAD NEWS--IS 
GETTING TO BE HIS BUSINESS. 

THE 39 YEAR OLD ‘BRINES, IN CHARGE OF THE KOREA WAR STAFF, HAS 
REPORTED MANY OF THE TOP EVENTS IN THE ORIENT SINCE HE ENTERED AP 
SERVICE IN JUNE, 1935. HE JOINED THE AP AT HONOLULUZ; WHERE HE WAS A 
REPORTER FOR THE STAR@BULLETIN. i beg) 

BRINES, A SHORT, ROTUND BALL OF ENERGY, WAS ASSIGNED TO TOKYO IN 
JUNE, 1939. HE HELPED COVER THE RUSSO-JAPANESE BORDER CONFLICTS 
ON THE SIBERIAN FRONTIER, AND SAW THE JAPANESE STRIDENTLY GET READY FOR 
A BIGGER ADVENTURE IN THE PACIFIC. 

IN 1938, HE WENT TO MANILA AS AP NIGHT EDITOR. HE WAS ON HAND WHEN 
THE JAPANESE INVADED THE PHILIPPINES LATE IN 1941. THE JAPANESE 
INTERNED HIM EARLY IN 1942. HE LATER WAS INTERNED IN SHANGHAI. 
1943, HE WAS REPATRIATED TO THE UNITED STATES. 

YOU'D THINK HE WOULD WANT TQ SETTLE DOWN, INSTEAD, AFTER _A TOUR 
ON THE SAN FRANCISCO FOREIGN DESK, ‘THE ENTHUSIASTIC BRINES WENT OUT TO 
THE PACIFIC AGAIN IN 1945—=-AS A WAR CORRESPONDENT. HE WAS CHIEF OF 
BUREAU AT MANILA FOR A TIME, THEN WENT TO JAPAN WITH THE OCCUPATION 
FORCES. HE WAS NAMED TOKYO CHIEF OF BUREAU IN MAY, 1946. 

BRINES DIDN'T WAIT FOR THE FIRST AMERICAN TROOPS TO ENTER TOKYO AT 
THE OUTSET. GETTING OFF A SHIP AT YOKOHOMA, HE BOARDED AN ELECTRIC 
TRAIN CROWDED WITH JAPANESE PASSENGERS AND RODE INTO TOWN. GOT A GOOD 
STORY, TOO. 

HIS FAMILIARITY WITH TOKYO AND THE JAPANESE LANGUAGE, WHICH HE 
SPEAKS WELL, HELPED HIM DEVELOP A-NUMBER OF EXCLUSIVE STORIES IN THE 
EARLY DAYS OF THE OCCUPATION, 

FOR INSTANCE, HE FOUND WHERE PREMIER HIDEKI TOJO LIVED BEFORE 
AMERICAN INTELLIGENCE OFFICERS GOT AROUND TO ITe AND HE WAS OUTSIDE 
THE LITTLE WAR LEADER'S HOME WHEN TOJO TRIED TO COMMIT SUICIDE. HE HAD 
GONE THERE FOR AN INTERVIEW. WHEN TOJO WAS EXECUTED AS A MAJOR WAR 
CRIMINAL, HE WROTE A FAST, CRISP BULLETIN TELLING ABOUT IT. 


BRINES HAS KNOWN GENERAL MACARTHUR SINCE HIS DAYS IN THE PHILIPP 
HE WAS ONE OF FOUR CORRESPONDENTS WHO ACCOMPANIED THE SUPREME COMMANDER 
ON A DARING FLIGHT TO THE SOUTH KOREAN FIGHTING FRONT THIS WEEK. 

HE HAS TRAVELED WIDELY THROUGHOUT THE ORIENT TO HELP COVER NEWS 
DEVELOPMENTS AND GET A POST-WAR SLANT ON CONDITIONS IN THAT EXPLOSIVE 
PART OF THE WORLD. IT HAS PAID OFF HANDSOMELY IN BACKGROUND FOR HIS 
ROLE IN DIRECTING AP FIELD OPERATIONS IN KOREA.

F INLAND 


HELSINKI=-FINLAND'S AVERAGE MAN IS INCLINED TO BELIEVE THAT 
PRESIDENT TRUMAN'S DECISION TO MEET FORCE WITH FORCE IN KOREA WAS 
THE RIGHT APPROACH. 

FINNISH OFFICIAL QUARTERS ARE RELUCTANT TO MAKE ANY COMMENT BEYOND 
STATEMENTS THAT FINLAND IS EAGER TO KEEP OUT OF ANY BIG POWER CONFLICTS. 
EDITORIAL COMMENTS, TOO, HAVE BEEN STRICTLY NEUTRAL. 

THAT PROSPECTS FOR WaRLD PEACE ARE NOT HOPELESS SEEMS TO BE THE 
PREVAILING VIEW IN POLITICAL CIRCLES. AS LONG AS WARFARE IS LIMITED 
TQ THE FAR EAST, FINLAND IS NOT DIRECTLY CONCERNED. THE SOVIET-FINNISH 
TREATY OF FRIENDSHIP BINDS FINLAND ONLY IN EVENT OF A THREAT OF WAR 
FROM "GERMANY OR HER ALLIES.” 


NORWAY 


OSLO-=-KOREAN WAR NEWS HAS SHOCKED NORWEGIANS. PARLIAMENT AND VARIOUS 
PARLIAMENTARY COMMITTEES HAVE GIVEN FULL CONSIDERATION TO THE VARIOUS 
STEPS TAKEN BY THE UNITED STATES AND THE UNITED NATIONS. HOWEVER 
AUTHORITIES HAVE TAKEN NO VISIBLE MEASURES TO DEAL WITH A POSS IBLE 
CRISIS. 7 

NORWEGIANS ARE FULLY ALIVE TO THE UNPLEASANT POSSIBILITIES SHOULD 
THEIR SOVIET NEIGHBOR MAKE A MOVE, BUT OUTWARDLY LIFE GOES ON AS USUAL. 


GERMANY 


FRANKFURT=--THE GERMANS, BOTH EAST AND WEST, PLAINLY ARE SCARED AT 
THE POSSIBILITY THE KOREAN STRUGGLE WILL DRAW EUROPE INTO A SHOOTING 
WARe WAR FEARS IN BERLIN APPARENTLY ARE WORSE THAN AT THE START OF 

THE SOVIET BLOCKADE OF BERLIN TWO YEARS AGO. 

BUT ANTI-COMMUNISTS HOPE UNITED STATES INTERVENTION WILL ROLL BACK 
THE NORTH KOREANS AND MAKE POSSIBLE A PEACEFUL SETTLEMENT. THE PEOPLE 
REMAIN CALM AND THERE HAS BEEN NO RUSH TO BUY UP SUPPLIES FOR AN EMER- 
GENCY. 

GERMAN ANXIETY ARISES FROM THE FEAR THAT COMMUNISTS MAY ATTEMPT THE 
SAME THING IN GERMANY THAT THEY DID IN KOREA. HOWEVER, THERE HAVE BEEN 
NO SIGNS SO FAR OF UNUSUAL ACTIVITY BY THE EAST ZONE PROPLE'S POLICE. 

SOME COMMUNIST COLLABORATORS IN EAST BERLIN SAY PRIVATELY THAT 
RUSSIA WILL RESTRICT THE KOREAN AFFAIR TO A STATUS SIMILAR TO THE 
SPANISH CIVIL WARe EAST-WEST RIVALRY THUS MIGHT DRAG ON FOR SEVERAL 
YEARS WITHOUT A SHOWDOWN. 

WEST GERMAN CHANCELLOR KONRAD ADENAUER TAKES THE VIEW THAT 
SERMANY IS NOT DIRECTLY CONCERNED IN KOREA AND IS REPORTED TO HAVE 
ISSUED STRICT ORDERS TO HIS CABINET NOT TO COMMENT IN ANY WAY. GERMAN 
NEWSPAPERS ARE CAREFULLY TRYING NOT TO GIVE THE PEOPLE THE WAR JITTERS.

AUSTRIA 


VIENNA--AUSTRIANS ARE BEGINNING TO BREATHE EASIER AFTER A WEEK OF 
WAR JITTERS. THERE STILL IS WIDESPREAD FEAR OF WAR, BUT ALSO GROWING 
CONFIDENCE IN THE UNITED NATIONS AND THE UNITED STATES. 

THE NEWSPAPER SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN SAID THERE IS NO DANGER OF A 
THIRD WORLD WAR AT PRESENT BECAUSE THE COMMUNISTS HAVE NOT YET 
CONSOLIDATED THEIR HOLD IN CHINA, RUSSIA IS NOT YET READY, AMERICA TOO 
WELL PREPARED AND STALIN TOO OLD’TO LOOK FOR NEW ADVENTURES. 

MEANWHILE RUSSIANS AND AMERICANS ARE GETTING ALONG AS USUAL HERE IN 
AUSTRIA, THE LAST PLACE IN THE WORLD WHERE THEY MEET AROUND THE TABLE 
OF AN ALLIED CONTROL COUNCIL. 

GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS HAVE PULLED NO PUNCHES IN DENOUNCING NORTH 
KOREA AS AN AGGRESSOR. SECRETARY OF STATE FERDINAND GRAF TOLD A POLI- 
TICAL RALLY, "THE COMMUNIST PEACE DOVE HAS BEEN UNMASKED. IT IS A 
HYENAe” CHANCELLOR LEOPOLD FIGL HAS BEEN SIMILARLY OUTSPOKEN.

TO PUT TANKS ACROSS THE HAN ON COOLIE BRIDGES 
WHERE THE RETREATING SOUTH KOREANS HAD BLOWN UP THE STEEL BRIDGES. 

THREE MAKESHIFT BRIDGES WERE REPORTED IN PLACE. 

"THERE WAS SOME INCREASE IN ENEMY ACTIVITY SOUTH OF THE HAN RIVER 
BUT NOT MUCH,” MACARTHUR*'S COMMUNIQUE REPORTED. 

AMERICN B39 BOMBERS MADE INSTRUMENT BOMBINGS THROUGH THE MURK AND

NORTH OF SUWON.

ONDON, SUNDAY, JULY 2=(AP)-THE TEXT OF THE SOVIET NOTE TO THE 


L 
UNITED STATES ON SOTRTO BUGS AS BROADCAST BY THE MOSCOW RADIO: (ABOUT 


300 ) 
THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT HAS RECEIVED FROM THE GOVERNMENT OF THE 


GERMAN DEMOCRATIC (COMMUNIST) REPUBLIC A REPORT TO THE EFFECT THAT 
BETWEEN MAY 22 AND JUNE 7 OF THIS YEAR AMERICAN PLANES, VIOLATING 
EXISTING RULES CONCERNING AVIATION FLIGHTS, DROPPED A LARGE QUANTITY 
OF COLORADO BEETLES, WHICH ARE A DANGEROUS PEST TO POTATO CROPS, IN 
THE DISTRICTS OF ZWICKAU, GLAUCHAU, PLAUEN, ALSNIZ, AUE, HAGENOW, 
LUDWIGSLUST, PARHIM, SCHWERIN, SCHOENBERG, EISENACH, GUESTROW, 
QUEDLINBURG, ROSTOCK, ALTENBURG, GOTHA AND OTHER PARTS OF THE 
GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC. dil «= 9% ace 

TOCETHER WITH THE ABOVESMENTIONED STATEMENT FROM THEUGOVERNMENT 
OF THE GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC, THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT RECEIVED A 
REPORT FROM THE SPECIAL GOVERNMENT COMMISSION OF THE GERMAN DEMOCRATIC 
REPUBLIC WHICH CONFIRMS THAT THE DROPPING OF COLORADO BEETLES TOOK 
PLACE OVER AN EXTENSIVE TERRITORY ACCORDING TO A PLAN WORKED OUT IN 
DETAIL, AND PURSUED THE AIM OF INFLICTING DAMAGE TO THE FOOD SUPPLIES 
OF THE GERMAN PEOPLE AND ALSO OF CREATING A THREAT THAT THE COLORADO 
BEETLE WOULD SPREAD TO POTATO=GROWING AREAS IN COUNTRIES BORDERING 
ON THE GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC. , 

THE NUMEROUS FACTS ESTABLISHED BY THE SPECIAL GOVERNMENT COMMISSIO 
REGARDING THE DROPPING OF COLORADO BEETLES ON THE TERRITORY OF THE 
GERMAN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC BY AMERICAN PLANES SHOW THAT THESE ACTS 
ARE DELIBERATE AND CONSEQUENTLY ARE OF A CRIMINAL NATURE. 

IN DRAWING THE ATTENTION OF THE GOVERNMENT OF THE UNITED STATES 
TO THE ABOVE-MENTIONED ACTIONS OF THE AMERICAN OCCUPATION AUTHORITIES 
IN GERMANY, THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT INSISTS THAT THE GUILTY PERSONS BE 
BROUGHT TO BOOK AND EXPECTS THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT TO ADOPT 
PROPER MEASURES TO GUARANTEE THAT THERE IS NO REPETITION OF SIMILAR 
FACTS IN THE FUTURE. 

IN CONNECTION WITH THE ABOVE, THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT EXPECTS THE 
UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT TO REPORT ON THE MEASURES IT ADOPTS.

IN HIS FAVOR,HOWEVER, WAS THE TROUBLED INTERNATIONAL SITUATION. 

THE FIGHTING IN THE FAR EAST MIGHT PERSUADE THE VARIOUS PARTIES 
OF THE CENTRIST COALITION TO PUT ASIDE THEIR DOMESTIC SQUABBLES 
FOR THE PRESENT. 

QUEUILLE WON HIS FIRST TEST EARLY TODAY IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY. 
HE WAS APPROVED AS PREMIER BY A VOTE OF 363 TO 208. IN HIS STATEMENT 
OF POLICY ASKING FOR INVESTITURE QUEUILLE PLEADED FOR UNITY TO PERMIT 
FRANCE TO DO ITS SHARE IN SOLVING THE INTERNATIONAL CRISIS. 

THE SOCIALISTS DECLINED, HOWEVER. THE PARTY'S EXECUTIVE 
COMMITTEE DECIDED NOT TO TAKE PART IN THE COALITION CABINET BUT 
SAID IT WOULD DELAY A DECISION ON WHETHER To GIVE QUEVILLE FURTHER 
LEGISLATIVE SUPPORT. WE 2 2 450 

NORMALLY, THE SOCIALISTS ARE ONE OF THE THREE BIG’ ELEMENTS” IN 
MIDDLE-OF-THE-ROAD COALITIONS IN FRANCE, BUT THEY CAUSED THE FALL 
OF THE CEORGES BIDAULT GOVERNMENT LAST SATURDAY BY INSISTING ON HIGHER 
WAGES FOR CIVIL SERVANTS AND SEEM INTENT ON STICKING TO THF nrMann 

QUEUILLE TOLD THE ASSEMBLY IN HIS ADDRESS LAST NIGHT THAT HE 
INTENDED TO PUSH A CHANCE IN THE METHOD OF ELECTING DEPUTIES. THIS 
IS DEMANDED BY HIS OWN PARTY, THE RADICAL SOCIALISTS, BUT OPPOSED 
BY BIDAULT'S POPULAR REPUBLICAN MOVEMENT (MRP) WHICH FEARS IT MAY 
LOSE SOME SEATS UNDER ANY SYSTEM OF CHANGE. 

IT WAS AGAINST THIS BACKGROUND OF DEEP-SEATED DIFFERENCES THAT 
QUEUILLE STARTED HIS ROUND OF CONSULTATIONS TO PICK MEMBERS OF HIS 
CABINET. 

THERE WAS NO INDICATION HOW LONG THIS MIGHT TAKE. AND THERE WERE 
SOME DOUBTS EXPRESSED THAT HE COULD SELECT A CABINET WHICH WOULD 
GET THE SUPPORT OF THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY UNLESS THE INTERNATIONAL 
SITUATION CAUSES A CHANGE OF HEART AMONG THE POLITICIANS. 

THE SOCIALISTS JOINED MOST OF FRANCE'S OTHER POLITICAL GROUPS IN 
VOTING TO CONFIRM QUEUILLE, WHO HEADED THE FRENCH GOVERNMENT FOR 
13 MONTHS IN 1947-48. ONLY THE COMMUNISTS, A SMALL GROUP OF 
DE GAULLISTS AND A FEW INDEPENDENTS VOTED AGAINST A SECOND 
PREMIERSHIP FOR THE $6-YEAR-OLD COUNTRY DOCTOR. 


THE VOTE WAS PRECEDED BY A LONG DEBATE PROVOKED BY A BITTER COMMUNIST 


ATTACK ON PRESIDENT TRUMAN'S POLICY OF MILITARY AID TO KOREA. THE 
DEBATE BROUGHT FORTH EXPRESSIONS OF SUPPORT FOR THE AMERICAN POLICY 
FROM NEARLY ALL FACTIONS EXCEPT THE COMMUNISTS. 

THE KOREAN ISSUE, HOWEVER, PLAYED NO _ PART IN THE VOTE TO CONFIRM 
QUEUILLE. THAT HINGED ENTIRELY ON DOMESTIC ISSUES.

PFC. RUDOLPH A. WHITE, 20, NEW YORK CITY; PFC. FLETCHER J. SAYLES,

SAID TODAY THAT SENATOR HICKENLOOPER'S STATEMENT THAT HE OPPOSED 
DEVELOPMENT OF THE HYDROGEN BOMB WAS A "DISTORTION OF FACTS." 





"LAST YEAR," HE SAID IN AN INTERVIEW, “I WAS NOT WILLING TO 
COME TO A DECISION UNTIL I KNEW MORE ABOUT THE SUBJECT. AS THE 
FACTS CAME IN MY ATTITUDE DID CHANGE." 

SENATOR HICKENLOOPER (R=IOWA), WHO OPPOSED PIKE'S RENOMINATION 
TO THE ATOMIC COMMISSION, ALSO SAID IN A RADIO INTERVIEW LAST NIGHT 
THAT PIKE "CONSISTENTLY OPPOSED THE DEVELOPMENT OR EXTENSION OF 
EXPERIMENTS IN THE SUPER=WEAPON FIELD." 

"A STATEMENT LIKE THAT IS COMPLETELY INCORRECT," PIKE SAID. 

HE SAID HICKENLOOPER "REFERS TO EVENTS OF SOME TIME BACK." 

PIKE'S FOUR YEAR TERM EXPIRED LAST MIDNIGHT. HE HAD BEEN ACTING 
CHAIRMAN OF THE COMMISSION, GORDON DEAN HAS BEEN NAMED ACTING 
CHAIRMAN. 

"GENERALLY SPEAKING," PIKE SAID, "WE SHOULD KNOW BETTER WHAT WE 
ARE DOING THAN WE DID LAST YEAR BEFORE SPENDING A GREAT DEAL OF 
THE GOVERNMENT'S MONEY. NOT ENOUGH INFORMATION HAD BEEN GATHERED 
TO WARRANT A MAJOR EXPENDITURE." 

"YE SHOULD KNOW WHAT WE WERE GETTING FOR WHAT WE WERE SPENDING 
AND WHETHER IT WAS WORTH WHILE SPENDING FOR THAT THAN FOR WHAT WE 
WERE ALREADY WORKING ON," HE ADDED. 

LAST YEAR, HE SAID, "I WAS NOT WILLING TO COME TO A DECISION 
UNTIL I KNEW THE FACTS." alas 

SINCE LAST YEAR, HE SAID, "WE HAVE OBTAINED, THE PACTSJAND ARE 
GOING AHEAD." WL &gt; 

HE SAID ANY ARGUMENT ABOUT DEVELOPMENT OF THE HYDROGEN BOMB 
ENDED IN JANUARY WHEN THE PRESIDENT DIRECTED THE COMMISSION TO 
"GO AHEAD WITH FURTHER WEAPONS, INCLUDING THE HYDROGEN BOMB." 

PIKE ARRIVED TODAY FROM WASHINGTON FOR A BRIEF VACATION AT HIS 
HOME HERE. 

HE SAID THAT AT THE HEARING IN WASHINGTON, WHERE THE SENATE-HOUSE 
ATOMIC COMMITTEE TURNED HIM DOWN FOR A NEW TERM BY A 5-4 VOTE, "NO 
CHARGES AND NO COMPLAINTS WERE MADE--AT LEAST OUT LOUD--AND 
NO QUESTIONS WERE ASKED" OF HIM. 

AT HIS DEXTER HOME, SENATOR BREWSTER (R=ME) SAID HE HAS ADVISED 
PIKE HE WILL SUPPORT HIS CONFIRMATION IN THE SENATE WEDNESDAY. 

BREWSTER SAID HE HAD BEEN TOLD BY FELLOW SENATORS THAT THE 
COMMITTEE ACTION WAS "SIMPLY A MATTER OF THE OPINION OF FIVE FELLOwS 
AGAINST FOUR." 

"THEY DIDN'T QUESTION HIS ABILITY," HE ADDED, "BUT THEY THOUGHT 
HE DIDN'T FIT IN, THE QUESTION OF POLITICS DIDN'T ENTER INTO IT

OTTAWA, JULY 2-(AP)-CANADA, HAVING OFFERED MILITARY AID, IS SHARING 
IN TADRS ABOUT THE NEED FOR A°UNITED NARZONS SET-UP_TO. DIRECT THE 
INTERNATIONAL FORCES AIMED AGAINST NORTH KQREAN AGGRESSION, OFFICIAL 
SOURCES SAID TONIGHT. 

THEY SAID CANADA IS SATISFIED TO HAVE UeSs GEN. DOUGLAS MACARTHUR 
CONTINUE AS COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF OF THE FORCES TAKING PART IN U.N. 
POLICE ACTION ON BEHALF OF SOUTH KOREA. 

THE QUESTION NOW TO BE RESOLVED IS THE LINK TO BE FORGED BETWEEN 
GEN. MACARTHUR'S TOKYO HEADQUARTERS AND LAKE SUCCESS IN A WAY THAT 
WOULD ESTABLISH THE UNITED INTERNATIONAL CHARACTER OF THAT ACTION. 

CANADA, IN OTHER WORDS, SHARES THE BELIEF THAT GEN. MACARTHUR 
SHOULD BECOME A UsNe COMMANDER. KOREAN ACTION NOW Is AN AMERICAN 
OPERATION WITH BRITISH AND AUSTRALIAN AID. 

THE NAVY SAID WEDNESDAY HAS BEEN DEFINITELY SET AS THE DAY THREE 
DESTROYERS, THE ATHABASKAN, CAYUGA AND SIOUX, WILL SAIL OUT OF 
ESQUIMALT, BeCe, NAVAL BASE AND HEAD FOR PEARL HARBOR TO BE CLOSER 
TO KOREA dp THE UeNe ACCEPTS CANADA'S OFFER OF THEIR USE.

FIRST LEAD KOREAN-CHINA (320) 

BY JOHN M.sHIGHTOWER 

WASHINGTON JULY 2-(AP)-THE UNITED STATES DISCLOSED TODAY IT HAS 
CAUTIONED NATIONALIST CHINA TO LOOK TO THE STATE OF ITS OWN DEFENSES 
ON FORMOSA BEFORE SENDING TROOPS TO HELP REPEL THE COMMUNIST INVADERS 
OF SOUTH KOREA. 

IMPLICIT IN THE SUGGESTION WAS THE IDEA THAT THIS COUNTRY WILL BE 
AT LEAST AS WELL PLEASED IF THE PROJECT IS DROPPED. 

IN CAREFUL DIPLOMATIC LANGUAGE, THE AMERICAN GOVERNMENT ADVISED THE 
CHINESE IN A NOTE SENT YESTERDAY TO CONSULT WITH GEN.«DOUGLAS MACARTHUP 
ON THE DEFENSE OF THE ISLAND BECAUSE "OF THE THREAT OF INVASION BY 
(CHINESE) COMMUNIST FORCES FROM THE MAINLAND.” ARRANGEMENTS FOR 
CONSULTATION BETWEEN THE HEADQUARTERS OF MACARTHUR AND MILITARY AUTHOR- 
ITIES UNDER GENERALISSIMO CHIANG KAI-SHEK ARE ALREADY UNDER WAY. 

CHIANG HAD OFFERED TO SEND A SEASONED ARMY OF 33,000 MEN WITH THE 
BEST EQUIPMENT HE HAD INTO THE FIGHTING IN KOREA AND TO GIVE THEM ATR 
AND NAVAL ESCORT FROM HIS OWN SLENDER RESOURCES. 

WHILE THE UNITED STATES DID NOT REJECT CHIANG'S OFFER OUTRIGHT 
THE TONE OF THE NOTE MADE IT APPARENT THAT AMERICAN GOVERNMENT AUTHOR- 
ITIES DO NOT FAVOR HIS TAKING THE ACTION HE SUGGESTED. IT WAS UNDER- 
STOOD THERE ARE TWO REASONS FOR THIS. 

THE FIRST IS THE BELIEF HERE THAT FORMOSA IS IN DANGER OF COMMUNIST 
ASSAULT AND NEEDS MAXIMUM PROTECTION. TO THAT END PRESIDENT TRUMAN 
EARLY THIS WEEK ORDERED THE SEVENTH FLEET TO PROTECT THE ISLAND. 

THE OTHER REASON IS THAT THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS MIGHT SEIZE UPON THE 
PRESENCE OF CHINESE NATIONALIST FORCES IN KOREA TO ENTER THE FIGHTING 
THEMSELVES ON THE SIDE OF THE NORTH KOREAN REDS AND THEREBY ADD IM- 
PORTANTLY TO RED KOREAN STRENGTH. 

AN EXCHANGE OF NOTES BETWEEN THE AMERICAN AND CHINESE GOVERNMENTS 
WAS GIVEN OUT AT THE STATE DEPARTMENT ABOUT THE TIME PRESIDENT TRUMAN 
RETURNED TO WASHINGTON FROM A WEEKEND CRUISE. 

MEANUHILE SECRETARY OF STATE ACHESON WAS PUTTING IN ANOTHER SUNDAY 
AFTERNOON AT HIS STATE DEPARTMENT DESK TO KEEP CLOSE CHECK ON THE

WASHINGTON, JULY 2=(AP)-TEXTS OF THE.CHINESE AND AMERICAN NOTES 
ON CHINA'S OFFER TO SEND TROOPS TO KOREA: 
a AIDE-MEMOIRE OF JUNE 29 
THE GOVERNMENT OF THE REPUBLIC OF CHINA RECEIVED TODAY A COMMUN- 
ICATION FROM THE SECRETARY GENERAL OF THE UNITED NATIONS REQUESTING 
IT, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE SECURITY COUNCIL 
ON JUNE 27, 1950, TO FURNISH SUCH ASSISTANCE TO THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA 
AS MAY BE NECESSARY TO HELP REPEL THE ARMED ATTACK FROM NORTH KOREA, 
THE CHINESE REPUBLIC IS WILLING TO SEND LAND TROOPS TO SOUTH KOREA TO 
ASSIST IN THE OPERATIONS FOR THE PURPOSE. THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT 
WILL BE GLAD TO BE APPRISED OF THE OPINION OF THE UNITED STATES 
GOVERNMENT AT ITS EARLIEST CONVENIENCE. IN VIEW OF THE URGENT 
SITUATION IN SOUTH KOREA, THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT IS INSTRUCTING 
THE CHIEF OF THE CHINESE MISSION IN JAPAN TO APPROACH GENERAL MAC- 
ARTHUR AND INQUIRE ABOUT THE POSITIVE MEASURES WHICH MAY BE DESIRED. 
es S aoe 
AIDE-MEMOIRE OF JUNE 30 
THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT WILL MAKE AVAILABLE FOR USE IN SOUTH KOREA 
TO REPEL THE ARMED ATTACK OF NORTH KOREA ONE ARMY OF SEASONED TROOPS 


OF APPROXIMATELY 33,000 MEN SUITABLE FOR OPERATIONS IN PLAINS OR HILLY 


TERRAIN, 

THESE TROOPS CARRY THE BEST EQUIPMENT AT CHINA'S DISPOSAL. 

FOR THE TRANSPORTATION OF THESE TROOPS THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT WILL 
PROVIDE 20 AIR TRANSPORTS OF THE TYPE OF C-46 AND, IF NECESSARY, CAN 
GIVE A REASONABLE AMOUNT OF AIR COVER. IF THE TROOPS ARE TO BE TRANS- 
PORTED BY SEA, THE CHINESE GOVERNMENT CAN PROVIDE A MODERATE AMOUNT 
OF NAVAL ESCORT, 





we 


THESE TROOPS CAN BE READY FOR EMBARKATION IN FIVE DAYS.

IDEAS-PROPAGANDA (420) 
BY EDWIN B.sHAAKINSON 

WASHINGTON, JULY 2&lt;(AP)-A PROPOSAL TO BEAT BACK COMMUNISM WITH 
A FREE FLOW OF IDEAS ON AN AMBITIOUS SCALE WILL GET PUBLIC SUPPORT 
THIS WEEK FROM GENERAL DWIGHT EISENHOWER, SECRETARY OF STATE ACHESON 
AND AN IMPOSING LIST OF PROMINENT FIGURES. 

SENATOR BENTON (D-CONN) SAID TODAY THEY WILL TESTIFY AT PUBLIC 
HEARINGS THIS WEEK BEFORE SENATE FOREIGN RELATIONS SUBCOMMITTEE HEAR- 
INGS ON A "MARSHALL-RLAN-OF IDEAS." 

BENTON, FRESHMAN SENATOR, FORMER ADVERTISING MAN AND ONE-TIME 
STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIAL, AS ENLISTED SUPPORT OF A DOZEN OTHER SEN- 
ATORS FOR AN INTENSIFIED DRIVE TO COUNTER AND OVERTAKE THE WORLD WIDE 
PROPAGANDA EFFORTS OF COMMUNISM. 

THEIR MAIN THEME IS THAT THE UNITED STATES AND ITS ALLIES IN THE 
BATTLE AGAINST COMMUNISM AROUND THE GLOBE, MUST FIND WAYS TO PIERCE 
THE SO-CALLED IRON CURTAIN AND REACH THE EYES. EARS AND MINDS OF 
PEOPLE NOW GETTING ONLY COMMUNIST-CONTROLLED fNFORMATION. 

SENATOR BENTON CALLS THE "COLD WAR" BETWEEN RUSSIA AND THE UNITED 
STATES "A STRUGGLE FOR THE MINDS AND LOYALTIES OF MANKIND." 

ALTHOUGH ACTIVELY SUPPORTING EFFORTS TO AID ANTI-COMMUNIST FORCES 
WITH DOLLARS AND ARMS, BENTON SAID THIS COUNTRY MUST REMEMBER THAT 
"BULLETS, BOMBS, SHELLS AND FLAME DO NOT CHANGE MEN'S MINDS OR WIN 
THEIR LOYALTY." 

"THE MENTAL CAP IS MORE DANGEROUS THAN THE DOLLAR GAP." BENTON 
SAID AND URGED THE SENATE TO ENDORSE THIS PROGRAM TO CLOZE IT: 

1. STEADY PRESSURE THROUGH THE UNITED NATIONS AND DIPLOMATIC CHANNEL 
FOR "FREEDOM OF THE PRESS" FOR ALL KINDS OF COMMUNICATION MEDIA. 

2, MORE SUPPORT FOR UNESCO (UNITED NATIONS EDUCATIONAL, SCIENTIFIC 
AND CULTURAL ORGANIZATION) AND THE PROGRAM OF EXCHANGING STUDENTS 
WITH FOREIGN NATIONS. 

3, DEVELOPMENT OF AN UNCENSORED WORLD WIDE RADIO COMMUNICATIONS 
NETWORK ABLE TO REACH ALL RECEIVING SETS. 

BENTON SAID THE PRESENT "VOICE OF AMERICA" RADIO BROADCASTS To 
FOREIGN NATIONS ARE "A WHISPER" BECAUSE CONGRESS IIAS BEEN STINGY 
ON APPROPRIATIONS.

BEAMING BROADCASTS THERE.

FOR A FREE EUROPE, INC. (NCFE), A GROUP OF PRIVATE AMERICAN CITIZENS.

FOUR COLUMNS OF NORTH KOREAN TROOPS PUSHED SOUTH FROM RED-HELD 
SEOUL YESTERDAY (SUN) AND WERE ADVANCING TOWARD AMERICAN GROUND TROOPS 
MOVING NORTH FROM THE TEMPORARY SOUTHERN CAPITAL OF TAEJON. 

TWO OF THE RED COLUMNS OUTFLANKED THE TOWN AND VITAL AIRSTRIP OF 
SUWON ON THE EAST AFTER A BATTLE IN WHICH THE SOUTHERN DEFENDERS LOST 
SEVEN STRONG RESISTANCE CENTERS. THE OTHER TWO ATTACK UNITS WERE 
DESCRIBED AS “TANK COLUMNS." 

AN AMERICAN SOURCE IN TAEJON ADMITTED THAT THE MILITARY SITUATION 
IN SOUTH KOREA HAD WORSENED OVER THE COLD, RAINY WEEK-END.

“THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT IS REVEALING STEP BY STEP ITS

TOKYO, TUESDAY, JULY 4-(AP)-FRIENDLY PLANES STAGED A MACHINEGUN 
AND ROCKET ATTACK NEAR ADVANCED U.S.POSITIONS IN SOUTH KOREA YESTERDAY 

AND AMERICAN AIR OFFICIALS SAID AN INVESTIGATION IS UNDERWAY. 

AN AMERICAN SERGEANT WAS SLIGHTLY WOUNDED. 

ASSOCIATED PRESS CORRESPONDENT TOM LAMBERT IN THE FIELD SAID 
THE PLANES WERE MUSTANG FIGHTERS BEARING AUSTRALIAN MARKINGS. 

LToGENeHeCeHeROBERTSON, COMMANDER OF BRITISH COMMONWEALTH OCCUPATION 
FORCES IN JAPAN, SAID NO AUSTRALIAN PLANES WERE ALOFT THEN 
AND THE ATTACKERS WERE U.S. F-80 JETS AND A "KOREAN MUSTANG." 
mneroesinic OFFICIALS SAID THAT POSITIVE IDENTIFICATION WAS "VIRTUALLY

THEY SAID THIS WAS NOT THE FIRST, AND PROBABLY WILL NOT BE THE 
LAST TIME, THAT FRIENDLY AIR CRAFT FIRE NEAR OR PERHAPS ON THEIR OWN 
TROOPS. THE KOREAN BATTLE IS FLUID AND CONFUSED. 

“ALL OF THESE INCIDENTS ARE REGRETTABLE,” SAID ONE OFFICER, 

"BUT THEY HAPPEN IN EVERY WAR." 

A SPOKESMAN AT ADVANCED HEADQUARTERS IN SOUTH KOREA SAID FLATLY 
THE IDENTITY OF THE PLANES WAS NOT KNOWN. 

LAMBERT SAID IN A TELEPHONE CALL TO TOKYO AFTER ROBERTSON 
MADE HIS STATEMENT THAT HE SAW NO JETS IN THE ATTACK, WHICH 
SENT HIM DIVING TO COVER.

KOREA*AIR FORCE (120) 

WASHINGTON, JULY 3-(AP)-THE AIR FORCE REPORTED AMERICAN AND 
AUSTRALIAN PLANES FLEW 105 SORTIES OVER KOREA TODAY AND ONE F-80 JET 
FIGHTER WAS LOST IN ACTION. 

THE REPORT COVERED THE 24-HOUR PERIOD ENDING AT MIDNIGHT, JULY 3, 
KOREAN TIME. A SPOKESMAN SAID RESULTS OF THE 105 SORTIES WERE 
*UNKNOWNe" A SORTIE IS ONE FLIGHT BY ONE PLANE.

TAIPEI, FORMOSA, JULY 3-(AP)-CHINESE NATIONALIST LEADER CHIANG 
KAI-SHEK SAID TONIGHT THE UNITED NATIONS SHOULD CHARGE SOVIET RUSSIA 
WITH INSTIGATING THE KOREAN WAR AND ASK HER TO HALT FURTHER NORTH KOREA 
ATTACKS ON THE SOUTHERN REPUBLIC, 

ADDRESSING A MEETING OF HIS GOVERNMENT'S OFFICIALS, CHIANG 
APPEALED TO THE UNITED NATIONS TO CONSOLIDATE ASIATIC PEOPLES IN THEIR 
STRUGGLE AGAINST COMMUNISN AND PREVENT THEM FROM BEING UTILIZED BY THE 
RUSSIANS OOLS OF AGGRESSION. 

HE SPOKE SHORTLY AFTER OTHER NATIONALIST SOURCES SAID THEY WERE 
DISAPPOINTED IN WASHINGTON'S REJECTION OF NATIONALISTS OFFERS TO SEND 
COMBAT TROOPS TO AID IN THE FIGHT TO HALT COMMUNIST NORTH KOREA'S 
INVASION OF THE SOUTH KOREA REPUBLIC. |

ON AN EQUAL FOOTING WITH EUROPE IN THEIR ANTI-COMMUNIST EFFORTS.

CONCENTRATING ALL THEIR ATTENTION ON EUROPE AND NEGLECTING ASIA." 

®ASIA WITH HALF THE WORLD*S POPULATION WILL BE A DECISIVE FACTOR 
IN THE FUTURE STRUGGLE BETWEEN THE DEMOCRACIES AND THE COMMUNIST 
AGGRESSORS." CHIANG ASSERTED.

FIGHT DEMOCRACIES WHILE THE RUSSIANS REMAINED IN THE BACKGROUND

RUSSIA THROUGH ITS PUPPETS AGAINST THE PEOPLES OF ASIA HAVE BEEN OVER}

TOKYO, TUESDAY, JULY 4-(AP)-A PERSONAL REPRESENTATIVE OF TRYGVE LIE 


SECRETARY GENERAL OF THE UNITED NATIONS, ARRIVED IN TOKYO BY PLANE T 
FOR A STUDY OF THE KOREAN CRISIS. 

COL. ALFRED KATZIN OF SOUTH AFRICA, ACCOMPANIED BY FOUR MEMBERS OF 
THE UNITED NATIONS STAFF, SAID HE WILL MAKE A FIRST-HAND SURVEY OF THE 
WAR THAT THREATENS WORLD PEACE. 

KATZIN TOLD THE ASSOCIATED PRESS THE PURPOSE OF HIS TOUR WAS TO MEET 
WITH TOP MILITARY OFFICIALS, MEMBERS OF THE U.N. COMMISSION TO KOREA 
AND REPRESENTATIVES OF THE SOUTH KOREAN GOVERNMENT. HE THEN WILL GIVE 
LIE A COMPLETE PICTURE OF THE SITUATION. 

KATZIN DECLINED TO DISCUSS ANY ASPECTS OF THE KOREAN WAR UNTIL HE 
HAS COMPLETED HIS WORK. 

ACCOMPANYING KATZIN WERE DONALD SULLIVAN OF THE UNITED STATES, 

CHIEF OF ADMINISTRATION TO THE U.N. SECRETARIAT; CECIL GOYDER OF GREAT

WASHINGTON, JULY 3-(AP)-THE AIR FORCE HAS RECEIVED REPORTS THAT A 
aL Agta OF PERSONS SIGHTED A MYSTERIOUS OBJECT TODAY NEAR ANCHORAGE, 

A SPOKESMAN SAID TONIGHT THAT SUCH REPORTS HAVE BEEN RECEIVED BUT 
THAT THE AIR FORCE DOES NOT KNOW WHAT THE OBJECT WAS. 

"SEVERAL PEOPLE HAVE REPORTED SEEING A MYSTERIOUS OBJECT IN THE 
SKY," THIS AIR FORCE SPOKESMAN SAID. "SO FAR WE HAVE HAD ONLY 
SKETCHY REPORTS, WITH NO DETAILS. WE HAVE NO _ IDEA WHAT IT WAS." 

HE SAID THE REPORTS QUOTED BOTH AIR FORCE PERSONNEL AND CIVILIANS 
AS SAYING THEY HAD SEEN THE OBJECT. 

THIS OFFICER SAID HE COULD NOT ATTEMPT TO DESCRIBE IT ON THE 
BASIS OF PRESENT INFORMATION HERE, BECAUSE IT WAS "VARIOUSLY DESCRIBED 
BY VARIOUS PEOPLE." 

THE AIR FORCE CONDUCTED A TWO-YEAR INQUIRY INTO REPORTS OF SO- 
CALLED FLYING SAUCERS AND CONCLUDED THAT THEY COULD BE ATTRIBUTED TO 
“MISINTERPRETATION OF VARIOUS CONVENTIONAL OBJECTS, A MILD FORM 
OF MASS HYSTERIA OR HOAXES."

SAN DIEGO, CALIF., JULY 4-(AP)-THE ELEVENTH NAVAL DISTRICT TODAY 
CLAMPED WARTIME SECRECY ON NEWS OF SHIP MOVEMENTS FOLLOWING THE ANNOUN- 
CEMENT FROM WASHINGTON YESTERDAY THAT MARINES OF THE FIRST DIVISION 
AT CAMP PENDLETON HAD BEEN ORDERED TO THE KOREAN WAR ZONE. __ 

ALL LEAVES HAVE BEEN CANCELLD FOR PERSONNEL AT CAMP PENDLETON 
HUGE MARINE TRAINING BASE AT OCEANSIDE, NORTH OF SAN DIEGO, AND HOME 
OF THE FIRST DIVISION. 

BRIG. GEN. E.A. CRAIG, ACTING PENDLETON COMMANDER, SAID THE 
DIVISION--WHICH HAS JUST FINISHED FIVE-WEEK INTENSIVE FIELD TRAINING-- 
IS READY "TO MOVE OUT IN A MINIMUM OF TIME, PREPARED FOR ANY MISSION." 

THE WASHINGTON ANNOUNCEMENT SA'D THE MARINES WOULD BE TRANSPORTED 
TO JAPAN BY SHIP AND WERE EXPECTED TO ARRIVE THERE IN ABOUT 16 DAYS. 

ONLY THREE 16-KNOT NAVAL TROOP TRANSPORTS ARE IN PORT AND IT Is 
BELIEVED IT WOULD BE IMPOSSIBLE FOR THEM TO MEET THE 16-DAY SCHEDULE 
EVEN IF LOADING STARTED AT ONCE. : 

THIS LED TO SPECULATION THAT THE NAVY MIGHT PRESS INTO SERVICE ONE 
QR MORE OF THE 21-KNOT TRANSPORTS OF THE MILITARY SEA TRANSPORTATION 
ERVICE. 

THE DECISION TO SEND THE FIRST DIVISION OVERSEAS CAME AS 7,000 
MARINES PARADED IN FULL BATTLE EQUIPMENT IN A COMBAT REVIEW, IN WHICH 
NEARLY 100 FIGHTER PLANS FROM THE EL TORO, CALIFe, MARINE AIR 
BASE ALSO PARTICIPATED. 

THE 11TH NAVAL DISTRICT SAID THAT FOR THE TIME BEING, AT LEAST,

ISSUED TODAY BY GENERAL MURMAMMRIAE TILA DQUARTERS ¢ Uo Fer East Air Force 

AIR ACTION AGAINST NORTH KOREAN GROUND ELEMENTS ON JULY 4 WAS 
LIMITED DURING THE EARLY MORNING BY POOR VISIBILITY AND LOW CEILINGS. 

EXCELLENT WEATHER CONDITIONS LATER IN THE DAY PERMITTED FAR EAST 
AIR FORCE UNITS TO STAGE A TOTAL OF 162 SORTIES INCLUDING 
GROUND STRAFING ATTACKS BY FIFTH AIRLFORCE AND RAAF FIGHTER PLANES 
AND 23 CARGO FLIGHTS FROM JAPANESE BASFS. 

NORTH KOREAN LOSSES CONSISTED OF THREE TRUCKS, ONE BUS AND TWO 
LOCOMOTIVES DESTROYED BY FIGHTER AIRCRAFT. ANOTHER LOCOMOTIVE WAS 
DAMAGED AND ONE CAR OF A TWELVE CAR TRAIN WAS LEFT BURNING AFTER A 
STRAFING ATTACK NORTHEAST OF SEOUL. A RAILROAD TRESTLE APPROX IMATELY 
ONE OR TWO MILES WEST OF INCHANGNI WAS DESTROYED. 

OTHER TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY, INCLUDING RAILROAD INSTALLATIONS, 
TRUCKS AND MISCELLANEOUS VEHICLES WERE HIT AND DAMAGED.

TOKYO, JULY 4-CAP)-THE TEXT OF GENERAL MACARTHUR"S STATEMENT ON 
OBSERVANCE OF THE RULES OF WARFARE FOLLOWS: 

PERSONNEL OF THE ARMED FOR F NORTH KOREA AND OTHER PERSONS OF 
NORTH KOREA WHO ARE TAKEN INTO CUSTODY OR FALL INTO THE HANDS OF ARMED 
FORCES NOW UNDER MY OPERATIONAL CONTROL IN CONNECTION WITH HOSTILITIES 
IN KOREA WILL BE TREATED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE HUMANITARIAN PRINCIPLES 
APPLIED BY AND RECOGNIZED BY CIVILIZED NATIONS INVOLVED IN ARMED 
CONFLICT. I WILL EXPECT SIMILAR TREATMENT FOR AMERICAN NATIONS AND 
MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES OF THE UNITED STATES, AS WELL AS OTHER 
NATIONALS AND MEMBERS OF OTHER ARMED FORCES WHO MAY JOIN THE 
UNITED STATES IN THE KOREAN CONFLICT AND WHO MAY AT ANY TIME BE IN 
NORTH KOREAN HANDS. OPERATING PURSUANT TO RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED BY 
THE UNITED NATIONS SECURITY COUNCIL, AND AS COMMANDER OF FORCES PLACED 
UNDER MY COMMAND BY SUCH RESOLUTIONS, I, WILL HOLD RESPONSIBLE ANY 
INDIVIDUAL @P NORTH KOREA WHO DEVIATES FROM THESE PRINCIPLES OR WHO 
CAUSES » PERMITS OR ORDERS ANY DEVIATION FROM SUCH PRINCIPLES.

NIGHT LEAD CHINESE 
BY SPENCER MOOSA 

TAIPEI. FORMOSA, JULY 4-(AP)-NATIONALIST NAVAL HEADQUARTERS TODAY 
SAID ITS SHIPS SMASHED A CHINESE COMMUNIST ATTEMPT TO INVADE THE 
TACHEN ISLANDS MONDAY, 

THE NATIONALISTS SAID THEIR WARSHIPS SANK 20 TROOP-LADEN COMMUNIST 
CRAFT AND FORCED OTHERS TO TURN BACK TO THE MAINLAND. 

THE TACHENS ARE TINY ISLANDS 20 MILES FROM THE CHINESE MAINLAND 
AND 220 MILES NORTH OF FORMOSA. THEY ARE GARRISONED MOSTLY BY 
CUERRILLAS, AND THE NATIONALISTS HAVE TRIED TO DEVELOP THEM AS A 
SUPPLY POINT FOR GUERRILLA RAIDS ON COMMUNIST CHINA. _ 

NAVAL HEADQUARTERS DESCRIBED MONDAY'S ACTION AS PURELY DEFENSIVE 
AND HENCE NOT IN VIOLATION OF NATIONALIST SUSPENSION OF OPERATIONS 
AGAINST THE MAINLAND, AS REQUESTED LAST WEEK BY PRESIDENT TRUMAN. 

THE PRESIDENT ASKED THE SUSPENSION IN HIS STATEMENT THAT U.S. 
WARSHIPS WOULD PREVENT CHINESE COMMUNIST INVASION OF FORMOSA. 

NATIONALIST QUARTERS SPECULATE THAT THE CHINESE REDS WILL DO THEIR 
UTMOST TO EXPLOIT THE SUSPENSION OF NATIONALIST OPERATIONS. 

DEFENSE MINISTRY SOURCES SAID THEY BELIEVE THE COMMUNISTS WILL 
PROBABLY STRIKE AT QUEMOY ISLAND, THE NATIONALIST DEFENSE OUTPOST 
NEAR RED-HELD AMOY, AND AT OTHER’ ISLANDS OFF THE MAINLAND COAST SUCH 
AS MATSU NEAR FOOCHOW. 

OFFICIALS SAID NO FINAL DECISION HAS YET BEEN COMMUNICATED TO 
TAIPEI BY GENERAL MACARTHUR ON THE NATIONALIST OFFER TO SEND 33,000 
TROOPS TO SOUTH KOREA TO HELP FIGHT THE COMMUNIST NORTHERN KOREAN 


INVADERS 
WHEN THIS OFFER WAS MADE, WASHINGTON ASKED THE NATIONALIST GOVERN-~ 
MENT TO HOLD OFF. IT WAS BELIEVED WASHINGTON DID THIS PARTLY IN 

FEAR THAT PARTICIPATION OF NATIONALIST TROOPS IN THE KOREAN FIGHTING 
MIGHT CAUSE COMMUNIST CHINA TO SEND TROOPS TO FIGHT ALONGSIDE THE 


NORTH KOREANS.

ON THIS JULY 4TH HOLIDAY, PRESIDENT TRUMAN SPENT THE DAY QUIETLY 
AT BLAIR HOUSE WHILE DISPATCHES FROM GENeMACARTHUR'S HEADQUARTERS 
ca REPORTED A RISING FURY OF BATTLE ALL ALONG THE SOUTH KOREAN 

THE PRESIDENT HAD NO ENGAGEMENTS SCHEDULED AND WAS REPORTED 
KEEPING A CLOSE WATCH ON DEVELOPMENTS IN THE 10 DAY OLD CONFLICT. 

THE SOUTH KOREAN AMBASSADOR, DR. JOHN MeCHANG, RELEASED A LETTER 
FROM MReTRUMAN IN WHICH THE PRESIDENT DECLARED: - 

"I DEEPLY APPRECIATE THE HEROISM OF THE KOREAN DEFENDERS IN THEIR 
FIGHT AGAINST THE INVADERS. BY THE STAUNCH RESISTANCE OF YOUR 
GOVERNMENT AND YOUR PEOPLE YOU ARE SHOWING THE WORLD THAT FREEDOM- 
LOVING PEOPLE WILL FIGHT AGAINST COMMUNISM WHEREVER IT ARISES. 


ASDAWX 
"ALL THE FREE PEOPLE OF THE WORLD ARE ON YOUR SIDE. THEY PRAY 

FOR THE SUCCESS OF THE KOREAN DEFENDERS AND THEY BITTERLY CONDEMN 

THE UNPROVOKED COMMUNIST ATTACK." 

MR» TRUMAN WENT ON TO SAY HE IS “DEEPLY GRIEVED BY THE TERRIBLE 
SUFFERING OF YOUR PEOPLE BECAUSE OF LOSS OF LIFE AND DESTRUCTION FROM 
THE BRUTAL COMMUNIST ATTACK." 

"Il KNOW THAT ALL THE FREE PEOPLE OF THE WORLD JOIN ME IN THIS SENTI- 
MENT»" THE PRESIDENT SAID.

WASHINGTON, JULY 4-CAP)=-GEN.sDOUGLAS MACARTHUR PROBABLY WILL BE 
NAMED UNITED NATIONS COMMANDER FOR THE KOREAN POLICE ACTION IN A FEW 
DAYS, AND THE FORCES UNDER HIM WILL BE GIVEN THE RIGHT TO FLY THE 
UNITED NATIONS FLAG. THOSE TWO STEPS ARE INCLUDED IN A FORMULA 
BEING CONSIDERED HERE AS RO MEATS OF SOLVE TS OE aC AMANT BROBLENS. 

THE PROBLEMS ARISE FROM THE FACT THAT THE UNITED NATIONS HAS NEVER 
BEEN -ABLE-TO-FORM POLICE FORCES OF ITS OWN AND MUST NOW RELY IN KOREA 
ON FORCES SENT IN BY MEMBER NATIONS UNDER LAST WEEK'S SECURITY 
COUNCIL RESOLUTION. 

CANADIAN AMBASSADOR HUME WRONG DISCUSSED THE PROBLEM TODAY WITH 
ASSISTANT SECRETARY OF STATE JOHN DeHICKERSON. LATER IT WAS IN- , 
DICATED THAT SOME ACTION IN THE FORM OF A RESOLUTION MIGHT BE TAKEN BY 
THE SECURITY COUNCIL IN NEW YORK IN A FEW DAYS "AFTER FULL DISCUSSIONS 
WITH DELEGATES OF OTHER NATIONS. 

ACCORDING TO THE FORMULA BEING DEVELOPED HERE, THE SECURITY COUNCIL 
WILL BE ASKED TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION PROVIDING: 

1. A CLEAR CONNECTION BETWEEN THE UNITED NATIONS AND GEN,MACARTHUR, 
THE AMERICAN COMMANDER IN THE FAR EAST, WHO IN ACTUAL FACT IS DIRECTIN 
THE KOREAN FIGHTING AGAINST THE COMMUNIST INVADERS FROM THE NORTH. __

LOS_ANCELES, JULY 4~(AP)-AMERICAN TROOPS CAN EXPECT LITTLE HELP FROM 
THE ARMY OR THE PEOPLE OF SOUTH KOREA, SAYS DR«KAZUO KAWAI, EDITOR-IN- 
CHIEF OF TOKYO'S NIPPON TIMES. — 

HE TOLD A TOWN HALL MEETING HERE YESTERDAY THAT THE KOREANS "HAVE 
NO LOVE FOR THE DEMOCRATIC GOVERNMENT AND LITTLE LOVE FOR THE UNITED 
STATES. THE WAR WILL BE A LONG AND COSTLY ONE." 

THE EDITOR, A SPECIALIST ON FAR EASTERN AFFAIRS NOW TEACHING HISTORY 
AT STANFORD UNIVERSITY, ADDED? 

"IT IS QUITE POSSIBLE THAT SOUTH KOREANS MAY FIGHT AGAINST THE 
AMERICAN ARMY AS GUERRILLA TROOPS BEHIND THE LINES." 

HE ASSERTED THAT NOTHING WILL BE SOLVED. BY PUSHING THE COMMUNISTS 
BACK BEYOND THE 38TH PARALLEL. "A POSITION THAT IS IMPOSSIBLE WILL BE 
MERELY REPLACED WITH ONE THAT IS ILLOGICAL AND UNTENABLE,” HE PREDICTED.

MEN GATHERED, IT WAS TALKED ABOUT. EVERYWHERE THERE WAS A THRILL OF

PARIS JULY 4-(AP)=PREMIER HENRI 'S NEW RIGHTIST GOVERNMENT 
WAS “TOPPLED BY THE VOTES OF SOCTALISTS COMMUNISTS AND DE GAULL 1S TS ON 
ITS FIRST TEST IN THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY TODAY, 336 TO 221. 

THE VOTE CAME ON A POINT OF PROCEDURE. TWO QUESTIONS HAD BEEN 
PLACED BEFORE THE HOUSE BY OPPOSITION DEPUTIES ON THE MAKEUP OF THE 
CABINET AND THE POLICY IT INTENDED TO FOLLOW. QUEUILLE ASKED THAT THE 
QUESTIONS BE PIGEON-HOLED. THE ASSEMBLY REJECTED HIS REQUEST. 

QUEUILLE, THOUGH NOT BOUND BY LAW TO QUIT, HANDED HIS 
RESIGNATION’ TO PRESIDENT VINCENT AURIOL IMMEDIATELY. AURIOL THEN 
BEGAN TALKS WITH PARLIAMENTARY LEADERS ON THE FORMATION OF ANOTHER 

V : , 

THE SOCIALISTS HAD PREVIOUSLY SUPPORTED QUEUILLE. IT WAS THEIR 
SWING TO THE OPPOSITION THAT DEFEATED THE RADICAL SOCIALIST LEADER 
AND HIS MINISTERS. 

QUEUILLE WAS BACKED ONLY BY HIS OWN RADICAL SOCIALIST PARTY, A 
PORTION OF EX-PREMIER GEORGES BIDAULT"S POPULAR REPUBLICAN MOVEMENT 
AND SOME INDEPENDENTS. 

THE SOCIALISTS BITTERLY OPPOSED TWO OF QUEUILLE'S NOMINEES-- 
EX-PREMIER PAUL REYNAUD, AN INDEPENDENT REPUBLICAN WHOM THEY REGARD 
1 AS TOO CONSERVATIVE, AND PAUL GIACOBBI, A FORMER DE GAULLIST. 

QUEUILLE HAD HOPED THE SOCIALISTS MIGHT ABSTAIN. IF THEY HAD 
DONE SO, HE MIGHT HAVE WON BY A BARE MAJORITY. BUT THE SOCIALIST 
DEPUTIES, URGED ON BY FORMER INTERIOR MINISTER JULES MOCH, DECIDED IN 
A PARTY CONFERENCE, 61 TO 26, TO THROW THEIR WEIGHT AGAINST THE 
TWO-DAY-OLD REGIME, 

SOCIALIST FLOOR LEADER CHARLES LUSSY TOLD QUEUILLE? 

"THE SOCIALIST GROUP DID NOT PARTICIPATE IN YOUR CABINET BECAUSE 
IT COULD NOT GET AN AGREEMENT ON MAJOR QUESTIONS X X Xe THE 
PRESENCE OF CERTAIN OF YOUR COLLABORATORS WAS A SURPRISE, TO US. 
MePAUL REYNAUD HAS NOT CHANGED.® ¥

"THE WORST THING FOR ME, A THING WHICH WOULD MAKE MY LIFE 
MISERABLE, WOULD BE TO SEE’ THE DESERTION--AS IF I HAD BETRAYED 
THEM--OF THOSE WHO SUPPORTED ME FOR 13 MONTHS." 

THIS WAS A REFERENCE TO QUEUILLE'S PREVIOUS CABINET, WHICH LASTED 
MORE THAN A YEAR WITH SOCIALIST BACKING. 

IT IS BELIEVED LIKELY THAT PRESIDENT AURIOL NOW WILL NAME A 
SOCIALIST AS PREMIER. IT IS DOUBTFUL, HOWEVER, THAT A SOCIALIST 
CAN NOW GET THE 311 VOTES NEEDED FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE ASSEMBLY. 

MOCH HAD A TRY LAST OCTOBER AND WON CONFIRMATION, BUT HE WAS 
UNABLE TO FORM A CABINET AND HAD TO GIVE UP. 

THE ASSEMBLY CONFIRMED QUEUILLE AS PREMIER BY 363 TO 208 LAST 
SATURDAY, WITH THE SOCIALISTS VOTING IN HIS FAVOR.

DOWN BIDAULT*S CABINET ON A QUESTION OF PAY INCREASES FOR GOVERNMENT

CAN STRIKE DOWN LIBERTY, PIECEMEAL, WITH FIRE AND SWORD.

ALL SENSE OF RESTRAINT.* |

IVES WHO WERE INDEPENDENT OF THE PARTY WHICH CONTROLLED THE ELECTION 
MACHINERY AND THE POLICE FORCE. 
DULLES SAID THAT THE SOUTH KOREA REPUBLIC COULD NOT BE OVERTHROWN 
FROM WITHIN AND THEREFORE WAS MADE THE TARGET FOR POWERFUL AGGRESSION.

ISTIC OF MILITARY DESPOTISM," HE SAID. “IT WAS, IN MINIATURE, THE 
KIND OF ATTACK THAT COULD HiT US IF WE ARE CONTENT TO LIVE IN’A WORLD 
WHERE SUCH METHODS ARE TOLERATED. THE STRUGGLE IN KOREA REPRESENTS 
THE TIMELESS ISSUE OF WHETHER LOVERS OF LIBERTY WILL BE VIGILANT 
ENOUGH, BRAVE ENOUGH AND UNITED ENOUGH TO SURVIVE DESPOTISM."

CADVANCE WASHINGTON, JULY 4=CAP)-THE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION 
AND THE NATION FACE A "CRISIS," THE FEDERATION OF AMERICAN SCIENTISTS 
SAID TODAY. 

A STATEMENT ISSUED BY FEDERATION CHAIRMAN WeA. HIGINBOTHAM SAID 
THIS CRISIS IS DUE TO FAILURE OF THE SENATE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMITTEE 
TO APPROVE THE RENOMINATION OF SUMNER PIKE, ACTING AEC CHAIRMAN. 

THE FIVE-MAN AEC NOW HAS ONLY THREE MEMBERS, THE STATEMENT CON- 
TINUED. IT SAID "THE SHATTERING EFFECT OF THIS. SITUATION ON THE 
OPERATIONS OF THE ENTIRE AEC AND THE MORALE OF ITS PERSONNEL IS 
DIFFICULT TO OVERESTIMATE." 

WHEN THE COMMITTEE TURNED THUMBS DOWN ON PIKE LAST WEEK, SOME 
MEMBERS DESCRIBED KIM AS "A SQUARE PEG IN A ROUND HOLE." PRESIDENT 
TRUMAN CALLED HIM ONE OF THE COMMISSION'S ABLEST AND MOST FAITHFUL 
MEMBERS, 

THE SCIENTISTS’ STATEMENT SAID$ 

"IT IS NOT OUR INTENTION TO ASSESS BLAME FOR THE PRESENT STATE OF 
AFFAIRS, NOR TO DWELL ON THE DIFFICULTY IN PLACING OUTSTANDING MEN IN 
THESE IMPORTANT POSITIONS. WHAT WE ARE CONCERNED WITH IS THAT THE 
EXECUTIVE AND LEGISLATIVE BRANCHES SHALL BOTH IMMEDIATELY BUCKLE DOW! 
TO THE TASKS ASSIGNED THEM UNDER THE ATOMIC ENERGY ACT, AND SHALL | 
SPEEDILY BY NOMINATION AND CONFIRMATION BRING THE AEC UP TO ITS FULL 
STRENGTH OF FIVE COMMISSIONERS AND A PERMANENT CHAIRMAN. 

"IN THE IMMEDIATE SITUATION, THE SENATE SHOULD GIVE FULL CONSIDER- 
ATION TO THE NOMINATION OF MR.PIKE, ONLY IN- THESE WAYS WILL THE 
AMERICAN PEOPLE BE CONVINCED THAT THE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION, IN 


WHICH THEY HAVE PLACED SO MUCH HOPE FOR PRESENT AND FUTURE SECURITY, 
IS NOT BEING DEGRADED BY INABILITY OF IMPORTANT GOVERNMENTAL OFFICIALS 
TO PUT ASIDE PETTY CONSIDERATIONS WHEN CONFRONTED BY AN ISSUE OF 
SUPREME MAGNITUDE."

AN ADVANCED COMMAND OUTPOST IN SOUTH KOREA, THURSDAY, JULY 6-(AP)- 
EIGHT RUSSIAN-MADE NORTH KOREAN TANKS STRUCK AMERICAN’ OUTPOSTS 
YESTERDAY AND AT LEAST TWO OF THEM THROUGH A RAIN OF SHELLS AND 
BAZOOKA FIRE, INFILTRATED AMERICAN POSITIONS AND CUT OFF ONE FORWARD 
ELEMENT. ~ 

THE ACTION BEGAN AT 8318 AeMe KOREAN TIME (5818 PoMe 
TIME TUESDAY) WHEN TANKS MOVING SOUTH DOWN THE ROAD FROM SUWON WERE 
UNDER FIRE BY UeSe MEDIUM ARTILLERY. THE REDS HAD CAPTURED SUWON 
TUESDAY. 


Ai S2KX 
WHEN THE TWO TANKS BROKE THROUGH, ADVANCING TOWARD THE AMERICAN 
NFANTRY POSITIONS, THE ARTILLERY wAs FORCED TO WITHHOLD FURTHER FIRE. 
AS NIGHT FELL AMERICANS WERE FIRING HEAVY MORTARS AT THE TANKS 
WHICH WERE PARKED MENACINGLY NEAR THE RAILWAY STATION AT SOJONG 
SOUTH OF SUWON. (DETAILED MAPS PUT SOJONG 18 MILES SOUTH OF SUWON.) 
UNLESS THE TANKS ARE ELIMINATED, IT IS POSSIBLE THEY MIGHT RAISE 
HAVOC BEHIND AMERICAN LINES AND with THE ADVANCED AMERICAN ELEMENTS 
WHICH WERE CUT OFF THROUGHOUT THE .

AMERICAN INFANTRYMEN AND BAZOOKA SQUADS FOUGHT A FOUR=HUUK 
BATTLE WITH THE TANKS THIS AFTERNOON WITHOUT KNOCKING THEM OUT. 

THE BATTLE WAS WITNESSED BY THIS CORRESPONDENT, CARL MYDANS OF 
TIME AND LIFE, MARGUERITE HIGGINS OF THE NEW YORK HERALD-TRIBUNE, 
DENNIS WARNER, AUSTRALIAN: JOURNALIST, AND ANDREW MC@ARTNEY -OF- 
REUTERS. BRITISH NEWS SERVICE. 

WE ARRIVED AT AN AMERICAN COMMAND POST EARLY YESTERDAY IN A 
DOWNPOUR OF RAIN JUST AS THE SENIOR OFFICER SLITHERED THROUGH THE 
MUD WITH INFORMATION ABOUT THE TANK BREAKTHROUGH. . 

THE COMMAND POST WAS IN A SQUALID LITTLE KOREAN FARMHOUSE. SEVERAL 
OFFICERS AND MEN HUDDLED UNDER THE PORCH OUT OF THE RAIN EATING 
BREAKFAST FROM A THERMOS CONTAINER. 

IN A CORNER OF THE FARMYARD, FIVE WHITE CHICKENS IN A COOP CLUCKED 
AND COMPLAINED DISMALLY. 

THE SENIOR OFFICER UNFOLDED A CRACKLING MAP ON THE PORCH FLOOR 
AND POINTED TO THE BREAKTHROUCH AREA, 

"THIS IS THE FIRST TIME NORTH KORFANS HAVE MET AMERICAN TROOPS AND 
I THINK THEY ARE GOING TO GET QUITE A SHOCK OUT OF IT.® HF DECLARED. 

"WE MUST FIND THOSE TANKS AND KNOCK HELL OUT OF THEM." 

CLUTCHING A "GREASE GUN," (SUB MACHINEGUN) IN ONE HAND AND A Pip. 
IN ANOTHER, THE OFFICER DIRECTED BAZOOKA SQUADS ORDERED OUT TO. HUNT 
AND KILL THE TANKS. : JUL x. 

THE COMMAND POST ERUPTED INTO ACTION. A SERGEANT CALLED UP THE 
HEADQUARTERS BAZOOKA SQUAD AND RELAYED THE ORDERS WHILE STANDING IN A 
PELTING RAIN WHICH RAN OFF THE ROOF IN A STREAM AND HISSED INTO A 
DIRTY PUDDLE. 

A LANKY GI WITH HIS BAYONET STUCK INTO HIS BOOTTOP AND TIED TO HIS 
LEG WITH A BIT OF GRASS ROPE SHRUGGED INTO HIS RAINCOAT AND PICKED 
UP THE LONG SLENDER STEEL TUBE KNOWN AS THE BAZOOKA. 

"LET'S GO, JACK," HE SAID CALMLY TO ANOTHER SOLDIER. 

"DON'T COME BACK UNLESS YOU GET THOSE TANKS,” THE SERGEANT INSTRUCTED 
HIS SQUAD AS THEY HEADED OUT THROUGH THE RAIN. 

THE BAZOOKA SQUAD MOVED OUT, THE LITTLE TEAM SLITHERING IN THE MUD. 
THEY MOVED OUT PAST GUN EMPLACEMENTS, PAST INFANTRY POSITIONS INTO 
A COUNTRYSIDE STRANGELY QUIET EXCEPT FOR THE DRUM OF THE RAIN. 

AS THEY MOVED NORTH THEY MET MANY KOREAN SOLDIERS FLEEING SOUTH 
INCLUDING AN ARM-WAVING CAVALRYMAN WHO PULLED UP HIS HORSE, SHOUTED 
"TANKS 4 TANKS," AND THEN WHIPPED HIS HORSE INTO A GALLOP SOUTH. 

ABOUT A MILE FROM SOJONG THE CAVALCADE HALTED AND BAZOOKA SQUAD 
SOLDIERS ENTERED THE THICK SHRUBBERY AT THE ROADSIDE. FIRST LT.

VAULTED OUT OF HI@ JEEP, CARBINE IN HAND.

THE MEN DUG IN. PAYNE SNAKED FORWARD TOWARD THE EDGE OF THE ROAD 
ADVANCED WARILY.

aT i aritine 5-(AP)=-DIPLOMATIC OBSERVERS TODAY PREDICTED SOVIET 


RUSSIA IS SETTING THE STAGE FOR A SURPRISE MOVE AGAINST THE UNITED 
STATES IN THE FAR EAST. 

THEY SAID THE RUSSIANS, PROBABLY WOULD RUSH CHINESE COMMUNIST 
TROOPS FROM MANCHURIA TO AID SOVIET-SUPPORTED NORTH KOREA IN THE KOREAN 
SUCH A MOVE "CAN BE EXPECTED ANY TIME WITHIN THE NEXT MONTH, AND 

PROBABLY WITHIN TWO WEEKS," THEY ADDED. ALL DEMANDED ANONYMITY. 

ONE OBSERVER GAVE THESE REASONS FOR FORECASTING) A SOVIET 
OFFENSIVE IN THE FAR EAST: UL ts DU ou 

1—--HIS COUNTRY (AND HE DECLINED USE OF HIS NATIONALITY. AS-WELL AS 
HIS NAME FOR DIPLOMATIC REASONS) HAS "DEFINITE WORD" THAT THE CHINESE 
REDS HAVE BEEN MASSING TROOPS IN MANCHURIA SINCE THEY CAPTURED HAINAN 
ISLAND, OFF THE SOUTH CHINA COAST, A MONTH AGO. 

FOR THREE DAYS, INDEPENDENT CHINESE NEWSPAPERS HERE HAVE 
REPORTED INTENSIF {ED COMMUNIST TROOP MOVEMENTS NORTHWARD FROM SOUTH 
CHINA. MY INFORMANT'S WORD TODAY IS THE FIRST OFFICIAL WORD THAT THIS 
REDEPLOYMENT OF CHINESE RED FORCES ACTUALLY HAS BEEN GOING ON FOR 
SOME TIME, AND WITH A DEFINITE PATTERN. 

THE DIPLOMAT ADDED THAT THE CHINESE RED TROOPS IN MANCHURIA CAN 
BE EXPECTED TO CROSS INTO NORTH KOREA AS RUSSIA'S ANSWER TO 
AMERICAN SUPPORT FOR INVADED SOUTH KOREA. 

Q--THE RECENT WITHDRAWAL FROM TOKYO OF HIGH LEVEL MEMBERS OF THE 
SOVIET MISSION COULD BE CONSIDERED AN "INDICATION THAT SOMETHING 
BIG IS BREWING." HE DECLINED TO ELABORATE. 

DIPLOMATIC OBSERVERS AGREE GENERALLY THAT CHINESE COMMUNIST 
PARTICIPATION IN KOREA IS VIRTUALLY CERTAIN. NEVERTHELESS, THEY ALSO 
ARE INCLINED TO BELIEVE THAT SOVIET RUSSIA HAS NOT YET MADE UP 
HER MIND AS TO HOW FAR SHE IS READY TO GO IN THE FAR EAST AT THIS 

ME. 
ONE OBSERVER, POINTING OUT THAT THE KOREAN CONFLICT HAS NOT YET 
APPEARED AS THE LEAD STORY IN EITHER OF HONG KONG'S TWO PRO-COMMUNIST 
CHINESE DAILIES, SAID: "WE KNOW FOR A FACT THAT THE NEWSPAPERS IN 
SOUTH CHINA HAVE EXPLICIT ORDERS NOT TO COMMENT ON POLICY MATTERS 
PERTAINING TO THE SITUATION IN KOREA. THIS MOST PROBABLY MEANS THAT 
THE RUSSIANS THEMSELVES HAVE NOT YET REACHED A POLICY DECISION ON 


THIS MATTER."

BY SPENCER MOOSA 

TAIPEI, JULY 5-(AP)=DISTINCT UNEASINESS IS NOTICEABLE IN NATIONALIST 
CIRCLES OVER THE BAN ON-AZR-AND SEA OPERATIONS_AGAINST RED CHINA 
ORDERED LAST_WEEK IN COMPLIANCE. WITH PRESIDENT TRUMAN'S" REQUEST. 

THE BAN IS APPARENTLY OF SUCH A NATURE THAT EVEN RECONNAISSANCE 
MISSIONS CAN NOT BE UNDERTAKEN BY THE NATIONALIST AIR FORCE. 

THE NATIONALISTS FEEL THE REDS WILL TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE SITUATION 
TO MASS ARMADAS FOR THE INVASION OF FORMOSA. SOME QUARTERS THINK 
THEY MIGHT UNDERTAKE THE INVASION DESPITE THE FACT THE U.S. 7TH 
FLEET IS PROTECTING FORMOSA. | 

MOSCOW, SO THE ARGUMENT GOES, MIGHT ORDER THE REDS TO ATTACK IN THE 
HOPE OF PROVOKING A CLASH BETWEEN THEM AND THE 7TH FLEET. 

THE NATIONALISTS ARE PRESSING IN WASHINGTON AND TOKYO FOR A CHANGE 
IN THE SITUATION SO THEY MAY RESUME OPERATIONS AGAINST THE MAINLAND. 

REPORTS ARE CURRENT THAT GENERAL MACARTHUR WILL SEND A MISSION TO 
TAIPEI WITHIN THE NEXT FEW DAYS TO DISCUSS THIS AND OTHER QUESTIONS. 

ALL INDICATIONS ARE THAT THE NATIONALISTS INTEND TO PRESS HARD FOR 
THE DISPATCH OF TROOPS TO KOREA TO JOIN IN THE BATTLE. THEY WANT TO 
SHOW THE WORLD THAT THE ARMIES THEY HAVE REORGANIZED ARE MADE OF 
DIFFERENT STUFF FROM THOSE WHICH COLLAPSED ON THE MAINLAND. 

IT IS LARGELY A MATTER OF PRIDE. BUT BEHIND IT THERE IS THE OBVIOUS 
WISH TO EMPHASIZE ONE POINT: THE NATIONALISTS REGARD THE RED CHINA 
MAINLAND AS THEIR OWN BIRTHRIGHT AND ARE DETERMINED TO OPPOSE ANY IDEA 
THAT POLICY MAKERS ABROAD MIGHT HAVE OF SUBSTITUTING A THIRD FORCE ON 


THE SUB=CONTINENT IN THE EVENT r

PAMPHLETS BORE THE IMPRINT OF THE BRITISH COMMUNIST PARTY.

THAN ONE-THIRD.

HAS REPORTED. pans 

EICHELBERGER, FORMER COMMANDER OF THE 8TH ARMY, SAID IN TESTIMONY 
MADE PUBLIC TODAY BY THE SENATE APPROPRIATIONS COMMITTEE THAT IF THE 
SOVIETS COULD GAIN CONTROL OF JAPAN AND SEIZE THE IMPERIAL FAMILY THEY 
COULD CREATE NUMEROUS RED ARMY DIVISIONS THERE.

OF DEFENSE, TOLD THE COMMITTEE THAT GENERAL DOUGLAS MACARTHUR SHOULD 
HAVE THE FULL CREDIT FOR PUTTING JAPAN ON ITS FEET ECONOMICALLY AND FOR 
KEEPING THE JAPANESE FRIENDLY TO THE UNITED STATES.

FACT WHICH IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO REALIZE, I BELIEVE, UNTIL THIS SITUATION 
OUT THERE I$ SEEN AT FIRST HAND. ALL I CAN SAY IS, THANK GOD WE HAVE 
SOMEBODY LIKE THAT IN CHARGE OF IT." 

EICHELBERGER SAID THAT PROBABLY 95 PER CENT OF THE JAPANESE ARE 
FRIENDLY TO THE UNITED STATES. HE SAID THE NUMBER AND INFLUENCE OF

OF TANGIBLE AID TO THE UNITED STATES SHOULD RUSSIA FORCE WAR UPON Us," 
HE ADDED. 

EICHELBERGER SAID THE JAPANESE ARE ONE OF THE FEW PEOPLES IN THE 
WORLD WHO CAN MEET THE RUSSIANS ON EQUAL TERMS IN COMBAT. HE OBSERVED 
THAT IF WAR WITH RUSSIA CAME THE AMERICAN PEOPLE WOULD SOON BE ASKING 
FOR JAPAN TO PLAY A PART IN IT. 

"PERHAPS THE FACT THAT JAPAN HAS A GREAT INDUSTRIAL AND MILITARY

WASHINGTON, JULY 5-(AP)-THE AIR FORCE HAS ORDERED A NUMBER OF 
WORLD WAR II TYPE PROPELLER FIGHTERS TQ THE FAR EAST WHERE, OFFICIALS 
SAY, MORE MODERN JET FIGHTERS ARE FINDING THEMSELVES HAMPERED BY 
BAD WEATHER IN THE KOREAN THEATRE. 

THE ORDER WAS DISCLOSED TODAY IN RESPONSE TO A REPORTERS’ QUESTION. 

THE PLANES BEING SENT ARE NORTH AMERICAN F-51 MUSTANGS, A TYPE 
STILL IN WIDE USE IN THE AIR NATIONAL GUARD THOUGH NOT tN THE 
AIR FORCE. 

FIVE AIR FORCE FIGHTER GROUPS ATTACKING NORTH KOREAN INVADING 
FORCES HAVE BEEN USING LOCKHEED F-80 JET PLANES, WHICH HAVE AN 
ANNOUNCED COMBAT RADIUS OF 500 MILES. 

JETS PERFORM BEST AT ALTITUDES OF 30,000 FEET AND UP. BUT OFFICIALS 
SAY BAD WEATHER AND TERRAIN HAVE FORCED PLANES OPERATING ON THE 400- 
MILE RUN FROM JAPAN TO KOREAN TARGETS TO FLY LOW, WHERE THE FUEL 
CONSUMPTION OF JETS IS VERY HIGH. 

THIS IN TURN CUTS THEIR EFFECTIVE RANGE, LEAVING THEM LITTLE TIME 
TO MANEUVER IN THE FIGHTING AREA. 

THE MUSTANG HAS A TOP SPEED OF OVER 450 MILES AN HOUR AND A RANGE 
WHICH PERMITTED IT TO ESCORT B-29S ACROSS THE 7OO-MILE STRETCH OF 
WATER BETWEEN IWO JIMA AND JAPAN DURING THE WAR. 

THE PROBLEM IS NOT ENTIRELY ONE OF RANGE, HOWEVER. OFFICERS 
POINTED OUT THAT GEN. MACARTHUR NEEDS THE JET FIGHTERS TO CARRY OUT 
HIS PRIMARY MISSION OF DEFENDING “ig See IF COMMUNIST FORCES MADE AN 
-80S WOULD BE NEEDED FOR THE 
DEFENSE JOB IN VIEW OF THEIR ST CLIMB AND HIGH ALTITUDE OPERATIONAL 
ABILITY. THE JETS CANNOT BE COMMITTED BOTH TO THE DEFENSE OF 
KOREA AND THE DEFENSE OF JAPAN.

(ADVANCE )-WASHIMGION, JULY 4=(AP)-SOUTH KOREAHAD AN ESTIMATED 
10 OOPS==-DESCRIBED AS WELL-DISCIPLINED AND "PREPARED TO 
MEET ANY CHALLENGE" WHEN NORTHERN COMMUNISTS INVADED. 

THE TROOP ESTIMATE AND DESCRIPTION WERE GIVEN TO THE SENATE APPRO- 
PRIATIONS COMMITTEE BY WILLIAM CeFOSTER, DEPUTY ADMINISTRATOR OF THE 
ECONOMIC COOPERATION ADMINISTRATION (ECA), ON JUNE 135 THAT WAS 12 
DAYS BEFORE THE KOREAN FIGHTING BROKE OUT. 

AT THAT TIME, FOSTER TOLD THE COMMITTEES 

"A VIGOROUS TRAINING PROGRAM HAS BUILT UP A WELL-DISCIPLINED ARMY OF 
100,000 SOLDIERS; ONE THAT IS PREPARED TO MEET ANY CHALLENGE BY NORTH 
KOREAN FORCES, AND ONE THAT HAS CLEANED OUT THE GUERRILLA BANDS IN 
SOUTH KOREA IN ONE AREA AFTER ANOTHER." 

ALTHOUGH THE BADLY BATTERED SOUTH KOREAN ARMY MADE FOSTER'S 
ESTIMATE LOOK OVERLY OPTIMISTIC, SENATOR KNOWLAND (R=CALIF) TOLD A 
REPORTER HE THINKS THE SOUTH KOREANS WILL PROVIDE GOOD FIGHTING MEN 
YET WHEN THEY ARE EQUIPPED TO COMBAT TANKS.

WASHINGTON, JULY 5=(AP)=DEFENSE OFFICIALS CONFIRMED TODAY THAT THE 
ESCORT CARRIER SICILY IS TAKING EXTRA AIRCRAFT AND SPARE PARTS TO 
THE LARGE CARRIER VALLEY FORGE, OPERATING OFF KOREAc 

THE SICILY SAILED FROM SAN DIEGO, CALe, TUESDAY AFTERNOON WITH HER 
DECKS DESCRIBED AS "LOADED WITH WARPLANES". 

AN OFFICIAL SAID NO MARINE UNITS ARE ABOARD THE SICILY. 

THE 13,000 TON CARRIER NORMALLY OPERATES WITH 30 FIGHTER AND ATTACK 
PLANES. AS A PLANE*FERRY, SHE COULD CARRY ABOUT 60 AIRCRAFT, THE 
EXACT NUMBER DEPENDING ON TYPES. 

THE SICILY, RATED AT 18 KNOTS, WAS BUILT AT TACOMA, WASHe, IN 19456 
A ONE-WAY TRIP TO THE JAPANESE AREA SHOULD TAKE ABOUT 20 DAYS. 

IF THE LITTLE CARRIER IS USED SOLELY TO FERRY WARPLANES IT CAN MAKE 
THE ROUND TRIP IN ABOUT 45 DAYS. 

HOWEVER, THE SICILY COULD DELIVER ABOUT 30 PLANES TO THE VALLEY 
FORGE AND REMAIN IN THE FAR EAST WITH A FULL COMPLEMENT TO OPERATE 
IN SUPPORT OF THE BIG CARRIER.

LAKE SUCCESS, JULY 5=(AP)=A PROPOSAL PERMITTENG- APPOINTMENT 
OF GEN. LAS MACARTHUR-AS COMMANDER OF UNITED. NATIONS FORCES 
FIGHTING COMMUNIST NORTH KOREA WAS REPORTED TONIGHT BEING COMPLETED 
FOR SECURITY COUNCIL ACTION FRIDAY. 

THE UsN. ANNOUNCED THE COUNCIL WILL MEET ON THE KOREAN SITUATION 
AT 10 AwM. (EST) FRIDAY. THIS WILL BE THE FIRST SESSION IN A 
WEEK FOR THE COUNCIL. 

HIGH POINTS OF A RESOLUTION BEING DRAFTED FOR THE MEETING 
WERE SAID TO BEs 3 

1. THE COUNCIL WILL AUTHORIZE THE UNITED STATES, AS THE NATION 
CONTRIBUTING THE BULK OF MEN AND ARMED MIGHT TO THE KOREAN WAR, TO 
DESIGNATE THE SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE UNITED EFFORT. THE 
OPINION HERE IS THAT MACARTHUR, OF COURSE, WILL BE DESIGNATED BY 
THE UeSe 

2. THE COUNCIL WILL RECOMMEND THAT ALL COUNTRIES, INCLUDING 
THE UNITED STATES, TAKING PART IN THE WAR FLY THE BLUE AND 
WHITE BANNER OF THE U.N. THIS WILL HAVE TO BE A RECOMMENDATION, 

IT WAS SAID, SINCE SOME COUNTRIES IN THE FIGHTING HAVE CONSTITUTIONAL 
RESTRICTIONS AGAINST THEIR MEN FIGHTING UNDER ANY BANNER BUT THEIR 
OWN. 

IT WAS SAID THE IDEA OF A SUPER WAR COUNCIL WAS ON THE POINT 
OF BEING QUIETLY SHELVED. IT MAY BE COME OUT IN SOME FORM BUT 
SEVERAL DELEGATIONS ARE ASKING JUST WHY IS IT NECESSARY. THE 1i1- 
MEMBER COUNCIL (EXCLUDING THE SOVIET UNION, WHICH STILL Is 
BOYCOTTING THE COUNCIL SESSION) IS A GROUP CONSIDERED SMALL 
ENOUGH TO FORM A WAR COUNCIL AND ITS AUTHORITY UNDER THE U.N,

AP SPECIAL WASHINGTON SERVICE 

WASHINGTON, JULY 5=(AP)=SENATOR KNOWLAND (R=CALIF) TODAY ACCUSED 
MICHAEL STRAUS, CHIEF OF THE RECLAMATION BUREAU, OF "SABOTAGING" A 
CHINESE NATIONALIST GOVERNMENT IRRIGATION PROJECT ON FORMOSA. 

STRAUS, JUST BACK FROM A VACATION, WAS NOT AVAILABLEIMMEDIATELY 
FOR COMMENT, 

KNOWLAND TOLD THE SENATE THAT STRAUS HAD REFUSED TO PERMIT WILLIAM 
I.GARDNER, A RECLAMATION BUREAU EMPLOYE, TO TAKE A TWO-MONTH LEAVE OF 
ABSENCE WITHOUT PAY TO GO TO FORMOSA AS AN ENGINEERING SPECIALIST FOR 
JOHNSON INTERNATIONAL A LOS ANGELES PIPE AND PUMP CO. 

THE COMPANY HAS A CONTRACT TO PUT IN 125 WELLS TO IRRIGATE FORMOSAN 
SUGAR AND RICE FIELDS. 


A STRAUS AIDE SAID, HOWEVER, THAT NO REQUEST FOR GARDNER'S SERVICES 
HAS BEEN RECEIVED FROM THE STATE DEPARTMENT, WHICH HANDLES SUCH MATTERS 


AS PART OF ITS TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM. 

THIS SOURCE SAID GARDNER HIMSELF HAS NOT ASKED PERMISSION TO GO 
TO FORMOSA AS A PRIVATE CITIZEN. 

THE AIDE ADDED THAT GARDNER IS "A HARD MAN TO SPARE, BADLY NEEDED 


IN THE CENTRAL VALLEY PROJECT IN CALIFORNIA, AND WOULD HAVE TO BE 
PULLED OFF AN IMPORTANT JOB SOMETHING WHICH SENATOR KNOWLAND PROBABLY 
WOULD NOT APPROVE EITHER." 

GARDNER IS A GEOLOGIST. 

KNOWLAND SAID STRAUS AND THE RECLAMATION BUREAU HAD REFUSED TO RE- 
LEASE GARDNER DESPITE STATE DEPARTMENT CLEARANCE. HE CALLED THE WHOLE 
MATTER A "SHOCKING EXAMPLE OF LACK OF COORDINATION AND COOPERATION® 
BETWEEN THE TWO AGENCIES BUT HELD THAT THE RECLAMATION BUREAU WAS AT 
FAULT. 

KNOWLAND SAID IT HAD BEEN THE PRACTICE OF THE RECLAMATION BUREAU 
TO LEND ITS SPECIALISTS TO PRIVATE COMPANIES, BUT IN THIS CASE STRAUS 
AND THE BUREAU WERE APPARENTLY UNWILLING TO COOPERATE. 

HE SAID THE EFFECT WAS TO "SABOTAGE A VERY USEFUL AND CONSTRUCTIVE 
PROGRAM® TO HELP FORMOSA ATTAIN ECONOMIC STABILITY.

ASEM YORK, JULY 5-CAP)-A NEW EXPLANATION OF A-LARGE PART OF THE 
DEATHS FROM ATOMIC BOMB WAS ADVANCED TODAY BY DR.PALUEL J.FLAGG, 
PRESIDENT OF THE SOCIETY FOR PREVENTION OF ASPHYXIAL DEATH. 

HE SAID 50 TO 85 PER CENT OF THE DEATHS ARE DUE IMMEDIATELY TO 
ASPHYXIATION, HE SAID THAT FEW DOCTORS KNOW HOW TO TREAT SERIOUS 
ASPHYXIATION AND THAT A LRGE SAVING OF LIFE IS POSSIBLE BY MAKING 
ADEQUATE PREPARATIONS. 

HE ANNOUNCED A CAMPAIGN TO RAISE $50,000 FOR TEACHING THE 
TECHNIQUES OF TREATING ASPHYXIATION. HE ALREADY HAS A COURSE 
ATTENDED BY DOCTORS, AND PROPOSES THAT THE MONEY BE USED ON A NON- 
PROFIT BASIS TO EXTEND MEDICAL INS ° 

ASPHYXIATION IS LACK OF OXYGEN. THIS LACK CAN COME FROM 
DIFFERENT CAUSES. THE OFFICIALLY REPORTED CAUSES OF DEATH IN THE 
JAPANESE ATOM BOMBS ARE RADIOACTIVITY, BLAST OR CONCUSSION, FLASH 
BURNS AND HEATe DR«DLAGG SAID THAT ALL THESE CAN CAUSE ASPHYXIATION, 

HE SAID THAT ASPHYXIATION IS A COMPLICATION IN MOST ATOMIC BOMB 
INJURIES AND IS THE IMMEDIATE CAUSE OF DEATH IN A MAJORITY 


BURNS AND HEATe DReFLAGG SAID THAT ALL THESE CAN CAUSE ASPHYXIATION. 

HE SAID THAT ASPHYXIATION IS A COMPLICATION IN MOST ATOMIC BOMB 
INJURIES AND IS THE IMMEDIATE CAUSE OF DEATH IN A MAJORITY. 

TREATING THE VICTIMS FOR ASPHYXIATION HE SAID WOULD PROLONG THEIR 
LIVES, AND IN MANY CASES MAKE IT POSSIBLE FOR THEM TO RECOVER FROM 
THEIR OTHER INJURIES. 

DReFLAGG SAID ASPHYXIATION SHOWS ITSELF IN THREE STAGES, AND THAT 
IN THE FIRST TWO FRESH AIR IS A CURE. THE THIRD STAGE IS A LIMP 
AND ALMOST LIFELESS CONDITION AND THEN, SAID THE DOCTOR, ONLY EXPERT 
MEDICAL TREATMENT CAN SAVE LIFE. IT IS FOR THIS STAGE HE SAID THAT 
TEACHING IS NEEDED. ; | 

HE PROPOSED THAT AMBULANCES BE EQUIPPED WITH APPARATUS TO TREAT 
ASPHYXIATION. AMBULANCES LACK THIS EQUIPMENT AT PRESENT, HE SAID. 
OXYGEN, TUBES TO GIVE IT, AND EVEN SUCH THINGS AS SUCTION WHICH 
WOULD PULL WATER, BLOOD OR OTHER THINGS OUT OF A CHOKING THROAT, 
DR.FLAGG SAID, ARE LACKING IN PRESENT AMBULANCES. 

HE EXHIBITED A FULLY EQUIPPED AMBULANCE, NAMED WAIKIKI BEACH 
BECAUSE THE FIRST ONE OF ITS KIND WAS MADE FOR USE FOR THE FAMOUS 
HONOLULU. BATHING BEACH TO REVIVE DROWNING PERSONS.»

ene GhDV ANCE) « «NEU YORK, JULY 5-(AP)-IMMEDIATE TRANSRER..OF ATOMIC 
GY TO PRIVATE INDUSTRY WAS PROPOSED TODAY BY DAVID E.LILIENTHAL, 
FORMER CHAIRMAN OF THE ATOMIC ENERGY COMMISSION. — 

HTS ROPOSAL WAS MADE IN AN ARTICLE TN-COLLIER'S. HE SAID HE HAS 
CHANGED HIS MIND. 

"I WAS AMONG THOSE," HE SAID, "WHO, BACK IN 1945 AND 1946, WERE 
UNABLE TO SEE ANY ALTERNATIVE TO THE COURSE OF GOVERNMENT MOMOPOL ¥. 
ON THE BASIS OF EXPERIENCE WE DID NOT HAVE IN 1946, AND IN VIEW OF 
SUCH NEW FACTS AS THE RUSSIAN BOMB, I AM CONVINCED THAT OUR MONOPOLY 
COURSE IS NO LONGER JUSTIFIED AND SHOULD BE DRASTICALLY CHANGED." 

THE BIGGEST GOLD BRICK IN HISTORY, HE SAID, IS THE NOTION THAT 
THE UNITED STATES HAS A SECRET FORMULA. 

LILIENTHAL SAID MILITARY SECRECY ABOUT ATOMIC WEAPONS SHOULD 
CONTINUE, BUT THAT THIS SECRECY SHOULD BE NO DIFFERENT THAN THAT 
SLANES WHICH CARRY THE BOMBS. 

uE SAID THAT ALMOST TO A MAN SCORES OF INDUSTRIAL LEADERS BELIEVE 
ATOMIC ENERGY CANNOT BE FULLY DEVELOPED UNDER PRESENT GOVERNMENT- 
DOMINATED CONDITIONS.

ABOUT THE PLANTS AND PROCESSES BY WHICH THE UNITED STATES IS PRODUCING 
ATOMIC ENERGY AND ITS PRODUCTS. THIS IS NOW HIGHLY SECRET.

THIRD, KILL THE PROVISION OF LAW WHICH PLACES A POLITICAL VETO OVER

FOURTH CONSIDER HOW TO GIVE ALLOWANCES TO PRIVATE INDUSTRY WHEN IT 
RISKS MILLIONS ON AN ATOMIC ENTERPRISE. 

KE OF THE REPEATED STATEMENTS ABOUT ATOMIC PROGRESS HAS BEEN THAT

BUT NO VOLUNTEERS ARE BEING ACCEPTED FROM THIS STRATEGIC COMMAND.

EUROPE AS THE MAIN SHOW “IF THIS FIGHT GETS BIG." 

CAPT.JOHN LeMOUTIER, A WARTIME ACE FROM PEORIA, ILLe, IS ONE OF

OBSERVERS HERE SEE THREE REASONS FOR ARAB REFUSAL TO GO ALONG WITH

1. A DESIRE TO RETALIATE AGAINST THE WEST, PARTICULARLY AGAINST 

THE UeSe,y FOR WHAT THE ARABS CONSIDER PAST SUPPORT OF ISRAEL. 

2e A DESIRE TO RETALIATE AGAINST THE U.N. AS AN INSTITUTION

THE COUNCIL TOOK NO ACTION IN 1947 WHEN EGYPT PROTESTED THE PRESENCE 
OF BRITISH FORCES IN THE SUEZ CANAL ZONE AND BRITISH DOMINATION OF THE 
ANGLO=EGYPTIAN CONDOMINIUM IN THE SUDAN. 

3e SELF-INTEREST. THE ARAB STATES BELIEVE NEUTRALITY WOULD BE 
HIGHLY PROFITABLE ECONOMICALLY AND POLITICALLY IF THE KOREAN FIGHTING 
SHOULD SPREAD INTO A WORLD CONFLICT. 

AT THE SAME TIME AL NAHDAH, NEWSPAPER PUBLISHED AT JORDAN'S CAPITAL 
AT AMMAN AND FREQUENT MIRROR OF KING ABDILLAH'S VIEWS, SAID "THERE 
IS NO SUCH THING AS NEUTRALITY." THE PAPER SUGGESTED THAT JORDAN, 
IRAQ, AND TURKEY FORM A DEFENSE ALLIANCE SINCE’ THEY WOULD FEEL THE 
BRUNT OF THE ATTACK IF SOVIET FORCES SHOULD STRIKE IN THE MIDDLE EAST.

ARAB LEADERS, APPARENTLY MADE NO CONVERTS. AFTER A WEEK OF BUSY

AT HIS NEWS CONFERENCE, PRESIDENT TRUMAN SOUNDED A NOTE A CALM 
OPTIMISM IN THE FACE OF SOME OF THE DARKEST REPORTS YET RECEIVED IN

CRESS FOR MORE MONEY FOR THE ARMED FORCES.

PRODUCTION.

BY ELTON C.FAY nt ’ 
WASHINGTON« JULY S-C(AP)“AMERICAN MOVES TO GET MORE POWER INTO THE 


iVu Mi dad 


DEFENSE OF SOMTH KOREA COINCIDED TODAY WITH SPECULATION ON THE VIRTUAL 
DISAPPEARANCE OF NORTH KOREAN WARPLANES FROM THE SKIES. " 

SOME MILITARY MEN WERE LED TO THE HOPE THAT THE STRATEGIC ATTACKS 
BY AMERICAN AND BRITISH AIRCRAFT WERE BEGINNING TO SHOW RESULTS. 

THEY QUICKLY ADDED, HOWEVER, THAT THIS SHOULD BE VIEWED AS ONLY 
ONE POSSIBLE EXPLANATION AND THAT THE REAL REASON IS NOT YET KNOWN 
HERE. 

OVERNIGHT THERE WERE TWO DEVELOPMENTS INDICATING STEPPED-UP AIR 
ACTIVITY TO BOLSTER THE SOUTH KOREAN DEFENSES 

1. THE AIR FORCE SAID IT WAS SENDING AN UNDISCLOSED NUMBER OF 
NORTH AMERICAN F-51 MUSTANG FIGHTERS TO THE FAR EASTERN AIR FORCES. 
THESE PLANES, ABLE TO OPERATE AT SLOWER SPEEDS AND GREATER RANGES 
THAN JETS, ARE VITALLY NEEDED TO GIVE AIR SUPPORT TO THE HARD-PRESSED 
GROUND FORCES OF THE AMERICAN AND SOUTH KOREAN ARMIES. THERE HAVE 
SEEN SOME IN ACTION, A FEW OF THEM FLOWN BY SOUTH KOREANS 4 OTHERS BY 
AUSTRALIAN AIR FORCE AND USAF PILOTS--BUT NOT ENOUGH. WHERE THE 
ADDITIONAL F-51S WILL COME FROM OR HOW THEY WILL BE TRANSPORTED FROM 
THE UNITED STATES TO THE FAR EAST WAS NOT STATED. DEFENSE OFFI- 
CIALS, IN A SEPARATE ACTION, CONFIRMED THAT THE ESCORT CARRIER SICILY 
IS TAKING EXTRA AIRCRAFT AND SPARE PARTS TO THE BIG CARRIER VALLEY 
FORGE, OPERATING OFF KOREA. THE SICILY SAILED TUESDAY FROM SAN DIEGO. 


SHE COULD MAKE THE TRIP IN 20 DAYS, CARRYING PERHAPS AS MANY AS &lt;o 

2. THE DEFENSE DEPARTMENT CONTRACTED WITH SEVEN AIRLINES To MAKE 
SPECIAL FLIGHTS FROM THE U.S. TO THE FAR EAST TO CARRY MEN AND 
SUPPLIES. THESE FLIGHTS WILL SUPPLEMENT THE REGULAR OPERATIONS oF 
THE MILITARY AIR TRANSPORT SERVICE. THEY WILL BE SIMILAR TO THE CHARTER 
FLIGHTS USED TO SUPPORT THE BERLIN AIRLIFT. 

IT WAS ALSO ANNOUNCED THAT PLANS TO CLOSE OUT AIR FORCE WEATHER 
AND COMMUNICATION STATIONS IN THE ALEUTIANS BY JULY 1 HAD BEEN 
DEFERRED. THESE STATIONS, ALONG THE NORTHERN ROUTE TO THE FAR East, 
ARE IMPORTANT AS NAVIGATIONAL AIDS TO THE PILOTS FLYING THROUGH THF 
STORM-RIDDEN NORTH PACIFIC AREA. 

FOR DAYS NOW, UeS. AND BRITISH AIRCRAFT HAVE BEEN HAMMERING AT 
NORTH KOREAN AIR FIELDS, RAIL LINES, FUEL DUMPS AND HIGHWAY CONVOYS. 
THIS STRATEGIC-TACTICAL PLAN HAS BEEN AIMED AT DESTROYING B0TH THE 
ENEMY'S SUPPLIES AND HIS MEANS OF GETTING THEM INTO USF. THOSE 
INCLUDE, IN ADDITION TO EQUIPMENT FOR NORTH KOREAN GROUND FORCES, 
THE FUEL AND AMMUNITION FOR PLANES. 

AIR STRATEGISTS HERE COMMENT THAT IT IS STRANGE THAT DURING THE 
LAST FEW DAYS THE NORTH KOREAN AIR FORCE HAS FAILED TO TAKE OFF FOP 


DEFENSE OF BOMB TARGETS. 


ASWX 
ONE VETERAN OF THE WORLD WAR II AIR CAMPAIGN SAW IN THE KOREAN 


PICTURE A POSSIBLE DUPLICATION, ON A SMALL SCALE, OF THE SITUATION 
THAT PREVAILED IN THE GERMAN LUFTUAFFE IN THE CLOs ING MONTHS OF THE 
WAR. THE GERMAN AIR FORCE THEN HAD PILOTS=--BUT LACKED ADEQUATE FUEL 
TO FLY, THANKS TO STRATEGIC ATTACK ON SUPPLY SOURCES AND TRANSPORT. 

REPORTS REACHING HERE INDICATE THAT DURING THE LAST THREE DAYS 
AMERICAN AIRMEN HAVE SEEN A TOTAL OF ONLY NINE ENEMY PLANES. ONE 
FLIGHT OF EIGHT YAK III FIGHTERS WAS SIGHTED, FLEEING WHEN AMERICAN 
AIRCRAFT APPROACHED. A SINGLE YAK 9 FIGHTER WAS SPOTTED ON ANOTHER 
OCCASION, BUT HE TOO HURRIED OFF. 

50 FAR THERE HAVE BEEN NO REPORTS OF ANY JET FIGHTERS OPERATING 
FOR THE NORTH KOREANS. ALL TYPES ENCOUNTERED HAVE BEEN CONVENTIONAL- 
ENGINED, YAK-DESIGNED FIGHTERS OR AIRCRAFT OF THE IL=-10 TYPE, A 
GROUND ATTACK PLANE USED FOR SUPPORT OF TROOPS. 

THE ASSUMPTION HERE IS THAT IF ANY JETS APPEAR TO CHALLENGE THE 
F-30S OF THE AIR FORCE OR JET PLANES PUT UP BY THE AMERICAN CARRIER 
IN THE YELLOW SEA THEY WILL NOT BE FLOWN BY NORTH KOREANS. IT IS 
RELARDED AS HIGHLY DOUBTFUL THAT THE NORTH KOREANS HAVE EITHER 
TRAINED JET PILOTS OR THE SKILLED MECHANICS NEEDED FOR MAIN- 

TENANCE OF JET AIRCRAFT. 

THE POUNDING OF NORTH KOREAN TARGETS STARTED OFF WITH B-29 MEDIUM 
BOMBERS AND F-51 FIGHTERS OF THE UNITED STATES AIR FORCE. DURING THE 
LAST FEW DAYS THE TEMPO OF THE ATTACK HAS BEEN STEPPED UP WITH THE 
APPEARANCE ON THE SCENE OF PLANES PUT UP FROM AN ESSEX-CLASS AMERICAN 
CARRIER AND A LIGHT BRITISH CARRIER. THESE CARRIERS OBVIOUSLY ARE 
LAUNCHING THEIR PLANES FROM POSITIONS IN THE YELLOW SEA, TO THE WEST 
OF KOREA AND CLOSE TO THE MAJOR TARGETS.

DOLLAR PLAN TO MAKE SOUTHERN KOREA INDEPENDENT IN ELECTRIC POWER, 


UeSe TECHNICIANS SAID TODAY. 
THE TECHNICIANS WERE MEMBERS OF A SIX-MAN TEAM WHICH MADE A TWO-

GRAM, THEY LEFT KOREA JUST A WEEK BEFORE THE OUTBREAK OF TROUBLE» | 
HYDROLOGIST WILLIAM DeROMIG, A LEADER OF THE GROUP, SAID TWO OF ME 
FOUR PROPOSED PROJECT SITES ALREADY HAVE BEEN SEIZED BY THE COMMUNISIS~ 
ONE OF THE RED-OCCUPIED SITES WOULD HAVE INVOLVED A DAM ON THE 
NORTH HAN RIVER NORTH OF CHUNCHON, WHICH WOULD HAVE BACKED WATER ACROSS 
THE 38TH PARALLEL INTO NORTH KOREA, AND A DAM SOUTH OF CHUNCHON ON 
HE HONGCHON RIVER. 
THE OTHER, ALSO IN RED HANDS, INVOLVED TWO PROPOSED DAMS ON THE 


KUM RIVER NEAR CHUNGJU AND YOJU. 
A THIRD PROJECT NOW THREATENED BY THE INVADERS, WOULD DIVERT THE 


HEADWATERS OF THE HAN RIVER FROM THE WEST TO THE EAST COAST NEAR 
SAMCHOK. 

THE FOURTH=-THE ONLY ONE WHICH WOULD IRRIGATE A CONSIDERABLE AREA 
ALONG WITH PRODUCTION OF POWER=--IS THE KUM-GANG PROJECT ON THE KUM 
RIVER, STILL WELL WITHIN SOUTH KOREAN LINES. 

ROMIG TOLD A REPORTER THE TEAM FOUND ALL OF THE PROJECTS WORTHY OF 
FURTHER STUDY, AND IS SO REPORTING TO THE ECONOMIC COOPERATION ADMIN- 


ISTRATION. THE THREE NORTHERNMOST 


ROMIG TOLD A REPORTER THE TEAM FOUND ALL OF THE PROJECTS WORTHY OF 
FURTHER STUDY, AND IS SO REPORTING TO THE ECONOMIC COOPERATION ADMIN- 
ISTRATION. THE THREE NORTHERNMOST PROJECTS COULD PRODUCE AT COSTS 
COMPARABLE TO THOSE FOR STEAM POWER, HE SAID. 

HAD KOREA REMAINED PEACEFUL, ROMIG ADDED, MORE DETAILED SURVEYS 
COULD HAVE BEEN STARTED LATER THIS SUMMER. 

ROMIG SAID CONSTRUCTION OF THE FOUR PROJECTS, ALONG WITH CONTINUED 
OPERATION OF STEAM AND HYDROELECTRIC PLANTS NOW IN USE, WOULD HAVE 
MADE SOUTH KOREA SELF=SUFFICIENT FROM A POWER STANDPOINT, 

NORTH KOREA HAS A PLENTIFUL SUPPLY OF POWER. BEFORE THE WAR IT WAS 
TRANSMITTED THROUGHOUT THE REPUBLIC. A YEAR AND A HALF AGO THE COM- 
MUNISTS CUT THE POWER LINES AT THE 38TH PARALLEL. SINCE THAT TIME 
MANY SOUTH KOREAN INDUSTRIAL PLANTS HAVE CLOSED FOR LACK OF 
POWER, AND ALL SOUTH KOREA HAS BEEN CRIPPLED BY ELECTRICITY SHORTAGES, 

ROMIG ADDED THAT THE COMMUNIST ADVANCE IS APPROACHING SOUTH KOREA'S 
LARGEST STEAM PLANT, AT YONGWOL. ITS LOSS WOULD BE A MAJOR BLOW, HE 
SAID.

WASHINGTON, JULY $-(AP)-A NEW "BILL OF RIGHTS" FOR MEN DRAFTED 
INTO THE ARMED FORCES WAS SUGGESTED TODAY BY REP.DWIGHT L.ROGERS 
D-FLA). wie 
OTTHILE THERE HAVE BEEN NO INDUCTIONS FOR 18 MONTHS, THE DRAFT 
LAW WHICH WAS EXTENDED LAST WEEK FOR ANOTHER YEAR WOULD ALLOW THE 
ORESIDENT TO ORDER INDUCTIONS AT ONCE IN THE EVENT THE WAR SITUATION 
BECOMES WORSE. . 

IF SUCH INDUCTIONS ARE ORDERED, ROGERS SAID, HE WILL SPONSOR 

NO 


LEGISLATION TO: 

1. INSURE THAT INDUCTED MEN LOSE THEIR REGULAR LIFE INSURANCE 
THROUGH PREMIUM LAPSES.« 

2. PROVIDE THAT THE GOVERNMENT MAKE RENT PAYMENTS WHEN NECESSARY 





TO PREVENT FAMILIES OF INDUCTED MEN FROM BEING EVICTED FOR NON-PAYMENT 
OF RENT. 

3. GUARANTEE THAT INDUCTED MEN SHALL NOT LOSE HOMES THEY ARE 
BUYING THROUGH FAILURE TO MEET MORTGAGE PAYMENTS. 

"THE LEGISLATION I HAVE IN MIND," ROGERS TOLD NEWSMEN, "WOULD 
PROVIDE THAT THE GOVERNMENT TAKE OVER PAYMENT OF RENTS AND MORTGAGES 
AND LIFE INSURANCE PREMIUMS IF THE MAN INDUCTED REQUESTS IT. THE 
GOVERNMENT WOULD MAKE THOSE PAYMENTS DIRECT TO THE LANDLORD, THE 
MOPTGACE HOLDER OR THE INSURANCE COMPANY DURING THE TIME A MAN IS IN 
SERVICE AND FOR SIx MONTHS AFTER HE GETS OUT, IN ORDER TO GIVE HIM A 
CHANCE TO GET BACK ON HIS FEET." 

THE PAYMENTS MADE BY THE GOVERNMENT WOULD BE IN THE FORM OF A LOAN 

THE INDUCTED MAN AND WOULD BE REPAYABLE, WITHOUT INTEREST, AFTER 

THE TIME OF REPAYMENT WOULD BE BASED ON LENGTH OF SERVICE. 
I BELIEVE IT WOULD BE REASONABLE TO GIVE A MAN FIVE YEARS REPAY- 
MENT TIME FOR EACH YEAR IN SERVICE," ROGERS SAID. "THAT WOULD 
SPPEAD OUT THE REPAYMENT PERIOD SO AS NOT TO MAKE THE OBLIGATION 
BURDENSOME. IF A MAN SERVED TWO YEARS, HE WOULD HAVE TEN YEARS IN 
WHICH TO REPAY THE GOVERNMENT ADVANCES." 

THE ONLY: COST TO THE GOVERNMENT. ROGERS SAID, WOULD BE THE 
INTEREST IT WOULD NAVE TO PAY ON MONEY IT PUTS UP TO MEET THE OBLIGA- 
TIONS OF MEN IN SERVICE. 

——*F THIN * ROGERS SAIDT-TTHAT SOMETHING MUST BE-DONE; TF THE” ~~ 
DRAFT IS USED AGAIN, TO PROTECT THE FAMILIES OF INDUCTED MEN AND TO 
PROTECT THEIR INSURANCE. IN MANY CASES A MAN JUST CAN'T PAY HIS INSUR- 
ANCE PREMIUMS OR HIS MORTGAGE PAYMENTS OR HIS RENT ON THE PAY HE 
RECTIVES WHILE IN THE MILITARY SERVICE. DURING THE RECENT WAR THE 
TAMILIES OF MANY MEN HAD TO GIVE UP THEIR HOMES OR MOVE INTO CHEAPER 
QUARTERS IN ORDER TO MAKE ENDS MEET. A LOT OF MEN LOST THEIR INSUR- 
ANCE, WHICH WAS ALL THEY HAD SAVED." 

ROGERS SPONSOPED THE G.I. TERMINAL PAY BILL AFTER WORLD WAR II. 
THAT LAW PROVIDED FOR PAYMENT OF ACCRUED LEAVE TO ENLISTED MEN AT THE 
TIME OF THEIR DISCHARGE. PREVIOUSLY, ONLY OFFICERS, RECEIVED. TERMINAL 
LEAVE PAY. JUL

ERY SHIFT OF COAL MINERS DOWNED TOOLS FOR 30 MINUTES IN PROTEST 
AGAINST THE PROSPECT THAT THE MONARCH WHO SURRENDERED BELGIUM TO

STRIKE. SHIP CONSTRUCTION AND REPAIR WORK ALSO HALTED TEMPORARILY.

AND HOUSE MET IN JOINT SESSION, INDICATED THE SHOWDOWN MAY BE 
DELAYED LONGER THAN THE FEW DAYS ORIGINALLY FORECAST.

ONLY 20 MINUTES AFTER IT OPENED. THEY DEMANDED THAT HOUSE PRESIDENT

S3eYEAR=OLD SENATOR CYRILLE VAN OVERBERGHE.

LEOPOLD SOCIAL CHRISTIAN PARTY, WHICH CONTROLS THE GOVERNMENT. BUT 
THE SOCIALISTS WON THEIR POINT. VAN OVERBERGHE TOOK OVER THE GAVEL 
WHEN THE MEETING RESUMED.

WITHOUT EVER GETTING TO THE DEBATE ITSELF: WHETHER THE REGENCY OF 
PRINCE CHARLES, LEOPOLD'S BROTHER, IS TO BE ENDED AND THE KING 


RETURNED TO BELGIUM.

BY MICHAEL GOLDSMITH 

GENEVA, JULY 6=€AP)-HUNGARY AND POLAND FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE 
WAR HAVE OFFERED INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY FOR EXPORT TO 
WESTERN EUROPE AND OVERSEAS, THE UNITED NATIONS ECONOMIC COMMISSION 
FOR EUROPE DISCLOSED TODAY. ae 

THE COMMISSION PUBLISHED A LIST OF 129 DIFFERENT ITEMS OF 
INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT OFFERED BY HUNGARY AND 36 ITEMS OFFERED BY 
POLAND. THE HUNGARIAN LIST INCLUDED MOTORS AND GENERATORS, OIL WELL 
mon el ELECTRIC STEEL FURNACES AND BUILDING AND CONSTRUCTION , 
EQUIPMENT. aes 

THE POLISH LIST INCLUDED BICYCLES, MACHINE TOOLS, MICROSCOPES, 
STEAM LOCOMOTIVES, COMBINE HARVESTERS AND MINING EQUIPMENT, 

THE LISTS WERE SUBMITTED BY THE TWO EAST-EUROPEAN NATIONS FOR 
INCLUSION IN A SURVEY OF THE EXPORT AVAILABILITY OF ENGINEERING 
PRODUCTS IN THE VARIOUS EUROPEAN COUNTRIES. THE SURVEY WAS PUBLISHED 
IN MAY, AND INCLUDED OFFERS FROM NINE WEST-EUROPEAN COUNTRIES AND THE 
WESTERN ZONES OF GERMANY. NONE OF THE EAST-EUROPEAN COUNTRIES HAD 
REPLIED TO A QUESTIONAIRE FROM THE ECONOMIC COMMISSION FOR EUROPE BY 
THE DEADLINE SET FOR PUBLICATION OF THIS SURVEY. 

OFFICIALS OF THE COMMISSION SAID TODAY THAT THE BELATED POLISH 
AND HUNGARIAN REPLIES HAD COME AS "PLEASANT SURPRISE.” THEY 
INDICATED THAT THE EASTERN SATELLITE COUNTRIES WERE EAGER TO REESTAB= 
LISH NORMAL COMMERCIAL RELATIONS WITH WESTERN EUROPE, THE OFFICIALS 
SAID. 

THE SOVIET UNION AND ITS SATELLITES HAVE BEEN DEMANDING FOR THE 
PAST TWO YEARS THAT EUROPE'S EAST-WEST TRADE BE REVIVED, BUT THEIR 
DEMANDS HAVE ALWAYS BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH VIOLENT DENUNCIATIONS OF AN 
ALLEGED PRESSURE BY THE UNITED STATES TO PREVENT THE EXPORT OF 
INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT FROM WESTERN EUROPE TO THE EAST. 

THE ACCENT OF THE COMMUNIST DEMANDS HAS ALWAYS BEEN ON THE EASTWARD 
MOVEMENT EQUIPMENT. NOW, FOR THE FIRST TIME, THE EAST HAS SUGGESTED 
A WESTWARD MOVEMENT OF EQUIPMENT, PRESUMABLY IN RETURN FOR OTHER, 
MORE COMPLICATED EQUIPMENT WHICH THE EASTERN COUNTRIES THEMSELVES 
CANNOT PRODUCE.

NEU. YORK, JULY = CAP)“ ANTORG RAP ING CORP., SOVIET 
PURCHASING AGENCY, SIX OF WHOSE OFF WERE INDICTED LAST YEAR FOR 
FAILURE TO REGISTER AS FOREIGN AGENTS, HAS SHIPPEQD_A_VAN LOAD OF 
FILING CABINETS TO THE SOVIET EMBA SHINGTON. 

A BROOKLYN MOVINC™CONCERN SAID S-sp its TRUCKS, LOADED WITH FIVE 
AND ONE=HALF TO SIX TONS OF CABINETS, LEFT AMTORG'S 210 MADISON AVENUE 
OFFICES FOR WASHINGTON TUESDAY NIGHT. 

NO REASON FOR THE TRANSFER OF DOCUMENTS WAS DISCLOSED, BUT IN THE 
EMBASSY THEY WOULD NOT BE SUBJECT TO SUBPOENA. 

TWO OF THE FIRM'S TRUCKS WERE SEEN AT THE RUSSIAN EMBASSY IN 
WASHINGTON YESTERDAY, BUT AN OFFICIAL OF THE CONCERN SAID ONLY ONE 
CARRIED RUSSIAN PROPERTY. THE OTHER, HE SAID, HAD A LOAD DESTINED FOR 
OTHER POINTS AND PROBABLY ACCOMPANIED THE TRUCK TO THE EMBASSY TO HELP 
UNLOAD. 

AMTORG'S OFFICES HERE SAID THE AGENCY IS TO MOVE TO SMALLER 
QUARTERS AT 49 WEST 37TH STREET. LAST DECEMBER IT WAS REPORTED THAT 
AMTORG WOULD ABANDON ITS NINE-STORY OFFICE BUILDING ON MADISON AVENUE 
AND SEEK ONE ABOUT ONE-THIRD AS LARGE. ITS 10-YEAR LEASE ON THE ‘ 
MADISON AVENUE BUILDING EXPIRED APRIL 30 LAST, AND THE AGENCY'S STAFF 
IS DOWN-TO 25 OR 30 EMPLOYES FROM THE STAFF OF 700 IT HAD THREE YEARS 
AGO. ITS VOLUME OF EXPORTS TO RUSSIA WERE REPORTED TO HAVE DWINDLED 
TO ABOUT $8,000,000 (M) A YEAR, COMPARED WITH $100,000,000 (M) 
ANNUALLY BEFORE THE COLD WAR BEGAN. . 

AMTORG AND ITS INDICTED OFFICIALS REGISTERED WITH THE ATTORNEY 
GENERAL A FEW DAYS AFTER THE INDICTMENT WAS RETURNED IN WASHINGTON 
LAST OCTOBER. THE AGENCY PLEADED NO DEFENSE BEFORE FEDERAL JUDGE 
ALEXANDER HOLTZOFF, WHO IMPOSED A SUSPENDED $10,000 FINE, 

AT THAT COURT SESSION U.S. ATTORNEY GEORGE MORRIS FAY TOLD THE 
COURT THE STATE DEPARTMENT HAD RECOMMENDED DISMISSAL OF THE INDICT- 
MENT AGAINST THE AMTORG OFFICIALS THEMSELVES, ON THE GROUND THAT SUCH 
ACTION WOULD SERVE THE BEST INTERESTS OF THIS COUNTR INTHE CONDUCT 
OF ITS FOREIGN AFFAIRS. THE SIX OFFICIALS WERE ALL RUSSIANS.

ON CAPITOL HILL, THE GENERAL RESPONSE TO THE MILITARY EXPANSION 
WAS ONE OF APPROVAL. LEADING REPUBLICANS SAID IT WAS WISE AND NECES- 
SARY. SOME SENATORS©--FOR EXAMPLE, FERGUSON (R-MICH) AND WHERRY 
(R-NEB)---ALSO COMMENTED THAT THE {NVOKING OF THE DRAFT SEEMS TO IN- 
DICATE A LONGER CAMPAIGN IN KOREA THAN WAS FIRST EXPECTED. 

THE NEW DRAFT LAW WHICH TAKES EFFECT JULY 9---SUNDAY---MAKES NO 
CHANGE IN THE AGES OF MEN WHO CAN BE DRAFTED. EVERY MALE MUST REGIS- 
TER WHEN HE BECOMES 18. ONLY THOSE WHO HAVE REACHED 19, AND WHO HAVE 
NOT YET BECOME 26. CAN BE DRAFTED (CERTAIN GROUPS ARE EXEMPTED). 

THEY CAN BE KEPT IN SERVICE FOR 21 MONTHS. NATIONAL GUARDSMEN AND 
RESERVES CAN ALSO BE CALLED FOR 21 MONTHS. 

MAJ«GEN«FLOYD LePARKS, CHIEF OF ARMY PUBLIC INFORMATION, TOLD 
REPORTERS THAT IF THE ARMED FORCES CAN BE BROUGHT TO FULL STRENGTH 
WITHOUT USING THE DRAFT, "WE WILL BE VERY HAPPY." HE SAID THAT SO 
FAR AS HE KNOWS, THE DECISION HAS NOT BEEN MADE TO CALL THE NA- 
TIONAL GUARD OR’RESERVES. HE ADDED THAT RESERVES WHO VOLUNTEER 


WILL BE WELCOMED.

WASHINGTON, JULY 7-(AP)=PRESIDENT TRUMAN'S DECISION TODAY TO 
INVOKE THE MILITARY DRAFT WAS VIEWED IN CONGRESS AS SENSIBLE. 

SOME OF THE LAWMAKERS SAW IT, TOO, AS AN INDICATION THAT THE 
KOREAN FIGHTING MAY BE LONG, TOUGH AND COSTLY. 

AS SENATOR EASTLAND (D-M{SS) PUT ITs 

"THE COUNTRY MUST BE PREPARED FOR ANY EVENTUALITY AND NO ONE CAN 
SAY WHERE THIS THING WILL END." 

SENATOR SALTONSTALL (R-MASS), A MEMBER OF THE ARMED SERVICES 
COMMITTEE, CALLED THE PRESIDENT*S ACTION "A WISE AND NECESSARY 
STEP.” HE ADDED THAT HE HOPES THAT THE ARMY, NAVY AND AIR FORCE MAN- 
POWER REQUIREMENTS WILL BE MET BY VOLUNTEERS, RESERVES AND NATIONAL 
GUARDSMEN AS MUCK AS POSSIBLE BEFORE MEN ARE CALLED UP UNDER SELECTIVE 

SENATOR FERGUSON (R-MICH) TOLD REPORTERS 

®l BELIEVE THAT WE SHOULD DO THROUGH THE UNITED NATIONS EVERYTHING 
THAT IS ESSENTIAL. Y DON'T FEEL THAT ANY OF OUR MEN SHOULD BE SAC- 
RIFICED BECAUSE OF A LACK OF MANPOWER." 

FERGUSON EXPRESSED HOPE THAT OTHER COUNTRIES WHICH JOINED IN UNI- 
TED NATIONS ACTION TO PROTECT SOUTHERN KOREA FROM COMMUNIST INVADERS 
ALSO WILL FURNISH MANPOWER, SO THE WORLD WILL FEEL THAT IT IS "A 
UNITED NATIONS ACTION, AND’ NOT AMERICA'S ALONE." 

BOTH FERGUSON AND SENATE REPUBLICAN LEADER WHERRY OF NEBRASKA OB- 
SERVED THAT THE DRAFT DECISION INDICATES A LONGER CAMPAIGN THAN FIRST

MORE THAN EVER, I BELYEVE THE PRESIDENT SHOULD REVIEW THE WHOLE SI- 
TUATION TO CONGRESS IN JOINT SESSION," WHERRY SAID.

FIRST LEAD JAPAN POLICE 

TOKYO, SATURDAY, JULY S-(AP)&lt;GENERAL MACARTHUR TODAY AUTHORIZED 
THE JAPANESE GOVERNMENT TO INCREASE ITS TOTAL POLICE FORCE BY 75,000 
MEN BY ESTABLISHING A "NATIONAL POLICE RESERVE." 

THIS WILL SWELL THE TOTAL OF JAPANESE POLICE TO 200,000 MEN. 
COLeMePeECHOLS, MACARTHUR"S PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICER, SAID HE 
INTERPRETED THE ORDER AS CREATING A NEW POLICE RESERVE FORCE OF THAT 
SIZE. THE ORDER AT FIRST WAS INTERPRETED AS MEANING MERELY ADDING 

45,000 MEN TO THE CURRENT NATIONAL POLICE FORCE OF 30,000 MEN. 

THERE ARE IN THE PRESENT FORCE FOR ALL JAPAN 95,000 METROPOLITAN 
POLICE WHICH WITH THE NATIONAL RURAL POLICE FORCE MAKES A TOTAL OF

THE PRESENT POLICE FORCE TOTALS 125,000 MEN, INCLUDING 
30,000 IN THE NATIONAL RURAL POLICE WHICH MACARTHUR AUTHORIZED SEPT. 
2 
*MACARTHUR'S LETTER SAID THAT BECAUSE OF POLICE EFFICIENCY "JAPAN 
STANDS OUT WITH A CALMNESS AND SERENITY WHICH LENDS EMPHASIS TO THE 
VIOLENCE, CONFUSION AND DISORDER WHICH EXIST IN OTHER NEARBY LANDS." 
MACARTHUR SAID THE MOVE WAS BEING MADE "TO INSURE THAT THIS 
FAVORABLE CONDITION WILL CONTINUE UNCHALLENGED BY LAWLESS MINORITIES. 
HERE AS ELSEWHERE COMMITTED TO THE SUBVERSION OF THE DUE PROCESSES 
OF Lav AND ASSAULTS OF OPPORTUNITY AGAINST THE PEACE AND PUBLIC 
MACARTHUR SAID HE VISUALIZED THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUFFICIENT LAW 
ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES FOR THE MAINTENANCE "OF INTERNAL SECURITY 
AND ORDER AND THE SAFEGUARD OF JAPAN'S COASTLINE AGAINST UNLAWFUL 
IMMIGRATION AND SMUGGLING." 
THE JAPANESE COAST GUARD NOW HAS A STRENGTH OF 10,000. 
MUCH OF THE SMUGGLING COMES FROM KOREA, SOME OF IT KNOWN TO BE 
FROM COMMUNIST NORTH KOREA.
