A NAVAL BASE IN JAPAN,JULY 7 (AP)-ALLIED NAVAL OPERATIONS IN KOREAN 
WATERS SHOWED THAT THE SMOOTH COOPERATION OF THE U.S.» AND BRITISH 
COMMONWEALTH IN WORLD WAR II HAS NOT BEEN LOST, OFFICERS HERE SAID 
TODAY. 

"THERE'S LESS BICKERING BETWEEN THE U.S. AND BRITISH FORCES IN THIS 
OPERATION THAN THERE IS BETWEEN OUR OWN SHIPS UNDER NORMAL CIRCUM- 
STANCES," ONE BRITISH LIEUTENANT SAID. q 

THE LARGEST BRITISH SHIP TO PUT IN HERE RECENTLY WAS THE CRUISER 
BELFAST, COMMANDED BY CAPT.SIR AUBREY ST.CLAIR FORD. | 

BRITISH NAVAL FORCES TAKING PART IN THE KOREAN \QPERATION ARE UNDER 
COMMAND OF REAR ADMIRAL WILLIAM G.ANDREWES. OU | 

THE BELFAST ESCORTED BRITISH AND AMERICAN CARRIERS WHOSE AIRCRAFT 
STRUCK AT NORTH KOREAN AIRFIELDS, LINES OF COMMUNICATION AND TROOP 
CONCENTRATIONS MONDAY AND TUESDAY. 

"THE CARRIERS WERE BUSY BUT IT WAS A QUIET TRIP FOR US," ONE 
BELFAST OFFICER SAID. "WE DIDN'T GET IN A ROUND." 

THAT WAS JUST FINE IN THE OPINION OF MOST VETERAN MEMBERS OF THE 
BELFAST CREW. 

ONE ROYAL MARINE SERGEANT, AeJeGARDENER OF FAIRHAM HAMPSHIRE, 
ENGLAND, SAID HE HAD SEEN ENOUGH ACTION DURING-WORLD WAR II. A 7 
RUGGED, FRIENDLY MAN, GARDENER TOOK PART IN THE COMMANDO RAID ON DIEPPE 
AND SERVED ON A DESTROYER AND THREE CRUISERS IN ACTION. 

ANOTHER VETERAN, PETTY OFFICER ReWeFENN OF MINSTER KENT, ENGLAND, 
LOOKED UP FROM A LETTER FROM HOME AND AGREED. 

BUT SOME OF THE YOUNGSTERS DIDN'T SEE IT THAT WAY. 

SEAMAN JIMMY ALEXANDER OF STERNRAER, SCOTLAND, SAID "IT'S 
TO SIT ON A BATTLE STATION BY THE HOUR WHEN NOTHING HAPPENS," 

THE BIGGEST WORRY THE MEN OF THE BELFAST HAVE IS THAT THE KOREAN 
OPERATIONS WILL KEEP THEM FROM RETURNING TO ENGLAND IN OCTOBER. 
BY THAT TIME THE BELFAST CREW WILL HAVE COMPLETED ITS TWO-YEAR HITCH 
IN FOREIGN WATERS. 

ROVAL MARINE LT.sMICHAEL RAIN DRYLY SUMMED IT UP: 

"YE DON'T MIND THIS JOP SO LONG AS IT DOESN'T KEEP US FROM

BY STAN SWINTON 

~,CAtRO, EGYPT, JULY 7=(AP)=FIVE ARAB LEAGUE NATIONS WERE REPORTED 
READY TODAY TO JOIN EGYPT IN HER POLICY OF "ABSOLUTE NEUTRALITY® 
TOWARD KOREA. ONLY HASHEMITE JORDAN APPEARED LIKELY TO SUPPORT THE 
UNITED NATIONS CALL FOR AID TO ANTI-COMMUNIST SOUTH KOREA. 

_ THE ARAB LEAGUE'S SECRETARY GENERAL, ABDEL RAHMAN AZZAM PASHA, TOLD 
NEWSMEN THE ARAB NATIONS "AGREE WITH EGYPT ON ITS ATTITUDE TOWARD 
KOREA." EGYPT, A MEMBER OF THE UeNe SECURITY COUNCIL, DID NOT 
VOTE WHEN THE REST OF THE COUNCIL ENDORSED U.S. MILITARY ACTION 
AGAINST THE COMMUNIST NORTH KOREAN GOVERNMENT. 

__THE FIVE NATIONS*-SYRIA, LEBANON, IRAQ, SAUDI ARABIA AND YEMEN-- 
WERE REPORTED AGREEING WITH EGYPT THAT U.N. ACTION TO HALT 
AGGRESSION HAD NOT BEEN FORTHCOMING ON OCCASION IN THE PAST. 

_ THEIR ATTITUDE HAS DISAPPOINTED AMERICAN AND BRITISH DIPLOMATS 
WhO HAVE BEEN BUSY FOR THE PAST WEEK EXPLAINING THE WESTERN POSITION 


S AMBASSADOR, SIR DAVII 


TO ARAB LEADERS. THE WESTERN DIPLOMATS NOW APPEAR TO BE FOLLOWING 
A HANDS&lt;OFF ATTITUDE, TRYING TO PREVENT ARAB RETALIATION FOR WHAT 
MIGHT BE CONSTRUED AS AN ATTEMPT TO BRING PRESSURE. 

JORDAN, HOWEVER, THOUGH NOT A U.N. MEMBER, APPEARED TO BE 
FOLLOWING A DIFFERENT COURSE. THE AMMAN NEWSPAPER AL NAHDAH, WHICH 
FREQUENTLY REFLECTS KING ABDULLAH'S VIEWS, SAID "THERE IS NO SUCH 
THING AS NEUTRALITYe" THE PAPER SUGGESTED A DEFENSE ALLIANCE OF 
JORDAN, IRAQ AND TURKEY TO MEET ANY SOVIET STRIKE IN THE MIDDLE EAST. 

OBSERVERS HERE ATTRIBUTED ARAB COOLNESS TOWARD THE SECURITY 
COUNCIL POLICY TO BITTERNESS OVER WHAT THEY CONSIDER THE PRO-ISRAELI 
POLICY OF THE WEST, AND PARTICULARLY THE U.S., IN THE PAST. 

LEAGUE MEMBERS ALSO HAVE NOT FORGOTTEN THAT THE COUNCIL IN 
1947 DID NOT ACT ON EGYPT'S PROTEST AGAINST THE CONTINUANCE OF 
BRITISH TROOPS IN THE SUEZ CANAL ZONE AND OF THE ANGLO-EGYPTIAN 
CONDOMINIUM IN THE SUDAN. 

THE ARAB STATES FEEL, TOO, THAT THEY WILL PROFIT ECONOMICALLY 
AND POLITICALLY FROM A NEUTRAL POSITION IF THE KOREAN FIGHTING GROWS 


INTO A WORLD CONFLICT.

MOSCOW, JULY 7=CAP)=-THE MOSCOW PRESS SAID TODAY THE UNITED STATES 


AND BRITAIN ARE TRYING TO COERCE EGYPT TO CHANGE HER NEUTRAL STAND ON 
THE KOREAN SITUATION, 

THE SOVIET NEWS AGENCY TASS SAID IN A DISPATCH FROM CAIRO THAT THE 
"BRITISH AND AMERICAN GOVERNMENTS THROUGH THEIR AMBASSADORS TO 
EGYPT CONTINUE TO BRING PRESSURE ON THE EGYPTIAN GOVERNMENT IN ORDER 
TO OBTAIN A CHANGE IN THE POLICY OF EGYPT ON THE KOREAN QUESTION," 

EGYPT HAS REFUSED TO BACK UNITED NATIONS EFFORTS TO AID SOUTH 
KOREA. 

A TASS DISPATCH FROM PARIS, WHICH APPEARED UNDER THE HEADLINE, 
"POSITION OF THE ARAB STATES ON THE KOREAN QUESTION," QUOTED THE 
CAIRO CORRESPONDENT OF THE FRENCH PRESS AGENCY AS SAYING EGYPT HAS 
RECEIVED WORD FROM SYRIA, LEBANON, YEMEN AND SAUDI ARABIA THAT THEY 
ARE FOLLOWING HER NEUTRAL STAND ON THE KOREAN QUESTION.

} NEW DELHI, INDIA, JULY 7=CAP)-INDIAN PREMIER JAWAHARLAL NEHRU 
TODAY SAID THE RETURN OF SOVIET RUSSIA TO THE UNITED NATIONS AND 
[abtitss10N TO THE U.N. OF COMMUNIST CHINA ARE "NECESSARY PREREQUISITES 
TO ENDING THE KOREAN HOSTILITIES." 

NEHRU TOLD A PRESS CONFERENCE BOTH HE AND HIS GOVERNMENT STAND 
READY TO MEDIATE IN THE KOREAN CONFLICT BUT "ONLY IF REQUESTED BY THE 
| PARTIES CONCERNED." 

INDIA, HE SAID, HAD BEEN WORKING THROUGH DIPLOMATIC CHANNELS TO 

SECURE U.N. MEMBERSHIP FOR THE PEIPING GOVERNMENT AS THE "BEST WAY 
TO RESTORE NORMALITY IN THE WORKING OF THE UNITED NATIONS." 

THE SECURITY COUNCIL, HE DECLARED, HAD NO ALTERNATIVE EXCEPT 
TO ASK FOR A CEASE FIRE, TO CALL NORTH KOREA THE AGGRESSOR AND 
ULTIMATELY TO USE FORCE.e INDIA HAD SUPPORTED THE COUNCIL ACTION 
BECAUSE SHE FELT IT WAS THE ONLY WAY TO AVOID AN EXTENSION OF THE 

ONFLICT, HE DECLARED. 

CON INDIA?IN ENDORSING THE COUNCIL RESOLUTION HAD SAID SHE STILL 
FAVORED MEDIATION IF AT ALL POSSIBLE. LATER THE INDIANS WERE 
REPORTED TO FEEL MEDIATION WOULD NOT BE POSSIBLE WHILE MILITARY 
ACTION CONTINUED. 

° NEHRU SAID TODAY THAT "ANY STEP, GOVERNMENTAL OR INDIVIDUAL, 
THAT MICHT BE HELPFUL MUST BE TAKEN." ASKED IF HE WOULD HEED A 
REQUEST FOR HIS PERSONAL INTERVENTION, THE PREMIER REPLIED: — 

MIF THERE IS ANY CHANCE OF PEACE COMING OUT OF NEGOTIATIONS, 
MALAI IEHRU WILL GO TO THE ENDS OF THE EARTH. ve 
eS ree cacak wee ARE "KEEN ON FINDING A WAY OUT, THEY WILL 

} " HE ADDED. . 
PENNILITARY ASSISTANCE TO SOUTH KOREA WAS BEYOND INDIA'S CAPACITY 
BECAUSE ITS FORCES WERE ORGANIZED SOLELY FOR DEFENSE, NEHRU DECLARED. 


‘NSWVERING A QUESTION, THE INDIAN PREMIER SMILINGLY SAID HE 
THOUGHT THERE WAS A "50-50" CHANCE THE KOREAN FIGHTING WOULD DEVELOP 
INTO A WORLD WAR. 

INDIA'S SUPPORT OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL STAND ON KOREA DID NOT 
MEAN HIS GOVERNMENT WAS ALIGNING INDIA WITH THE WESTERN BLOC, NEHRU 
SAID. AN ALIGNMENT WITH EITHER THE WESTERN OR SOVIET BLOC WOULD MEAN 
IT HAD "CEASED TO COUNT" AND WAS "JUST DITTO SOMEONE ELSE," HE DECLARED.

KOREAN INVADERS A FORCE "WHICH WOULD CONTAIN A SUBSTANTIAL CONTINGENT 
OF ASIATIC TROOPS WHOSE MERE PRESENCE WOULD REFUTE ANY CHARGE OF 
"WHITE IMPERIALISM, ' 

"IN THE TRUE MEANING 
FIGHT FOR "ASIA FOR THE 
NEW CONQUEROR."

"SUCH AN ARMY IS ESSENTIAL NOT ONLY TO BACK UP THE LAND, SEA 
AND AIR FORCES ALREADY ENGAGED BUT ALSO TO IMPRESS UPON ALL THE

‘FORCES MOBILIZED UNDER A UNITED NATIONS MANDATE ARE NOT WASING

JULY 7-CAP)-THE FOREIGN OFFICE SAID TODAY ROMANIA HAS ASKED

THIS MONEY WILL COME FROM THE $600,000,000 AUTHORIZED BY CONGRESS 
TO PROMOTE MULTILATERAL TRADE IN EUROPE, 

MILTON KATZ, CHIEF MARSHALL PLAN ADMINISTRATOR IN EUROPE, 

SAT IN ON THE OEEC COUNCIL SESSION FOR THE UNITED STATES 
AS A NON-VOTING MEMBER. HE HAILED THE EPU AS ESTABLISHING AN 
EFFECTIVE EUROPEAN BANKING AND PAYMENTS SYSTEM. 

KATZ SAID BRITAIN'S DECISION TO JOIN THE EPU WAS A FUNDAMENTAL 
MODIFICATION OF BRITISH COMMERCIAL POLICY SINCE THE WAR. 

BRITAIN BROUGHT THE WHOLE STERLING AREA INTO EPU, THUS 
LINKING THE STERLING ZONE WITH WESTERN EUROPEAN NATIONS AND 
THEIR RESPECTIVE OVERSEAS AREAS IN THE PAYMENT SCHEME. 

SWITZERLAND'S ADHERENCE WAS ASSURED AFTER OTHER MINISTERS 
INSERTED A SPECIAL CLAUSE COVERING NATIONS WHICH HAVE RELEASED 
UP TO 85 PER CENT OF THEIR FOREIGN TRADE FROM QUOTA RESTRICTIONS. 
THUS FAR, ONLY THE SWISS HAVE DONE SO, BUT THE CLAUSE IS EQUALLY 
AVAILABLE TO ALL OTHER MEMBERS. 

THIS CLAUSE PROVIDES THAT WHEN A NATION'S ECONOMIC POSITION 
IS SERIOUSLY MENACED BY THE EPU OPERATION, IT MAY REAPPLY 
COMMERCIAL DISCRIMINATIONS AGAINST OTHER MEMBERS FOR EIGHT 
WEEKS PENDING A REEXAMINATION OF THE SITUATION, 

THE EPU AGREEMENT PROVIDES FOR AN APPEALS BOARD OF FIVE 
MEMBERS TO HEAR DISPUTES ON DISCRIMINATORY PRACTICES AND TO 
REPORT TO THE OEEC COUNCIL FOR DECISION. THE FLVE MEMBERS ARE 
TO BE FINANCIAL EXPERTS FROM COUNTRIES WHICH ARE NOT PARTIES TO 
THE DISPUTE. 

THE EPU ORGANIZATION, UNDER THE AGREEMENT, IS TO BE RUN BY A 
MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE OF SEVEN PERSONS NAMED BY THE OEEC COUNCIL FOR 
dixeee oF ONE YEARe THESE MANAGERS MAY BE REAPPOINTED FOR ADDITIONAL

BY STAN SWINTON 

CAIRO, JULY 7-CAP)=FOREIGN CORRESPONDENTS AND EGYPTIAN 
JOURNALISTS SOON MAY FACE PRISON TERMS FOR PUBLISHING ANYTHING ABOUT 
EGYPT'S ROYAL FAMILY WITHOUT WRITTEN PERMISSION, 

WAFD GOVERNMENT, WHICH CAME INTO OFFICE ON A PLATFORM PLEDGING 
ABOLITION OF CENSORSHIP, IS SPONSORING LEGISLATION STATING? 

"ANYONE WHO PUBLISHES IN THE PRESS OR IN OTHER PUBLICATIONS 


i . = fase ef af ww, 


WITHOUT WRITTEN PERMISSION FROM THE MINISTER OF INTERIOR, NEWS, 
PICTURES, DRAWINGS OR SYMBOLS OF THE PERSONAL AFFAIRS OF THE ROYAL 
FAMILY, OR ANY OF ITS MEMBERS, SHALL BE PUNISHED WITH A TERM 

OF IMPRISONMENT UP TO SIX MONTHS AND/OR A FINE OF £100 ($287)." 

THE LEGISLATION SEEMS VIRTUALLY ASSURED OF PASSAGE UNLESS THE 
GOVERNMENT CHANGES ITS PLANS. EGYPT'S PRESS SYNDICATE, JOURNALISTS’ 
ORGANIZATION, IS ON RECORD AGAINST THE BILL BUT OFFERED TO ACCEPT 
A WATERED=-DOWN VERSION WITH A MAXIMUM PENALTY OF A_£100 FINE, 

THE MEASURE WOULD TOP ALREADY STRINGENT CENSORSHIP ON ROYAL 
NEWS OR PICTURES COMING INTO OR GOING OUT OF THE COUNTRY. 

_ EGYPTIAN PRINCESS FATHIA MARRIED RIAD GHALI, A CHRISTIAN, IN 
SAN FRANCISCO IN DEFIANCE OF KING FAROUK. ALL NEWS OF THE CEREMONY 
WAS DELETED FROM INCOMING CABLES. PHOTOS ALSO WERE BANNED. 
BUT EGYPTIAN NEWSPAPERS TUNED IN THEIR RADIOS TO FOREIGN NEWS 
BROADCASTS AND PUBLISHED LENGTHY REPORTS ON THE WEDDING. 

KING FAROUK APPROVED THE MARRIAGE OF POPULAR PRINCESS FAIKA 
TO FUAD SADEK BEY, TENNIS@PLAYING EGYPTIAN DIPLOMAT. THE COUPLE 
ARRIVED HOME BY WAY OF EUROPE. SOME PICTURES SHOWED THEM WALKING 
HAND-IN-HAND OR WITH SADEK BEY STROLLING A BIT AHEAD OF HIS WIFE. 

WHEN THESE ARRIVED IN CAIRO, ALL PHOTOS WHICH DID NOT SHOW 
PRINCESS FAIKA CLEARLY WALKING IN FRONT OF HER HUSBAND WERE 
CONFISCATED. A CENSOR EXPLAINED THE PUBLIC COULD NOT SEE A PRINCESS 
WALKING EVEN WITH OR BEHIND A COMMONER HUSBAND. 

THE NEW LEGISLATION IS PHRASED SO THAT A PRISON SENTENCE IS 
MANDATORY FOR NEWSMEN SENDING ROYAL FAMILY NEWS WITHOUT WRITTEN 
PERMISSION, WHETHER OR NOT THE NEWS IS CONSIDERED 
DEROGATORY. | JUL ere]! 

UNDER THE WORDING, EVEN TO REPORT THAT THE KING RECEIVED A 
FOREIGN AMBASSADOR IN AUDIENCE == A ROUTINE, REGULAR AFFAIR--WOULD 
MEAN PRISON, 

EGYPT HAS NOT EXPLAINED WHY IT FEELS THE LEGISLATION 
NECESSARY. PRIVATELY, EGYPTIAN OFFICIALS PROTEST ABOUT PUBLICITY 
GIVEN AT HOME AND ABROAD TO RECENT DEVELOPMENTS CONCERNING 
EGYPT'S RULERS. .

COMMANDER OF THE FIRST MARINE DIVISION AT CAMP PENDLETON, CALIFe THE

KOREAN WAR. 

HE SURVEY PARTY WILL CONFER WITH AMERICAN AND FOREIGN OFFICIALS 
INDO@CHINA, INDONESIA, MALAYA, BURMA, THAILAND .AND THE PHILIPPINES.

WE LEFT BEHIND. WE LEFT SOME OF THOSE POOR KIDS---" 

THE PAIN SHOWED IN THE VOICE OF PVT.JOHN EASTERLING, 19 
OHIO, A LANKY MACHINEGUNNER WHO STAYED AT HIS GUN ALONE AFTER 14 
HOURS FIGHTING, TO COVER THE WITHDRAWAL OF HIS OUTFIT.

SAID WITH GREAT WEARINESS, "WHAT COULD WE DO? ONE MACHINEGUN AND 50

A MEDICAL AIDE BEGAN SEARCHING THE POCKETS OF THE DARK-HAIRED 
AMERICAN CORPSE FOR WHAT THE ARMY CALLS "PERSONAL EFFECTS." 

THERE IS THE SAME OLD SIMILARITY ABOUT "PERSONAL EFFECTS" IN THIS 
SAVAGE LITTLE WAR AS IN THE LAST BIG ONE. ALMOST ALWAYS THERE IS A 
WALLET, WITH PICTURES OF A MIDDLE AGED OR ELDERLY WOMAN, AND A GIRL. 
“THERE IS A KEY RING, A KNIFE, A ROSARY SOMETIMES, A BIT OF PAPER, 
BUT FEW LETTERS YET, FOR MAIL HAS BEEN SLOW CATCHING UP. 

FOR SOME, MAIL DOES NOT MATTER AT THE MOMENT, LIKE THE AMERICAN 
BOY FLAT ON’A BLANKET WITH THE PLASMA FLOWING INTO HIM. YOU COULD 
TELL HE WAS ALIVE AS A PULSE BEAT FLUTTERED IN HIS THROAT. HIS 
EYES WERE CLOSED AND HIS FINGER, GRIMY WITH THE SAME MUD THAT WEIGHTED 
HIS BOOTS AND HIS COMBAT GREEN UNIFORM, WERE LIMP AND STILL.

AMERICAN HEADQUARTERS IN KOREA, JULY 8=(AP)-ONE SLENDER THREAD 
LINKS THE WORLD WITH THE KOREAN SCENE WHERE HISTORY IS BEING WRITTEN. 
THAT THREAD IS THE SINGLE TELEPHONE CIRCUIT FROM HERE TO TOKYO. 

ALL THE FRONTLINE NEWS OF THE CRUCIAL CONFLICT IS CHANNELED 
THROUGH THAT ONE LINE. 

IT IS SHARED BY THE MILITARY. THE UNITED NATIONS COMMISSION AND 
CORRESPONDENTS. THERE ARE 40 CORRESPONDENTS ALREADY ON THE 
SCENE AND A SCORE, OF OTHERS EN ROUTE--AND THE PRESS COMES THIRD IN 
PRIORITY ON THE TELEPHONE. 

ONLY ANOTHER NEWS MAN CAN FULLY APPRECIATE THE MENTAL ANGUISH

OUT THEIR HOTTEST STORIES. BUT PERHAPS THIS EXPLANATION OF THE 
SYSTEM WILL GIVE THE NEWSPAPER READER SOME IDEAS 

THERE IS NO CENSORSHIP, BUT THERE IS A CODE OF VOLUNTARY 
COOPERATION FOR MILITARY SECURITY (WHICH VARIOUS CORRESPONDENTS 
INTERPRET IN VARIOUS WAYS). EVERY CORRESPONDENT MUST FILE WITH A 
SIGNAL CORPS OFFICER WHAT HE WISHES TO TELEPHONE. THE OFFICER PUTS 
A NUMBER ON IT IN THE ORDER RECEIVED. THE CORRESPONDENT MUST WAIT. 
UNTIL ALL COPY AHEAD OF HIS IS CLEARED BEFORE HE GETS A CRACK AT T 
TELEPHONE.

BUT Nou IT HAS BEEN AGREED TO LET EACH MAN TAKE AS LONG AS HE NEEDS. 
THERE IS A CATCH TO THIS: THE MAN WHO WRITES A LENGTHY STORY FINDS 
THAT THE OTHERS WHO WROTE SHORT BULLETINS HAVE GOTTEN IN AHEAD OF HIM. 
HIS STORY MAY BE BETTER AND MORE DETAILED, BUT IT IS LIKELY TO BE SO 
FAR BEHIND AS TO BE ALMOST WORTHLESS.

WASHINGTON, JULY 8-(AP)-PRES IDENT TRUMAN TODAY NAMED GENERAL DOUGLAS 
MACARTHUR TO THE UNPRECEDENTED POST OF SUPREME COMMANDER FOR UNITED 
NATIONS FORCES FIGHTING THE COMMUNISTS IN KOREA. THE GENERAL WAS 
DIRECTED TO FLY THE BLUE AND WHITE U.NeFLAG. 

THE ACTION COINCIDED WITH REPORTS FROM EUROPE THAT RUSSIA MAY BE 
INTERESTED IN TRYING TO END THE KOREAN CLASH=-OR, CONTRARILY, MAY BE 
MANEUVERING TO RAISE FALSE HOPES IN THE WEST. 

THE TWO DEVELOPMENTS SHARPLY REVIVED THE DIPLOMATIC SIDE OF THE . 
KOREAN SITUATION AND THIS PRESUMABLY FIGURED IN AN HOUR LONG CONFERENCE 
WHICH MR» TRUMAN HAD WITH SECRETARY OF STATE ACHESON BEFORE MAKING THE 
MACARTHUR ANNOUNCEMENT. 

THE REPORTS OF DIPLOMATIC ACTIVITY IN MOSCOW CAME FROM LONDON. 

THEY GREW OUT OF A MEETING , THURSDAY BETWEEN DEPUTY FOREIGN MINISTER 
ANDREI GROMYKO AND BRITISH AMBASSADOR SIR DAVID KELLY. 

BRITAIN HAD ASKED SEVERAL DAYS EARLIER THAT THE RUSSIANS INTERVENE 
IN KOREA TO RESTORE PEACE--A POLITE WAY OF SUGGESTING THAT THE KREMLIN 
CALL OFF THE NORTH KOREAN COMMUNISTS. ACCORDING TO TODAY'S LONDON 
REPORT, GROMYKO IS SUPPOSED TO HAVE ASKED KELLY WHAT BRITAIN THOUGHT 
RUSSIA MIGHT DO. THUS HE APPARENTLY DID NOT REJECT THE BRITISH IDEA 
OUTRIGHT AS A SIMILAR PROPOSAL FROM THE UNITED STATES WAS REJECTED. 

THIS REPORTED SHOW OF INTEREST BY GROMYKO WAS INTERPRETED IN LONDON 
DISPATCHES AS A POSSIBLE RUSSIAN PEACE FEELERe AUTHORITIES HERE DID 
NOT CONFIRM OR DENY THAT THE ACTUAL EVENT OCCURRED. BUT THEY NOTED 
THAT IT COULD BE (1) A HOPEFUL OPENING, (2) A DIPLOMATIC COVER TO 
STALL OFF THE WEST WITH MEANINGLESS TALK WHILE THE KOREAN FIGHT GOES 
ON OR (3) A DEVICE TO RAISE FALSE HOPES IN THE WORLD: BY HINTING AT 
PEACE WITHOUT ANY INTENTION TO WORK FOR IT. 

THE BRITISH FOREIGN OFFICE, THE BRITISH EMBASSY HERE AND THE STATE 
DEPARTMENT ALL DECLINED COMMENT. BRITAIN AND THE UNITED STATES HAVE 
BEEN REPORTED KEEPING IN CLOSE TOUCH WITH EACH OTHER ON THE WHOLE 
KOREAN SITUATIONe THE AMERICAN GOVERNMENT GOVERNMENT OBVIOUSLY HAS 
BEEN INFORMED OF THE GROMYKO“KELLY CONFERENCE.

WILL FOLLOW OuT EVERY LEAD THAT OFFERS ANY PROSPECT OF RESTORING A

JASHINGTON” Sere AP)=PRESIDENT T ' 
8-(AP)=PRESIDENT TRUMAN'S DECISION TO ENLARGE 
AMERICAN ARMED FORCES FURNISHES THE WORLD NEW PROOF THAT THE UNITED 
STATES INTENDS TO SEE THE KOREAN FIGHT THROUGH TO A FINISH. 
WHILE RUSSIA IS EXPECTED TO ASSAIL THE ACTION AS FURTHER EVIDENCE 
OF AMERICAN "AGGRESSION, THERE IS GROWING CONFIDENCE HERE THAT THE 
SOVIETS DO NOT PLAN TO PRECIPITATE A WORLD WAR. 
RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITIES BELIEVE THEREFORE THAT THE DRAFT ANNOUNCE- 
MENT WILL NOT BE SEIZED UPON BY THE KREMLIN AS A "PROVOCATIVE" ACT 
BY THE UNITED STATES, REGARDLESS OF WHAT PROPAGANDA USE THE RUSSIANS 


MAKE OF IT. 
ON THE OTHER HAND, COUNTRIES SUPPORTING THE UNITED NATIONS STAND 
ON KOREA ARE EXPECTED TO HAIL THE DRAFT MOVE AS PROOF OF AMERICAN 
DETERMINATION TO MAKE A SUCCESSFUL FIGHT FOR SOUTH KOREAN INDEPENDENCE, 
EVEN AT THE COST OF PLACING HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS MORE MEN UNDER ARMS. 
THE OFFICIAL ANNOUNCEMENT YESTERDAY STRESSED THAT THE DECISION TO 
USE THE ae IF NECESSARY, WAS MADE AS A RESULT OF THE KOREAN . 
SITUATION. IN THIS BRAND ot IT WAS UNDERSTOOD THAT TWO SPECIFIC 
RATEGY WERE OF PRIMARY CONCERN? 
1. THE COURSE OF THE FIGHTING IN KOREA HAS INDICATED A NEED FOR 





GREATER TROOP STRENGTH IN ACTUAL COMBAT THAN WAS ORIGINALLY THOUGHT 
NECESSARY. THIS STRENGTH HAS TO BE FURNISHED WITHOUT STRIPPING 
AMERICAN DEFENSES OR THOSE OF OTHER NON-COMMUNIST AREAS OUTSIDE KOREA. 

2. FROM THE START OF THE KOREAN INCIDENT TWO WEEKS ACO THE Posst- 
BILITY HAS EXISTED THAT IT WAS A DIVERSIONARY MOVE BY THE SOVIET 
COMMUNIST BLOC, TO BE FOLLOWED UP BY AN ATTACK IN SOME OTHER SECTOR 
OF THE EAST-WEST CONFLICT. SUCH A DEVELOPMENT COULD REQUIRE AN 
ADDITIONAL COMMITMENT OF AMERICAN FORCES. 

HAVING THESE PROBLEMS IN MIND, POLITICAL AND MILITARY STRATEGISTS 
WERE REPORTED TO FEEL THAT THE UNITED STATES COULD NOT PERMIT 
ITS ARMED STRENGTH TO BECOME UNBALANCED. 

THE STATE DEPARTMENT IS UNDERSTOOD TO HAVE RECOMMENDED IN RECENT 
DAYS THE IMMEDIATE REPLACEMENT IN THIS COUNTRY OF ANY DIVISIONS 
DEPLOYED FOR ACTION ON THE KOREAN FRONT, SO THAT TOTAL AMERICAN 
READINESS FOR ACTION WOULD BE MAINTAINED. 


AL 3WX 
THIS RECOMMENDATION, COINCIDING WITH THE ADVICE|OF MILITARY LEA- 
DERS, FITS INTO THE BASI¢ POLICY THAT THE BEST WAY TO PREVENT MORE 
SERIOUS TROUBLE WITH RUSSIA IS TO MAINTAIN THE STRENGTH TO DEAL WITH 
ANY COMMUNIST CHALLENGE WHICH MAY ARISE. 
AT THE SAME TIME, MR«TRUMAN AND HIS ADVISERS ARE REPORTED ANXIOUS 
TO TAKE ONLY THOSE STEPS CONSIDERED ESSENTIAL FOR THE JOB AT HAND. 
THE PRESIDENT HAS STATED EMPHATICALLY THAT HE DOES NOT CONSIDER THE 
UNITED STATES AT WAR, BUT RATHER ENGAGED IN A UNITED NATIONS POLICE 
HIS ORDER YESTERDAY, CALLING FOR A LIMITED INCREASE IN THE ARMED 
FORCES RATHER THAN A GENERAL MOBILIZATION, FELL SHORT OF THE ORDER 
HE MIGHT HAVE ISSUED TO DEAL WITH A MORE WIDESPREAD CRISIS. | 
ANOTHER FACTOR IN TOP LEVEL GOVERNMENT CALCULATIONS IS THAT THE 
CONFLICT BETWEEN THE COMMUNIST AND NON-COMMUNIST NATIONS IS EXPECTED | 
TO CONTINUE FOR MANY YEARS, BARRING UNFORESEEN DEVELOPMENTS » 
ITS “TOTAL STRENGTH, ECONOMIC AS WELL AS MILITARY, FOR THE LONG PULL.

LEXINGTON, KYs, JULY 8-(AP)=-THE COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF OF THE VETERANS 
OF FOREIGN WARS TONIGHT CALLED FOR IMMEDIATE LIMITED MOBILIZATION OF 
RESERVE COMPONENTS OF THE MILITARY AND OF INDUSTRY. 

"IT IS TRAGICALLY TRUE THAT THE COMMITMENT OF OUR FORCES IN THE 
DEFENSE OF SOUTH KOREA HAS WEAKENED US TO THE POINT WHERE WE WOULD NOT 
BE ABLE TO MOUNT ANOTHER MAJOR OPERATION ELSEWHERE IN THE WORLD." 

CLYDE AsLEWIS OF PLATTSBURG, NeYe, TOLD THE 30TH ANNUAL ENCAMPMENT OF 
THE KENTUCKY DEPARTMENT. VFW. 

THE WORLD WAR II VETERAN SAID "WE KNOW THE DESIGN OF SOVIET RUSSIA 
IS TO FORCE US TO SPREAD OUR FORCES THINLY THROUGHOUT THE WORLD. 

RUSSIA HOPES AND INTENDS THAT SEPARATE DISTURBANCES IN WIDELY SEPARATED 
AREAS WILL COMMIT OUR LIMITED FORCES To A NUMBER OF COSTLY BUT STRATE- 
SICALLY INDECISIVE ACTIONS. RUSSIA HAS MORE THAN 20 PRESSURE POINTS 
THROUGH WHICH SHE CAN CAUSE TROUBLE." 

EMPHASIZING THAT THERE IS NO OCCASION FOR THE HYSTERIA WHICH WOULD 
BE OCCASIONED BY AN OVERNIGHT FULL-SCALE MOBILIZATION OF OUR MILITARY 
AND INDUSTRIAL FORCES, LEWIS ADDED "BUT CERTAINLY THE AMERICAN PEOPLE 
ARE SANE ENOUGH TO ACCEPT A GRADUAL AND ORDERLY MARSHALING OF OUR 

"THE VFW COMMENDS THE PRESIDENT FOR GOING AS FAR AS HE DID. WE 
RESPECTFULLY SUGGEST, HOWEVER, THAT THE HOT AND COLD WARS REQUIRE 


BROADER MOBILIZATION OF OUR MILITARY AND INDUSTRIAL POTENTIALe « «

=(AP)-RIC EFENSE MINISTER RENE PLEVEN STARTED 
THE COMPLEX JOB TODAY OF PIECING TOGETHER A NEW FRENCH CABINET AS 
FRANCE'S LATEST GOVERNMENT CRISIS ENTERED ITS THIRD WEEK. 

TO BE SUCCESSFUL PLEVEN NEEDS THE BACKING OF THREE MAIN GROUPS-- 
EX=PREMIER HENRI QUEUILLE'S RIGHT-OF-CENTER RADICAL SOCIALISTS 
FORMER PREMIER GEORGES BIDAULT'S PRO-CATHOLIC POPULAR REPUBLICAN 
MOVEMENT (MRP) AND THE SOCIALISTS.« 

THE 49-YEAR-OLD PLEVEN IS A MEMBER OF THE DEMOCRATIC AND 
SOCIALIST UNION OF THE RESISTANCE (UDSR), A SMALL POLITICAL GROUP 
ALLIED WITH THE RADICALS.

PARIS, JULY 8-(AP)-EUROPE'S 18 MARSHALL PLAN COUNTRIES PREPARED 
TODAY TO’DO BUSINESS THROUGH THEIR OWN INTERNATIONAL BANK. A EUROPEAN 
PAYMENTS UNION (EPU) TO UNFETTER TRADE BY CANCELLING OUT FOREIGN 
CURRENCY SHORTAGES. , 

THE NATIONS, MEMBERS OF THE EUROPEAN ECONOMIC COOPERATION ORGANI- 
ZATION (OFEC), AGREED UNANIMOUSLY YESTERDAY TO SET UP THE CURRENCY 
CLEARING HOUSE. OFEC SECRETARY-GENERAL ROBERT MARJOLIN CALLED IT THE 
"HOST IMPORTANT FINANCIAL DECISION® SINCE FOUNDATION ‘OF THE WORLD BANK 

EXPERTS NOW WILL DRAW UP DETAILED RULES FOR EPU OPERATIONS. THEY 
HOPE TO HAVE A FINAL CONVENTION READY FOR SIGNATURE EARLY IN AUCUST. 
ITS PROVISIONS WILL BE RETROACTIVE TO JULY 1. 

PREVIOUSLY EUROPEAN NATIONS, THEIR TRADE GEARED TO A SYSTEM OF 
BILATERAL AGREEMENTS WITH EACH OTHER, COULD BUY ONLY IN THE 
COUNTRIES WHOSE CURRENCY THEY HAD STOCKS OF. NOW THEY WILL DEPOSIT 
THEIR HOLDINGS WITH THE CENTRAL AGENCY, RECEIVING IN RETURN EPU 
CREDITS GOOD FOR PURCHASES IN ANY OTHER MEMBER COUNTRY. 

THE UNION PROVIDES EUROPE"S FIRST POSTWAR MULTILATERAL TRADING 
SYSTEM. THE ADHERENCE TO IT OF BRITAIN AND THE STERLING AREA 
LINKS THAT MAJOR FINANCIAL BLOC WITH EUROPEAN NATIONS IN A FUNDAMENTAL 
MODIFICATION OF POSTWAR BRITISH COMMERCIAL POLICY. 

MARJOLIN SAID MEMBER NATIONS WOULD TAKE TWO INITIAL STEPS AFTER 
SIGNING THE UNION CONVENTION. THEY MUST CANCEL DISCRIMINATIONS 
AGAINST IMPORTS FROM ANY MEMBER COUNTRY. ALSO THEY MUST FREE 60 PER 
CENT OF THEIR IMPORTS FROM QUOTA RESTRICTIONS. THE OEEC MEMBERS 
ALREADY HAVE AGREED TO REMOVE 50 PER CENT OF THEIR IMPORT QUOTAS. 

THE UNITED STATES WILL FURNISH THE FUNDS--BETWEEN $300,000,000 
AND $375,000,000--FOR THE EPU'S INITIAL OPERATING CAPITAL AND ADMINIS- 
TRATIVE COSTS. THE MONEY WILL COME FROM THE $600,000,000 APPROPRIATED 
BY CONGRESS TO PROMOTE FREER TRADE IN EUROPE. 

THE PAYMENTS UNION WILL OPERATE UNDER THE OFEC COUNCIL. WHICH 
WILL NAME A SEVEN-MAN MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE TO SUPERVISE OPERATIONS. 
A FIVE-MAN APPEAL BOARD OF FINANCIAL EXPERTS WILL HEAR DISPUTES ON 


aa PRACTICES AND REPORT TO THE OEEC COUNCIL FOR

HONG KONG, SUNDAY JULY 9=-(AP)=-SURVIVORS OF THE ILLFATED SHIP VALVE 
SAID TODAY CHINESE COMMUNIST MINESWEEPERS SAVED THEM WHEN THEIR MOTOR 
VESSEL HIT A MINE AND SANK JUNE 20 OFF SHANGHAI, 

SURVIVORS ARRIVING HERE SAID THE VALVE SANK WITHIN FOUR MINUTES 
AFTER STRIKING A MINE PRESUMABLY LAID BY THE CHINESE NATIONALISTS IN 
THEIR BLOCKADE OF SHANGHAI. 

ONE OF THE CREW OF 41 WAS KILLED BY THE EXPLOSION. THE REST WERE 
RESCUED BY EIGHT COMMUNIST MINESWEEPERS WHICH WERE NEARBY CLEARING 
MINES FROM THE YANGTZE RIVER APPROACHES TO SHANGHAI. 

THE VALVE, A PANAMANIAN REGISTRY, WENT DOWN ALMOST SIMULTANEOUSLY 
WITH THE GREEK SHIP ARGOS, WHICH ALSO HIT A MINE IN THE MOUTH OF THE 
YANGTZE. ALL THE ARGOS CREW MEMBERS WERE BELIEVED TO BE SAFE. 

TWENTY-SIX OF THE VALVE'S CREW ARRIVED IN HONG KONG YESTERDAY. 
THEY HAD TRAVELED OVERLAND FROM SHANGHAI. OTHERS, INCLUDING THE 
BRITISH CAPTAIN,TeJe KING, STILL ARE IN CANTON WAITING FOR CHINESE 
COMMUNIST AUTHORITIES TO GRANT THEM EXIT PERMITS.

OPENLY ENOUGH, THE RUSSIANS ANNOUNCE COMMUNIST INTENTIONS IN ASIA. 
ON MAY 17 PRAVDA, VOICE OF THE COMMUNIST CENTRAL COMMITTEE, VOWED THAT 
"NO INTRIGUES OF THE AMERICANS CAN SUPPRESS THE GROWING NATIONAL LIBFRA- 
TION MOVEMENT IN ASIA. THE PEOPLES OF THE COUNTRIES OF SOUTHEAST 
ASIA WILL NOT BE THE SLAVES OF AMERICAN MONOPOLIES.® 

PRAVDA PICTURED CHINA AS A WILLING SERVANT OF RUSSIAN POLICY IN THIs 
RESPECT. IT ANNOUNCED JUNE 25--THE DAY OF THE KOREAN INVASION--THAT 
COMMUNIST CHIEF MAO TZE-TUNG BASED HIS POLICY ON SINO-SOVIET UNITY 
AND THE REALIZATION THAT "OUR GREAT PURPOSE IS TO UNITE CLOSELY WITH 
THE SOVIET UNION, WITH COUNTRIES OF PEOPLE'S DEMOCRACY AND WITH ALL 
PEACE-LOVING DEMOCRATIC FORCES IN THE ENTIRE WORLD.” 

BRANDISHING THE BANNER OF LAND REFORM TO WOO LANDLESS AND POVERTY- 
RIDDEN PEASANTS OF ASIA, THE COMMUNISTS OBVIOUSLY HOPE TO SWEEP THROUGH 
ALL ASIA WITH LITTLE REGISTANCE, BANISHING ALL WESTERN INFLUENCE. 

THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS HAVE TOLD THE UNITED NATIONS THEY INTEND TO Go 
RIGHT AHEAD AND "LIBERATE" FORMOSA, ASTRIDE THE AMERICAN PACIFIC DEFENSE

TOKYO,JULY 10-(AP)-TEXT OF THE FAR EAST AIR FORCES COM UE 
ISSUED AT 3:35 P.M. JAPAN DAYLIGHT TIME (12235 A.M. ABINDAY, EST)! 

FEAF FIGHTERS AND LIGHT BOMBERS HAMMERED AT THE WESTERN SECTOR OF 
THE KOREAN BATTLEFRONT ON SUNDAY, JULY 9, DESTROYING LARGE QUANTITIES OF 
NORTH KOREAN EQUIPMENT AND MATERIEL. pap 

THE MARKED SUCCESS ENCOUNTERED IN SUNDAY'S AIR ACTION WAS 
ATTRIBUTED TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF COORDINATED AIR AND GROUND CONTROL OF 
AIR OPERATIONS. TECHNIQUES EVOLVED OVER THE PAST TWO WEEKS HAVE MADE 
IT POSSIBLE TO MOVE AIRCRAFT RAPIDLY TO POINTS OF DANGEROUS NORTH KODTAN 
STRENGTH AT THE PRECISE TIME EFFECTIVE SUPPORT FROM THE AIR IS MOST 

&amp; LUe 

LOW LEVEL STRAFING AND BOMBING ATTACKS, CONDUCTED FOR THE MOST PART 
BY FIFTH AIR FORCE F-80S AND B-26S, CAUSED HEAVY LOSSES TO THE NORTH 
KOREAN FORCES IN SPITE OF BAD FLYING WEATHER THROUGHOUT THE MORNINC 
EARLY AFTERNOON. 

AIR ASSAULTS WERE CONCENTRATED IN THE AREA FROM CHONAN NORTH TO OSAN, 
ALTHOUGH STRIKES WERE ALSO MOUNTED AGAINST OTHER TARGETS. INCLUDINC 
SUSAN-NI AND UTCHIN ON THE EAST COAST. PRIMARY OBJECTIVES WERE TANK, 
TRUCK AND TROOP CONCENTRATIONS MOVING SOUTH OF THE BATTLE LINES. 


A231FX

TARGETS IN THE CHONAN SECTOR, AND F=82S STRAFED AND BOMBED TRUCKS , 
TROOPS AND BUILDINGS IN THE SAME AREA. NAPALM BOMBS WERE DROPPED 

RAAF MUSTANGS AGAIN JOINED THE F-S0S IN AN EXPANDING PROGRAM 
OF GROUND ATTACK. AMONG THE TARGETS STRUCK BY THE AUSTRALIAN PILOTS 
WAS A GROUP OF BUILDINGS FORMING PART OF THE NORTH KOREAN ARMY 
INSTALLATION AT CHONGJU. RAAF FIGHTER SORTIES HAVE PLAYED A KEY PART 
IN SUCCESSFUL KOREAN OPERATIONS SINCE EARLY IN JULY.

DESTRUCTION OF 33 TANKS» 69 TRUCKS, 1 LOCOMOTIVE, 9 BOXCARS, 2 HALF-

1 LOCOMOTIVES WERE DAMAGED. A LARGE NUMBER OF OTHER VEICLES, INCLUDING

TOK¥O, JULY 9-(AP)-GENERAL DOUGLAS MACARTHUR--THE UNITED NATIONS" 
FIRST MILITARY COMMANDER--IS CONDUCTING THE KOREAN CAMPAIGN FROM A 
RELATIVELY PLAIN OFFICE IN A FORMER INSURANCE BUILDING. 

IT'S THE SAME OFFICE HE USED WHEN HIS JOB WAS LIMITED TO BEING 
SUPREME COMMANDER FOR THE ALLIzD POWERS IN THE OCCUPATION OF JAPAN. 
AND FROM ALL OUTWARD APPEARANCES, NEITHER HIS NEW POSITION NOR, THE 
INCREASED RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE MILITARY CAMPAIGN HAVE CHANGED THE 
70-YEAR-OLD GENERAL'S WORKING DAY. 

HE MAY LEAVE THE OFFICE A BIT LATER NOW. THAN USUAL--PERHAPS AROUND 


ALBERT Me 
S7 GOODENOUGH STe, BOSTON, 


9 P.Me AND THERE MAY BE LESS TIME FOR VISITS WITH CALLERS WHOM HE 
LIKES TO LECTURE ON A VAST RANGE OF INTERNATIONAL TOPICS. 

BUT THE GENERAL ALREADY HAS ESTABLISHED A RIGID, SEVEN DAY WORKING 
SCHEDULE, WITHOUT PAUSE FOR HOLIDAYS. HE ALSO KEPT CLOSELY IN TOUCI 
WITH THE MILITARY ASPECTS OF HIS COMMAND. IN RECENT YEARS, HOWEVER, 
HIS PUBLIC STATEMENTS LARGELY HAVE BEEN ON JAPAN'S ECONOMIC AND 
POLITICAL PROBLEMS. 

IT MIGHT BE SUSPECTED THE MAJOR CHANGE NOW IS THAT GEN.MACARTHUR 
IS MORE INTERESTED IN HIS JOB. HE SEEMED TEN YEARS YOUNGER WHEN HE WAS 
MAKING PLANS JUNE 2% FOR HIS DRAMATIC FLIGHT TO THE KOREAN BATTLE 

AT THAT TIME HE TALKED TO FOUR NEWSMEN BRIEFLY IN HIS FAMILIAR 
OFFICE. HIS DESK WAS BARE OF PAPERS ALTHOUGH THERE MUST HAVE BEEN 
INNUMERABLE REPORTS SENT TO HIM ON THE PROGRESS OF HOSTILITIES WHICH 
HAD JUST RESULTED IN THE FALL OF SEOUL. 

MACARTHUR KEEPS IN CLOSE TOUCH WITH THE STAFF OFFICERS WHO 
ACTUALLY ARE COORDINATING THE KOREAN CAMPAIGN. A SPECIAL WAR ROOM HAS 
BEEN ESTABLISHED IN HEADQUARTERS, CLOSELY GUARDED BY SENTRIES. 

KEY STAFF OFFICERS MEET DAILY’ TO GO OVER DEVELOPMENTS. GENERAL 
OFFICERS FROM EACH OF THE MAIN STAFF SECTIONS--FROM INTELLIGENCE TO 
LOGISTICS--DEVOTE FULL 24-HOUR ATTENTION TO THE CAMPAIGN. 

THEIR REPORTS GO REGULARLY TO MACARTHUR, WHO KEEPS HIMSELF INFORMED 
OF DETAILS--AND REMEMBERS THEM. 

WHEN NEWSMEN ACCOMPANYING HIM TO SOUTH KOREA WERE CONCERNED ABOUT 
PICTURES OF THE EVENT, MACARTHUR REMEMBERED THAT TWO SIGNAL CORPS 
ENLISTED MEN HAD BEEN ASSIGNED THE PREVIOUS DAY AS PHOTOGRAPHERS TO 
SUWON, THE NOW-FALLEN CITY WHERE HE LANDED, 

HOSTILITIES HAVE NOT ALTERED THE RIGID ANONYMITY OF MACARTHUR'S 
HOME LIFE FITHER. THE GENERAL DOFS NOT ACCEPT SOCIAL INVITATIONS 
AND MRSeMACARTHUR USUALLY APPEARS PUBLICLY ONLY DURING THE DAYTIME. 
THEIR EVENINGS ARE SPENT WITH THEIR SON ARTHUR, AND A FEV FRIENDS WHO 
ATTEND REGULAR PRIVATE MOTION PICTURE SHOWS AT THE EMBASSY=-MACARTHUP's 

MRS eMACARTHUR AND ARTHUR YERE WITH THE GENERAL NINE YEARS ACO WHEN 
HE LEFT OFFICIAL RETIREMENT TO BECOME COMMANDER IN CHIEF OF AMERICAN

AMERICAN HEADQUARTERS.IN..KOREA, JULY 9-(AP)-CGRUIOUSLY, AMERICAN 
REVERSES IN EARLY SMALL-SCALE COMBAT WITH NORTH KOREAN TROOPS HAVE 
BOOSTED THE MORALE OF THE SOUTH KOREAN ARMY, AMERICAN MILITARY SOURCES 
SAID TODAY. 

THE SOUTH KOREANS ARE OUTFIGHTING THEIR NORTHERN BROTHERS NOW IN 
EVERY CLASH OF INFANTRY AGAINST INFANTRY. SINCE PRACTICALLY ALL OF 
THE NORTH KOREAN ARMOR IS COMMITTED AGAINST THE AMERICAN FORCES 
THIS MEANS THE SOUTH KOREANS ARE HOLDING THEIR OWN AND EVEN GAINING 
GROUND. 

THE MATTER OF MORALE RESTS ON THE FACT THE NORTH KOREAN ARMOR 
DEFEATED THE AMERICANS TOO. THE SOUTH KOREANS HAVE REGAINED FACE, 
ALWAYS AN IMPORTANT FACTOR IN THE FAR EAST. 

THE NORTHERN INVADERS HAVE AN UNKNOWN NUMBER OF MEN ALONG THE 
EXTENSIVE FRONT FROM THE EAST COAST CLOSE TO THE 37TH PARALLEL TO 
WHERE THE AMERICAN FORCES ARE LINED UP NEAR THE WEST COAST. 

WITHOUT DISCLOSING MILITARY INFORMATION IT CAN BE SAID THE NORTH 
vOREAN ARMY STRENGTH HAS PRACTICALLY EQUALLED, 

NUMERICALLY, BY THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA ARMY AT THE OUTSET--EACH 
REPORTEDLY HAVING AROUND 100,000 MEN. SINCE THEN, HOWEVER, THE SOUTH 
NOREANS HAVE BEEN DISORGANIZED AND HURT BY CASUALTIES. 

THE NORTHERN STRENGTH IS PLACED NOW AT 15 DIVISIONS CONTAINING ABOUT 
6,000 COMBAT TROOPS IN EACH DIVISION, PLUS AN UNKNOWN NUMBER OF SERVICE 
AND SUPPORTING TROOPS. 

WHEN THE WAR STARTED TWO WEEKS AGO TODAY SOUTH KOREAN WAS ABLE 
TO SEND ABOUT 50,000 COMBAT TROOPS INTO BATTLE AGAINST THE INVADERS. 
LOSSES HAVE NOT’ BEEN DISCLOSED, BUT MANY SOUTHERN TROOPS CUT OFF 
BY THE SWIFT-PROGRESS OF THE ARMORED MOTORIZED. COLUMNS OF THE ENEMY. 
HAVE SIFTED BACK AND BEEN REORGANIZED. 

SIMPLE RECRUITMENT--PICKING UP OF ABLE BODIED MALES--PROBABLY HAS 
BROUGHT THE NUMERICAL ARMY STRENGTH TO THAT OF THE INVADERS. TRAINING 
IS SOMETHING ELSE AGAIN. 

THE KOREAN REPUBLIC'S ARMY IS BEING REORGANIZED CONSTANTLY, ONE 
EXPERIENCED AMERICAN MILITARY ADVISER SAID. 

“IT NOW IS COMPOSED OF A HEADQUARTERS FIRST CORPS INCLUDING THE 
CAPITAL DIVISION, FIRST DIVISION AND SECOND DIVISION. THER® ARE THE 
SIXTH DIVISION AND THE EIGHTH DIVISION, AS OTHER MAJOR COMMANDS 
AS WELL AS SUCH SEPARATE UNITS AS THE 23RD REGIMENT PLUS SEPARATE 
THE FIRST AND SECOND BATTALIONS, A CAVALRY REGIMENT AND A

ADVANCED AMERICAN HEADQUARTERS IN KOREA,JULY 9-(AP)-MARTLAL LAW 
WAS PROCLAIMED IN SOUTH KOREA, EFFECTIVE TODAY. 

THE ORDER WAS SIGNED“YESTERDAY BY MAJeGEN.CHUNG IL KWUN, CHIEF OF 
STAFF AND COMMANDING GENERAL OF THE SOUTH KOREAN ARMED FORCES. 

THE ORDER FORBIDS DISTURBING THE COUNTRY'S ECONOMIC LIFE BY HOARDING 
GOODS, OR BY ABANDONING JOBS WITHOUT ADEQUATE REASONS. IT ALSO 
FORBIDS SPREADING RUMORS OR CAUSING AGITATION. 

VIOLATIONS ARE PUNISHABLE UNDER THE CONSTITUTION, GENERAL CHUNG 
SAID BUT THERE WAS NO IMMEDIATE INDICATION WHETHER THIS INCLUDED 
THE DEATH PENALTY.

LONDON, JULY 9-(AP)-THE BRITISH ADMIRALTY ANNOUNCED THAT THE 
CRUISER JAMAICA, OPERATING OFF KOREA, WAS STRUCK BY A SHELL FROM A 
SHORE BATTERY. 
FIVE MEN WERE KILLED OUTRIGHT AND ANOTHER HAS DIED OF WOUNDS 
THE ADMIRALTY REPORTED. THE CRUISER, IT ADDED, WAS NOT MATERTALLY 
DAMAGED. 
THE JAMAICA IS AN 8,000 TON VESSEL OF THE FIJI CLASS. 
FIVE OF THE DEAD WERE SOLDIERS, TWO BEING ARTILLERYMEN. 
THE ADMIRALTY DID NOT DISCLOSE WHY SOLDIERS WERE ON THE CRUISER. 
THE BRITISH PRESS ASSOCIATION SAID IT WAS LIKELY 
THE SOLDIERS WERE TAKEN ABOARD AT HONG KONG FOR A CRUISE BEFORE THE 
FIGHTING IN KOREA STARTED, AND THAT THEY COULD NOT BE LANDED BEFORE 


THE JAMAICA WAS ORDERED INTO ACTION IN KOREAN WATERS.

WILLING TO SUPPORT ANY NECESSARY INCREASE IN MILITARY FUNDS TO PROVIDE 
THE MEN AND EQUIPMENT NEEDED FOR A DECISIVE VICTORY IN.KOREA.

TIONAL MILITARY FUNDS. 


BUT HE ADDED THAT HE DOESN'T BELIEVE THE TIME HAS YET ARRIVED TO

BEEN MUCH SPECULATION IN CONGRESS.

(ADVANCE) NEW YORK) JULY 9-CAP)-ARNE SUNDE, NORWEGIAN PRESIDENT OF 
THE SECURITY COUNCIL, SAID TODAY THE UNITED STATES HAS BEENASKED TO 
LEAD AN "INTERNATIONAL POLICE ACTION", NOT A WAR, IN KOREA. 

HIS STATEMENT, PREPARED FOR A UNITED NATIONS BROADCAST, WAS ONE OF 
EIGHT WRITTEN BY U.Ne LEADERS FOR DELIVERY OVER THE NBC NETWORK. THE 
OTHER SPEAKERS INCLUDED AMBASSADOR WARREN AUSTIN, CHIEF OF THE U.S. 
DELEGATION; SIR GLADWYN JEB3, CHIEF OF THE BRITISH DELEGATIONs KEITH 
SHANN OF AUSTRALIAS SIR CARL BERENDSEN, CHIEF OF THE NEW ZEALAND 
DELEGATION AND PRINCE WAN OF THAILAND.

LEADERSHIP IN THIS CAMPAIGN." Thee at |

THE CONFLICT WITHIN THE TERRITORY OF KOREA." 
AUSTIN SAID A UNIFIED COMMAND IN THE KOREAN FIELD UNDER GEN. 
DOUGLAS MACARTHUR WAS OF IMPORTANCE BECAUSE "THE QUICKER IT IS OVER 
THE SOONER WE WILL TAKE THAT GREAT ADVANCE TOWARD PEACE IN GENERAL.” 

HE DESCRIBED THE NORTH KOREAN ATTACK AS "THE FIRST STEP WITHOUT 
DOUST IN THE FORM OF AGGRESSION THAT WOULD ADVANCE AROUND THE WORLD 
IF IT WERE NOT STOPPED IN ITS TRACKS." 

PRINCE WAN REPORTED THAILAND WAS UNABLE TO GIVE MILITARY ASSISTANCE 
BUT HAS OFFERED "FOODSTUFF SUCH AS RICE" TO SOUTH KOREA. 

SIR CARL SAID "ON THE INSPIRING INITIATIVE OF THE UNITED STATES

TO DELAY ACTION BY A VETO.

ATTACKING THE ACTION AS ILLEGAL WAS "PURE PROPAGANDA MADE WITHOUT 
ANY REGARD FOR THE TRUTH AND OBVIOUSLY BASED UPON HITLER'S POLICY 
THAT THE BIGGER THE LIE THE BETTER ITS CHANCE OF BEING BELIEVED." 

SHANN DECLARED IF THE SECURITY COUNCIL HAD NOT FACED UP TO ITS 
RESPONSIBILITIES THE "EVENTUAL CHANCES OF A THIRD WORLD WAR WOULD 
HAVE BEEN GREATLY INCREASED." 

SIR GLADWYN ASSERTED THAT THE ACTION HAD SHOWN THE SECURITY COUNCIL

HONG KONG, JULY 10-(AP)-ELEVEN NATIONALIST HORN-TYPE MINES HAVE 
BEEN SWEPT FROM THE HARBOR OF SWATOW OPPOSITE FORMOSA THIS WEEK. 

CAPT.BePATEY OF THE BRITISH STEAMSHIP EMPIRE PARK REPORTED 
REMOVAL OF THE MINES WHEN HIS VESSEL RETURNED HERE TODAY WITH 500 TONS 
OF CARGO FROM THAT COMMUNIST-HELD FUKIEN PORT. 

PATEY SAID CHINESE COMMUNIST PORT AUTHORITIES PERMIT NO LANDINGS, 
SAILINGS OR LOADINGS DURING DAYLIGHT BECAUSE OF POSSIBLE NATIONALIST 
AIR RAIDS, HE SAID A HEAVY TYPE OF FLOATING CRANE IS STANDING BY THE 
SUBMERGED BUTTERFIELD AND SWIRE FREIGHT ANHUI FOR SALVAGE OPERATIONS. 

ONLY THE ANHUI*S SUPERSTRUCTURE IS ABOVE WATER. SHE HIT A | 
NATIONALIST MINE EARLY LAST MONTH BUT ALL HANDS WERE RESCUED. SHE HAS 
AN 11 BY 5 FOOT HOLE IN HER PORT SIDE, SALVAGE AUTHORITIES TOLD PATEY. 

TWO RIVER BOATS WHICH LEFT HERE FRIDAY REACHED CANTON SAFELY, IT 
WAS REPORTED TODAY. THEY SAILED EMPTY ON A TRIAL RUN TO SEE WHETHER 
TRADE WITH THE BIG KWANGTUNG PORT COULD BE RESUMED. THE ONCE HEAVY 
TRADE WITH CANTON HAS BEEN DOWN TO A TRICKLE OF MOTOR JUNKS GOING BY 
WAY OF THE PORTUGUESE COLONY OF MACAO, DUE TO THE BLOCKADE OF THE 
PEARL RIVER'S APPROACHES BY NATIONALIST WARSHIPS, WHICH WERE 
WITHDRAWN ONLY LAST WEEKEND.

TOKYO, JULY 10-(AP)-EXPANDED AMERICAN AIR POWER HURLED AGAINST KEY 
BATTLE AREAS DESTROYED OR DAMAGED 4&amp;6 COMMUNIST KOREAN TANKS AND CAUSED 
"HEAVY LOSSES" TO RED GROUND TROOPS STRUGGLING TOWARD THE FRONT SUNDAY, 
A FAR EAST AIR FORCE COMMUNIQUE ANNOUNCED. 

MARKED SUCCESS IN THESE ATTACKS WAS ATTRIBUTED TO DEVELOPMENT OF 
"COORDINATED AIR AND GROUND CONTROL OF AIR OPERATIONS." THIS PERMITS 
FAST MOVEMENT OF AERIAL FIREPOWER TO THE POINTS OF "DANGEROUS NORTH 
SOREAN STRENGTH” WHERE IT IS MOST NEEDED, THE COMMUNIQUE SAID. 

FIGHTERS AND LIGHT BOMBERS CONCENTRATED ON HEAVY RED TROOP MOVEMENTS 
ALONG THE 22-MILE STRETCH OF ROAD BETWEEN CHONAN ON THE EDGE OF THE 
3ATTLEFRONT NORTHWARD TO OSAN. THERE FOUR DIVISIONS ARE GRINDING TOWAR 
THE FRONT.» : 

A TOTAL OF 153 COMBAT SORTIES BY FAST FIGHTERS AND B-26 BOMBERS 
DESTROYED 33 TANKS, 69 TRUCKS, 1 LOCOMOTIVE, 9 BOXCARS, 2 HALF=TRAC 
6 JEEPS, AND 2 LARGE TUNS. BESIDES THIS, 15 TANKS, 49 TRUCKS AND 1 
LOCOMOTIVE WERE DAMAGED, THE COMMUNIQUE SAID. 

"NUMEROUS CASUALTIES*® WERE REPORTED AMONG GROUND TROOPS CAUGHT 
UNDER THE HAIL OF ROCKETS, BOMBS, MACHINEGUN FIRE AND -- FOR THE FIRST 
TIME REPORTED IN THIS WAR’ -- THE’ JELLY-LIKE EXPLOSIVE LIQUID CALLED

BY EDDY GILMORE JUL 41 1956 
MOSCOW, JULY 10-(AP)&lt;PRAVDA TODAY DESCRIBED THE UNITED NATION 

SECURITY COUNCIL-AS "HALF WRECKED." on 


THE COMMUNIST PARTY NEWSPAPER, IN A DISPATCH FROM LAKE SUCCESS, 


SAID THE ACTION OF THE’ *REMNANTS® OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL IN PUTTING” 


FORCES IN KOREA UNDER GEN, MACARTHUR AND THE U.N. FLAG WAS A "SHAMEFUL 
FARCE® PLAYED OUT UNDER INSTRUCTIONS FROM THE UeSe STATE DEPARTMENT. 

THE U.N. WAS BEING MISUSED, SAID THE DISPATCH, BY “AGGRESSIVE 
CIRCLES OF THE UNITED STATES IN ORDER TO JUSTIFY THEIR CRIMINAL ROLE 
AS GENDARMES IN KOREA AND OTHER NATIONS OF ASIA." 

"THUS THERE IS BEING FORMED UNDER THE FLAG OF THE U.N. A COALITION 
OF IMPERIALISTS AND BEASTS OF PREY FOR THE BLOODY SUPPRESSION OF THE 
KOREAN PEOPLE,” THE PAPER ADDED. | 

PRAVDA SAID THE SECURITY COUNCIL, “BASIC ORGAN OF THE U.Ne, IS FAC@- 
TUALLY PARALYZED AND WITHOUT LEGAL AUTHORITY®* BECAUSE UNITED STATES 
POLICIES MADE IMPOSSIBLE THE PARTICIPATION OF THE SOVIET UNION AND THE 
CHINESE COMMUNIST GOVERNMENT, 

SEEKING TO GIVE PURPORTED AMERICAN REACTION TO KOREAN DEVELOP= 


MENTS, THE DISPATCH SAID MANY AMERICANS FEEL THAT THEIR MILITARY LEADERS 


HAVE GONE TOO FAR AND "HOUR BY HOUR ARE DRAGGING THE NATION INTO AN 
OPEN WAR." 

THERE WAS NOTHING HERE, HOWEVER, TO INDICATE THAT THE SOVIET 
UNION BELIEVES ANOTHER WORLD WAR INEVITABLE. SINCE THE FIGHTING IN 
KOREA BEGAN, SOVIET COMMENTATORS HAVE STRESSED THAT THOSE SEEKING 
PEACE WILL PREVAIL. : 

THE DISPATCH SAID THOUSANDS OF AMERICANS, INCLUDING 500,000 IN 
NEW YORK, HAVE SIGNED THE COMMUNIST-SPONSORED STOCKHOLM PEACE PETITION, 
IT REPORTED, HOWEVER, THAT SOME PERSONS CIRCULATING THE PETITION WERE 
JAILED OR SUBJECTED TO OTHER HUMILIATIONS,. 

THE OFFICIAL PARTY NEWSPAPER REPRINTED A LITERARY GAZETTE ARTICLE 
ATTACKING SIX MEMBERS OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL AND CALLING THEM "BLOODY 
FOOLS" FOR VOTING TO APPLY MILITARY SANCTIONS AGAINST NORTH KOREA. 

OTHER DISPATCHES IN THE SOVIET PRESS SAID VOLUNTEERS FOR NORTH 
KOREAN FORCES NOW TOTALED 500,000, AND REPORTED THAT 60 UNITED STATES 
SOLDIERS AND OFFICERS HAD BEEN CAPTURED IN CHONAN IN KOREA.’ .

(200) 19TH BOMB GROUP 

WASHINGTON, JULY 10-(AP)-THE AIR FORCE'S 19TH BOMBARDMENT GROUP 
WHOSE StS IAVE BEEN BOMBING ENEMY TARGETS IN KOREA, WAS THE FIRST 
UeSe UNIT TO DROP BOMBS IN WORLD WAR IIe CAPT. COLIN KELLY WAS ONE 
OF ITS PILOTS. 

THE 19TH, EQUIPPED WITH THE EARLY MODEL Bo17S, WAS BASED AT CLARK 
FIELD IN THE PHILIPPINES WHEN THE JAPANESE STRUCK. ITS 93RD SQUADRON 
WAS OPERATING ON THE MORNING OF DECe 7, 1941, FROM ANOTHER FIELD 
AND THUS ESCAPED THE HAMMERING THE ENEMY PLANES GAVE ALL AIRCRAFT AT 
CLARKe 

AMONG THE PILOTS WHO GOT THEIR B-17S INTO THE AIR WAS KELLY, ONE 
OF THE FIRST AMERICANS TO DIE IN WORLD WAR II. HIS BOMBER WENT DOWN 
AFTER BOMBING A JAPANESE BATTLESHIP. 

ALTHOUGH LOSSES STEADILY WHITTLED DOWN THE GROUP'S STRENGTH, THE 
OUTFIT HUNG ON AT PHILIPPINES BASES, CONDUCTING BOMBING OPERATIONS 
UNTIL DECEMBER 24. 


ON THAT DAY, THE GROUP FLEW TO AUSTRALIA AND LATER CONTINUED POUNDING AT YOUR HEADQUARTERS WNTIL PEACE Ts REESTABLISHED. HE HOPES 


JAPANESE TARGETS. LATE IN 1942 IT WAS ORDERED BACK TO THE UNITED 
STATES. IN 1944. AFTER BEING RE-FORMED AND TRAINED, THE GROUP WENT 
BACK INTO THE WAR WITH B-29S. AFTER REACHING GUAM EARLY IN 1945 
HE 49TH JOINED IN THE LONG RANGE AIR BOMBARDMENT OF THE JAPANESE 
HOMELAND. 

COLeTHEODORE QUENTIN GRAFF, 45-YEAR OLD NATIVE OF COLUMBIA, MOe, 
I$ CURRENTLY GROUP COMMANDER. GRAFF FOUGHT IN THE MEDITERRANEAN 
AIR CAMPAIGN DURING WORLD WAR IIe HIS MOTHER, MRS«LULU E.GRAFF, LIVES 
AT 313 MAGNOLIA AVE«, PERRYVILLE, MOe

LAKE .SUCCESS, JULY 10-(AP)-NATIONALIST CHINA'S~CHIEF U.N. DELEGATE 
TODAY DENOUNCED COMMUNIST NORTH AGGRESSION AGAINST SOUTH KOREA 
AND TOLD THE LITTLE ASSEMBLY THE KOREAN COMMUNIST TACTICS ARE SIMILAR 
TO "SOVIET AGGRESSION" AGAINST CHINA. 

THE DELEGATE, Tebew-dSSANG, SERVED NOTICE HE WOULD ASK THE LITTLE 
ASSEMBLY TO DISCUSS THE CHINESE ISSUE. IT WAS SAID OFF THE ASSEMBLY 
FLOOR THAT HE WOULD SEEK A MEETING LATE IN JULY OR EARLY IN NEXT 
MONTH. THE LITTLE ASSEMBLY MET WITHOUT THE RUSSIANS, WHO HAVE BOY- 
COTTED IT FROM ITS ESTABLISHMENT IN 1948. 

AS TSIANG SPOKE, SOME HIGH DIPLOMATS SAID COMMUNIST CHINA LOST ALL 
CHANCES OF GAINING UNITED NATIONS RECOGNITION WHEN THE COMMUNIST NORTH 
KOREANS ATTACKED THE SOUTH. 

EARLIER A UeN. SPOKESMAN SAID SECRETARY-GENERAL TRYGVE LIE 
HAS NOT CHANGED HIS POSITION ON THE ISSUE OF CHINESE REPRESENTATION. 
LIE FAVORS RECOGNITION OF THE GOVERNMENT EXERCISING EFFECTIVE AUTHORITY 
OVER A COUNTRY. THIS, IN CHINA'S CASE, WOULD MEAN THE RED CHINESE 
REGIME INSTEAD OF THE NATIONALISTS SINCE THE COMMUNISTS CONTROL THE 
CHINESE MAINLAND. 

THE SPOKESMAN ALSO SAID LIE HAS NOT ABANDONED AND WILL NOT ABANDON 
HIS EFFORTS FOR PEACE AS OUTLINED IN HIS 10“POINT MEMORANDUM. LIE HAS 
BEEN CONCENTRATING ON RESTORING PEACE IN KOREA AND THERE HAD BEEN SOME 
INDICATIONS THAT THE WAR HAD SHELVED HIS EFFORTS ON HIS PROGRAM FOR 
PEACE BETWEEN THE EAST AND THE WEST. 

THE SPOKESMAN SAID THAT, ON THE CONTRARY, AFTER PEACE HAS BEEN 
RESTORED IN KOREA BY U.N. ACTION, THE ROLE OF THE U.N. AS A UNIVERSAL 
ORGANIZATION THROUGH WHICH MODERATION AND CONCILIATION SHOULD BE ATTEMP- 
TED WILL BE MORE NECESSARY THAN EVER. | 

JOAO CARLOZ MUNIZ OF BRAZIL, PRESIDENT OF THE LITTLE ASSEMBLY, 
PRAISED PRESIDENT TRUMAN FOR MAKING A HISTORICAL DECISION IN HELPING 
THE U.N. RESIST AGGRESSION. HE SAID THAT WITHOUT THE DEMONSTRATION 
OF AID FROM THE UNITED STATES THE SECURITY COUNCIL RESOLUTIONS AGAINST 
THE NORTH KOREANS STILL WOULD HAVE BEEN WITHOUT ENFORCEMENT. HE SAID 
THE KOREAN CRISIS IS A TURNING POINT IN U.N. HISTORY.

LAKE SUCCESS, JULY 10-(AP)=-A UeN. SPOKESMAN SAID TODAY SECRETARY- 
GENERAL TRYGVE LIE HAS NO INTENTION OF ABANDONING HIS EFFORTS FOR 
PEACE UNDER A 10=POINT MEMORANDUM MADE PUBLIC BEFORE THE_KOREAN 

SIS. 

THE SPOKESMAN SAID LIE IS CONCENTRATING ON THE KOREAN. WAR NOW IN 
AN EFFORT TO RESTORE PEACE AT THE EARLIEST POSSIBLE MOMENT. 

AFTER PEACE HAS BEEN RESTORED, THE SPOKESMAN ADDED, THE ROLE OF 
THE U.N. AS A UNIVERSAL ORGANIZATION THROUGH WHICH MEDIATION AND 
CONCILIATION SHOULD BE ATTEMPTED WILL BE MORE NECESSARY THAN EVER. 

HE SAID ALSO THAT LIE'S POSITION ON THE CHINESE REPRESENTATION 
ISSUE HAS NOT CHANGED. 

THE SECRETARY=GENERAL CIRCULATED LAST FEBRUARY A MEMORANDUM SAYING 
A GOVERNMENT HAVING THE MOST EFFECTIVE AUTHORITY IN A COUNTRY SHOULD 
BE RECOGNIZED AS THE GOVERNMENT OF THAT COUNTRY. THIS WOULD MEAN 
RECOGNITION OF COMMUNIST CHINA SINCE THE COMMUNISTS CONTROL THE 
CHINESE MAINLAND. INDIA HAS SUGGESTED SHE WILL RAISE THE CHINESE 
QUESTION SOON IN THE U.N. BUT OBSERVERS HERE SAID THE CHANCES OF 
SEATING A CHINESE COMMUNIST DELEGATION NOW, WHILE THE UeNe IS FIGHTING 
NORTH KOREAN COMMUNISTS, ARE SLIM. 

LIE IS BUSY DAILY AND OFTEN AT NIGHT ON CONFERENCES ON THE KOREAN 
WAR. AT THE FIRST MEETING OF THE SECURITY COUNCIL AFTER THE CRISIS 
BROKE, ON JUNE 25, LIE SAID IT WAS THE PLAIN DUTY OF THE COUNCIL TO 
TAKE ACTION. 

WHEN THE COUNCIL DID ACT, JOHN M. CHANG, KOREAN AMBASSADOR TO 
WASHINGTON, TOLD A REPORTER THAT THE NORTH KOREANS OUGHT TO BE 
CHASED RIGHT ON BEYOND THE 38TH PARALLEL, WHICH IS THE BOUNDARY 
SEPARATING NORTH AND SOUTH KOREA. 

BUT CHANG WOULD NOT FIND MUCH SUPPORT FOR SUCH A MOVE IN THE 
PRESENT TEMPER OF THE DELEGATES. SOME OF THOSE COUNTRIES BACKING 
THE UeNe ACTION HAVE EXPRESSED DETERMINATION TO DRIVE THE NORTH 
KOREANS BACK ACROSS THE BORDER AND RESTORE PEACE. 

BUT NO ONE IN AUTHORITY HERE HAS CALLED FOR U.Ne FORCES TO PURSUE 
THE NORTH KOREANS BEYOND THE 38TH PARALLEL. INSTEAD, THERE ARE 
SEVERAL DELEGATES WHO HOLD THE VIEW THAT ONCE THE INVASION HAS BEEN 
REPELLED AND PEACE HAS BEEN RESTORED, THERE MIGHT BE A CHANCE FOR 
MEDIATION, BUT NO ONE HAS CALLED FOR THE U.N. FORCES TO KEEP GOING 
ACROSS THE 38TH PARALLEL. :

IT REMAINS TO BE SEEN WHAT IMPACT THE REFUGEES WILL HAVE ON THE 
POLITICAL SITUATION IN WEST GERMANY, WHERE SOCIALISTS AND THE RIGHT 
WING CHRISTIAN DEMOCRATS ARE THE TWO BIG PARTIES. 

IN ELECTION CAMPAIGNING THE REFUGEES CALLED FOR EQUAL SHARING OF 
THE WAR BURDEN IN WEST GERMANY, JOBS FOR UNEMPLOYED REFUGEES, A 
RESETTLEMENT PROGRAM AND RECOGNITION OF OFFICIAL RIGHTS FOR REFUGEES 
WHO FORMERLY HELD PUBLIC OFFICE IN THE EAST. 

THERE ARE NO MARKED LEANINGS AMONG THE REFUGEES, EITHER TO LEFT 
OR RIGHT, EXCEPT THAT THEY ARE ANTI-COMMUNIST,

THE REFUGEE PAETY A DEFINITE VOICE IN THE 69-MEMBER SCHLESWIG- 
HOLSTEIN STATE PARLIAMENT, THE REFUGEES CUT DEEP INTO THE STRENGTH 
OF THE ESTABLISHED PARTIES, ESPECIALLY THE SOCIALISTS WHO HAD DOMINATED 
THE STATE GOVERNMENT SINCE 1947

ASSIGNMENT TO INDOCHINA OF A RESIDENT AMERICAN MILITARY MISSION.

BY TOM LAMBERT ; 
WITH AMERICAN FORCES "IN SOUTH KOREA, JULY 11-CAP)-ONE WEEK AGO TODAY 


UeSe ARMED FORCES WENT INTO ACTION IN THE SOUTH KOREAN WAR AGAINST 
COMMUNISM. THE WEEK HAS BEEN ONE OF AMERICAN WITHDRAWAL AND LOSSES. 
THIS IS NOT TO SAY THAT THE WAR HERE IS LOST--FAR FROM IT. BUT IT 
IS TO SAY THAT FOR ONE WEEK SURPRISINGLY STRONG NORTH KOREAN FORCES 
HAVE MAULED ONE OF THE MOST POWERFUL NATIONS ON EARTH. 
MILITARY SECURITY FORBIDS NAMING THE FRONT LINE AS IT IS TODAY. 
BUT A REVIEW OF GENERAL MACARTHUR'S COMMUNIQUES AND STATEMENTS OF AN 
ADVANCED HEADQUARTERS SPOKESMAN DISCLOSES THAT THE AMERICANS HAVE BEEN 
PUSHED BACK AND BACK SINCE THEY WENT INTO THE LINES. 
THERE ARE VARIOUS REASONS FOR THIS. SOME OF THEM SOUND UNPLEASANTLY 
LIKE THOSE ADVANCED FOR EARLY AMERICAN DEFEAT IN THE LAST WAR. 
WE WERE NOT PREPARED FOR THIS FIGHT. IN FACT IT IS EXTREMELY 
DOUBTFUL THAT WE KNEW THE RED INVASION WAS COMING. ONE MUST ASK IF 
WE KNOW ABOUT AND ARE PREPARED FOR ANY OTHER POSSIBLE COMMUNIST ATTACks. 
WE HAVE NOT YET BEEN ABLE TO MUSTER THE STRENGTH AND WEIGHT WHICH 
GAVE US VICTORY OVER GERMANY AND JAPAN. THIS QUESTIONS THEN ARISES: 
COULD WE MUSTER STRENGTH AND POWER QUICKLY ENOUGH TO SAVE OURSELVES 
IF OUR COUNTRY WERE ATTACKED? 
WE HAVE UNDERESTIMATED THE NORTH KOREANS, AS HAS BEEN, AND WILL BE, 





ADMITTED BY Ue S. SOLDIERS AND GENERALS ALIKE. j 
WE ARE FAST LOSING THE EARLY CONTEMPT WE HAD FOR THE NORTH KOREANS. 
THE WITHDRAWALS AND LOSSES OUT HERE HAVE AFFECTED THE MORALE OF THE 
SOLDIERS WHO, LIKE ALL AMERICANS, HATE TO LOSE A FIGHT. 
IN THEIR OUTCRIES AGAINST WHAT HAS HAPPENED HERE THIS PAST WEEK, 
MEN AND OFFICERS COMPLAINS 


83KX 

OUR FORCE IS NOT STRONG ENOUGH. 

WE ARE OUTNUMBERED. 

THE AIR FORCE HAS LET THEM DOWN BY FAILING TO HALT EVERY RED TANK 
ON KOREA'S ROADS. 

WE ARE BEING COMMITTED IN A PIECEMEAL AND HAPHAZARD FASHION. 

OUR MOUNTED EQUIPMENT IS NOT POWERFUL ENOUGH TO HALT THE 
RICE-PADDY-TREADING, HILL-CLIMBING REDS FROM NORTH KOREA---HALF 
CUFRRILLA BUT WELL TRAINED. 

THIS CAMPAIGN IS IN ITS INFANCY, HOWEVER, AND AS IT DEVELOPS so 
WILL OUR STRENGTH AND POWER. 

EVERYONE HERE IS CONFIDENT THE NORTH KOREANS ARE IN FOR THE JOLT oF 
THEIR LIVES WHEN WE GET SET AND START MOVING NORTH. 

IN THE MEANTIME WE HAVE LOST GROUND WHICH MUST BE RETAKEN---AT A 


COST 
IT BECAME HIGH THE DAY THE FIRST AMERICAN 


AND THE COST IS HIGH. 
SOLDIER WAS KILLED. 

OUR SOLDIERS, GENERALLY SPEAKING, SEEM TO HAVE NO STOMACH FOR 
THIS WAR. THIS IS A PERSONAL OPINION, BUT I DOUBT IF MANY OF THEM 
KNOW THAT IN FIGHTING THE REDS HERE THEY ARE FIGHTING FOR THEMSELVES. 

AN OCCASIONAL SOLDIER MENTIONS RUSSIA AND COMMUNISM, OF COURSE, AND 
SOME OF THEM WONDER IF THE THIRD WORLD WAR HAS STARTED HERE. 

MANY OF THEM THINK, HOWEVER, THE SOUTH KOREANS SHOULD FIGHT THEIR 
oree BATTLE AND SEEMINGLY WOULD CARE LITTLE IF THIS COUNTRY FELL TO THE 
BUT THE AMERICANS ARE LEARNING SOMETHING HERE. THEY ARE LEARNING 
THAT A COMMUNIST ENEMY IS AN IMPLACABLE, DEADLY ENEMY WITH NO 

THOUGHT FOR LIFE. 

A GOOD MANYSOLDIERS OF A HITHERTO OCCUPATION ARMY ARE DEVELOPING 
INTO GOOD COMBAT MEN. THE LIAISON AND COORDINATION THAT LEAD TO 
aay 3 A ARE BEING FORCED UNDER THE MOST TRYING CONDITIONS.

TOKYO,WEDNESDAY, JULY 12-(AP)-ALLIED AIRCRAFT, MEETING THEIR 
FIRST COMMUNIST AIR OPPOSITION IN MORE THAN A WEEK, BOMBED AND 
ETRAFED TARGETS ALONG THE KOREAN BATTLEFRONT WITH "EXCELLENT RESULTS". 
TUESDAY, THE FAR EAST AIR FORCE ANNOUNCED TODAY. 
AFTER TWO DAYS OF POWERFUL HAMMER BLOWS IN SUPPORT OF GROUND 
TROOPS 9 THE TEMPO FELL OFF WITH ONLY 150 COMBAT SORTIES FLOWN DURING 


THIS WAS ABOUT HALF OF MONDAY'S STRIKE TOTAL. 

THE FEAF COMMUNIQUE SAID AMERICAN AND AUSTRALIAN FIGHTERS 
KNOCKED OUT SIX TANKS, WHICH BROUGHT THE TOTAL TO 45 FOR TWO DAYS. 
IT ALSO REPORTED 51 RED TRUCKS AND 12 RAILWAY BOX CARS DESTROYED.

FEAF COMMUNIQUE TEXT (600) 
TOKYO, JULY 11-(AP)-THE TEXT OF A FAR EAST AIR FORCE COMMUNIQUE 
ISSUED TODAY (TIME NOT GIVEN): 
, NEARLY 300 FAR EAST AIR FORCES AND ROYAL AUSTRALIAN AIR FORCE 
AIRCRAFT ROARED OVER THE WESTERN SECTOR OF THE KOREAN FRONT ON JULY 


10 IN THE MOST EXTENSIVE AND DESTRUCTIVE SINGLE DAY OF AIR OPERATIONS 
SINCE THE OFFENSIVE AGAINST THE NORTH KOREANS BEGAN. 

AMERICAN Fe80 JET FIGHTERS, F-82 ALL-WEATHER FIGHTERS, B-26 
LIGHT BOMBERS AND B-29 MEDIUM BOMBERS WERE JOINED BY RAAF MUSTANGS 
IN AN ALL-OUT ATTACK ON COMMUNICATIONS LINES FROM CHONUI NORTH TO 
SUWON AND EAST TO CHONGJU,. 

GOOD FLYING WEATHER WAS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE STEPPED-UP TEMPO OF 
AIR ACTIVITY OVER KOREA AS WELL AS FOR NEW RECORDS IN TERMS OF NORTH 
KOREAN MATERIEL AND GROUND INSTALLATIONS DESTROYED DURING THE DAY, 

B29"S AND Be26"S HIT MANY KEY MILITARY TARGETS IN THE CHONAN- 
PYONGTAEK=SUWON AREA. FULL ASSESSMENT OF THE RESULTS OF 20TH AIR 
FORCE Be29 HIGH ALTITUDE RAIDS COULD NOT BE MADE IMMEDIATELY BUT A 
HIGHWAY BRIDGE AT PYONGTAEK WAS KNOCKED OUT AND REPORTS INDICATED ALL 
ATTACKS ON RAILROAD YARDS, TROOP CONCENTRATIONS, TRAINS, BRIDGES AND 
OTHER TARGETS WERE SUCCESSFULLY CARRIED OUT. 

FIFTH AIR FORCE Be26"S DESTROYED RAILROAD BRIDGES AT CHONAN AND 
PYONGTAEK AS WELL AS THREE HIGHWAY BRIDGES IN THE PYONGTAEK AREA. THE 
CENTER SPAN OF THE EAST BRIDGE IN A THREE BRIDGE GROUP AT CHONAN WAS 
KNOCKED OUT ALONG WITH TRACKAGE AT THE SOUTH END OF THE SAME BRIDGE, 
RAILROAD BRIDGES AT ANSONG, SONGHWAN AND HEITAKU AIRFIELD SOUTHWEST 
OF PYONGTAEK AND A RAILROAD OVERPASS AT SONGHWAN WERE DAMAGED. B-26' 
ALSO HIT A POSSIBLE AMMUNITION DUMP NEAR CHONAN. 

SMALLER NUMBERS OF FIFTH AIR FORCE F-82S TOOK PART IN BOMBING AND 
STRAFING ATTACKS IN THE SAME AREA. TWO 500 POUND BOMBS DROPPED NEAR 
CHONAN CAUSED AN EXPLOSION VIOLENT ENOUGH TO ROCK THE AIRCRAFT AT 
2,500 FEET. DAMAGE WAS CAUSED BY NAPALM (JELLIED GASOLINE FIREBOMBS) 
BOMB DROPS AND STRAFING OF A CONVOY NEAR PYONGTAEK. 

FeSOS FROM THE FIFTH AIR FORCE FLEW THE GREATEST NUMBER OF MISSIONS 
AND TOOK THE HEAVIEST TOLL IN NORTH KOREAN PERSONNEL AND EQUIPMENT, 
NEARLY 200 F-80 SORTIES WERE FLOWN AND VIRTUALLY ALL REPORTED SUCCESS- 
FUL GROUND STRAFING AND ROCKET ATTACKS ON TANKS, CARGO VEHICLES AND : 
GROUND FORCE MATERIEL. ONE BRIDGE, THREE TO FOUR MILES SOUTH OF CHONAN, 
WAS DESTROYED BY FegQ ROCKET FIRE AND TWO OTHER BRIDGES WEST OF CHONAN 
WERE DAMAGED. 

WITH A FEW EXCEPTIONS MISSIONS FLOWN BY FIGHTER AND BOMBER AIRCRAFT 
DURING THE DAY WERE AIMED AT NORTH KOREAN COMMUNICATIONS LINES SOUTE 
FROM SEOUL TO THE BATTLE LINE ON THE WESTERN FRONT. ONLY ONE MISSION, 
AN F-&amp;O STRIKE AT UTCHIN, WAS DIRECTED AT AN EAST COAST TARGET BUT OTHER 
F=80 MISSIONS STRUCK CHECHON AND CHUNGJU IN THE CENTRAL SECTOR.

ADVANCED AMERICAN HEADQUARTERS, KOREA, JULY 11-(AP)-MAYBE YOU'VE 
READ ABOUT HOW WORRIED SOME GI'S CET WHEN THEY SEE WHITE GARBED 
KOREANS SPACED RATHER RECULARLY ON HILLS IDES SURROUNDING AMERICAN 

GI'S SPECULATE THAT THEY ARE GUERRILLAS OR SPIES, BUT AMERICANS WHO 
KNOW KOREANS SAY THEY PROBABLY ARE JUST CIVILIANS TAKING A LOOK AT 

"IF THEY'RE AROUND AND THE ENEMY STARTS CLOSING IN," ONE FIELD 
OFFICER SAID, "I'M GOING TO TELL MY MEN TO LET THEM HAVE IT ALONG WITH 
THE UNIFORMED NORTH KOREAN SOLDIERS." 

THIS IS THE EXPLANATION OFFERED BY THE COMMANDING GENERAL OF 
ADVANCED AMERICAN HEADQUARTERS WHO SPENT CONSIDERABLE TIME HERE IN THE 
EARLY DAYS AFTER WORLD WAR II AND UNDERSTANDS THE KOREANS AS WELL AS 
ANY MAN IN THE ARMY: 

"T THINK THEY ARE JUST FARMERS FROM THE RICE PADDIES BELOW. THEY 
ARE VERY CURIOUS PEOPLE. THEY PICK OUT GRANDSTAND SEATS THAT THEY 
HOPE ARE OUT OF THE WAY AND WATCH FOR SOMETHING TO HAPPEN. 

WE MUST BE CAREFUL WHEN WE OPERATE THAT THEY DO NOT GIVE AWAY OUR 
POSITION BY GATHERING IN A RING AROUND US." 

FOREIGNERS ON THE STREETS OF KOREA ALWAYS GATHER CROWDS WHICH 
SOMETIMES SURROUND THEM SO CLOSELY THEY ACTUALLY HAVE DIFFICULTY 
ear IN WARTIME PATIENCE RUNS THINNER AND ENCIRCLEMENT MIGHT BE

THERE WAS MORE TO THIS EXCLUSIVE BATHROOM INTERVIEW BUT SUBSEQUENT

COOPERATION UP AND DOWN THE LINE BY MEN OF THE ARMED FORCES ENABLE

FOR ANY ONE DAY. AND IF THE GENERAL*S READINESS TO SAY THE MARCH

A MESSAGE RUNNER LEFT IMMEDIATELY FOR AN ADVANCED COOMMAND POST. 
FROM A HIGH RIDGE AMERICAN ARTILLERY SHELLS COULD BE SEEN PLUNKING 
INTO NORTH KOREAN POSITIONS. MACHINEGUN BULLETS, ROCKETS AND HOWITZER 
SHELLS ALSO WHISTLED ACROSS THE RIVER BED AND A VILLAGE AHEAD. RETURN 
FIRE WAS NOT QUITE AS INTENSE BUT ENEMY FOOT SOLDIERS WERE SEEN 
ADVANCING BY TWOS AND THREES, TAKING COVER EVERY FEW FEET. 

THEN THREE AMERICAN PLANES ZOOMED DOWN FROM THE CLOUDS AND SPAT 
OUT BULLETS ONLY YARDS FROM WHERE AMERICAN SOLDIERS WERE DUG IN 


ASSEX : 

WHETHER ENEMY TROOPS WERE THAT CLOSE ALONG THE ROAD, RAILROAD 
AND RIVER WHICH PASSED BETWEEN HIGH VALLEY SLOPES AT THAT POINT, OR 
WHETHER THE STRAFING WAS MISDIRECTED, WAS UNKNOWN. ONLY ONE PASs BY 
THE JETS WAS MADE BUT AN AERIAL SHOW DURING THE AFTERNOON WAS 
SPECTACULAR AND MUCH SAFER FOR U. S» PERSONNEL. 

TWELVE AMERICAN AND AUSTRALIAN PLANES CIRCLED THE TARGET AREA 
FOR MORE THAN A HALF HOUR SPEWING ROCKETS AND MACHINEGUN BULLETS. 
WHAT AN OBSERVER SAID WAS A TANK WAS SEEN TO GO UP IN FLAME AND A 
SCORE OF FIRES SENT DENSE SMOKE SKYWARD FROM THE VILLAGE ABOUT 
3,500 YARDS AWAY. 

AN AMERICAN FIGHTING UNIT HAD BEEN OUTFLANKED BY INFILTRATION 
TROOPS AND AN ARMY CAPTAIN TOLD MEt "WE ARE SENDING MORE TROOPS 

NEW CONTACT. 

SEVERAL U.S. TANKS RATTLED UP THE ROAD IN SUPPORT OF THE 

FOOT SOLDIERS. WE WATCHED THEM ALL THE WAY AND THEY MADE IT, THANKS 
Z , 

ENEMY BURSTS BECAME LESS FREQUENT AND WE MADE OUR WAY DOWN TO 

THE ROAD. IT WAS TIME TO RETURN TO HEADQUARTERS AND POUND OUT THE 


STORY. 
HITCH HIKING WAS THE ONLY MEANS OF TRAVEL. A BATTLEWORN TANK ONLY 


MINUTES BEFORE EXCHANGING FIRE WITH THE ENEMY, RUMBLED UP. IT 

4 UP THE HITCH HIKER AND DEPOSITED HIM EIGHT MILES CLOSER TO THE 

SOMEWHERE ALONG THE LINE AT A COMMAND POST_AN OFFICER BURST IN 

AND RELATED DETAILS OF WHAT WAS DESCRIBED AS THE FIRST KNOWN ATROCITY 

OF THE WAR INVOLVING AMERICANS. MEN WHO HAD SURRENDERED HAD BEEN SHOT 
i THE HEAD AND THEIR BODIES FOUND WITH THEIR HANDS TIED BEHIND 


EM. 
RESUMING HITCH HIKING, THE NEXT LIFT WAS IN A WEAPON CARRIER WHERE 
CAPT RICHARD E.KOTCH, OF 401 JOHNSON ST., LITTLE ROCK, ARKey AN 
ORDNANCE MAINTENANCE EXPERT AND COMMERCIAL PILOT, EXPLAINED SUCH THINGS 
AS NAPALM, THE STUFF THAT MAKES HIT TANKS TOO HOT TO LIVE IN. 
THIS RIDE STOPPED AT AN AIRSTRIP WHERE 1ST LT. KENNETH GLOVER OF 
DE SMET, SoD, AGREED TO TAKE A PASSENGER ON HIS NEXT OBSERVATION 
FLIGHT.’ IT WAS OVER THE SAME TERRITORY WHERE THE ARTILLERY BATTLE, 
TROOP ADVANCE, TANK ENGAGEMENT, THE ALLEGED ATROCITY AND AIR 
STRIKES HAD OCCURRED. 
FOR MORE THAN AN HOUR WE CRUISED AT 125 MILES AN HOUR OVER THE 
AREA WHILE FOUR JETS STRUCK NEW TARGETS. WE LISTENED IN ON 
CONVERSATIONS BETWEEN THE GROUND AND FIGHTING PLANES AND DIRECTING 


PLANES SUCH AS OURS. 


IN THERE SMITH OF (216 STUTSON ST.) 


AGE : 

THE ROCKETS FROM THE SPEEDY JETS KNOCKED OUT FIVE TANKS WHILE WE 
WATCHED THEM START OVER DESIGNATED AREAS. WE SAW THE FLAMES AND THE 
COLUMNS OF SMOKE. WE SAW TRACER BULLETS STEAM DOWNWARD, THE PLANES 
FOLLOWING THEM ALMOST TO THE GROUND, THEN VEERING UPWARD SHARPLY, 
CIRCLING AND GOING IN AGAIN. 

AFTER 90 MINUTES WE DROPPED DOWN AT AN AIRSTRIP. ONE AMERICAN 
L-5 AND ONE SOUTH KOREAN L-5 (OBSERVATION PLANES) HAD BEEN LOST DURING 
THE DAY. WHEN ANY PLANES BASED ELSEWHERE WENT DOWN IT WAS KNOWN ONLY 
BY THEIR HOME BASES--NO ONE REPORTED SEEING ANY CRASH. 

THE COMMANDING GENERAL'S WORDS WERE 15 HOURS AND MANY EXPERIENCES 
OLD WHEN THESE WORDS FINALLY WERE PUT ON PAPER. PERHAPS THE WEIGHED 
OPINION OF AN ORDINARY GI MIGHT BE BEST MENTIONED HERE. 

CPL. JOSEPH WeKIRK, 23, WHOSE PARENTS LIVE IN BEAUMONT, TEX., 

AND WHO SHARED A FOXHOLE ON THE MOUNTAINSIDE DURING THE DAYTIME 


WAR SHOW SAID: 
"WE WILL HAVE THIS WAR CLEANED UP BEFORE THE FIRST OF AUGUST--I 


HOPE."

SALAH EDDIN TODAY REITERATED APPROVAL OF THE UeNe’S DENUNCIATION OF 
NORTH KOREAN AGGRESSION, BUT RESTATED EGYPTIAN REASONS FOR REFRAINING 
FROM SUPPORT OF UNITED NATIONS MILITARY ACTION, 

HE SAID THE UNITED NATIONS HAD AN "EASYGOING ATTITUDE AND EVEN 
TAKES DECISIONS AT HELPING AGGRESSORS® IN THE MIDDLE EAST AND BIG 
"IMPERIALISTIC*® POWERS TAKE THE SAME ATTITUDE. HE DID NOT MENTION 
PALESTINE IN THIS CONNECTION, BUT IT SEEMED PLAIN THAT EGYPT IS NOT 
TAKING PART IN THE U.N. CAMPAIGN IN KOREA BECAUSE SHE STILL IS BITTER 
OVER THE UNITED NATIONS STAND ON ISRAEL. 

OBSERVERS FELT THAT SALAH EDDIN, IN EXPRESSING HOPE FOR AN 
ANTI-COMMUNIST SUCCESS IN KOREA, HAD GONE ABOUT AS FAR AS HE COULD IN 
PULLING BACK INTO THE WESTERN CAMP WITHOUT OFFENDING NATIONALISTIC 
EGYPTIAN OPINION, 

EGYPT WAS LEFT ALMOST ALONE WHEN THE OTHER SIX STATES IN THE

TOKYO,THURSDAY, JULY 13-(AP)-OUTNUMBERED AND OUTGUNNED AMERICAN 
TROOPS, HAMMERED BACK SOUTH OF THE KUM RIVER, BRACED TODAY FOR THE NEXT 
NORTH KOREAN TANK-LED ASSAULT. FRONTLINE REPORTS SAID THE AMERICANS 
WERE “WELL PLACED" IN NEW DEFENSE POSITIONS OF THEIR OWN CHOOSING. 

A GALLANT REARGUARD ACTION SLOWED THE COMMUNIST OFFENSIVE UNTIL 
THE AMERICANS MADE THEIR WAY ACROSS THE LAST RIVER BARRIER BEFORE 
TAEJON IN A DAYLIGHT RETREAT, DESCRIBED AS "EFFICIENTLY" CARRIED OUT.

WITH UeSe FORCES IN KOREA, JULY 12-(AP)=TANK-LED NORTH KOREAN 
TROOPS, PLUNGING SOUTHWARD UNDER A RED MORTAR AND ARTILLERY BARRAGE, 
SMASHED INTO UeSs FORCES TODAY AND DROVE THEM FRON CHOCHIWON. 

THE COMMUNISTS BEGAN THEIR ASSAULT ON THE CITY, EIGHT AIR MILES 
NORTH OF THE KUM RIVER, IN MID-MORNING--A DEPARTURE FROM THEIR USUAL 
DAWN OFFENSIVE. 

CIN TOKYO, GENERAL MACARTHUR ANNOUNCED THE AMERICANS HAD PULLED 
BACK TO PREPARED POSITIONS SOUTH OF THE KUM.) 

BUT THE REMAINDER OF THE RED ATTACK WAS IN THE NoW FAMILIAR 
AND DEADLY PATTERN--FLANKING AND INFILTRATION. THE REDS INFILTRATED 
HEAVILY ALONG THE LEFT FLANK OF THE AMERICAN POSITIONS, EXPOSING 
THE CITY TO ATTACK. 

THE NORTHERN INVADERS OPENED UP WITH MORTARS AND ARTILLERY. 

THEIR SHELLS WALKED DOWN THE HIGHWAY LEADING INTO CHOCHIWON JUST 


AHEAD OF THE RED INFANTRY. 

BY 1230 PeMe (10230 PeMe, EoSeTe, TUESDAY) THEY HAD THE CITY 
20, AIR MILES NORTH OF THE KEY CENTER OF TAEJON, UNDER A BLISTERING 

THE REDS FLANKED ONE MAJOR AMERICAN UNIT COMMAND \POST \AND - 
SHELLED IT FROM THE CITY. nf

THEY MINGLED WITH REFUGEES CLOGGING THE ROADS. THESE SOUTH KOREAN 
CIVILIANS HAD TAKEN TO THE ROADS EARLIER IN THE MORNING, APPARENTLY 
SENSING ANOTHER COMMUNIST THRUST. 

UeSe GROUND FORCES THUS WENT INTO THEIR SECOND WEEK OF THE 
KOREAN WAR AS THEY BEGAN IT--RETREATING. THEIR CASUALTIES IN THE 
CHOCHIWON BATTLE WERE NOT DISCLOSED. PRESUMABLY THEY WERE HEAVY. 

REPORTS FROM THE BATTLE LINE SAID THE REDS AGAIN WERE USING THE 
RUSSIAN-BUILT TANKS WHICH SPEARHEADED THEIR INVASION OF SOUTH KOREA, 
SHATTERED THE SOUTH KOREAN ARMY IN THE FIRST SHOCK OF BATTLE, AND 
FORCED THE AMERICANS STEADILY BACK IN A GAMELY-FOUGHT DELAYING 


ACTION.

WALKED ITS EMPTY STREETS.

IF BY A GIANT'S HEEL.

WITH AMERICAN FORCES IN KOREA, JULY 12-(AP)-A BITTER, BEATEN LITTLE 
BAND OF GI'S SPRAWLED IN EXHAUSTION ON A SUNNY KOREAN HILLSIDE THIS 
AFTERNOON--WEARY SURVIVORS OF ONE OF THE MOST SAVAGE BATTLES FOUGHT 
BY AMERICANS IN THE KOREAN WAR. 

THEIR BITTERNESS WAS MORE PRONOUNCED THAN THEIR EXHAUSTION, WHICH 
WAS ALMOST COMPLETE. THEY TALKED OF ENCIRCLEMENTS AND INFILTRATIONS. 
A GRIMY, BEWHISKERED, BLOODSHOT-EYED OFFICER GRITTED HIS TEETH: 

"YOU DON'T FIGHT TWO TANK EQUIPPED DIVISIONS WITH .30 CALIBER 
CARBINES. I NEVER SAW SUCH A USELESS DAMNED WAR IN ALL MY LIFE.” 

BITTER THOUGH THEY WERE, THIS GI BAND HAD FOUGHT A GALLANT 
DELAYING ACTION AGAINST TREMENDOUS ODDS. 

TWO DAYS AGO THIS HANDFUL OF SOLDIERS WAS PART OF A SIZEABLE UNIT. 
IN A MORNING-LONG BATTLE WITH NORTH KOREAN TANKS AND TROOPS YESTERDAY 
THEY WERE WHITTLED DOWN. | 

MANY OF THE ORIGINAL GROUP STILL ARE IN THE HILLS AFTER A PLUNGING 
RISH FROM THEIR ENCIRCLED POSITIONS. BUT MANY OF THEM=-WOUNDED AND 
DEAD ALIKE--ARE IN NORTH KOREANS HANDS OR TERRITORYs ©... 

THE BATTLE BEGAN TWO DAYS AGO WHEN THE UNIT PUSHED. OFF TO ATTACK 
THE REDS WHO WERE BATTERING ANOTHER AMERICAN OUTFIT. THE UNIT MOVED UP

BUT THE ALERT REDS WHO HAD BEEN MORTARING THE UNIT'S POSITION HAD A

SNEAKED INTO THE AMERICAN LINE. WHEN THE GI's RETURNED TO THEIR 
ORIGINAL POSITION THEY HAD TO FIGHT COMMUNISTS IN THE DARK FOR 
THEIR OWN FOXHOLES. 

THE RED ASSAULT BEGAN YESTERDAY AT ABOUT 5230 A.M. THE 
COMMUNISTS RODE GHOSTLIKE OUT OF A DEEP GROUND FOG. THEIR FIRST 
SHOTS CLIPPED THE ECHOES OF A BUGLE CALL WHICH SIGNALLED THEIR ATTACK. 

THE FOG SHROUDED EVERYTHING BUT THE FLASHES OF THEIR AUTOMATIC 
WEAPONS AS THE REDS SWEPT IN. 

THE REDS WERE IN FRONT, TO THE LEFT AND RIGHT AND AT THE REAR.

AS FOR ECONOMY, THE TEXAN WENT ON? 

"FAR MORE DOLLARS ARE BEING LOST IN SOUTH KOREA THAN ALL THE DOLLARS

CONFIDENCE WAS UNJUSTIFIED, OUR EMPHASIS WAS WRONG."

IS AT THIS MOMENT." yi 4 

LEGISLATORS IN BOTH HOUSES OF CONGRESS REFLECTED GROWING CONCERN 
OVER THE SITUATION IN KOREA AND WHAT IT MAY MEAN FOR THE FUTURE.

THIS WOULD NOT BE A STEP TOWARD WORLD WAR, HE SAID, BUT WOULD BE A 
MOVE "TO QUARANTINE THOSE WHO ARE COURTING WAR." 

IN A SENATE SPEECH, MCCARRAN CALLED THE SOVIET BLOC REGIMES "AN

"LEFT'S USE EVERYTHING WE CAN TO END THIS WAR NOW."

WITH ONE ARM TIED BEHIND THEIR BACKS--YET THAT IS WHAT IS HAPPENING," 
JOHNSON TOLD THE SENATE.

BY WAYNE.OLIVER 

NEW YORK, JULY 12-(AP)-ONE OF THE NATION'S MOST SPECTACULAR NEW 
INDUSTRIES, TELEVISION, WOULD BE.AMONG THE FIRST AFFECTED BY WAR OR A 
SPEED-UPIA.OUR ” PROGRAM. 

THAT'S BECAUS THE CLOSE KINSHIP OF TELEVISION, A MARVEL OF HOME 
ENTERTAINMENT, TO THE HUNDREDS OF CONTROL DEVICES WHICH GIVE OUR MODERN 
WEAPONS THEIR’ DEADLINESS--AS WELL AS TO RADAR AND MILITARY 
COMMUNICATIONS. 

ALL ARE ELECTRONICS DEVICES AND THE TELEVISION AND RADIO INDUSTRY 
IS THE ELECTRONICS INDUSTRY. IF IT IS CALLED UPON BY THE GOVERNMENT 
TO MAKE A LOT MORE OF THESE DEVICES, THE INDUSTRY WILL HAVE TO MAKE 
FEWER TELEVISION AND RADIO SETS AND’ LESS BROADCASTING EQUIPMENT. 

HOWEVER, MANUFACTURERS SAY THAT SO FAR THERE HAS BEEN NO INCREASE 
IN GOVERNMENT DEMANDS ON THEIR FACILITIES. THEY EMPHASIZE THERE'S 
NO CAUSE FOR PUBLIC ALARM OVER THE PROSPECTS OF SHORTAGES OR A SHUT- 
DOWN OF CIVILIAN PRODUCTION. 

IN FACT, ONE HIGHLY PLACED INDUSTRY SOURCE EXPRESSED DOUBT THE 
GOVERNMENT WOULD COMPLETELY SUSPEND CIVILIAN TELEVISION PRODUCTION IN

NIGHT LEAD FRENCH (450) 
BY CARL HARTMAN 

PARIS, JULY 12-C€AP)=PREMIER RENE PLEVEN ANNOUNCED THE MAKEUP OF A 
NEW CABINET TONIGHT AND THE END OF FRANCE'S 18=-DAY GOVERNMENT CRISIS 
SEEMED. ASSURED. 

PLEVEN IS A RIGHTIST. A MEMBER OF THE SMALL DEMOCRATIC AND SOCIAL= 
IST UNION OF RESISTANCE (UDSR) AND BEEN CONSIDERED FRIENDLY TO GEN. 
CHARLES DE GAULLE, HE WILL HEAD A CABINET MADE UP OF SOCIALISTS, RADICAL 
SOCIALISTS AND POPULAR REPUBLICANS, PLUS THREE INDEPENDENTS AND TWO 
MEMBERS OF HIS OWN GROUP, 

THIS IS ESSENTIALLY THE SAME COMBINATION OF CENTER PARTIES WHICH RULED 
nsdn THROUGH RECENT YEARS UNTIL LAST FEBRUARY, WHEN THE SOCIALISTS 
WITHDREW. 

THE RETURN OF THE SOCIALISTS TO THE CABINET APPEARED TO ASSURE 


BS 


PLEVEN THE SUPPORT OF THEIR POWERFUL BLOCK OF 98 VOTES WHEN HE GOES 
BEFORE THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY TOMORROW TO SEEK PARLIAMENTARY APPROVAL. 

FOREIGN MINISTER ROBERT SCHUMAN, A POPULAR REPUBLICAN, AND INTERIOR 
MINISTER HENRI QUEUILLE, A RADICAL SOCIALIST, KEEP THEIR POSTS IN 
THE NEW GOVERNMENT. SCHUMAN IS SPONSOR OF THE FRENCH PLAN TO POOL 
WESTERN EUROPE'S COAL AND STEEL. : 

GEORGES BIDAULT, WHOSE CABINET FELL JUNE 24 ON THE ISSUE OF SALARY 
INCREASES FOR GOVERNMENT EMPLOYES, IS NOT IN THE NEW CABINET. 

BUT THIS CATHOLIC LEFT-OF-CENTER MRP (POPULAR REPUBLICANS) CONTRI- 
BUTED THE MAN TO RUN AN IMPORTANT NEW JOB. HE IS JEAN LETOURNEAU, 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR THE ASSOCIATED STATES OF INDOCHINA. LETOURNEAU 
TAKES INDOCHINA AWAY FROM THE CONSERVATIVE-MINDED OVERSEAS MINISTRY 
AND THE RESULT MAY BE A NEW POLITICAL DEAL FOR THOS COMMUNIST-THREATENED 
STATES. 

QUEUILLE'S RIGHT=OF=CENTER RADICAL SOCIALISTS ALSO ARE REPRESENTED 
BY PAUL GIACOBBI, A RECENT FOLLOWER OF GEN. DE GAULLE, WHO HOLDS A NEW 
MINISTRY WITHOUT PORTFOLIO. | 

SOCIALIST ENMITY TOWARD BIDAULT AND GIACOBBI WRECKED A CABINET WHICH 
QUEUILLE PUT TOGETHER 12 DAYS AGO, BUT SOCIALIST OBJECTIONS TO GIACOBBI 
WERE NOW UNDERSTOOD TO BE OVERCOME. | 

THE CHIEF SOCIALISTS ENTERING THE GOVERNMENT ARE JULES MOCH, FORMER 
STRONG MAN MINISTER OF INTERIOR WHO TAKES PLEVEN'S OLD JOB OF 
DEFENSE MINISTER$ AND GUY MOLLET, SOCIALIST SECRETARY-GENERAL, WHO IS 
TO BE MINISTER OF STATE FOR THE AFFAIRS OF THE COUNCIL OF EUROPE. 


B7 (Q) 

THE SOCIALISTS ALSO WERE GIVEN CONTROL OF THE EDUCATION MINISTRY, 
WHERE THEY HAVE BEEN AT ODDS WITH THE POPULAR REPUBLICANS. 
PIERRE-OLIVIER LAPIE GOT THE POST. 

THE POLITICAL COMPLEXION OF THE CABINET RESEMBLED THAT FORMED BY 
BIDAULT LAST OCTOBER. PLEVEN'S TEAM, LIKE BIDAULT'S, INCLUDES SIX 
POPULAR REPUBLICANS AND FIVE SOCIALISTS, BUT TAKES IN FOUR RADICALS 
WHERE THERE WERE THREE. | Nii 4 : 
BECAUSE PLEVEN HEADS IT, INSTEAD OF BIDAULT, FRENCH EXPERTS 
LABELLED IT SLIGHTLY MORE TO THE RIGHT.

UP NEAR THE BERING SEA COAST AS AN AID TO THE ALASKA SCOUTS IN THEIR 
COAST-WATCHING JOB. 
COL. JOSEPH ALEXANDER, CHIEF OF THE TERRITORY'S NATIONAL GUARD, 
SAID TODAY THE HANGAR FOR’ SMALL SCOUT PLANES IS BEINC BUILT AT 
BETHEL, ON THE KUSKOKWIM RIVER. THE AIRPLANES WILL BE USED IN 
SUPPORT OF ESKIMO BATTALIONS WHICH ARE BEING OUTFITTED To ACT AS 
THE "EYES AND EARS" OF THE MILITARY ALONG THE DESOLATE BERING COAST. 
MOST OF THE SCOUTS ARE HUNTERS, TRAPPERS, FISHERMEN AND GUIDES 
WHO KNOW THE BARREN COUNTRYSIDE WELL. 
A SIMILAR OUTFIT OF ALASKANS BECAME FAMED IN 
WORLD WAR II AS "CASTNER'S CUTTHROATS® FOR THEIR ACTIVITIES ALONG 
THE COAST AND IN THE ALEUTIANS.«

NIGHT LEAD ACHESON-YUGOSLAV (650) 

BY JOHN MeHIGHTOWER 

WA TON, JULY 12=(AP)-IN THE ROUNDABOUT LANGUAGE OF DIPLOMACY, 
SECRE OF STATE. ACHESON GAVE THE RUSSIANS TWO WARNINGS TODAY: 

1. ANY FURTHER AGGRESSION IN THE WORLD=&lt;-SUCH AS A SOVIET SATELLITE 
ATTEMPT TO OVERRUN YUGOSLAVIA--WILL BE VIEWED WITH THE UTMOST SERIOUS- 
NESS BY THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT. ACHESON CAREFULLY REFRAINED FROM 
SAYING AT A NEWS CONFERENCE WHAT THE UNITED STATES WOULD DO, THOUGH 
HIS WORDS LEFT THE IMPRESSION IT WOULD REACT VIGOROUSLY. 

2e COMMENTING ON COMMUNIST PROPAGANDA AGAINST THE USE OF ATOM BOMBS, 
ACHESON SAID "THE REAL CRIME AGAINST HUMANITY IS AGGRESSION” AND THE 
WEAPONS USED ARE QUITE INCIDENTAL. 

AGAIN, HE DIDN'T PUT IT INTO WORDS. BUT WHAT HE SEEMED TO IMPLY 
WAS THIS$ THAT IF THE UNITED STATES WERE TO BECOME INVOLVED IN A 
MAJOR WAR AND AMERICAN LEADERS DECIDED THE ATOM BOMB SHOULD BE USED TO 
SAVE THE FREE WORLD FROM AGGRESSORS,. NO AMOUNT OF RUSSIAN PROPAGANDA 
WOULD CHANGE THE DECISION. 

THOUGH THE WARNINGS WERE PUT INDIRECTLY, INQUIRY AT THE STATE DEPART 
MENT LEFT NO DOUBT THAT THEY WERE INTENDED FOR THE ATTENTION OF THE 
KREMLIN AND HAD BEEN MOST CAREFULLY CONSIDERED BEFORE ACHESON WENT INTO 
HIS NEWS CONFERENCE. 

THE LATEST OF A SERIES OF REPORTS ON THE SOVIET COMMUNIST THREAT TO 
YUGOSLAVIA CAME TODAY IN PRESS DISPATCHES QUOTING THE OFFICIAL COMMU- 
NIST PARTY PAPER IN BELGRADE. THE PAPER SAID THAT BULGARIAN MOTORIZED 





UNITS WERE HEADING TOWARD THE YUGOSLAV BORDER WITH COMBAT EQUIPMENT. 
THERE HAVE BEEN NUMEROUS REPORTS OF BULGARIAN TROOP CONCENTRATIONS 
ALONG THE YUGOSLAV BORDER IN THE LAST TWO OR THREE MONTHS. 


STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIALS SAY IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO TELL WHETHER THESE 


ALLEGED MOVEMENTS BY SOVIET SATELLITE FORCES ARE PRELIMINARY TO AN 


ATTACK ON YUGOSLAVIA OR ARE SIMPLY MANEUVERS DESIGNED TO KEEP YUGOSLAVIA 


AND THE NON-COMMUNIST WORLD IN A STATE OF UNEASINESS. 

IN THE PAST THE TENDENCY HERE HAS BEEN TO DISCOUNT THE DANGER OF 
AN ACTUAL ATTACK ON THE GROUND THAT THE RUSSIANS PROBABLY WOULD NOT 
WANT TO START SERIOUS TROUBLE AT THIS TIME. HOWEVER, SINCE THE KOREAN 
COMMUNIST INVASION OF SOUTH KOREA OFFICIAL WASHINGTON TAKES ALL SUCH 
REPORTS MORE SERIOUSLY. 

IT WAS AGAINST THIS BACKGROUND THAT ACHESON PREPARED TO ANSWER ANY 
QUESTIONS WHICH MIGHT BE ASKED ABOUT THE NEWS REPORTS OF POSSIBLE 
DANGER TO YUGOSLAVIAe HE FIRST SAID THAT HE HAD SEEN THE REPORTS IN 
THE PRESS AND REMARKED THAT IN THE TENSION OF THE WORLD TODAY THERE 
ARE LIKELY TO BE MANY SUCH REPORTS. od

M

CONTROL AND NAVIGATION,

ABOUT AS A DUAL WEAPONS AND POWER PRODUCER UNLESS THE NEED FOR 

NUCLEAR WEAPONS DISAPPEARS .« 

THERE SEEMED A STRONG DEGREE OF DOUBT TO DReWEINBERG THAT ATOMIC 
POWER FOR PEACEFUL USES ALONE WOULD EVER BE DEVELOPED THROUGH PRIVATE 
CAPITAL--BECAUSE OF THE DIFFICULTY AND COST OF DOING THE JOB. 

"EVEN NOW, MORE THAN 10 YEARS SINCE THE DISCOVERY OF NUCLEAR

THE PROBLEM THEN WOULD BE HOW TO PILE A HUGE LOAD OF MUNITIONS 
ORDERS ON THE STEEL, AUTO AND OTHER BASIC INDUSTRIES, WHICH ALREADY 
ARE RUNNING AT OR NEAR CAPACITY IN FILLING THE BOOM DEMANDS OF A 
PROSPEROUS CIVILIAN ECONOMY. 

TO ALLOCATE METALS, EITHER BY VOLUNTARY OR MANDATORY MEASURES 
WOULD BE TO RUN THE RISK OF GREY MARKETS, HOARDING AND SPECULATION; 
ALSO, THE PRICE OF SUBSTITUTE MATERIALS WOULD RISE. THIS, IN TURN, 
WOULD CREATE DEMANDS FOR PRICE CONTROL, THEN FOR WAGE CONTROL TO 
HELP HOLD THE PRICE LINE, AND FINALLY FOR MANPOWER CONTROL TO DIs- 
COURAGE WORKERS FROM LEAVING ESSENTIAL INDUSTRIES. 

SUCH CYCLES WERE TYPICAL OF WORLD WAR II EXPERIENCE, AND ARE 
SAID TO UNDERLY THE REASONING THAT IT WOULD BE BETTER FOR THE Gov- 
ERNMENT TO WAIT, IF POSSIBLE, UNTIL MILITARY NEEDS HAVE CRYSTALIZED 
BEFORE PUSHING AHEAD WITH A REQUEST FOR CONTROL LEGISLATION. 

SUMMING UP, OFFICIALS SAID MReTRUMAN HAS THREE CHOICES, IF HE 
FINALLY COMES’TO THE DECISION THAT CONTROL POWERS ARE INEVITABLE. 


THESE ARE? i) 4 
FIRST, TO SEEK EACH PIECE OF LEGISLATION AS IT BECOMES- NECES- 

SARY. THIS, IT IS AGREED» WOULD BE LESS DISRUPTIVE IMMEDIATELY TO 

BUSINESS AND FAR LESS LIKELY TO START A PANICKY BUYING AND HOARDING 


RUSH AMONG CONSUMERS--BUT IT IS SEEN AS THE LEAST EFFECTIVE SYSTEM. 


A11 WX 
SECOND » TO TAKE THE BULL BY THE HORNS AND SEEK QUICK CONTROLS 
OF EVERY TYPE WHICH MIGHT PROVE NEEDED FOR A LONG AND COSTLY EFFORT. 

THIRD, TO SEEK “STANDBY" AUTHORITY PROVIDING ALL THE POWERS WHICH 
MIGHT BE NEEDED, WITH THE UNDERSTANDING THAT THEY WOULD BE BROUGHT 
INTO PLAY ONLY AS CONDITIONS WARRANTED. 

THE LAST ALTERNATIVE WAS THE ONE ENVISAGED BY NSRB IN PREPARING 
THE PROPOSED EMERGENCY MOBILIZATION ACT, WHICH HAS BEEN UNDER CONSTANT 
REVISION. THIS 20-TITLE BILL, OFFICIALS HAVE STATED, WOULD NOT BE 
INVOKED EXCEPT UPON THE DECLARATION OF A NATIONAL EMERGENCY. ITS 
DETAILED CONTENTS HAVE NEVER BEEN REVEALED. 

THERE IS CONSIDERABLE OPPOSITION TO ANY REQUEST FOR STANDBY POWERS 
AT THE PRESENT TIME 9 ON GROUNDS THAT SUCH A MOVE MIGHT SPUR BUYING, 
THUS CREATING THE VERY SHORTAGES THE LEGISLATION WOULD BE INTENDED 
TO AVOID.

_ WASHINGTON, JULY 13-(AP)-RUSSIA IS BELIEVED TO HAVE AN ASSORTED 
COLLECTION OF “ABOUT 800 NAVAL CRAFT DEPLOYED NEAR THE KOREAN WAR 
AREA=-INCLUDING BETWEEN 70 AND 80 SUBMARINES. 

NAVAL SOURCES HERE FIGURE THAT PERHAPS A THIRD OF THIS SCHOOL 
OF SUBMARINES ARE TEE NEW XXI SNORKELS. 

ALTHOUGH THE 800 TOTAL ESTIMATE IS NUMERICALLY BIG, THERE IS NO 
PRESENT EVIDENCE THAT IT COMPRISES ANYTHING LIKE A BALANCED NAVAL 
FORCE. THOSE STUDYING THE SITUATION BELIEVE MANY OF THESE VESSELS ARE 
SMALL CRAFT OF VARIOUS TYPES AND THAT CERTAINLY NOTHING BIGGER THAN 
CRUISERS ARE IN THE ARFA. 

SO FAR AS CAN BE DETERMINED, THE RUSSIAN NAVY STILL POSSESSES NO 
AIRCRAFT CARRIERS. 
ONE UNKNOWN FAVTOR SEEMS TO BE HOW MANY OF THE SMALLER SOVIET 
VESSELS MAY BE LANDING CRAFT OR TYPES THAT COULD BE USED IN EMERGENCY 
FOR AN AMPHIBIOUS OPERATION. 

THE PRESENCE IN TEE FAR EAST OF ANY SIZEABLE NUMBER OF LANDING CRAFT 
COULD BE OF GRAVE CONCERN TO AMERICAN FORCES. THEY COULD BE USED TO 
PROVIDE AN AMPHIBIOUS "LIFT" FOR NORTH KOREAN FLANKING OPERATIONS 
DOWN THE SOUTH KOREAN COAST LINES. OR THEY MIGHT SOME DAY BE USED 
IN AN ATTEMPTED OPERATION AGAINST THE AMERICAN DEFENSE BASTION IN 
JAPAN, SHOULD RUSSIA AND THE UNITED STATES FALL INTO GLOVES-OFF WAR. 

HOWEVER, IT IS THE RUSSIAN SUBMARINE FORCE THAT IS DRAWING MOST 
UeS.s ATTENTION. 

AS DEPLOYED, THE RED SUB FLEET IN THE FAR EAST SEEMS TO HAVE AS 
ITS MAIN JOB THE POTENTIAL DUTY OF CUTTING THE ASIATIC-INDONFS TIAN 
LIFELINE ALONG WHICH THE UNITED STATES WOULD SEND HELP IN EVENT OF 
GENERAL WAR IN THE ORIENT. JUL 7 4 ) 

AN ALMOST EQUALLY IMPORTANT MISSION IS TO CARRY ON REGONNAISSANCE 
OF AMERICAN AND BRITISH NAVAL SHIP, TRANSPORT SHIP AND AIR MOVEMENT IN 
THE WESTERN PACIFIC AND THE INLAND SEAS BORDERING EASTERN ASTA. 

IF THERE HAVE BEEN ANY SIGHTINGS OF SUSPICIOUS ACTIONS BY RUSSIAN 
SUBMARINES IN THOSE WATERS, THE PENTAGON HAS KEPT IT SECRET.~ 

THE RED NAVY APPARENTLY IS BASING ITS FAR EAST SUBMARINE FLEET AT 
A NUMBER OF PORTS, RATHER THAN A FEW MAJOR PORTS, IN THE SOVIET- 
CONTROLLED AREAS. 

THE REASON FOR THIS MAY NOT BE DICTATED ENTIRELY BY STRATECY. 
THE DISPERSAL PROBABLY IS CAUSED IN PART BY THE FACT THAT HARBOR 
FACILITIES ARE LIMITED AT ANY ONE PORT.

BY ALEX SINGLETON 

BELGRADE YUGOSLAVIA, JULY 13-(AP)-YUGOSLAV LEADERS APPEAR CONVINCED 
THIS NATION HAS TAKEN ALL POSSIBLE PRECAUTIONS AGAINST. THE CHANCE IT 
MAY BE MARKED NEXT ON A RUSSIAN-SELECTED HIT PARADE OF CONQUEST. 

PREMIER MARSHAL..TITO WAS AT HIS SUMMER RESORT ISLAND OF BRIONI, IN 
THE ADRIATIC, TODAY. MANY OF HIS MINISTERS ALSO WERE ON HOLIDAY. 

WHILE THE YUGOSLAV PEOPLE WARILY WATCHED DEVELOPMENTS IN KOREA, 
THE ARMED FORCES WERE ALERT TO THE POSSIBILITY OF TROUBLE CLOSER 


AO 
——T , ~ te ‘ : Sin, 
we * i y I 4 


RUMORS WERE RIFE OF TROOP MOVEMENTS, TANK MANEUVERS AND FRONTIER 
SORTIES NEAR THE COUNTRY'S EASTERN BORDER. THREE SOVIET SATELLITES-- 
HUNGARY, ROMANIA AND BULGARIA--LIE ALONG THAT BORDER. BUT THESE 
MID-SUMMER RUMORS ARE AS SEASONAL HERE.AS EARLY_HARVESTING--.. _.. 
ESPECIALLY SINCE THE MOSCOW-LED COMINFORM OUSTED TITO IN 1948. 

(UsSe MILITARY EXPERTS IN BERLIN, STUDYING COMMUNIST MOVES IN THE 
BALKANS. HAVE CONCLUDED THE YUGOSLAV ARMY IS BOTE WILLING AND ABLE 
TO STAND OFF ANY THREAT FROM THE BORDERING NATIONS. A SENIOR 
AMERICAN OFFICER SAID THURSDAY YUGOSLAVIA NOW HAS 30 WELL DRILLED 
DIVISIONS AND "THE ONLY WAY THEY WILL TAKE TITO IS IF THE RED ARMY 
ITSELF MARCHES INe"™ THE YUGOSLAV FORCE--PERHAPS 300,000 MEN--UWAS 
DESCRIBED AS ACTUALLY OUTNUMBERING THE ARMIES OF BULGARIA AND 
ROMANIA, WHICH HAVE BEEN DOING MOST OF THE SABER-RATTLING.) 

NO @NE HERE IS CERTAIN WHETHER THE BORDER RUMORS ARE MERELY 
ROUTINE PRESSURE AGAINST YUGOSLAVIA OR A REAL PRELUDE TO INVASION. 

BUT, IN THE LIGHT OF THE INVASION OF SOUTH KOREA BY NORTH KOREAN 
COMMUNISTS, THE YUGOSLAVS APPEAR CONSIDERABLY MORE CONCERNED THAN 
THEY WERE A YEAR AGO, WHEN A SIMILAR BATCH OF RUMORS STIRRED 
WORLD-WIDE SPECULATION. 

ON THE LIPS OF MANY YUGOSLAVS--AS IN THE CASE OF PEOPLES ELSEWHERE-- 
WAS THE QUESTION: DOFS THE KOREAN CRISIS MEAN A THIRD WORLD WAR? 
NONE HAD READY A POSITIVE ANSWER. 

THERE WERE, HOWEVER, A VARIETY OF THEORIES. 

ONE WAS THAT THE KOREAN WAR WILL HELP TAKE PRESSURE OFF 


| "Sanne AT LEAST TEMPORARILY. 


THE MOST PESSIMISTIC VIEW WAS THAT THE KOREAN AFFAIR WAS 
CALCULATED BY MOSCOW TO SIPHON OFF A BIG PART OF AMERICAN MILITARY 
STRENGTH TO THE PACIFIC AND THUS GIVE RUSSIA A FREER HAND TO SHIFT 
AGAIN TO OBJECTIVES IN THE WEST. , 

PRIVATE EXPRESSIONS BY THE YUGOSLAVS LEAVE LITTLE DOUBT WHERE 
THEIR SYMPATHIES LIE. SMARTING UNDER BELT-TIGHTENING CONDITIONS 
RESULTING FROM THE COMINFORM'S ECONOMIC BOYCOTT, MANY OF THEM ARE 
HOPING THE KOREAN DECISION WILL END RUSSIAN EXPANS ION MOVES. 
PRICES ARE HIGH AND THERE ARE SHORTAGES IN SOME BASIC FOODS. 

THE OFFICIAL PRESS AND RADIO STEERS A MIDDLE COURSE ON KOREA. 
pi Saal ONLY OFFICIAL REPORTS OF DEVELOPMENTS, WITHOUT EDITORIAL 


IT WAS REPORTED THAT HUNGARY HAS BEEN SPEEDING THE REMOVAL OF 
PROeTITO FACTIONS FROM HER BORDER AREAS. din 

THE BELGRADE RADIO, QUOTING THE OFFICIAL YUGOSLAV NEWS -ACGENCY 
TANJUG, SAID HUNGARIAN AUTHORITIES PLACED A NUMBER OF PEOPLE FROM THE 
VILLAGES OF GARAJ AND DJIRICI IN RAILWAY CARS AND SHIPPED THEM OFF TO 
UNKNOWN DESTINATIONS, FIFTY PERSONS WERE SAID TO HAVE BEEN REMOVED 
BY TRAIN FROM THE VILLAGE OF BACKANJA. 

THE ACTION APPARENTLY REPRESENTED ANOTHER IN A SERIES OF MOVES ON 
BOTH SIDES TO TIGHTEN BORDER CONTROLS. YUGOSLAVIA RECENTLY ISSUED AN 
ORDER BARRING TRAVEL WITHIN 15 MILES OF HER BORDERS EXCEPT WITH A 
SPECIAL PERMIT.
