WASHINGTON, JULY 13-C(AP)&lt;UeSe COMMUNISTS HAVE INCREASED. THEIR 
UNDERGROUND OPERATIONS DURING THE PAST YEAR, FBI DIRECTOR AR 
HOOVER TODAY. THE RESULT, HE SAID, IS THE HEAVIEST WORK LOAD 
HIS AGENCY EVER HAS HANDLED. 

IN AN ANNUAL REVIEW OF FBI ACTIVITIES FOR THE FISCAL YEAR WHICH 
ENDED JUNE 30, HOOVER SAID THE NUMBER OF INVESTIGATIONS INVOLVING 
INTERNAL SECURITY AND NATIONAL DEFENSE IS AT A RECORD LEVEL, EXCEEDING 
THE VOLUME OF SIMILAR WORK DURING THE WORLD WAR II YEARS. 

"THE INCREASED WORK LOAD," THE REPORT SAID. "STEMS FROM THE ACTI- 
VITIES OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY AND THE EXPANDED ORBIT OF THEIR UNDER- 
GROUND OPERATIONS. 

"INCREASED SECURITY CONSCIOUSNESS ON THE PART OF THE PARTY LEADER- 
SHIP HAS BROUGHT ABOUT DECENTRALIZATION OF PARTY ADMINISTRATIVE 
MACHINERY AND TRANSFERAL OF PREVIOUSLY OPEN OPERATIONS TO AN UNDER- 
GROUND APPARATUS. 

"THESE DEVELOPMENTS HAVE COMPLICATED THE FBI TASK, OF MAINTAINING 
COVERAGE OF COMMUNIST ACTIVITY." ' 

THE FBI DIRECTOR RECENTLY ASKED CONGRESS FOR MORE THAN 300 ADDI- 
TIONAL AGENTS, SAYING THEY WERE REQUIRED PRINCIPALLY FOR INTERNAL 
SECURITY INVESTIGATIONS. 

THE ANNUAL REPORT SHOWED g,921 CONVICTIONS IN FBI CASES OF ALL 
KINDS DURING THE 1950 FISCAL YEAR, A SIX PER CENT INCREASE OVER 

HOOVER SAID THAT IN LINE WITH PREVIOUS YEARS, 96.9 PER CENT OF 
ALL TRTAIS GROWING OUT OF FBI INQUIRIES RESULTED IN CONVICTIONS.

NEW YORK, JULY 13-(AP)-THE NEW YORK TIMES SAID TODAY THAT DELAYS 
1 PLANE PROBUCTION --VORSE THAMLIM WORLD WAR 2--LIE AHEAD IF THE HEAT 

THE PROGRESS OF SCIENCE IS THE CAUSE. 

"IF THE AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURING INDUSTRY OF THE UNITED stares WERE 
CALLED UPON NOW TO START AN ALL-OUT PRODUCTION EFFORT," THE TIMES SAID, 
"IT WOULD TAKE TEN MONTHS LONGER TO REACH AN ANNUAL ooTPUT RATE OF 
50,000 PLANES THAN IT DID IN WORLD WAR 2." 

"THE STORY, WRITTEN BY FREDERICK GRAHAM, SAID "IT TOOK EXACTLY 24 
MONTHS TO REACH THE GOAL AFTER THE LATE PRESIDENT FRANKLIN De 
ROOSEVELT IN MAY, 1940, CALLED FOR A TOTAL PLANE PRODUCTION OF 50,000 
UNITS A YEAR." 

"Ir A SIMILAR EFFORT WERE STARTED NOW," THE STORY STATED, "IT 
WOULD REQUIRE 34 MONTHS TO REACH THE TARGET FICURE." 

THIS SITUATION EXISTS, GRAHAM WROTE AFTER A SURVEY, "DESPITE THE 
READY AVAILABILITY OF MORE THAN A SCORE OF STAND-BY AtRCRAFT 
MANUFACTURING PLANTS BUILT FOR WORLD WAR 2, A VAST STORE OF MACHINE 
TOOLS NOW IN "MOTHBALLS," A HUGE STOCKPILE OF MATERIALS AND A 
RESERVOIR OF TRAINED PERSONNEL." 

THE STORY ADDED: 

"KEY MEN IN THE AIRCRAFT MANUFACTURING INDUSTRY SAY THE LONGER 
TIME REQUIRED NOW TO BUILD UP TO 50,000 PLANES A YEAR IS FASILY 
EXPLAINED: THE MODERN WARPLANE IS ABOUT TWICE AS HEAVY AS ITS WORLD 
WAR 2 COUNTERPART, AND BECAUSE IT IS INFINITELY MORE COMPLEX, IT 
REQUIRES ABOUT TwiCE AS MANY MAN-HOURS TO BUILD. xxx"

BY TOM LAMBERT 

SOMEWHERE IN SOUTH KOREA SATURDAY, JULY 15-(AP)-ANOTHER AMERICAN 
RETREAT ALONG THE SOUTH KOREAN FRONT SEEMED IN PROSPECT TODAY AS NORTH 
KOREAN COMMUNISTS CROSSED THE KUM RIVER. 

THE REDS HAVE SHOWN SMART TACTICS SINCE FIRST BATTLING AMERICANS ON 
JULY 5e AGAIN, THEY SEEM TO BE USING THEIR FLANKING AND 
INFILTRATION MOVES « THEY WILL BE HARD TO COUNTER UNTIL U.S. FORCES 
ARE BOLSTERED ENOUGH TO MEET THRUSTS ANYWHERE ALONG THEIR LINE. 

THE PROBABLE GENERAL WITHDRAWAL FROM THE KUM RIVER WILL BE ANOTHER 
IN A SERIES OF RETREATS FROM SUCH PLACES AS OSAN eens CHONAN, 
AND CHOCHIWON -=- ALL PRIMARILY BECAUSE OF THE REDS* OVERWHELMING 
SUPERIORITY IN NUMBERS AND EQUIPMENT EVERYWHERE EXCEPT IN THE AIRe 

AT A REGIMENTAL OR DIVISIONAL LEVEL, THE SOUTH KOREA WAR THUS 
LOOKS BAD FOR THE U.S. ACTUALLY, A HANDFUL OF AMERICANS HAS YIELDED 
GROUND DOGGEDLY TO THE REDS. 


, IN SOME CASES AMERICANS HAVE BEHAVED BADLY, DISCARDING WEAPONS 
AND FLEEING IN DISORGANIZATION BEFORE THE RED ADVANCE. |_|

AND ROCKET MISSIONS. en pea

WASHINGTON, JULY 14-(AP)-RUSSIA MAY BE TRYING TO LURE THE UNITED 
STATES INTO SO GREAT A MILITARY EFFORT IN KOREA THAT IT COULD BE HELP- 
LESS TO CHALLENGE LARGE-SCALE AGGRESSION ELSEWHERE. 

_ ILLUSTRATING THIS IS A QUESTION POSED FOR PRESIDENT TRUMAN AT A 
NEWS CONFERENCE YESTERDAY AND HIS CAUTIOUS REPLY. 

vy LE,WAS ASKED, "ARE VE PREPARED TO RESIST AGGRESSION EVERYWHERE 

N THE WORLD?" — 

HIS REPLY WAS THAT THE SITUATION WOULD HAVE TO BE MET AS IT DEV- 
ELOPED. 

MILITARY LEADERS AT THE PENTAGON ATTACH IMPORTANCE TO PERSISTENT 
RUMORS OF CONCENTRATION OF CHINESE COMMUNIST FORCES AND THE ENROLL- 
“ENT OF RUSSIAN VOLUNTEERS FOR THE AID OF THE NORTH KOREAN COMMUNIST 
ARMY. 

BUT THIS FOREIGN-POWER HELP MAY NOT BE THROWN SUDDENLY INTO THE 
WAR TO CRUSH SOUTH KOREANS AND DRIVE AMERICAN FORCES OUT OF KOREA FOR 
A QUICK VICTORY. INSTEAD, THE MOSCOW-DICTATED STRATEGY MAY BE TO 

FEED THE HELP IN GRADUALLY, ALWAYS MAINTAINING SUPERIORITY IN FORCE-- 
AND COMPELLING THE UNITED $TATES TO PUT MORE AND MORE DIVISIONS, 

PLANES AND WARSHIPS INTO THE CAMPAIGN. 

MEANWHILE IN THESE EARLY MONTHS OF THE WAR, THE KOREAN CAMPAIGN 
AFFORD RUSSIA OPPORTUNITY TO MEASURE THE’ BATTLE-SKILL OF AMERICAN

GENsOMAR BRADLEY, CHAIRMAN OF THE JOINT CHIEFS OF STAFF. WAs 
REPORTED BY CHAIRMAN TYDINGS (D-MD) OF THE SENATE ARMED SERVICES 
COMMITTEE AS HAVING SAID DEFENSE DEPARTMENT AND OTHER OFFICIALS ARE 
CAREFULLY WATCHING FIVE OR SIX "SENSITIVE AREAS" ASIDE FROM KOREA. 

THESE AREAS WERE NOT SPECIFICALLY IDENTIFIED BY TYDINGS, BUT 
OBVIOUSLY THEY INCLUDED SUCH POINTS AS THE POWDER-KEG IN EUROPE, THE 
MIDDLE EAST, SOUTHEAST ASIA, FORMOSA AND THE PHILIPPINES. AGGRESSION 
COULD OCCUR’AT ANY ONE OR MANY OF THESE "SENSITIVE" POINTS. 

ALONG WITH THIS IS ANOTHER QUESTION THAT MUST BE FACED WHEN, AS 
AMERICAN CHIEFS ARE CONFIDENT, THE TIDE OF BATTLE TURNS AND THE 
NORTH KOREAN INVADERS OF THE EREF REPUBLIC OF KOREA ARE ROLLED BACK: 

DOFS THE "POLICE ACTION." WHICH MR.TRUMAN STILL USES TO DFSIGNATE 
THE KOREAN SITUATION, CONTEMPLATE PUSHING ON NORTHWARD PAST THE 38TH 
PARALLEL WHICH RUSSIA AND THE WESTERN POWERS FIXED AS A BOUNDARY WHEN 
RUSSIA REFUSED TO ALLOW A KOREAN-WIDF ELECTION? 

AGAIN, MRe TRUMAN SAID THAT DECISION WILL BE MADE WHEN IT BECAME 
NECESSARY. 

IF THE DECISION PROVES TO BE FOR CONTINUING ON NORTHWARD, MORE 
MILITARY EXPENDITURES MUST BE MADE.

ce HOW MUCH, IF ANY's CAN BE HELD BACK FOR COPING«WITH }/POSSTBLE

3e HOW MUCH MORE MILITARY MANPOWER AND INDUSTRIAL STRENGTH

THEY KNOW WHAT THEY HAVE NOW. IT IS ALARMINGLY SIMPLE--TEN REGULAR 
ARMY DIVISIONS; AN AIR FORCE OF 48 GROUPS WHICH IS STILL CHANGING 
OVER FROM OLD @ARTIME MODELS TO PLANES OF NEW DESIGN: A NAVY WHICH HAS 
ONLY ABOUT 30 COMBATANT VESSELS IN ACTIVE SERVICE BUT STILL IS BY 
FAR THE WORLD'S MOST POWERFUL. 

FOUR OF THE TEN DIVISIONS ARE IN THE FAR EAST, AT LEAST ONE ALREADY 
IS_IN THE KOREAN BATTLE, OTHERS ARE READY OR PERHAPS GOING UP AS 
CLOSE-bY RESERVES. ONE IS IN GERMANY, WHERE CRISIS IS ALWAYS CLOSE 
BY. OF THE FIVE IN THE UNITED STATES, ONE HAS BEEN TAGGED FOR 
EARLY DEPARTURE FOR THE FAR EAST AND tLEMENTS OF OTHER DIVISIONS ALSO 
ARE BEING READIED. 

WHERE DO THE REPLACEMENTS FOR THE DIVISIONS COME FROM?

NIGHT LEAD PRICES-CONTROLS (320) 

WASHINGTON, JULY 14-(AP)-A SHARP, WAR-SPAWNED RISE IN THE WHOLE- 
SALE PRICES OF MANY THINGS PEOPLE EAT, WEAR OR USE WAS CONFIRMED BY 
THE GOVERNMENT TODAY. 

RESIDENT TRUMAN DISCUSSED THE QUESTION OF POSSIBLE HOME-FRONT 


MOBILIZATION WITH HIS CABINET AT A MORNING MEETING. 


IT WAS APPARENT, HOWEVER, THAT THE ADMINISTRATION HAD NOT 
REACHED A DECISION ON WHETHER TO ASK CONGRESS FOR ANY CONTROLS ON 
THE PRICE OR DISTRIBUTION OF GOODS. 

SENATOR TAFT OF OHIO, THE REPUBLICAN LEADER, SAID HE WOULD OPPOSE 
GIVING THE PRESIDENT ANY "BLANK CHECK OR STANDBY AUTHORITY" TO PUT 
CONTROLS INTO OPERATION. TAFT SAID HE THINKS CONGRESS OUGHT TO 
STAY ON THE JOB AND ADOPT ANY LEGISLATION THAT BECOMES NECESSARY 
IN THE LIGHT OF EVENTS. 

THE CABINET MEMBERS DECLINED TO GET SPECIFIC ABOUT THEIR CON- 
FERENCE WITH MReTRUMAN OTHER THAN TO SAY THAT NO DECISIONS WERE 

THE PRESIDENT SAID AT HIS NEWS CONFERENCE YESTERDAY THAT EVERY PHASE 
OF POSSIBLE INDUSTRIAL MOBILIZATION IS BEING CONSIDERED, AND THAT THE 
NEEDED STEPS WOULD BE TAKEN AT THE PROPER TIME. ON THE OTHER HAND 
HE INDICATED THAT HE HAS NO IMMEDIATE INTENTION OF ASKING FOR EMER- 
GENCY AUTHORITY TO PUT IN PRICE OR WAGE CONTROLS, ALLOCATE SCARCE 
MATERIALS OR ORDER THE CONVERSATION OF INDUSTRY TO WAR PRODUCTION.

NIGHT LEAD WHEAT 
BY OVID A.MARTIN 

WASHINGTON, JULY 14&lt;(AP)©A 20 PERCENT LARGER WHEAT CROP NEXT YEAR 
WAS URGED BY THE GOVERNMENT TODAY TO SUPPLY POSSIBLE LARGE SCALE WAR 
NEEDS, 

THE AGRICULTURE DEPARTMENT RECOMMENDED A CROP OF 1,150,000,000 
BUSHELS~-193,000,000 MORE THAN THIS YEARS INDICATED CROP--TO ASSURE 
THE WATION A "SAE® SUPPLY. 

IN KOREA BECAUSE OF THE EXISTENCE OF A BIG CARRYOVER OR RESERVE FROM 
PAST CROPS. MOST OF THIS RESERVE, WHICH TOTALS 450,000,000 BUSHELS, 
IS STORED UNDER GOVERNMENT PRICE SUPPORT PROGRAMS. 

THE GOAL OUTLINED BY THE DEPARTMENT WOULD PROVIDE LARGER SUPPLIES 
OF WHEAT FOR LIVESTOCK FEED AS WELL AS FOR EXPORT. WHILE NOT NORMALLY 
CONSIDERED A LIVESTOCK FEED, LARGE QUANTITIES OF WHEAT WERE DIVERTED 
TO SUCH USE IN THE EARLY STAGES OF WORLD WAR II TO EXPAND PRODUCTION © 
OF MEATS, MILK AND POULTRY PRODUCTS. AT THAT TIME, THE GOVERNMENT 


aa Bee a~ 


+ WORLD WAR IT esas e WHO MADE 
0 


MADE WHEAT AVAILABLE FOR Pezp AT CUT RATE PRICES. 

IN ANNOUNCING THE 20 PERCENT HIGHER GOAL, THE DEPARTMENT DID NOT 
REFER DIRECTLY TO THE INTERNATIONAL SITUATION. BUT IT DID SAY THAT 
THE GOVERNMENT WOULD RATHER HAVE TOO MUCH WHEAT THAN NOT ENOUGH TO MEST 
ANY REQUIREMENTS, 

THE GOAL ASSUMED THE POSSIBLE USE OF 225,000,000 BUSHELS OF WHEAT 
FROM THE 1951 CROP TO PRODUCE LIVESTOCK PRODUCTS--OR MORE THAN DOUBLE 
THE RATE THE GRAIN IS BEING USED FOR THAT PURPOSE NOW. THIS ASSUMPTION 
VAS MADE IN THE FACE OF THE FACT THAT THIS YEAR*S CORN CROP--NEXT 
YEAR'S FEED@-MAY BE A FIFTH LARGER THAN THE GOVERNMENT'S GOAL FOR CORN. 

TO ACHIEVE THE WHEAT GOAL, THE DEPARTMENT SET A NATIONAL PLANTING 
ALLOTMENT OF 72,78%,820 ACRES COMPARED WITH 71,523,000 SEEDED FOR THIS 
YEAR'S CROP, HOWEVER, PROBABLY NO MORE THAN 60,000,000 ACRES WILL BE 
HARVESTED THIS YEAR, SUE TO HEAVY ABANDONMENT IN DRY AREAS. 

THE NATIONAL ALLOTMENT WILL BE APPORTIONED AMONG INDIVIDUAL FARMERS. 
GROWERS WILL BE FREE TO PLANT IN EXCESS OF ALLOTMENTS, BUT ONLY THOSE 
WHO REMAIN WITHIN ALLOTMENTS WILL BE ELIGIBLE FOR PRICE SUPPORT AID, 
WHICH AVERAGES $1.99 A BUSHEL THIS YEAR.

NOTE TO ASSOCIATED PRESS MEMBERS &amp; MANAGING EDITORS 

(FOR PUBLICATION FOR PROMOTIONAL PURPOSES IF DESIRED) 

IT'S A TOUGHER CAMPAIGN IN KOREA THAN ANY ONE DREAMED, AND THE 
ASSOCIATED PRESS IS EXPANDING ITS STAFF OPERATIONS TO ASSURE INTENSIVE 
NEWS AND PICTURE COVERAGE OF THE BIGGEST STORY SINCE WORLD WAR II--A 
OTORY THAT IS FLAMING IN THE WESTERN PACIFIC AND ECHOING WITH 
REPERCUSSIONS ‘ROUND THE WORLD. 5 

REINFORCEMENTS HAVE BEEN ASSIGNED TO JOIN THE STAFF DOING SO*NOBLY 
ON THE KOREAN FRONT AND IN TOKYO, WHILE OTHER ASSOCIATED PRESS MEN HAVE 
BEEN DEPLOYED IN SENSITIVE AREAS ELSEWHERE IN THE WORLD TO BE ON THE 
ALERT FOR ALL NEWS DEVELOPMENTS.

LONDON, JULY 14-(AP)&lt;A PRIVATE ENGINEERING FIRM HAS BEEN COMM- 
ISSIONED PY THE GOVERNMENT TO DESIGN A PROTOTYPE OF AN ATOMIC POWER 
UNIT FOR LARGE SHIPS, SCIENTIFIC CIRCLES REPORT. 

THE PROBLEM PRESENTED TO THE FIRM, IT WAS UNDERSTOOD, IS TO 
DESIGN AN ATOMIC POWER UNIT SMALL ENOUGH TO BE FEASIBLE IN A SHIP, 
YET PRACTICAL IN OPERATION. A STUDY OF A PROTOTYPE WOULD ENABLE THE 
GOVERNMENT TO DECIDE WHETHER THE TIME IS RIPE TO PUT AN ATOWIC POWER 
UNIT IN A SHIP TO A PRACTICAL TEST. 

THE MINISTRY OF SUPPLY, IN CHARGE OF ATOMIC POWER DEVELOPMENTS, 
NOT DENY THE REPORTS BUT WOULD NOT ELABORATE ON THEM.

ronan ULY 14-(AP)-BRITAIN ASKED MOSCOW TODAY TO ADMIT AN 
ARTIAL» INTEDNATIONAL COMMISSION INTO RUSSIA TO INVESTIGAGE 
IET CLAIMS THAT ONLY 13,546 GERMAN PRISONERS OF WAR REMAIN 

RUSSIA ANNOUNCED MAY &amp; THAT REPATREATEON-OF GERMAN 
RISONERS HAD BEEN COMPLETED EXCEPT FOR THAT NUMBER, CHILLING 

HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF GERMANS WITH RELATIVES STILL MISSING. | 
A FORMAL BRITISH NOTE TO THE RUSSIAN FOREIGN OFFICE DECLARED THE 

MAY &amp; ANNOUNCEMENT WAS RECEIVED WITH "SHOCK AND GRAVE CONCERN 

IN GERMANY AND THROUGHOUT THE CIVILIZED WORLD." THE ANNOUNCEMENT 

SAID THE ONLY GERMANS LEFT IN THE SOVIET UNION WERE THOSE 

ONCDEMNED FOR SERIOUS WAR CRIMES, THOSE WHOSE ALLEGED WAR CRIMES 

BEING INVESTIGATED AND A FEW WHO WERE “4, 

TEMPORARILY DETAINED BECAUSE OF ILLNESS. : 

THE NEWS SHATTERED THE HOPES OF HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS OF GERMANS 

WITH RELATIVES MISSING. REACTION IN WEST GERMANY WAS BITTER 

WITH GERMAN OFFICIALS DECLARING THAT 1,500,000 GERMANS ARE STILL 

MISSING, INCLUDING "TENS OF THOUSANDS OF DEPORTED CIVILIANS." 

THE UeSe STATE DEPARTMENT HAS LABELED THE RUSSIAN CLAIM 

"FANTASTIC AND ABSURD." IT ESTIMATED THE NUMBER OF GERMANS 

STILL BEING HELD AT "AT LEAST" 200,000. 

BEFORE THE SOVIET ANNOUNCEMENT WAS MADE, THE UNITED STATES 

AND FRANCE ACCUSED MOSCOW OF LYING ABOUT ITS REPATRIATION CLAIMS 

TO HIDE THE FATE OF HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS STILL UNACCOUNTED FOR. 

THERE WAS SPECULATION THAT MANY OF THEM WERE BEING USED 

IN FORCED LABOR BATTALIONS, OR THAT THEY WERE BEING TRAINED TO 

FORM A PRO-SOVIET EAST GERMAN ARMY. , 

THE BRITISH NOTE TODAY ACCUSED RUSSIA OF HIDING THE FATE 

OF "TENS OF THOUSANDS® OF PRISONERS, AND URGED RUSSIA TOs 
1. IDENTIFY AND GIVE THE WHEREABOUTS OF THE PRISONERS 

ADMITTEDLY STILL BEING HELD. 

2. PERMIT THE PRISONERS TO CORRESPOND WITH THEIR FAMILIES. 
3. "GIVE FULL DETAILS OF ANY PERS ONS WHOM THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT, 

BY CLASSIFICATION AS CIVILIAN WORKERS OR IN ANY OTHER WAY 

HAVE DEPRIVED OF PRISONER OF WAR STATUS AND HAVE THEREBY EXCLUDED 

FROM THEIR PRISONER OF WAR STATISTICS."

WASHINGTON, JULY 14-CAP)-JCHN J.EDMISTON, WHO JOINED THE COMMUNIST 
PARTY TO SERVE THE FBI_AS AN UNDERCOVER AGENT, HAS HAD A VARIED CAREER. 
AMONG OTHER THINGS, HE HAS BEEN A PRACTICING ATTORNEY, REAL ESTATE 
DEALER» RADIO COMMENTATOR, PRESS AGENT, GOVERNMENT WORKER AND NEWSPAP- 
THIS CAME OUT AS HE LAID BEFORE THE HOUSE UNAMERICAN ACTIVITIES 


rg THIS WEEK HIS STORY OF COMMUNIST ACTIVITY IN OHIO OF A DECe- 
GO. 


BORN IN COLUMBUS, OHIO, DEC. 3, 1899, EDMISTON WAS GRADUATED FROM 
THE NEW LEXINGTON, OHIO, HIGH SCHOOL, OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY (1919) 
AND HARVARD LAW SCHOOL (1922). 


HE BEGAN PRACTICING LAW AT DAYTONA, FLA., IN 1924, REMAINING THERE 
UNTIL 1928 WHEN HE RETURNED TO COLUMBUS TO ENTER THE REAL ESTATE BUS- 
INESS. HE LEFT REAL ESTATE FOR WEVSPAPER AND RADIO WORK IN 1934. 
FIRST HE WAS A NEWS COMMENTATOR FOR MUZAK, INC., IN CLEVELAND FOR TWO 
YEARS, THEN BECAME A FINANCIAL REPORTER FOR THE TOLEDO NEWS BEE. 

AFTER THAT, HE RETURNED TO COLUMBUS IN 1938 TO GO INTO PRESS AGENT- 
ING. HE CONTINUED IN THIS THROUGH 1941, THE LAST TWO YEARS IN WHAT 
HE CALLS "A NOMINAL WAY" BECAUSE GOOD ACCOUNTS WERE HARD) 10 GET AND) 
HOLD. JUL To Neu 

FROM PRESS AGENTING HE WENT TO WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR BASE AT DAYTON 
WHERE HE WAS CONNECTED WITH MOTION PICTURE PRODUCTION FROM 1942 TO 
1947. THEN HE JOINED THE STAFF OF THE DAYTON JOURNAL HERALD AND 
NOW IS A BUSINESS REPORTER, 

EDMISTON, WHOSE WIFE MARTHA ALSO JOINED THE COMMUNIST PARTY AS AN 
FBI UNDERCOVER AGENT, SAID HE FIRST LEARNED ABOUT COMMUNISM FROM 
EsSeGRATTAN, WHOM HE CALLED "A VERY INTERESTING FELLOW X X X A PER- 
SON OF CONSIDERABLE LEFT WING TENDENCIES. GRATTAN AT THIS TIME 
(1931 OR 1932) WAS A COMPOSITOR ON A COLUMBUS WEWSPAPER.* 


BIOWX

RAN INTO GRATTAN AND ASKED HIM WHAT HE WAS “UP TO NOW". GRATTAN RE- 
PLIED HE WAS SECRETARY OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY IN COLUMBUS, THE WIT-. 
NESS SAID. 

"MY WIFE WAS PRESENT WITH ME," EDMISTON TOLD THE COMMITTEE. “WE 
WENT OUT TO HIS APARTMENT AND THERE WERE A NUMBER OF YOUNG WOMEN THERE 
WHOM HE INTRODUCED AS COMRADES."

TOKYO, SUNDAY, JULY 16--U.S.COUNT HAVE HURLED SOME NOR 
KOREAN TROOPS BACK ACROSS THE KUM RIVER, CENERAL MACARTHUR REPORTED 
TODAY, BUT THE Cot IRM BRIDGEHEAD 15 MILES OR 


TODAY, BUT THE COMMUNISTS"STILL HOLD A 

FIELD DISPATCHES REPORTED THE NORTH KOREANS WERE CHECKED GENERALLY 
ALONG THE KUM. DISPATCHES SAID ONE NEW RED CROSSING ATTEMPT WAS 
REPULSED BEFORE DAWN TODAY. THE COMMUNISTS CAME ACROSS THE SHALLOW 
KUM UNDER COVER OF MORTAR FIRE AND TANK GUNS ON THE NORTH BANK. 
MOST OF THEM DIED IN THE RIVER OR ON THE SANDY BANKS. 

ALERT DEFENSE LIKEWISE THREW BACK NUMEROUS FEELER THRUSTS ACROSS 
THE RIVER BY COMMUNIST PATROLS. 

FIELD DISPATCHES INDICATED THE COMMUNISTS FROM THEIR BRIDGEHEAD 
IN THE SAMGYO AREA, 20 MILES NORTHWEST OF TAEJON. HAD INFILTRATED 
ABOUT FIVE MILES TOWARD THAT FORMER REFUGEE CAPITAL OF SOUTH KOREA. 

THERE THEY WERE CHECKED BY STIFFENING UeS.DEFENSES 

MACARTHUR'S COMMUNIQUE COVERED ONLY THE FIGHTING OF FRIDAY AND 
SATURDAY. Wedd 1950. 

IT SAID THE 34TH UsSeINFANTRY REGIMENT IN A COUNTERTHRUST ‘DROVE 
COMMUNIST FORCES BACK ACROSS THE KUM FRIDAY NIGHT NEAR SAMGYO. 

BUT THE COMMUNISTS APPARENTLY SURGED RIGHT BACKe A MACARTHUR 
COMMUNIQUE SATURDAY SAID THE REDS PLANTED A BRIDGEHEAD IN THE 
SAMGYO AREA SATURDAY MORNING. 

A COMMUNIQUE THIS MORNING SAID THE BRIDGEHEAD WAS INTACT DESPITE 
HEAVY LOSSES FROM WARPLANE ATTACKS AND UeSeGROUND FIRE. 

THE 19TH UsSeINFANTRY REGIMENT BROKE UP ANOTHER RED CROSSING 
ATTEMPT SATURDAY MORNING NEAR SOHANG. WHICH IS SIX MILES 
NORTHEAST OF SAMGYO, THE COMMUNIQUE REPORTED. 

THE COMMUNIQUE PRAISED THE TACTICS OF THE U.sS~sINFANTRY IT DECLARED 
THEY HAD INFLICTED "HEAVY LOSSES AGAINST THE NORTH KOREANS.” 

"THE DEFENDERS," SAID THE COMMUNIQUE, "DEPLOYED IN DEPTH BEHIND 
THE SOUTH BANK OF THE RIVER, ALLOWED POCKETS OF TWO AND THREE HUNDRED 
TO BUILD UP AND THEN BY COUNTERATTACK OF INFANTRY BACKED UP WITH 
ARTILLERY AND AIR. FORCED THE INVADERS BACK INTO THE RIVER." 

WITHOUT ELABORATION, MACARTHUR'S COMMUNIQUE REPORTED THE VETERAN 
NORTH KOREAN FIRST DIVISION WAS OPERATING WELL TO THE WEST OF TAEJON. 

IT DID NOT SAY WHETHER THE FIRST WAS ACROSS THE KUM RIVER BUT 
REPORTED IT WAS "PROBING THE NORTH-SOUTH HIGHWAY TO NONSAN." NONSAN 
LIES DEEP ON TAEJON'S FLANK 21 MILES TO THE SOUTHWEST AND ON THE 
AMERICAN SIDE OF THE RIVER. 

THIS MAY BE THE RED FORCE ON THE NORTH BANK OF THE RIVER WHICH A 
FIELD DISPATCH SAID WAS MOVING UNOPPOSED DOWN THE ROAD TOWARD THE 
PORT OF KUNSAN, 45 MILES SOUTHWEST OF TAEJON. 

A SIX-MILE ADVANCE ALSO WAS REPORTED BY RED TROOPS PUSHING OUT FAR 
TO THE EAST OF TAEJON IN A MOVEMENT WHICH POSES AN ULTIMATE THREAT 
TO AMERICAN SUPPLY BASES. 

THE COMMUNIQUE SAID THE NORTHERNERS WERE ONLY A MILE FROM YONGJU 
WHICH IS 72 AIR MILES NORTHEAST OF TAEJON,. FIFTY-FIVE ROAD MILES TO 
THE EAST LIES THE COMMUNIST BEACHHEAD IN THE UTCHIN AREA. 

BETWEEN THIS EASTERN END OF THE FRONT AND TAEJON, THE COMMUNIQUE 
SAID SOUTH KOREAN TROOPS WERE FIGHTING A DELAYING ACTION WEST OF 
MUNGYONG, A VILLAGE 45 MILES NORTHEAST OF TAEJON.

BY DAVID J. WILKIE | 
ASSOCIATED PRESS AUTOMOTIVE EDITOR 

DETROIT. JULY 15-(AP)-THE AUTO INDUSTRY RIGHT NOW HAS NO 
ARMAMENT WORK GROWING OUT OF THE KOREAN WAR. 

IT IS READY TO PUT ALL ITS INDUSTRIAL MIGHT INTO A WAR JOB IF THE 
OCCASION REQUIRES. BUT IT FIRST MUST KNOW PRECISELY WHAT ITS 
VARIOUS PLANTS WILL BE ASKED TO BUILD. 

UNTIL THAT TIMP COMES THE CAR MANUFACTURERS ARE MAKING NO CHANGES 
IN THEIR SHORT-TERM OR LONG-RANGE PLANNING. THEY ARE CONTINUING THEIR 
PLANS TO MAINTAIN HIGH LEVEL PEACETIME EMPLOYMENT AND PROCEEDING WITH 
PREPARATIONS FOR 1951 MODEL CAR INTRODUCTIONS LATER THIS YEAR AS 
ORIGINALLY SCHEDULED. 

SUCH ARE THE REPLIES OF VIRTUALLY EVERY AUTOMOBILE MAKER TO 
NUMFROUS INQUIRIES AS TO WHAT EFFECT THE ASIATIC SITUATION MAY HAVE 
ON THEIR PEACETIME PRODUCTION PROGRAMS « 

IT IS TRUE THAT JUST ABOUT EVERY AUTOMOBILE PLANT HAS BEEN 
SURVEYED TO DETERMINE WHAT KIND OF ARMS PRODUCTION IT BEST IS FITTED 
FOR. IT IS ALSO TRUE THE CLOSEST POSSIBLE LIAISON IS BEING MAINTAINED 
BETWEEN AUTO INDUSTRY AND MILITARY PROCUREMENT. 
BUT. INDUSTRY EXECUTIVES SAY, WHAT EVENTUALLY IS NEEDED MAY BE 
ENTIRELY DIFFERENT FROM WHAT LESSONS OF THE LAST WAR MIGHT INDICATE. 

OUT OF ALL THE PRELIMINARY STUDIES AND THE EXPERIENCES FOLLOWING 
PFARL HARBOR WOULD COME A SPEEDIER CONVERSION THAN WAS POSSIBLE IN 
THE EARLY DAYS OF THE LAST WARe 

AT THE SAME TIME ARMS WORK IS VASTLY DIFFERENT FROM WHAT THE AUTO 
FACTORIES CURRENTLY ARE DOING. IT WOULD TAKE WEEKS TO TEAR OUT

NEWARK,NeJe,JULY 15=C(AP)*EASTERN AIR LINES TODAY RELEASED FOUR OF 
ITS SEVEN FOUR=ENGINED CARGO PLANES TO CARRY MILITARY MATERIEL IN 
RESPONSE TO AN APPEAL OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE. 

CAPT.EDDIE RICKENBACKER, PRESIDENT AND GENERAL MANAGER, SAID THE 
PLANES WERE PLACED AT THE IMMEDIATE DISPOSAL OF THE GOVERNMENT, 
TOGETHER WITH THEIR CREWS AND GROUND FACILITIES NEEDED FOR OPERATION. 

THE ACTION, HE SAID, NECESSARILY WILL LIMIT EAL AIR FREIGHT SERVICE 
BETWEEN NEW YORK AND TEXAS, FLORIDA, CHICAGO AND DETROIT. THE LINE 
ALSO OPERATES A NUMBER OF TWO-ENGINED CARGO CARRIERS. 

RICKENBACKER SAID EAL WAS "MORE THAN WILLING” TO PROVIDE FACILITIES 
DURING THE KOREAN AND PRESENT WORLD EMERGENCY. 


THE FOUR-ENGINED CARGO CARRIERS, A C-54 VERSION OF THE DOUGLAS, CAN 
HAUL 18,000 POUNDS OF CARGO EACH, EAL SAID.

CALLED MEETING LAST NIGHT.

LAKE SUCCESS, JULY 15=(AP)-AMERICA AND THE REST OF THE UNITED 
NATIONS WATCHED ANXIOUSLY TODAY FOR REPLIES FROM 52 U.N. MEMBERS TO 
SECRETARY=GENERAL TRYGVE LIE'S CALL FOR ALL-OUT FIGHTING AID TO STEM

LIE EXPRESSED HIS CONCERN OVER THE UeNe SITUATION IN KOREA AT A

THE UeNe MEMBERS EXCEPT THE DISSENTING SOVIET BLOC AND COMMUNIST

ECYPT IS BACKING IT NOW.

BRUSSELS, BELGIUM, JULY 15-(AP)-SOME BELGIANS ARE DUSTING 
OFF FLAGS AND ROYAL PICTURES TO WELCOME BACK KING LEOPOLD III, NOW 
EXPECTED TO RETURN TO HIS THRONE IN A FEW DAYS. 

NEARLY AS MANY MORE SHOW HARDENING OPPOSITION, 

MANY BELGIANS BELIEVE THE END OF LEOPOLD'S LONG EXILE IN 
SWITZERLAND WILL SETTLE NOTHING UNLESS HE AGREES TO ABDICATE AND 
TRANSFER HIS POWERS TO PRINCE BAUDOUIN, HIS 19-YEAR OLD SON. 

EVEN SOME LEOPOLD SUPPORTERS ADMIT THIS IS THE ONLY WAY THEY CAN 
SEE TO HEAL THE RIFT IN THE REALM THAT STARTED WHEN LEOPOLD 
SURRENDERED TO THE GERMANS AFTER ONLY 18 DAYS OF FIGHTING IN 1940. 

THE BITTERNESS WAS EMPHASIZED BY CLASHES OF ANTI“LEOPOLD STRIKERS 
WITH POLICE AT LIEGE TODAY. THE STRIKERS ATTACKED STREET CARS AND 
SMASHED WINDOWS OF A LARGE DEPARTMENT STORE WHICH FAILED TO HEED THE 
CALL FOR A REGIONAL WALKOUT AS A DEMONSTRATION AGAINST THE KING. 
SEVERAL DEMONSTRATORS WERE ARRESTED. 

SOCIALISTS AND COMMUNISTS ARE THE MOST VOCAL OF LEOPOLD'S OPPONENTS. 
BACKING HIM ARE THE CATHOLIC SOCIAL CHRISTIANS, WHO CONTROL THE 
GOVERNMENT AND BOTH HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT. 

NEXT FRIDAY IS BELGIUM'S NATIONAL FETE DAY.

THE MORE POWERFUL WEAPON OF A NATIONWIDE GENERAL STRIKE. 

SOCIALIST LEADER MAX BUSET, ADDRESSING STRIKING MINERS IN THE 
BORINAGE REGION FRIDAY, SAID THE SOCIALISTS WOULD NEVER ACCEPT MINIS- 
TERIAL PORTFOLIOS OR DECORATIONS FROM KING LEOPOLD. | 

THEY WILL CONTINUE TO SAY WHAT THEY THINK AND DEFY PROSECUTION, HE 
SAID. 

A STONE LION WITH THE MOTTO "UNITY IS STRENGTH" LOOKS DOWN FROM A 

WALL OF BELGIUM*S HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES, WHERE SCENES OF DISUNITY 
AND DISORDER HAVE MARKED PARLIAMENT'S DEBATE ON RETURN OF THE KING. 
HIS PUBLIC AND HIS PRIVATE LIFE, HIS CONSTITUTIONAL ACTIONS AND HIS 
FAMILY HAVE BEEN ATTACKED OR DEFENDED IN THE JOINT SESSIONS THERE WHICH 
OPENED MORE THAN A WEEK AGO.

VATICAN CITY,JULY 15-C(AP)-POPE PIUS XII SAID TODAY THAT THE IDEA 


OF UNIFYING EUROPE EXPRESSES A NEED *TO BREAK OR AT LEAST TO 
LOOSEN, BOTH POLITICALLY AND ECONOMICALLY, THE STIFFNESS OF THE OLD 
FRAMES OF GEOGRAPHICAL FRONTIERS." WU 46.1950 
THE POPE ADDRESSED IN FRENCH A GROUP OF 200 JURISTS” FROM ALL OVER 
Meee WORLD WHO GATHERED HERE TO STUDY THE POSSIBILITY OF UNIFYING CIVIL 
AW CODES. 
THE PONTIFF POINTED TO THE DIFFICULTIES OF A COMPLETE UNIFICATION 
OF CIVIL LAW, "EVEN FOR A RESTRICTED NUMBER OF STATES,* AND ADDED3 
"THE ECONOMIC, SOCIAL OR CULTURAL CONDITIONS WOULD BE SO DIFFER- 
ENT IN CERTAIN COUNTRIES THAT UNIFORMITY INCLUDING ALL NATIONS AND 
os LAWS WOULD NOT RESPOND TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF COMMONWEL= 
ARE." 
HOWEVER, HE URGED THE JURISTS TO KEEP THREE POINTS IN MIND3 
"1. THE MOST ATTENTIVE AND EFFICIENT PROTECTION OF THOSE WHO HAVE 
THE LARGEST NEEDS, NAMELY ABANDONED CHILDREN AND WOMENs, LEGISLATORS 
SHOULD REGULATE THEIR CONDUCT TOWARD THEM AS FATHERS OR MOTHERS} 
"2. THE JURIDICAL REGIME OF THOSE COMPELLED TO MOVE FREQUENTLY 
ao ga REGULAR INTERVALS FROM ONE COUNTRY TO ANOTHER SHOULD BE 
M De 
"3. RECOGNITION AND REALIZATION, DIRECT AND INDIRECT, OF THE 
NATURAL RIGHTS OF MAN, WHICH, AS INHERENT TO HUMAN NATURE, ARE ALWAYS 
CLOSE TO THE COMMON INTEREST; EVEN MORE, THESE (RIGHTS) MUST BE 
TAKEN AS THE ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF COMMON GOOD." 
ELABORATING ON THIS LAST POINT, THE POPE SAID “IT IS THE DUTY OF

BY SEYMOUR TOPPING 

SAIGON, INDOCHINA, JULY 15=(AP)-FRENCH AUTHORITIES ARE ASKING AMERICAN 
OFFICIALS HERE IF FROZEN CHINESE NATIONALIST FUNDS IN THE UNITED STATES 
COULD BE USED TO PAY FOR THE COST OF KEEPING SOME 30,000 NATIONALIST 
SOLDIERS INTERNED IN INDOCHINA. 

THE FRENCH STRESS THEY HAVE MADE NO FORMAL APPLICATION, BUT ARE 
EXPLORING THE AVAILABILITY OF THE FUNDS AND THE ATTITUDE OF THE NATIO- 
NALIST GOVERNMENT ON FORMOSA. | 

THE CHINESE ASSETS WERE FROZEN BY WASHINGTON UNTIL LITIGATION BETWEEN 
THE CHINESE COMMUNISTS AND THE NATIONALISTS OVER THEM COULD BE CONCLU- 
DED. THEY INCLUDE FUNDS WHICH OTHERWISE WOULD BE USED BY OFFICES 
WHICH ARE UNDER RED CONTROL IN CHINA. | 

THE FRENCH SAY THEY ARE SPENDING AN ESTIMATED 7,000,000 (M) INDO- 
CHINESE PIASTRES TO SUPPORT THE INTERNEES WHO FLED ACROSS THE BORDER 
LAST DECEMBER TO ESCAPE THE REDS. (THE PIASTRE IS OFFICIALLY WORTH 
5 UeSe CENTS, BUT IN HONGKONG THE OPEN MARKET QUOTES IT AT LESS THAN 
HALF THAT FIGURE). 

ABOUT 15,000 INTERNEES ARE ON PHUQUOC ISLAND OFF THE SOUTHWEST COAST 
OF INDOCHINA, ANOTHER 6,000 ARE INN CAMPS AROUND THE SHORE OF CAMRANH 
BAY, 170 MILES NORTHEAST OF SAIGON. 

THE INTERNEES HAVE BEEN A CONSTANT AND COSTLY HEADACHE TO THE FRENCH, 
WHO APPARENTLY ARE TRYING TO ADHERE TO INTERNATIONAL RULES IN THEIR 
TREATMENT. THEY FEAR THAT THE CHINESE REDS WILL SOMEHOW USE THE INTER= 
NEES AS A PRETEXT TO CAUSE FURTHER TROUBLE ALONG THE VULNERABLE BORDER 
WITH CHINA.

NEW YORK, JULY 15-(AP)-THE ALL-AMERICAN CONFERENCE TO COMBAT 
COMMUNISM (CAPS) SAID TODAY THAT SIGNATURES ON PEACE PETITIONS NOW 
BEING DISTRIBUTED IN THIS COUNTRY WILL BE USED AS A "SUCKER LIST" FOR 
SUBVERSIVE PROPAGANDA, 

THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL OF THE CONFERENCE SAID THE PETITIONS WERE 
"A DELIBERATE ATTEMPT TO EMBARRASS AND BLACKMAIL OUR GOVERNMENT IN ITS 
PRESENT EFFORT TO STAY THE HAND OF THE AGGRESSORS." 

THE PEACE PETITION NOW IS BEING DISTRIBUTED BY THE PEACE 
INFORMATION CENTER, WHICH CLAIMS 1,000,000 (M) AMERICANS ALREADY 
HAVE SIGNED IT. IT IS PATTERNED AFTER THE PETITION OF THE WORLD 
PEACE APPEAL, WHICH WAS ORGANIZED RECENTLY IN STOCKHOLM AND IS 

UPPORTED BY RUSSIA. 
. THE CONFERENCE STATEMENT SAID THE PETITION IS BEING CIRCULATED IN 
THIS COUNTRY UNDER DIRECTION OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY. 

"IT WILL BE USED AS A PROPAGANDA DEVICE TO CREATE ABROAD THE 
IMPRESSION OF DISUNITY IN OUR COUNTRY,® THE STATEMENT CONTINUED. 

"THE NEXT STEP WILL BE TO USE THE NAMES SIGNED TO THIS PETITION 
AS A "SUCKER LIST’ TO BE LATER BOMBARDED BY FALSE AND SUBVERSIVE 
PROPAGANDA." XXX 

AMONG THE ORGANIZATIONS REPRESENTED ON THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL ARE 
VETERANS’ GROUPS, RELIGIOUS ORGANIZATIONS, THE AMERICAN FEDERATION 
OF LABOR, AND FRATERNAL ORGANIZATIONS. 

THE CONFERENCE, SET UP LAST MAY WITH MORE THAN 60 MEMBER 
ORGANIZATIONS, CLAIMS A MEMBERSHIP OF 80,000,000 (M).

WASHINGTON, JULY 15=(AP)=-SERVICEMEN STILL ARE PROTECTED AGAINST 
ARBITRARY MORTGAGE FORECLOSURES, EVICTIONS, GARNISHMENT OF PAY AND 
OTHER CIVIL COURT ACTIONS. 

A SPOKESMAN FOR THE VETERANS ADMINISTRATION TOLD A REPORTER TODAY 
THE AGENCY IS GETTING HUNDREDS OF CALLS FROM WORRIED MEN AND WOMEN 
NOW IN MILITARY SERVICE. 


"THE SOLDIERS AND SAILORS CIVIL RELIEF ACT OF 1940 IS IN FULL FORCE," 
"SECTIONS OF THE ACT NULLIFIED BY THE JULY 25, 1947, PROCLA@ - 


HE SAID. 
MATION OF TERMINATION OF THE WAR WERE REINSTATED BY THE DRAFT ACT OF | 
1948, IN THE DRAFT ACT OF 1950 THEY WERE EXTENDED TO JULY 9, 
1951." 
THE ACT APPLIES TO ALL MEMBERS OF THE ARMY, NAVY, MARINE CORPS 
AND COAST GUARD, AND TO ALL PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICE OFFICERS DETAILED 
WITH THE ARMY OR NAVY. JUL 16 1550 
IT APPLIES TO ALL WHO ARE ON ACTIVE DUTY WITH ANY BRANCH,~AS WELL 
AS TO THOSE TAKING TRAINING OR EDUCATION UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF 
THE UNITED STATES, PRELIMINARY TO INDUCTION INTO MILITARY SERVICE. 
THE LAW PROVIDES THAT THE COURT APPOINT AN ATTORNEY TO PROTECT 
THE INTEREST OF A SERVICEMAN WHO IS ABSENT FROM A COURT ACTION. 
THE COURT MAY STAY THE ACTION, OR STAY EXECUTION OF AN ORDER OR 
JUDGMENT AGAINST A PERSON ON MILITARY DUTY, IF IT IS FOUND THAT THE 


SERVICEMAN HAS A MERITORIOUS OR LEGAL DEFENSE OR THAT HIS CIVIL RIGHTS 


MAY BE PREJUDICED BY HIS MILITARY SERVICE. 

THUS THE LAW PROVIDES FOR A STAY FOR THE PERIOD OF MILITARY SERVICE 
AND THREE MONTHS AFTERWARD, AGAINST3 

1. ATTACHMENT OR GARNISHMENT OF PROPERTY, MONEY OR DEBTS IN THE 
HANDS OF ANOTHER. 

2. EVICTION FROM PREMISES RENTING FOR NOT MORE THAN $80 A MONTH 
AND USED CHIEFLY FOR DWELLING PURPOSE BY THE SERVICEMAN’S WIFE, CHILD- 
REN OR DEPENDENTS. DEFENSE OFFICIALS MAY ORDER AN ALLOTMENT OF THE 
SERVICEMAN’S PAY TO BE APPLIED AGAINST RENTALS. 

3. REPOSSESSION, FOR NON-PAYMENT OF INSTALLMENTS, OF PURCHASED 
PROPERTY. 

4. ENFORCED COLLECTION OF PROPERTY TAXES FALLING DUE DURING 
MILITARY SERVICE. 


THE LAW ALSO PROHIBITS THE FORFEITING OF HOMESTEADING LAND OR MINING

(ADVANCE) WASHINGTON, JULY 15-(AP)-THE UNITED STATES’ ULTRA LONG- 
RANGE BOMBER FORCE» THE WEAPON DESIGNED FOR INSTANTANEOUS RETALIATION 
SHOULD AMERICA BE ATTACKED, IS SITTING OUT THIS KOREAN WAR. 

IT APPEARS DESTINED TO STAY OUT OF ACTION UNLESS MORE THAN KOREA 
e 

AIRMEN SAID TODAY THERE IS NO INDICATION THE Be-36 INTERCONTINENTAL 
BOMBERS WILL BE NEEDED OR THAT ANY OF THE GIANT PLANES WOULD APPEAR IN &amp; 
THE WAR ZONEUNLESS THE AIR FORCE SHOULD DECIDE IT WANTED TO TEST A 
FEW UNDER COMBAT CONDITIONS. 

THE POINT THEY MAKE IS THAT IN THE KOREAN THEATRE THERE ARE VIRTUAL 
LY NO STRATEGIC BOMBING TARGETS, EXCEPT FOR AN OIL REFINERY OR TWO 
AND SOME RAIL CENTERS. 

PROPONENTS OF THE B-36 SAY 17 ISN'T INTENDED FOR ISLAND WARFARE 
FOR MAKING SHORT STRIKES AT RANGES OF ONLY A FEW HUNDRED MILES. THEY 
FEEL IT IS RESERVED PRIMARILY FOR OPERATION FROM HOME BASES AGAINST 
TARGETS DEEP_IN SOME DISTANT ENEMY HOMELAND. 

THIS ISN'T TO SAY THE B-36 CAN'T OR WON'T BE USED FOR SHORT-HAUL 
JOBS» ITS ENORMOUS LOAD-LIFTING CAPABILITY COULD HAVE ADVANTAGE. | 
THE B-36 CAN GET INTO THE AIR FOR EXTREMELY SHORT MISSIONS WITH MORE 
THAN 80,000 POUNDS OF BOMBS. BUT ITS INTENDED MISSION IS LONG RANGE 
STRATEGIC BOMBING. 

STRATEGIC BOMBING IS SUSTAINED AIR ATTACK ON WAR PLANTS» INDUSTRIAL 
CITIES, ALL THE PLACES WHERE MUNITIONS FOR FIGHTING A WAR ARE PRODUCED

KOREA. THEY COME FROM BEYOND THE CURTAIN TO JHE NORTH,: FROM ANOTHER

, TACTICAL AIR OPERATION ARE INTENDED TO "ISOLATE THE BATTLEFIELD.”

QUARTERS AND COMMAND POSTS. TACTICAL AIR WAR INVOLVES JUST ABOUT

TOKYO, MONDAY, JULY 17-(AP)-FOLLOWING IS THE TEXT OF COMMUNIQUE 
NOs 85 FROM GENERAL MACARTHUR'S HEADQUARTERS ISSUED AT 9 AeM. MONDAY, 
JAPAN DAYLIGHT TIME (6 PeMe SUNDAY, EASTERN STANDARD TIME) 

PRIOR TO THE PRESENT EMERGENCY, THE SUPPLY OF PETROLEIUM PRODUCTS FOR 
THE CIVIL ECONOMY OF THE REPUBLIC’ OF KOREA WAS ACCOMPLISHED BY THE 
KOREAN OIL STORAGE COMPANY, A DELAWARE CORPORATION OWNED BY FOREIGN 
COMMERCIAL OIL COMPANIES AND OPERATING UNDER A SUPPLY AND SERVICE 
CONTRACT WITH THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. 

SUSSEQUENT TO THE INVASION OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA BY NORTH COM- 
MUNIST FORCES. ALL PETROLEUM “PERSONNEL WERE EVACUATED TO JAPAN LEAVING 
PETROLEUM FACILITIES AND STOCKS IN THE CUSTODY OF NATIVE KOREANS. 
““"THE UNITED STATES GOVERNMENT IMMEDIATELY TOOK STEPS TO GIVE 
LOGISTIC SUPPORT TO THE SOUTH KOREAN ARMIES. IN ACCORDANCE WITH UeS. 
DIRECTIVES, THE AREA PETROLEUM OFFICE, UNDER THE LOGISTIC RESPON- 
SIBILITY OF THE UeSeARMY AND STAFFED BY REPRESENTATIVES OF THE ARMY, 
NAVY AND ATR FORCE. ASSUMED RESPONSIBILITY TO SUPPLY PETROLEUM TO ALL 
UNITED NATIONS FORCES OPERATING IN KOREA. 

THE INITIAL ACTION REQUIRED THAT A TERMINAL IN KOREA BE ADEQUATELY 
STAFFED AND OPERATED. THE AREA PETROLEUM OFFICE INITIATED A SEARCH 
AMONG EVACUEES FROM KOREA AND LOCATED KOSCO PERSONNEL FAMILIAR 
WITH KOREAN PETROLEUM TERMINAL OPERATION. SIX OF THESE PERSONNEL 
WERE LOCATED AND UPON CAREFUL INTERROGATION REVEALED THAT AN AVAILABLE 

ERMINAL WAS WELL STOCKED AND IN EXCELLENT OPERATING CONDITION. 
COLeEARL ReCHASE, THE AREA PETROLEUM OFFICER, IMMEDIATELY MADE ARRANGE- 
MENTS FOR THESE {NDIVIDUALS (WHO VOLUNTEERED FOR THIS DUTY), PLUS A 
SMALL DETACHMENT OF MILITARY PERSONNEL, TO BE FLOWN TO KOREA AND THE 
TERMINAL OPENED FOR IMMEDIATE OPERATION. PUL Py 7% 

THE TERMINAL WAS OPENED AND STARTED OPERATION ON JULY Se . SINCE’ THAT 
DATE, THIS TERMINAL HAS BEEN CAPABLE OF SUPPLYING THE REQUIREMENTS TO 
ALL MILITARY FORCES IN KOREA, WITH AUTOMATIC RESUPPLY FROM OTHER SOURCES 
IN THE FAR EAST COMMAND. 

THE STAFF OF THE AREA PETROLEUM OFFICE, THROUGH CONSTRUCTIVE PLANNING 
AND FORESIGHT, HAS PROVIDED FOR ADEQUATE STOCK OF PETROLEUM PRODUCTS TO 
SATISFY THE IMMEDIATE REQUIREMENTS OF ALL THE UNITED NATIONS FORCES 
OPERATING IN THE FAR EAST AREA. 

NO FUTURE SHORTAGES ARE CONTEMPLATED AS ARRANGEMENTS HAVE BEEN 
MADE TO INSURE A CONSTANT FLOW OF PETROLEUM SUPPLY TO REACH PETROLEUM 
TERMINALS IN THE FAR EAST IN SUFFICIENT QUANTITIES TO MEET ALL MILITARY 
REQUIREMENTS. 

(END TEXT)

(400) STARS AND STRIPES (BA ASKED) 

TOKYO, JULY 16-(AP)=THE HEAT AND SAVAGERY OF THE FIGHTING IN 
KOREA IS GETTING ACROSS TO AMERICAN TROORS..HERE THROUGH THE OFFICIAL 
ARMY NEWSPAPER, "STARS AND STRIPES." BUT THIS ASPECT OF THE WAR 
IS DESCRIBED MAINLY IN PICTURES. 

THE NEWSPAPER APPARENTLY IS UNDER EDITORIAL WRAPS. SO IS THE ARMED 
THE RADIO APPEARS TO BE UNDER TIGHTER CONTROL, 
POSSIBLY BECAUSE ITS BROADCASTS ARE MORE ACCESSIBLE TO COMMUNIST 
MONITORS THAN A PRINTED NEWSPAPER. 

TOP@=RANKING OFFICERS NEVER HAVE ACKNOWLEDGED THE EXISTENCE OF 
CENSORSHIP OVER THESE TWO SOLDIER INFORMATION SERVICES. BUT 
THROUGHOUT THE OCCUPATION ALL STORIES BEARING ON ARMY OR OCCUPATION 
POLICY HAVE BEEN SCRUTINIZED BEFORE PUBLICATION BY KEY OFFICERSe 
MANY STORIES HAVE BEEN *KILLED.® 

SINCE AMERICAN FORCES ENTERED THE KOREAN CAMPAIGN, THE SCREENING 
SEEMS TIGHTER. ON THE WHOLE, “STARS AND STRIPES" AND THE RADIO HAVE 
CONFINED THEIR GENERAL COVERAGE TO INFORMATION CONTAINED IN OFFICIAL 
COMMUNIQUES. 

SOMETIMES LEAD STORIES BASED ON THE COMMUNIQUES AND DISTRIBUTED BY 
AMERICAN NEWS AGENCIES ARE USED. ON OTHER OCCASIONS EVEN THESE 
APPARENTLY HAVE BEEN TOO "HOT" AND AT THE LAST MINUTE "STARS AND 
STRIPES" MET A DELAYED DEADLINE BY CARRYING ONLY THE TEXT OF 
COMMUNIQUES. ac po we 

THE PAPER AND THE RADIO BOTH SUBSCRIBE TO THE ASSOCIATED PRESS, 
UNITED PRESS, AND INTERNATIONAL NEWS SERVICE. NEITHER HAS USED 
ANY STORIES REFLECTING THE DESPAIR AND SHOCK OF FRONTLINE 

AMERICAN TROOPS AFTER THEIR FIRST CONTACT WITH THE ENEMY. 

THE NEWSPAPER USED A FULL FRONT PAGE LAYOUT OF PICTURES SHOWING 
AMERICAN SOLDIERS WHO HAD SURRENDERED AND WHO HAD BEEN SHOT BY THE NOR’ 
KOREANS WHILE THEIR HANDS WERE TIED. THE CAPTION READ: *WITHOUT A 
CHANCE," 

OTHER PHOTOGRAPHERS HAVE RANGED FROM THOSE SHOWING THE LONELINESS 
OF A FRONTLINE AMERICAN OUTPOST TO OTHERS VIVIDLY PORTRAYING THE HEAT 
AND THE DIRT. 

ONE OF THE TWO CORRESPONDENTS KILLED DURING HOSTILITIES WAS CPL. 
ERNIE PEELER OF "STARS AND STRIPES," A FORMER SAN BERNARDINO, CALIFe, 
NEWSMAN. HE HAD ARRIVED AT THE FRONT ONLY A SHORT TIME BEFORE AND HAD 
BEGUN SENDING BACK FEATURE DISPATCHES WITH A GI ANGLE. 

SOLDIERS HAVE GRUMBLED AT THE RESTRAINTS. FRONTLINE TROOPS HAVE 
BEEN QUOTED AS SAYING THE PAPER WAS DESCRIBING THEIR ACTIVITIES TOO 
LIGHTLY. 

ARMY OFFICERS HAVE SAID THAT "STARS AND STRIPES" AND THE ARMED 
FORCES RADIO ARE WATCHED FOR THEIR EFFECT ON TROOP MORALE. 

PRESUMABLY THIS MEANS, IN THE PRESENT CIRCUMSTANCES, THERE IS AN 
EFFORT TO WITHHOLD SOME OF THE UGLINESS FROM YOUNGSTERS WHO MAY 


BE SENT TO THE LINE NEXT.

WASHINGTON, JULY 16-(AP)-YONGJEMMGKIM, PRESIDENT OF THE KOREAN 
AFFAIRS INSTITUTE, TODAY SUGGESTED REPLACING THE SOUTH KOREAN GOVERN- 
MENT OF SYNGMAN RHEE WITH A UNITED NATIONS CIVIL GOVERNMENT. 

THE INSTITUTE IS A FOUR=MAN AFFAIR, COMPOSED OF MEMBERS OF THE 
KIM FAMILY IN THE UNITED STATES. IT WAS INCORPORATED IN CALIFORNIA 
IN 1943 AS A NON=PROFIT CULTURAL ORGANIZATION. 

KIM, IN A LETTER TO TRYGVE LIE, SECRETARY GENERAL OF THE UNITED 
NATIONS, SAID$ 

"AS THE RECENT ELECTION PROVED, THE PRESENT GOVERNMENT OF THE 
REPUBLIC OF (SOUTH) KOREA IS DISCREDITED BECAUSE OF ITS REPRESSION 
AND MISRULE. 

"THEREFORE IT IS ESSENTIAL TGAT THE UNITED NATIONS CREATE A BODY 
TO TAKE OVER THE CIVIL ADMINISTRATION WITHOUT DELAY UNTIL KOREA'S 
CASE IS FINALLY SETTLED. OTHERWISE IT WILL APPEAR NOT ONLY TO THE 
KOREANS, BUT TO THE OTHER PEOPLES OF ASIA AS WELL, THAT THE UNITED 
NATIONS IS ATTEMPTING TO SAVE AN UNPOPULAR GOVERNMENT." 

KIM ALSO SUGGESTED THAT MEDIATION OF THE CONFLICT BETWEEN NORTH 
KOREA AND SOUTH KOREA "IS THE IMMEDIATE TASK AT HAND" SINCE, HE 
DECLARED, CATASTROPHE IS FACING MILLIONS OF INNOCENT KOREANS.« 

KIM ASSERTED THAT "IN COMMON WITH MOST ORIENTALS, THE KOREAN 
PEOPLE AS A WHOLE HAVE NO CLEAR UNDERSTANDING OF, OR AFFINITY WITH, 
EITHER DEMOCRACY OR COMMUNISM. X X X IT WOULD BE ONLY WISHFUL THINKING 
THEREFORE, FOR AMERICANS TO EXPECT ANY LARGE SEGMENT OF THE KOREAN 
NATION SPONTANEOUSLY TO RALLY TO THEIR SIDE." 

THE MEMBERS OF THE KOREAN INSTITUTE, BESIDE YONGJEUNG KIM ARE 
C.H, KIM, HARRY Ss KIM AND WARREN Y. KIM, OF REEDLEY, CALIF. THE KIMS

BY WILLIAM ANDERSON (640) 

BASTOGNE, BELGIUM, JULY 16-(AP)-THOUSANDS OF GRATEFUL BELGIANS 
STOOD IN POURING RAIN TODAY ON THE HILL OF LE MARDASSON TO HONOR 
AMERICAN SOLDIERS WHO FELL IN THE ARDENNES BATTLE OF THE BULGE. 

THE BELGIANS PAID THEIR SOLEMN TRIBUTE AT THE UNVEILING OF THE 
BASTOGNE HILLTOP STAR-SHAPED MONUMENT COMMEMORATING THE BATTLE OF 
FIVE YEARS AGO. 

THE VAST THRONG, WHICH INCLUDED MANY AMERICANS, STOOD BAREHEADED 
AS THE FLAG-DECKED’ MONUMENT WAS OFFICIALLY DEDICATED "TO THE ENDURING 
FRIENDSHIP OF THE PEOPLE OF BELGIUM AND AMERICA." 

A MESSAGE FROM PRESIDENT TRUMAN WAS READ AT THE CEREMONY BY 
AMERICAN AMBASSADOR ROBERT DeMURPHY. 

MAJ. GEN. ANTHONY C. MCAULIFFE, WHO DEFIED A GERMAN DEMAND TO 
SURRENDER. WITH HIS FAMOUS "NUTS" ’RETORT, DEDICATED THE MEMORIAL. 

GEN. MCAULIFFE'S 101ST AIRBORNE DIVISION -- PART OF GEN. GEORGE 
S. PATTON'S THIRD ARMY -- WAS SURROUNDED BY 25 GERMAN DIVISIONS WHICH 
BROKE THROUCH THE ARDENNES IN DECEMBER, 1944, IN A DESPERATE ATTEMPT 
TO REACH THE PORT OF ANTWERP AND SHUT OFF SUPPLIES TO THE ALLIED FORCES 
DRIVING TOWARD CERMANY. THE 101ST HELD OUT FOR SEVEN DAYS AGAINST 
THE ENEMY DRIVE. SUBSEQUENTLY LARGE CONCENTRATIONS OF ALLIED PLANES 
AND GROUND TROOPS FORCED THE NAZIS BACK. 

ANTWERP WAS SAVED AND THE ROAD TO GERMANY OPENED, BUT 76,890 
AMERICAN SOLDIERS WERE DEAD, WOUNDED OR MISSING ON BELGIAN UOIL. 

"NOW ' 


AMERICAN SOLDIERS WERE es ge OR MISSING ON BELGIAN SOIL. 


"NOW BELGIUM AND THE UNITED STATES, WITH OTHER ATLANTIC NATIONS, 
ARE JOINED IN COMRADESHIP TO RESIST A NEW THREAT TO OUR LIBERTIES 
SAID GEN. MCAULIFFE. "MY GOVERNMENT HAS ANNOUNCED THAT A THREAT To 
THE FREEDOM OF BELGIUM, OR TO ANY OTHER FREE NATION, IS ALSO A 
THREAT TO THE FREEDOM OF THE UNITED STATES." 

MCAULIFFE SAID AT THE FIRST SIGN OF MILITARY ATTACK THE RESOURCES 
OF THE FREE NATIONS WILL BE THROWN INTO THE COMMON CAUSE OF DEFENSE. 

"WITH OUR COMBINED SCIENTIFIC AND INDUSTRIAL SUPREMACY AND THE 
DETERMINATION OF OUR PEOPLES NOT TO BE ENSLAVED," HE ADDED, “THERE

REMEMBER THAT FREEDOM CAN BE MAINTAINED ONLY BY STRENGTH AND VIGILANCE 
AND BY WILLINGNESS TO FIGHT FOR ITS PRESERVATION.” 

_, "THE YOUNGER BROTHERS .OF THOSE WHOSE MEMORY WE HONOR TODAY ARE 
FIGHTING NOW WITH EQUAL TENACITY AND COURAGE FOR FREEDOM ON A FAR- 
FLUNG (KOREAN) BATTLE FRONT,*® THE AMBASSADOR SAID.

AMERICAN WAR EFFORT." 

{HE MONUMENT STANDS 40 FEET HIGH. IN BRONZE LETTERS ARE THE 
NAMES OF THE 48 STATES. ON THE INSIDE WALL OF A HOLLOW CIRCLE AT THE 
MONUMENT CENTER IS WRITTEN THE HISTORY OF THE BATTLE, WITH THE NAMES 
AND INSIGNIA OF THE PARTICIPATING UNITS. 

FROM THE AIR THE MONUMENT FORMS A FIVE-POINTED STAR, THE TIPS OF 
WHICH ARE 101 FEET, SIX INCHES FROM THE CENTER.

FOLLOWING IS THE TEXT OF PRESIDENT TRUMAN'S MESSAGE, READ 
BY AMBASSADOR MURPHY: 

AS YOU DEDICATE THE NOBLE MONUMENTS TO THE AMERICAN ARMED FORCES AT 
BASTOGNE, IT IS DIFFICULT TO REALIZE THAT ONLY A FEW SHORT YEARS 
AGO THE FIELDS AND FORESTS OF THE ARDENNES BORE ONE OF THE MOST 
BITTER BATTLES OF THE WAR. ON THIS SPOT THE BACKBONE OF HITLER'S ARMED 
FORCES WAS BROKEN, FOR HIS INABILITY TO REDUCE BASTOGNE DOOMED HIS 
FINAL OFFENSIVE TO FAILURE. 

THIS MEMORIAL, EMBAZONED WITH THE NAMES OF THE 48 STATES OF THE 
UNITED STATES, IS MORE THAN A MEMORIAL TO THOSE MEN AND WOMEN OF 
THE AMERICAN ARMED FORCES WHO GAVE THEIR LIVES IN ORDER THAT 
FREEDOM AND DEMOCRACY MIGHT LIVE. IT IS AN ENDURING TESTIMONIAL TO THE 
COMMON DEVOTION OF OUR TWO COUNTRIES TO THE CAUSE OF FREEDOM AND TO 
THEIR PARTNERSHIP IN ARMS FOR ITS DEFENSE, 

BELGIUM AND THE UNITED STATES SHARE A LOVE OF FREEDOM THAT 





SPRINGS FROM THE ROOTS OF OUR NATIONAL CHARACTERS. WE HAVE STOOD 
SIDE BY SIDE THROUGHOUT TWO WORLDWIDE CONFLICTS IN DEFENSE OF 
FREEDOM, TODAY WE FIND OURSELVES PARTNERS IN PEACE IN THE NORTH 
ATLANTIC TREATY. BOTH OF OUR NATIONS FERVENTLY DESIRE PEACE~- 
PERMANENT, EVERLASTING PEACE--BUT NEITHER OF US IS WILLING TO BUY 
THAT PEACE AT THE PRICE OF OUR LIBERTY. AS WE HAVE STOOD UNITED BEFORE 
WHEN OUR LIBERTY HAS BEEN ENDANGERED, WE STAND UNITED TODAY IN THE 
HOPE THAT PROOF OF OUR DETERMINATION TO FIGHT AGAIN FOR OUR 
LIBERTY, IF NECESSARY, WILL MAKE IT UNNECESSARY FOR US TO DO SO. 
IN FREEDOM THERE IS STRENGTH AND IN UNION THERE IS STRENGTH. BOTH 
OUR NATIONS ARE FOUNDED ON THESE PRINCIPLES. 

THIS MONUMENT COMMEMORATES OUR JOINT EFFORTS IN A BATTLE WITH 
HITLERITE GERMANY. NEVER AGAIN MUST WE PERMIT GERMANY OR ANY OTHER 
NATION TO LAUNCH SUCH DESTRUCTION. IN SPITE OF THE SUFFERING SO 
BRAVELY ENDURED BY BELGIUM AS A RESULT OF GERMAN AGGRESSION, THE 
BELGIAN PEOPLE HAVE SHOWN VISION, RESTRAINT AND UNDERSTANDING TOWARD 
THE GERMAN. 

IN THIS ATTITUDE WE FIND A SOURCE OF HOPE AND ENCOURAGEMENT, 

FOR ONLY VISION, RESTRAINT, AND UNDERSTANDING CAN BUILD A NEW 
EUROPE, ALL OF WHOSE PEOPLES CAN LIVE AND WORK TOGETHER IN PEACE 
AND FREEDOM. 

IN FUTURE YEARS WE CAN HOPE THAT OUR CHILDREN AND GRAND CHILDREN 
WILL LOOK UPON THIS MEMORIAL AND KNOW ITS MEANING BUT WITHOUT THE 
BURNING MEMORY OF WAR'S HORROR--HAVING READ OF IT IN THEIR HISTORY 
BOOKS BUT NOT KNOWING ITS ACTUALITY--AND WITH THE CONTINUED COOPERATION 
OF THE FREEDOM-LOVING NATIONS OF THE WORLD, WITH GOD'S HELP AND HIS 
GUIDANCE, THAT HOPE MAY WELL BECOME A REALITY. 

(END TEXT)

“MIGRATION FROM-OMER@ROPULATED NATIONS OF WESTERN EUROPE. 

THE MARSHALL PLAN NATIONS THEMSELVES WILL CONTRIBUTE AN ADDITIONAL 
$200,000 TOWARD THE PROJECT IN THEIR OWN CURRENCIES, THE EUROPEAN 
RECOVERY AGENCY SAID. 

ALONG WITH ITS ANNOUNCEMENT, ECA MADE PUBLIC A LETTER FROM 
PRESIDENT TRUMAN DESCRIBING THE PROGRAM AS "A NECESSARY STEP TOWARD 
THE SOLUTION OF ONE OF THE BASIC PROBLEMS WHICH WESTERN EUROPE EN- 
COUNTERS IN ITS RECOVERY EFFORT." 

THE MONEY WILL BE USED FOR TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE IN CONNECTION WITH 
EFFORTS TO HELP EMIGRANTS--CHIEFLY FROM ITALY AND WESTERN RERMANY-- 
FIND JOBS ELSEWHERE. 

UNDER SUPERVISION OF THE INTERNATIONAL LABOR ORGANIZATION, A UNITED 
NATIONS AGENCY, SURVEYS WILL BE CONDUCTED IN OVER-POPULATED NATIONS 
TO DETERMINE THE NUMBERS AND SKILLS OF PERSONS LIKELY TO EMIGRATE 
AT THE SAME TIME PROPOSED "IMMIGRATION COUNTRIES*® WILL BE SURVEYED TO 
DETERMINE THEIR EMPLOYMENT PROSPECTS.

ATTACKS ALONG THE U. Se 24TH DIVISION, HAVE ALSO REORGANIZED THEIR

AVERAGED ONLY FOUR MILES A DAY FROM CHONAN TO THE OUTSKIRTS OF TAEJON.

OCCUPIED BY THE COMMUNIST FOURTH AND FIFTH DIVISIONS.

INTEGRATED AS A TEAM FOR THESE STRIKES AND HAVE INFLICTED HEAVY 
DAMAGE ON RED PERSONNEL AND MATERIEL. 

NAVAL FORCES ON TE EAST COAST CONTINUED TO POUND THE TARGETS 
ON THE COASTAL ROAD, 

SUCCESSFUL FIRING INTO CLIFFS HAVE CAUSED LANDSLIDES WHICH HAVE 
SLOWED DOWN MOVEMENTS ALONG THE EAST COAST ROADS.

LONDON, JULY 17-(AP)-THE FIVE BRUSSELS UNION_ALLIES, FACED WITH 
DEMANDS ON THEIR MILITARY RESOURCES BECAUSE OF THE KOREAN_WAR, 
UNEXPECTEDLY CALLED A MEETING OF THEIR DEFENSE MINISTERS FOR THURSDAY. 

A FOREIGN OFFICE SPOKESMAN SAID TODAY THE MEETING WILL BE HELD AT 
FONTAINBLEAU NEAR PARIS. HE DESCRIBED IT AS "ROUTINE." THE FIVE 
ALLIES ARE BRITAIN, FRANCE, BELGIUM, HOLLAND AND LUXEMBOURG. 

THEIR CONFERENCE IS EXPECTED TO COVER MOST ASPECTS OF WEST 
EUROPE'S STRATEGIC OFFENSE PROBLEMS IN THE LIGHT OF THE POWERS' FAR 
EASTERN COMMITMENTS. BRITAIN, FRANCE AND HOLLAND ALL HAVE MILITARY 
COMMITMENTS IN THE FAR EAST. 

THEIR SESSION WILL BE FOLLOWED FIVE DAYS LATER BY THE FIRST MEETING 
OF SPECIALLY APPOINTED DEPUTIES REPRESENTING THE 12 ATLANTIC PACT 
ALLIES. THEY WILL MEET IN LONDON. AMERICA'S CHARLES M.SPOFFORD IS 
EXPECTED TO BE NAMED PERMANENT CHAIRMAN OF THE COUNCIL. 

THE DEPUTIES’ JOB--ASSIGNED TO THEM LAST MAY BY THE FOREIGN 
MINISTERS OF THE ATLANTIC PACT NATIONS=-WILL BE TO SPEED WESTERN 
REARMAMENT AND TO FIGURE OUT A MASTER=PLAN FOR WESTERN DEFENSEe 

INFORMED DIPLOMATIC SOURCES SAID THE DEFENSE MINISTERS ARE LIKELY 
JOINTLY TO CONSIDER THE UNITED NATIONS REQUEST TO MEMBERS, TO SEND_ 
GROUND FORCES TO KOREA. JUL 18 igad 

THE BRUSSELS UNION PARTNERS ARE BOUND BY THEIR ALLIANCE TO ACT 
IN CONCERT IN THEIR STRATEGIC AND DEFENSE PROBLEMS. 

INFORMANTS SAID ANY ACTION WHICH ONE OF THE PARTNERS MIGHT TAKE 
IN COMPLYING WITH THE U.N. CALL FOR HELP IN KOREA, INEVITABLY WOULD 
AFFECT THE FORCES WHICH THEY HAVE AT THEIR DISPOSAL FOR WEST 
EUROPEAN DEFENSE. 

JOB OF THE MINISTERS PRESUMABLY IS TO WORK OUT JUST WHAT 
HELP THE PARTNERSHIP AS A WHOLE CAN AFFORD TO SEND TO KOREA 
WITHOUT LEAVING THE DEFENSES OF WEST EUROPE WIDE OPEN,

BY ALEX SINGLETON 

BELGRADE, JULY 17=C€AP)-A GOVERNMENT-SPONSORED YUGOSLAV..PEACE 
CONGRESS FORMALLY CONDEMNED TODAY RUSSIA'S "TERRORISTIC" CAMPAIGN 
OF PRESSURE AGAINST THIS COUNTRY. IT CALLED FOR SETTLEMENT OF ALL 
INTERNATIONAL DISPUTES BY AGREEMENT. 

THE CONFERENCE BRINGING TOGETHER MORE THAN A THOUSAND 
REPRESENTATIVES OF PEACE ORGANIZATIONS THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY, 

SET FORTH ITS STAND IN A NINE=POINT RESOLUTION REGISTERING 
YUGOSLAVIA'S DETERMINATION TO REMAIN INDEPENDENT IN THE COLD WAR 
BETWEEN THE EAST AND WEST. 

"YUGOSLAVIA HAS NOT AND CAN NOT HAVE ANY AGGRESSIVE DESIGNS 
TOWARDS OTHER COUNTRIES AND WILL NEVER RESORT TO ARMS AS A MEANS 
OF ITS NATIONAL POLICY EXCEPT IN SELF DEFENSE,” THE RESOLUTION SAID. 

THE RESOLUTION WAS ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY AFTER MILOVAN DJILAS, A TOP 
RANKING SPOKESMAN FOR PREMIER MARSHAL TITO'S GOVERNMENT, DENOUNCED 
THE RUSSIAN-LED COMINFORM'S "HEIGHTENED CAMPAIGN OF LIES AND THREATS 
AND ORGANIZATION OF VARIOUS SALLIES AGAINST OUR LAND.® 

SIMULTANEOUSLY, HE PROCLAIMED YUGOSLAVIA'S HOPE AND WILLINGNESS 
THAT "ALL QUESTIONS WHICH THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT AND THE GOVERNMENTS 
OF THE EASTERN EUROPEAN COUNTRIES CONSIDER TO BE DISPUTED COULD 
BE SETTLED BY AGREEMENT WITHOUT DAMAGE TO THE SOVEREIGNTY OR PRESTIGE 
OF ANY ONE OF THEM." 

THE CONGRESS ALSO ADOPTED ANOTHER RESOLUTION INVITING 
REPRESENTATIVES OF WORLD PEACE ORGANIZATIONS TO VISIT THIS 
COUNTRY TO SEE FOR THEMSELVES WHETHER OR NOT THERE IS ANY 
JUSTIFICATION IN-THE-COMINFORM'S CHARGES THAT YUGOSLAVIA IS PREPARING 
FOR AN AGGRESSIVE WAR. 

THE RESOLUTION SAID THE DELEGATION ALSO SHOULD VISIT THE OTHER 
EASTERN EUROPEAN COUNTRIES TO SEE WHO SHOULD BE BLAMED FOR ANY 
"AGGRESSIVE PREPARATION."

IN "DELAYING ACTION" (WHICH IS WHAT THE AMERICAN FORCES ARE DOING IN 
XOREA NOW) REQUIRES APPROXIMATELY 436 TONS OF SUPPLIES A DAY. THIS 
INCLUDES 4S TONS OF FOOD AND SIMILAR EQUIPMENT; 42 TONS OF CLOTHING, 
WEAPONS REPLACEMENTS. VEHICULAR MATERIAL, CONSTRUCTION AND ENGINEER 
FQUIPMENT: 111 TONS OF FUEL AND LUBRICANTS; 235 TONS OF AMMUNITION,

OPERATIONS. ANTI-TANK MINES ETCe

MENTS, STRANGELY, DROP OFF TO AN ESTIMATED 296 TONS. THIS IS BECAUSE 
CONTACT WITH THE’ ENEMY IS LESS, WITH A CONSEQUENT REDUCTION IN EXPEN- 
DITURE OF SUCH ITEMS AS AMMUNITION. HOWEVER, OTHER ITEMS GO UP, 
INCLUDING FUEL USED FOR PURSUING THE ENEMY.

WASHINGTON. JULY 17-CAP)-SENATOR LODGE (R=-MASS) URGENTLY CALLED 
TODAY FOR IMMEDIATE MOBILIZATION OF AMERICAN MANPOWER AND INDUSTRY, AND 
A SPEED-UP IN REARMING WESTERN EUROPE, TO BLOCK RUSSIAN AIMS FOR 
WORLD DOMINATION. 

"IN SOBER TRUTH OUR VERY NATIONAL EXISTENCE IS AT STAKE," LODGE 
TOLD THE SENATE. "WE HAVE NOT A MINUTE TO LOSE. WE MUST NOT 
STUMBLE AROUND AT THE THRESHOLD OF DISASTER." 

LODGE'S SPFECH CAME SHORTLY AFTER SENATOR BRIDGES (R-NH) HAD SAID 
CONGRESS WILL GIVE THE ARMED SERVICES ANY NEEDED INCREASE IN FUNDS 
"OUT THEY VILL HAVE TO USE IT BETTER THAN SOME MONEY HAS BEEN USED IN 

IE PAST." | 

LODGE, A MEMBER OF THE SENATE FOREIGN RELATIONS COMMITTEE, SAID IT 
IS "CENTRALLY ACCEPTED THAT THE SOVIETS WILL HAVE ENOUGH ATOMIC 
BOMBS TO STRIKE A RUGCED BLOW AT THE UNITED STATES IN 1952-53." 

HE SUGGESTED THAT THE KOREAN INVASION, FOLLOWED BY SIMILAR MOVES IN 
OTHER STRATEGIC AREAS AND LATER SEIZURE AF THE RUHR AND JAPAN, COULD 
INCLUDE WITH AN ATOMIC ATTACK ON THIS NATION. 

IT ALL FITS NEATLY INTO THE TIME SCHEDULE AND CONCIDES WITH WHAT 
WE ARE TOLD ABOUT THE SOVIET PLANE-CUN-TANK BUILDING PROGRAMS, HE SAID. 

LODGE CONTENDED THERE IS NO NEED TO "SIT IDLY BY AND STUPIDLY 
WATCH SUCH A GRIM TRAGEDY UNFOLD BEFORE OUR FRIGHTENED EYES." 

HE SAID WE MUST RECOGNIZE THAT WE ARE IN A MAJOR WAR IN KOREA AND 
MUST "QUICKLY CREATE A SITUATION OF MILITARY STRENGTH." HE ADDED THAT 
THIS MEANS NOTHING LESS THAN "IMMEDIATE MOBILIZATION OF AMERICAN 


MANPOWER AND INDUSTRY,"

MANF AN HNOPPOSED AMPHIBIOUS LANDING ON THE EAST COAST.

A Us Ss BEAGHHEAD IN KOREA, (BY COURIER TO TOKYO( JULY 18-8 AP)= 
U. S. GROUND TROOPS MADE THEIR FIRST AMPHIBIOUS ASSAULT LANDING OF TEE 
KOREAN CAMPAIGN TODAY. —s_ 


AMERICAN SOLDIERS STORMED ASHORE UNOPPOSED ON THE EAST COAST OF THz 
PENINSULA. 


THE LANDING WAS MADE IN STRENGTH IN FRONT OF THE ENEMY LINE. 
VTWAS IN AN AREA WHERE NORTH KOREAN GUERRILLAS HAVE BEEN ACTIVE 
BUT NOT A SHOT WAS FIRED AGAINST THE AMERICANS. 


THE TROOPS LANDED FROM A CONVOY PROTECTED BY AMERICAN WARSHIPS AND 
COVERED BY AN AIR UMBRELLA OF U. Se AND BRITISH FIGHTER PLANES. 

THE SWIFT MOVE FROM THE SEA WAS DESIGNED TO BLOCK THE COMMUNIST 
ARMY'S SOUTHWARD DRIVE BY REINFORCING U. S. AND SOUTH KOREAN FORCES 


ADVANCE PARTIES HAD GONE INTO THE INVASION AREA AS MUCH AS A d 
WEEK BEFORE D-DAY. THE LANDING SITE WAS CAREFULLY SELECTED TO INSURE 
A MINIMUM OF OPPOSITION. BUT REPORTS INDICATED THE NORTH KOREANS WERE 
NOT VERY FAR AWAY. 

H-HOUR WAS 0700 (7 _A.sMe)s WITHIN A SHORT TIME THE AMERICANS HAD 
MOVED INLAND FIVE TO SEVEN MILES WITH A STRONG FORCE BUILDING 
UP IN FRONT OF THE NORTHERN ADVANCE IN THAT SECTOR. 

BECAUSE OF THE COMPARATIVE SAFETY OF THE LANDING SITE, THE ASSAULT 
FORCES WERE MORE AFRAID OF POSSIBLE DAMAGE FROM APPROACHING TYPHOONS 
THAN FROM ENEMY ACTION. 

TWO TYPHOONS WERE REPORTED APPROACHING THE KOREAN PENINSULA *ROM 
THE SOUTHWEST AND IT WAS FEARED THEY MIGHT RIP ACROSS THIS AREA. 


THE AMERICAN LANDING WAS THE BIGGEST MOVEMENT OF TROOPS INTO THE 
SOUTH KOREAN FRONT SINCE THE 24TH INFANTRY DIVISION WAS COMMITTED 
TO ACTION IN SMALL UNITS IN THE FIRST DELAYING ACTIONS AGAINST THE REDS. 
THE COMMANDING GENERAL TOLD NEWS CORRESPONDENTS : 
"OUR JOB IS TO KILL NORTH KOREAN TROOPS UNTIL THE UNITED NATIONS HAS 
WON A VICTORY IN KOREA.” | 
THE AMPHIBIOUS FLEET MOVED THROUGH WATERS WHERE RUSSIAN SUBMARINES 
HAVE BEEN KNOWN TO OPERATE. BUT THE TASK FORCE WAS NOT ATTACKED AND 
NO ENEMY SHIPS OR AIRCRAFT WERE SIGHTED DURING THE LANDING OPERATION. 
NORMALLY, SUCH AN OPERATION WOULD REQUIRE LONG AND DETAILED PLANNING. 
ity ENTIRE LANDING WAS PLANNED AND EXECUTED OVER A SPAN OF ONLY 
DIVERSIONARY GUNFIRE WAS REPORTED SOME DISTANCE UP THE COAST BY 
NAVAL UNITS SUPPORTING THE LANDINGS. 


"AFTER THE LANDING. CORRESPONDENTS WENT INLAND BY TRUCK A CONSIDER- 
COUNTRYSIDE WAS PEACEFUL. THE ONLY ACTIVITY WAS

KOREAN DEFENDERS A MORE BALANCED FRONT BEHIND WHICH A BUILDUP OF MEN 
AND MATERIALS CAN BE MADE MORE SAFELY. IT ALSO WILL RELIEVE OTHER 
Seta ten Aire err Bie oor ee 
CAN SUPPL n

TED DURING THE PACIFIC WARs MANY OF THE OFFICERS INVOLVED SERVED IN 
BIOUS CAMPAIGNS AGA e

LANDING oRAF TS THE LITTLE BOATS CHURNED THROUGH THE CALM WATER TO 


THE BEACH UNDER A HOT SUN. 


AT A COMMAND POST INLAND, CORRESPONDENTS WERE TOLD THAT AMERICAN 
PATROLS HAD MADE DEEP FORAYS INTO QUESTIONABLE TERRITORY WITHOUT 
CONTACTING THE REDS. KOREAN RESIDENTS IN THE AREA SAID THERE HAD 
BEEN SOME GUERRILLA ACTIVITY BUT THEY DID NOT DESCRIBE SPECIFIC 

CONVERSATIONS WITH TROOPS ENCOUNTERED DEEP INLAND REVEALED THAT 
UTMOST SECRECY HAD SURROUNDED THE AMPHIBIOUS OPERATION. THEY

KOREAN WAR INTERPRETIVE (600) 
BY C.YATES MCDANTIEL 

WASHINGTON, JULY 18-(AP)-AMERICAN MILITARY EXPERTS SPECULATED 
TODAY THAT THE KOREAN REDS MAY.HAVE COMMITTED A MILITARY SIN THAT 
WILL LEAD TO THEIR OWN UNDOING WHEN THEY PLUNGED RECKLESSLY SOUTH 
WITHOUT EVEN MINIMUM AIR SUPPORT. | 

THE 1950 MILITARY COPYBOOKS SAY THAT DISASTER IS THE EVENTUAL 
PENALTY FOR LEAVING THE "AIR FLANK" OF AN ARMY UNCOVERED. 

AMERICAN OFFICERS ARE PUZZLED WHY THE NORTH KOREAN HIGH COMMAND-- 
OR THEIR RUSSIAN MASTERS--NEGLECTED TO PROVIDE AIR BALANCE FOR THEIR 
HEAVY-HITTING GROUND TROOPS. 

MAYBE THEY JUST THOUGHT IT WOULDN'T BE NECESSARY. CERTAINLY 
THE INVADERS COULD NOT HAVE KNOWN THAT THE UNITED STATES WOULD JUMP 
IN SO PROMPTLY WITH POWERFUL AERIAL COUNTER=STROKES. 

THE RED KOREANS STARTED OFF WITH A HANDFUL OF RUSSIAN-MADE YAK-9 
PISTON ENGINED FIGHTERS AND A FEW SLOWER GROUND SUPPORT PLANES. EVEN 
THIS HANDFUL GAVE THEM TEMPORARY BUT COMPLETE SUPERIORITY OVER THE 
VIRTUALLY NON-EXISTENT SOUTH KOREAN AIR FORCE. 

SINCE THE UsSeAIR FORCE, ABLY ASSISTED BY HARD FIGHTING AUSTRALIAN 
MUSTANGS, TOOK THE AIR OVER KOREA, RED AIRPLANES HAVE BEEN LITTLE 
MORE THAN A MINOR NUISANCE. THEY’ HAVE JUMPED ON AND SHOT DOWN A FEW 
ALLIED PLANES AND OCCASIONALLY HAVE BEEN GLIMPSED THROUGH THE CLUDS. 

BUT SINCE THE FIRST FEW DAYS OF THE WAR, THE RED AIR FORCE HAS 
MADE NO SERIOUS ATTEMPT TO INTERFERE WITH 
GROUND STRENGTH IN SOUTH KOREA. 

YET THE UeSeSUPPLY LINES BOTH IN THE BATTLE AREA AND ALONG THE 
RAILROAD AND HIGHWAY ROUTES TO PUSAN ARE HIGHLY VULNERABLE. PUSAN 
ON THE SOUTHEAST COAST OF KOREA, IS THE ONLY PORT WHERE AMERICAN SHIPS 
CAN TIE UP TO DOCKS AND UNLOAD MEN AND EQUIPMENT DIRECTLY ON WAITING 
FREIGHT CARS AND MOTOR TRUCKS. 

NORTH KOREA, BY CONTRAST, HAS FAR LESS TO LOSE FROM STRATEGIC 
BOMBING THAT MOST COUNTRIES? SHE GOT PRACTICALLY ALL OF HER SHOOTING 
HARDWARE READY MADE. HER TANKS CAME FROM RUSSIA, AS DID SOME OF HER 
ARTILLERY. THE REST CAME FROM STOCKPILES OF SURRENDERED JAPANESE

THE RETIRED 69-YEAR-OLD GENERAL, WHOSE ROSE THROUGH THE RANKS FROM A 


PRIVATE IN THE SPANISH-AMERICAN WAR TO 
WORLD WAR TT. SAT IN THE DEN OF HIS SAN ANTONE D ROME = — a oS 





_ HE EXPRESSED CONFIDENCE IN TULIMATE VICTORY BUT SAID? 


"IT SEEMS AMAZING THAT A POTENTIALLY VERY POWERFUL NATION LIKE THE

ae eTHIE WAR te’ 

IN A SMALL AREA. KOREA IS ABOUT THE SIZE OF MINNESOTA 
SHAPED MORE LIKE FLORIDA. THE DIFFICULTIES IN FIGHTING IN KOREA ’ 
INCLUDE POOR COMMUNICATIONS AND ROADS, AND THIS IS THE RAINY SEASON. 

"BUT WE MANAGED TO OPERATE IN NEW GUINEA WHERE THERE WERE NO 
COMMUNICATIONS AT ALL AND THE TERRAIN WAS TERRIBLE. BUT WE DID HAVE 
A FIGHTING TEAM THERE. X x X 

"EVERYBODY KNEW HIS BUSINESS--WHAT TO DO IN AN EMERGENCY. YOU 
CAN'T EXPECT THAT OF GREEN TROOPS.

S BUDGET (630) 

NIGHT LEAD BRITISH 
BY GLENN WILLIAMS 

LONDON, JULY 18-(AP)-BRITAIN ANNOUNCED TODAY SHE HAS CHOPPED 
OFF ALL OfL SHIPMENTS TO COMMUNIST CHINA. 

A FOREIGN OFFICE SPOKESMAN SAID THE ACTION WAS A DIRECT RESULT OF 
THIS COUNTRY’S PARTICIPATING IN UNITED NATIONS BATTLE TO ROLL BACK 
THE COMMUNIST INVADERS OF SOUTH KOREA. THE BRITISH ARMY, NAVY AND AIR 
FORCE IN THE FAR EAST NEED ALL OIL STOCKS IN THAT AREA, RE SAID, AND 
HAVE DECIDED TO TAKE THEM OVER FOR THEIR OWN USE. 

EARLIER THIS MONTH BRITAIN TURNED DOWN AN AMERICAN SUGGESTION TO 
LIMIT OIL SHIPMENTS TO RED CHINA, IN LINE WITH A SIMILAR AMERICAN 
SHUTDOWN. THE UNITED STATES, DIPLOMATIC INFORMANTS SAID, THEN RENEWED 

THE STATE DEPARTMENT IN WASHINGTON TODAY SAID IT WAS HIGHLY...) 
GRATIFIED. OFFICIALS BELIEVED THE EMBARGO WOULD EFFECTIVELY SHUT OFF 
ALL WESTERN OIL TO THE CHINESE MAINLAND, WHERE IT MIGHT FIND ITS WAY 
TO NORTH KOREAN FORCES. 

BY SO ACTING BRITAIN POSSIBLY RISKED WHATEVER CHANCE SHE HAS OF 
COMPLETING A FULL EXCHANGE OF DIPLOMATIC REPRESENTATIVES WITH THE 
CHINESE COMMUNIST REGIME AT PEIPING, WHICH SHE HAS RECOGNIZED. 

THIS DECISION WAS ACCOMPANIED BY’ THESE OTHER DEVELOPMENTS : 

te PRIME MINISTER ATTLEE MADE IT CLEAR BRITAIN FEELS THAT THE 
NORTH KOREANS WILL HAVE TO PULL BACK TO THEIR 38TH PARALLEL BOUNDARY 
BEFORE PEACE CAN BE RESTORED. HE THUS GAVE A COOL RECEPTION TO PRIME 
MINISTER STALIN'S EXPRESSED WILLINGNESS TO SEEK A PEACEFUL SETTLEMENT 
IN THE UeNe--IF RED CHINA IS REPRESENTED. 

2. THREE NEW CASES OF SUSPECTED SABOTAGE ABOARD THREE BRITISH 
DESTROYERS, POSSIBLY OF COMMUNIST ORIGIN, WERE REPORTED. SECURITY 
MEASURES WERE TIGHTENED AT NAVAL BASES AND A NAVAL COURT OF INQUIRY 
BEGAN QUESTIONING 50 WITNESSES CONCERNING THE EXPLOSION OF NINE 
MUNITIONS BARGES AT PORTSMOUTH LAST FRIDAY. THE CONSERVATIVE DAILY 
MAIL SAID THE BARGES WERE LOADED WITH AMMUNITION DESTINED FOR KOREA. 

3. SEVERAL MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT EXPRESSED CONCERN WHETHER BRITAIN 
IS READY TO MEET FORCE WITH FORCE IF NEED BE. QUESTIONERS IN THE HOUSE 
OF COMMONS FIRED CRITICAL INQUIRIES AT THE GOVERNMENT ABOUT THE 
PREPAREDNESS OF THE DRAFT MACHINERY, ANTI-AIRCRAFT DEFENSES AND FASTER 
RECRUITING OF VOLUNTEERS FOR THE TERRITORIAL ARMY, THE BRITISH 
FQUIVALENT OF THE U.S. NATIONAL GUARD.

(ADVANCE) LONDON, JULY 13-(AP)-A HIGH RANKING AIRMAN CALLED TODAY 
FOR STRONGER BRITISH AIR DEFENSES AT THE EXPENSE, IF NECESSARY, OF 

HE WELFARE STATE PROGRAM. 

AIR CHIEF MARSHAL SIR GUY BARROD, RETIRED, WARNED THAT THIS 
ISLAND KINGDOM'S AIR DEFENSES ARE SERIOUSLY DEFICIENT IN A "GRAVE 
AND DETERIORATING INTERNATIONAL SITUATION," 

"THE ROYAL AIR FORCE AND ITS AUXILIARIES MUST BE STRENGTHENED 
AT ANY COST AND WITHOUT DELAY," HE SAID. “IF THAT REQUIRES MORE 
MONEY, THAT MUST BE FOUND, EVEN IF IT BE AT THE SACRIFICE OF THINGS 
THAT WE WOULD ALL LIKE TO HAVE." 

HE URGED A GREATER SHARE OF BRITAIN'S £3,000,000,000 
($8,400,000,000) BUDGET FOR DEFENSE PURPOSES AND LESS FOR "THINGS THAT 
WE HAVE ONLY RECENTLY BEGUN TO ENJOY." 

SIR GUY ADDRESSED THE AIR LEAGUE, A PRIVATE ORGANIZATION DEVOTED 
TO STRONG AIR DEFENSES. HE WAS DEPUTY ALLIED COMMANDER-IN-CHIEF IN 
SOUTHEAST ASIA IN 1943. 

THE AIR MARSHAL URGED HIGHER PAY INCENTIVES FOR THE RAF.

PARIS, JULY 18-€AP)=NO SIOLOGICAL HARM COMES FROM THE MARRIAGE 

F PERSONS OF DIFFERENT RACES, SAYS A REPORT PUSLISHED YESTERDAY BY A 
UNITED NATLONS GROUP, 

"STATEMENTS THAT HUMAN HYBRIDS FREQUENTLY SHOW UNDESIRABLE TRAITS, 
BOTH PHYSICALLY AND MENTALLY, PHYSICAL DISHARMONIES AND MENTAL 
DEGENERACIES ARE NOT SUPPORTED BY THE FACTS. X X X SOCIAL RESULTS 
OF RACE MIXTURE, WHETHER FOR GOOD OR ILL, ARE TO BE TRACED TO SOCIAL 
FACTORS," IT SAID. 

THE REPORT, PUBLISHED BY THE UNITED NATIONS EDUCATIONAL, SCIENTIFIC 
AND CULTURAL ORGANIZATION (UNESCO), WAS COMPILED BY A GROUP OF 
EIGHT SCIENTISTS HEADED BY PROF. MONTAGUE FRANCIS ASHLEY MONTAGU, 

A PHILADELPHIA ANTHROPOLOGIST. 

THE SCIENTISTS CONCLUDED THAT "RACE DISCRIMINATION HAS NO 
SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION IN BIOLOGICAL FACTe" ALL HUMAN RACES ARE 
ESSENTIALLY ALIKE, IT SAID. 

UNESCO TERMED THE 2,000-¥ORD REPORT THE "MOST AUTHORITATIVE 
STATEMENT OF MODERN SCIENTIFIC DOCTRINE ON THE CONTROVERSIAL SUBJECT 
OF RACE THAT HAS EVER BEEN ISSUED" AND THE "MOST FAR-REACHING AND 
COMPETENT PRONOUNCEMENT OF ITS KIND EVER MADE."

COURT DECISIONS AND CONTROL THE CARRYING OUT OF COURT SENTENCES.

TEARAN IRAN, JULY 18(AP)©A TOP IRANIAN.BANK OFFICIAL SAID TODAY 
THAT A FAIRER SHARE OF OIL ROYALTIES FROM BRITAIN, COUPLED WITH 
NECESSARY GOVERNMENT REFORMS, WOULD MAKE IT UNNECESSARY FOR IRAN 
TO SEEK A LOAN FROM THE UNITED STATES. 

DISCUSSING A NEW AGREEMENT NOW BEING NEGOTIATED BETWEEN THE 
GIANT BRITISH=OWNED ANGLO“IRANIAN OIL COMPANY AND IRAN'S GOVERNMENT, 
ABOL HASSAN EBTEHAJ, MEAD OF THE GOVERNMENT BANK, SAD SAID IRAN IS 
AT PRESENT RECEIVING "ONLY AN INSIGNIFICANT SHARE” OF THE REVENUE 
EARNED BY THE COMPANY. 

HE SAID THE PROPOSED AGREEMENT WOULD GIVE IRAN AN ESTIMATED 
£30,000 ,000 ($84,000,000) THIS YEAR -= AN IMPORTANT ADDITION TO THE 
COUNTRY’S ECONOMY, 

EBTEHAJ SAID UsSe LOANS NOW BEING NEGOTIATED WOULD NOT BE 
NECESSARY IF IRAN GOT AN EQUITABLE PORTION OF THE ANGLO-IRANIAN 
COMPANY'S PROFITS. HE MAINTAINED THAT IRAN SHOULD GET AT LEAST 
50 PER CENT OF THE NET PROFITS, WHICH IS MUCH MORE THAN SHE HAS 
RECEIVED IN THE PAST AND ALSO MORE THAN PROVIDED FOR IN THE NEW 
PROPOSED AGREEMENTS. 

ESTIMATED ANGLO@IRANIAN PROFITS FOR 1948 WERE ABOUT £70,000,000 
($196,000,000), HE SAID, OF WHICH IRAN WOULD RECEIVE ONLY 
€£9,000,000 ($25,200,000) UNDER THE OLD AGREEMENT, OR £18,000,000 
($50,400,000) UNDER THE PROPOSED NEW PACT. 

HE POINTED OUT THAT THE OIL COMPANY PAID MORE IN TAXES TO THE 
BRITISH GOVERNMENT@-£26,000,000 ($72,800,000)-=THAN IT DID TO IRAN 
FROM WHENCE IT GAINED ITS PROFITS. 

"THAT IS NOT FAIR AND JUST,® HE SAID. "THE COUNTRY SUPPLYING 
THE_OIL 1S ENTITLED TO A BIGGER SHARE THAN ANOTHER GOVERNMENT THAT 
HAS DONE NOTHING.® 

HE ADDED THAT, ALTHOUGH THE OIL COMPANY HAD MADE HUGE PROFITS IN 
IRAN, IT HAD INVESTED ONLY £33,000,000 ($92,400,000) IN CAPITAL IN 
THIS COUNTRY. THUS, ME SAID, THE COMPANY HAD RECOVERED ITS CAPITAL 
INVESTMENT SEVERAL TIMES OVER’ Wi} 4940:
