TOKYO, THURSDAY, JULY 20-(AP)-THE TEXT OF A COMMUNIQUE, NO. 100, 
ISSUED TODAY BY GENERAL MACARTHUR'’S HEADQUARTERS AT 12315 P.M. 
(9315 P.M., EST, WEDNESDAY): 

GENERAL MACARTHUR ANNOUNCED TODAY THAT ON-THE-SPOT BATTLEFIELD 
PROMOTIONS FOR ENLISTED MEN AND OFFICERS CAN NOW BE MADE IN THE 
KOREAN THEATER OF OPERATIONS FOR EXCEPTIONAL PERFORMANCE IN 
COMBAT. 

ALSO FOR THE KOREAN THEATER ONLY, THE ®FREEZE" HAS BEEN LIFTED 
ON PROMOTIONS TO THE TOP FOUR ENLISTED GRADES, AND OTHER RESTRICTIONS 
HAVE BEEN REMOVED ON ENLISTED PROMOTIONS -= RESTRICTIONS THAT HAVE 
BEEN IN EFFECT FOR SOME TIME. 

BATTLEFIELD PROMOTION OF ENLISTED MEN TO THE NEXT HIGHEST GRADE 
MAY BE MADE ON THE SPOT, WITHOUT REGARD TO PREVIOUS TIME IN GRADE, 
UNDER AUTHORITY GRANTED TO LTeGEN.WALTON HeWALKER, COMMANDING 
GENERAL OF EIGHTH U.sSe ARMY FORCES IN KOREA. THIS INCLUDES 
PROMOTION OF ENLISTED MEN AND ALSO WARRANT OFFICERS TO THE RANK OF 
OND LIEUTENANT. 

FOR OFFICER PERSONNEL, OTHER THAN WARRANT OFFICERS, BATTLEFIELD 
PROMOTIONS MAY BE GIVEN THOSE WHO HAVE SERVED A MINIMUM OF SIX 
MONTHS IN GRADE AND WHO HAVE PERFORMED IN AN EXCEPTIONAL MANNER 
FOR AT LEAST ONE MONTH DURING COMBAT.

ENLISTED MEN MUST HAVE DEMONSTRATED FITNESS TO FILL TABLE OR ORGANIZ- 
ATION OR TABLE OF DISTRIBUTION VACANCIES, IN ADDITION TO THE AFOREMENT-

MOVED THE GUN TO THE FRONT WITHOUT INFANTRY SUPPORT AND FIRED 
AT THE ENEMY TANKS.

PRECED NEW YORK KRIPS (B34) 

LONDON, JULY 19-¢AP)-JOSEE_KRIPS, CONDUCTOR OF THE VIENNA STATE 
OPERA, CHARGED TODAY HE WAS BARRED FROM AMERICA BY IMMIGRATION 
OFFICIALS DESPITE A CLEARANCE FROM THE UeS. STATE DEPARTMENT. 

KRIPS AND HIS BLONDE WIFE, MARIA, WERE DETAINED ON ELLIS ISLAND 
SUNDAY WHILE EN ROUTE TO CHICAGO. HE HAD PLANNED TO MAKE HIS FIRST 


AMERICAN APPEARANCE AS A CONDUCTOR WITH THE CHICAGO SYMPHONY ORCHESTRA. 


YESTERDAY. 

MR. AND MRS.KRIPS ARRIVED IN LONDON BY AIR EN ROUTE BACK TO VIENNA} 
"WE THINK IT ALL HAPPENED BECAUSE THE AMERICANS ARE VERY NERVOUS 
THE MOMENT OVER KOREA," HE TOLD REPORTERS AT LONDON AIRPORT. 

"MY WIFE AND I BELIEVE THAT SOMEONE WROTE TO AMERICA SAYING THAT 
ARE COMMUNISTS. 

"I AM NOT A COMMUNIST OR A FASCIST AND I BELONG TO NO PARTY. 

I WILL NOT CONDUCT AGAIN IN AMERICA OR THE AMERICAN ZONE OF GERMANY 
UNTIL MY NAME IS CLEARED." 

KRIPS SAID HIS LAWYER TOLD HIM AT ELLIS ISLAND YESTERDAY THE STATE 
DEPARTMENT "HAD GIVEN ME PEERMISSION TO ENTER AMERICA AS OFTEN AS I 
LIKED--BUT THE IMMIGRATION OFFICERS HAD DIFFERENT IDEAS." 

KRIPS CLAIMED THE IMMIGRATION MEN TOLD HIM HE HAD TWO ALTERNATIVES. 
"ONE WAS TO LEAVE AMERICA WILLINGLY. THE OTHER WAS TO BE DEPORTED, 
IN WHICH CASE I WOULD BE BARRED FROM ENTERING AMERICA EVER AGAIN. 
THIS LEFT ME NO CHOICE BUT OT LEAVE.”

ATOM BOMB. THEY WERE CHARGED WITH DISTURBING THE PEACE. 

ONE RINGLEADER WAS SENTENCED TO TWO WEEKS IN JAIL. OTHERS GOT SHORT 
JAIL TERMS OR FINES UP TO 10 MARKS ($2.30).

CARDS.

BERLIN, JULY 19-(AP)-WEST BERLIN AUTHORITIES TODAY ORDERED TRIALS 
AGAINST 6ég COMMUNIST AGITATORS ARRESTED YESTERDAY WHEN THEY TRIED 
TO OBTAIN SIGNATURES TO THE SOVIET PROPAGANDA PETITION FOR OUTLAWING 
THE ATOMIC BOMB. 

THE WEST BERLIN POLICE GRABBED 1,556 MEN AND WOMEN WHO TRIED TO 
CIRCULATE THE RUSSIAN-INSPIRED PETITIONS IN THE THREE WEST SECTORS 
YESTERDAY AFTERNOON AND LAST NIGHT. 

THE POLICE RELEASED 888 OF THE PERSONS AFTER SCOLDING THEM FOR TRYIN 
TO STIR UP TROUBLE. 

THE REMAINING GROUP WILL BE CHARGED WITH STAGING PROPHIBITED 
DEMONSTRATIONS AND DISTRIBUTING "ILLEGAL PROPAGANDA,” A GERMAN POLICE 
AUTHORITY SAID. 

THE PENALTY RANGES FROM SEVERAL DAYS TO A MAXIMUM OF ONE MONTH IN 
JAIL, THIS OFFICIAL SAID.

OF THE METHODIST FEDERATION FOR SOCIAL ACTION. 

THE FEDERATION IS COMPOSED OF METHODIST LAYMEN AND CHURCHMEN AS

NEW YORK, JULY 19=-C(AP)-AN ANGRY AUSTRIAN SYMPHONY CONDUCTOR CALLED 
OFF HIS AMERICAN DEBUT YESTERDAY AND FLEW BACK TO EUROPE AFTER A 
BRUSH WITH U.eSe IMMIGRATION AUTHORITIES. | 

THE CONDUCTOR, 48-YEAR-OLD JOSEF KRIPS, HAD BEEN INVITED TO THE 
UNITED STATES TO LEAD THE CHICAGO SYMPHONY IN FOUR SUMMER CONCERTS 
THIS WEEK. HE IS CHIEF CONDUCTOR OF THE VIENNA STATE OPERA AND ALSO 
LEADS THE VIENNA PHILHARMONIC ORCHESTRA. 

HE AND HIS WIFE ARRIVED HERE BY AIR MONDAY AND WERE IMMEDIATELY 
8S go A THE IMMIGRATION SERVICE==-FOR REASONS THAT HAVE NOT BEEN 

IMMIGRATION SUPERVISOR EDWARD Je SHAUGHNESSY SAID ONLY THAT 
"CERTAIN INFORMATION" HAD BEEN RECEIVED ABOUT KRIPS, AND HE WOULD 
NOT DISCLOSE ITS NATURE. HE GAVE KRIPS THE CHOICE OF LEAVING 
VOLUNTARILY OR BEING DEPORTED, ALTHOUGH HE HAD AN AMERICAN ENTRY 
VISA. 

THE AUSTRIAN GOVERNMENT INTERCEBDED IN KRIPS* BEHALF, BUT WITHOUT 
SUCCESS. 

"NO AUSTRIAN AUTHORITY HERE HAS BEEN INFORMED OF THE REASON FOR 
HIS DETENTION,” AUSTRIAN CONSUL FRANZ LEITNER SAID. 

KRIPS SAID HE HAD NO IDEA WHAT THE OBJECTION TO HIS VISIT MIGHT 
e 


"I HAVE NEVER BEEN IN A POLITICAL PARTY--RIGHT OR LEFT," HE SAID. 

"I HAVE NEVER BEEN IN THE COMMUNIST PARTY. I AM A CATHOLIC. MY 
PARTY IS THAT OF BEETHOVEN AND MOZART.” 

HE ADDED THAT THE ONLY THING HE COULD RECALL THAT MIGHT HAVE 
BEEN HELD AGAINST HIM WAS A TRIP TO MOSCOW AND LENINGRAD IN 1947. HE 
SAID HE CONDUCTED THERE AT THE REQUEST OF HIS OWN GOVERNMENT. 

THE KRIPS AFFAIR RECALLED THE SOMEWHAT SIMILAR INCIDENT INVOLVING 
GERMAN PIANIST WALTER GIESEKING, WHO ALSO FLEW BACK TO EUROPE FROM 
NEW YORK LAST JANe25 AFTER HE WAS HELD BY SHAUGHNESSY'S OFFICE. HE, 
TOO, HAD A STATE DEPARTMENT ENTRY VISA. 

GIESEKING’S APPEARANCE HAD BEEN PUBLICLY PROTESTED BY JEWISH 
GROUPS, WHO SAID HE HAD NAZI SYMPATHIES. 

THE APPOINTMENT OF WILHELM FURTWANGLER AS CONDUCTOR OF THE CHICAGO 
SYMPHONY WAS BLOCKED RECENTLY BY PROTESTS FROM JEWISH AND OTHER 
MUSICIANS THAT HE WAS A PRO-NAZI. BOTH GIESEKING AND FURTWANGLER, 
aoe” OF WHOM ARE JEWS, PERFORMED IN GERMANY DURING THE NAZI

TOKYO, JULY 20-(AP)=-FAILURE OF THE SOUTH KOREANS TO HOLD THE HAN 
RIVER LINE SOUTH OF SEOUL RESULTED IN THE UNITED STATES" "DESPERATE 
DECISION" TO COMMIT AMERICAN INFANTRYMEN PIECEMEAL IN THE KOREAN WAR. 

THE GAMBLE HAS PAID OFFe GENERAL MACARTHUR SAID TODAY NORTH KOREA 
"HAS LOST ITS CHANCE FOR VICTORY." 

WHEN THE INVADERS BREACHED THE WIDE AND DEEP HAN THREE WEEKS AGO 
THEY HAD A CLEAR ROAD--AND RELATIVELY LITTLE SOUTH KOREAN OPPOSITION-- 
ALL THE WAY TO PUSANe HAD THEY REACHED PUSAN, THE COMMUNISTS WOULD 
HAVE CONTROLLED THE WHOLE PENINSULA AND DEPRIVED A RELIEF FORCE OF 
ANY SUITABLE BEACHHEAD FOR POURING IN SUPPLIES AND MEN NEEDED FOR A 
COUNTERATTACK. 

MACARTHUR TOLD SOUTH KOREAN LEADERS AT SUWON JUNE 29 TO DEFEND THE 
HAN RIVER AT ALL COSTS TO GIVE HIM TIME. BUT THE LINE BROKE WITHIN 
HOURS AFTER THE CONFERENCES. 

IT WAS DECIDED THEN TO PUR U.S. INFANTRYMEN INTO KOREA AS QUICKLY 
AS POSSIBLE BY AIR AND SEAe THIS WAS CONTRARY TO ALL MILITARY PRACTICE. 

THESE YOUNG, GREEN KIDS, IN THE LONELINESS OF A FRONTLINE POSITION, 
FIRST WAVERED, THEN BEGAN To HOLD. AT GREAT SACRIFICE THEY SLOWED 
THE TRIUMPHANT RED RACE TO A WALK IN THE CRITICAL DAYS WHEN TIME WAS SO 
PRESS ING. 


AT THE FRONT, THESE YOUNG COMBAT TROOPS COULD GET ONLY A GLIMPSE OF 
THE POWER BEING BUILT UP BEHIND THEM. THEY COULD ONLY HEAR RUMORS OF 
THE HAMMERING WHICH ALLIED AIR POWER WAS DELIVERING TO THE ENEMY DEEP 
IN HIS OWN TERRITORY. . 

BUT AIR POWER DID COME TO THEIR DIRECT AID. BOMBERS AND FIGHTERS 
DESTROYED TANKS, TRUCKS AND RAILROAD EQUIPMENT AND STRAFED TROOP 
CONCENTRATIONS. SUPPLY BASES WERE DEALT HEAVY BLOWS THAT DESTROYED 
THE ENEMY'S NEEDED FUEL AND AMMUNITION. 

A1D1FX 

ALONG THE EAST COAST, AMERICAN AND BRITISH NAVAL FORCES BLOCKED 
ANY SERIOUS ALTERNATE THREAT TO PUSAN. 

"UE BOUGHT PRECIOUS TIME," SAID MACARTHUR. IN LESS THAN THREE WEEKS, 
THREE FULLY EQUIPPED DIVISIONS HAVE LANDED, A VAST PILE OF SUPPLIES 
HAS CONE ASHORE AND THE NAVY AND AIR FORCE HAVE BEEN REINFORCED. 

TUO GROUPS TOTALING 50 B-29S, TRANSFERRED INTACT 8,000 MILES, MADE 
THEIR FIRST SUCCESSFUL MISSION EIGHT DAYS FROM THE TIME THEY Got THEIR

TEXT (550) 

TOKYO,JULY 10-CAP)=TEXT OF GENERAL MACARTHUR'S COMMUNI 
ISSUED AT 2255 P.M. (11855 PeM. WEDNESDAY)$ WL 94 406) 
ACCORDING TO STORIES TOLD BY HUNDREDS OF CAPTURED NORTH .KOREAN ~ ™ 

SOLDIERS, LIFE IN A COMMUNIST ARMY IS NOT ALL "BEER AND SKITTLES." 

TEE NORTH KOREANS DO NOT SURRENDER EASILY BECAUSE THEY EXPECT TO 
BE EXECUTED. ONCE THEY FIND THEY ARE NOT GOING TO BE SHOT, THEY BECOME 
ANXIOUS TO EXPOSE THE TACTICS THE COMMUNISTS USED TO ENLIST THEIR 
SUPPORT. THE STORIES REVEAL A STARTINGLY LOW STATE OF TRAINING AND 
MORALE IN SOME OF THE BELATEDLY ORGANIZED NORTH KOREAN UNITS. 

A CLEAR PICTURE OF A RECENTLY FORMED NORTH KOREAN INFANTRY DIVISION, 
THE 15TH, HAS BEEN ASSEMBLED BY UeSe INTELLIGENCE AGENCIES. BATTLE- 

ESTED OFFICERS AND NON=COMMISSIONED OFFICERS FROM MANCHURIA AND CHINA 
FORMED THE CORE OF THE DIVISION WHICH WAS ACTIVATED AT KUMHWA IN 
NORTHWESTERN KOREA. SPECIALISTS, THE TANK CREWS, MORTAR AND MACHINE 
GUNNERS AND ALL THE OTHER SKILLED MANPOWER TRAINED IN THE NORTH KOREAN 
ARMY, PROVIDED THE SKELETON OF THE DIVISION. THE VETERAN, WELL-TRAINED 
CADRE WAS BROUGHT TO DIVISION STRENGTH IN JUNE OF THIS YEAR WITH DRAFTED 
MEN, 

MOST OF THE CONSCRIPTS WERE YOUNG FARMERS CALLED UP IN APRIL, 

1950, FOR TRAINING IN AN ORGANIZATION CALLED THE "YOUNG MEN'S DEMOCRATI 
TRAINING SCHOOL." DURING THE FIRST MONTH, THE SCHOOL TAUGHT CLOSE 
ORDER DRILL AND THE SECOND MONTH WAS SPENT IN THE FIELD BUT, IN MANY 
CASES, THE TRAINEES FIRED AS LITTLE AS THREE PRACTICE SHOTSe THE 
TRAINING PROGRAM WASN'T AS LIMITED IN POLITICAL "EDUCATION®," HOWEVER, 
AS AT FREQUENT INTERVALS, THE UNIT POLITICAL AND CULTURAL OFFICER 
LECTURED THE MEN ON COMMUNIST THEORY. 

ON JUNE 26, THE STUDENTS OF THE YOUNG MEN'S DEMOCRATIC SCHOOL WERE 
ISSUED ARMS AND AMMUNITION AND OFFICIALLY NOTIFIED THAT THEY WERE - 
MEMBERS OF THE 15TH NORTH KOREAN INFANTRY DIVISION. THE NEXT DAY THEY 
JOINED IN THE INVASION OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. 

THE DRAFTED MEN FEARED THEIR BRUTAL, BATTLE-HARDENED LEADERS, YET 
THEY WERE AFRAID TO DESERT BECAUSE THAT MEANT SURE DEATH BY EXECUTION 


QUE NO. 106 


IF CAUGHT. AS A RESULT, THEY ENDURED THE HARD MARCHES AND THE LACK OF 
FOOD AND REST UNTIL JULY 4 WHEN THEY HAD THEIR FIRST COMBAT CONTACT 
WITH SOUTH KOREAN UNITS NEAR THE HAN RIVER. 


B4iKX (EGQC) 

BETTER TRAINED UNITS HAD SPEARHEADED THE ADVANCE AND SCREENED 
THE 15TH FROM THE UNITED NATIONS TROOPS UNTIL THIS TIME. THEIR FIRST 
CONTACT WITH REPUBLIC OF KOREA DEFENDERS BROUGHT HEAVY CASUALTIES AND 
PANIC SPREAD THROUGH THE RANKS OF THIS FOOTSORE AND WEARY UNIT. ONLY 
THE PRESENCE OF THEIR FANATIC LEADERS KEPT THEM AT THE BATTLE LINE--= 
EVEN THEN MANY DESERTED OR FLED TO THE REAR. 

SINCE THEN THE 15TH DIVISION HAS BEEN KEPT IN THE CENTER OF THE LINE 
WHERE THEY HAVE EXPERIENCED MODERATE SUCCESSES DUE MAINLY TO THE FACT 
THAT THEY FACE NO ARMOR OR ARTILLERY. ALSO, THEY ARE SUPPORTED ON 
EITHER FLANK BY OLDER, BETTER@-TRAINED NORTH KOREAN DIVISIONS ABLE TO 
CARRY MOST OF THE LOAD IN ROUGH GOING. 

THOSE 


EITHER FLANK BY OLDER, BETTER-TRAINED NORTH KOREAN DIVISIONS ABLE TO 
CARRY MOST OF THE LOAD IN ROUGH GOING, 

THOSE CAPTURED DESCRIBE MORALE IN THE DIVISION AS EXTREMELY LOW. 
ALREADY THEY ARE BADLY SHAKEN BY THE ATTACKS OF THE COMBINED AIR FLEETS 
FLYING UNDER THE BANNER OF THE UNITED NATIONS. 

THE APPEARANCE OF AUSTRALIAN AND AMERICAN AIRPLANES OVERHEAD WAS 
THE FIRST INDICATION THE NORTH KOREAN SOLDIERS HAD THAT UNITED NATIONS 
FORCES HAD JOINED THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA IN REPELLING THE INVASION. 

THE PRISONERS FEEL THAT THE NORTH KOREAN ARMY'S SUCCESS SO FAR HAS 
BEEN DUE TO OVERWHELMING NUMERICAL SUPERIORITY COMBINED WITH TEMPORARY 
ADVANTAGE IN THE NUMBER OF TANKS,~ “THEY SAY THAT-THE MEN PROBABLY 
WILL CARRY ON AS LONG AS THEY KEEP WINNING, BUT WHEN THEY START TO 
LOSE IT WILL BE A DIFFERENT STORY. .

TOKYO, JULY 20-(AP)=&lt;TEXT OF MACARTHUR COMMUNIQUE NO.108, ISSUED AT 
7815 PeMe (C4815 AeMe, EST) TODAYS ! 

THE UeSe ARMY'S NEW 3.5 INCH ROCKET, A LAUNCHER, WHICH MADE A: ‘HIGH 
SUCCESSFUL ENTRY INTO THE KOREAN WAR TODAY, IS A MODERN VERSION OF 
THE ARMY'S WORLD WAR W 2e36=INCH ROCKET LAUNCHER, COMMONLY KNOWN AS 
THE BAZOOKA. 


BATTLE*TESTED MEN OF THE 24TH INFANTRY DIVISION, SUPPLIED WITH THE 


NEW LAUNCHER ONLY A SHORT TIME BEFORE, FIRED IT AT SEVEN RED TANKS THAT 


WERE APPROACHING TAEJON THIS MORNING. RESULT: SEVEN ENEMY TANKS 


DESTROYED. 
HOW THIS MODERN WEAPON AND ITS AMMUNITION WAS MANUFACTURED IN THE 
UNITED STATES, SHIPPED TO KOREA AND PLACED IN THE HANDS OF OUR 


s+iwg 
FIGHTING 


MEN IN A FEW DAYS TIME IS ANOTHER EXAMPLE OF THE DETERMINA- 
TION OF AMERICAN INDUSTRY AND UesSe ARMY LOGISTICIANS THAT THE ARMED 
FORCES OF THE FREE NATIONS WILL BE PROVIDED WITH THE BEST OF EQUIPMENT 
AND SUPPLIES, WHEREVER THEY MAY BE AND IN THE SHORTEST POSSIBLE TIME. 

ACTUALLY, EXPERIMENTAL WORK ON THE NEW ROCKET LAUNCHER BEGAN ABOUT 
THE TIME WORLD WAR 2 ENDED, WHEN ARMY ORDNANCE AND TACTICAL EXPERTS 
REALIZED THE NEED FOR AN ANTITANK WEAPON WITH GREATER ARMOR PENETRA- 
TION AND FASTER MUZZLE VELOCITY THAN WAS PROVIDED BY THE 2.36-INCH 
ROCKET. 

U.sS. ORDNANCE CONTINUED TO MAKE IMPROVEMENTS ON THE 2¢36-INCH 
LAUNCHER, INCREASING ITS RANGE AND ACCURACY, BUT IN THE MEANTIME 
DEVELOPED THE LARGER WEAPON, THE TWO ARE SIMILAR EXCEPT THAT THE NEW 
WEAPON IS LARGER AND IS FIRED FROM THE SHOULDER. 

THE 3,5-INCH ROCKET LAUNCHER IS A TWO-PIECE, SMOOTH-BORE, ELECTRI- 
CALLY OPERATED WEAPON OF THE OPEN TUBE TYPE AND HAS NO RECOIL. 
THE 2.36-INCH LAUNCHER, THE NEW WEAPON HAS AN ATTACKED MONOPOD AND A 
BIPOD FOR STABILIZATION WHEN FIRING FROM THE PRONE POSITION. DESPITE 
ITS LARGER SIZE, IT WEIGHS ONLY A FEW POUNDS MORE THAN THE OLDER 
VERSION, 

AMMUNITION FOR THE NEW LAUNCHER IS APPROXIMATELY 23 INCHES LONG AND 
WEIGHS SLIGHTLY MORE THAN EIGHT POUNDS. THE WAR HEAD CONTAINS A POWER- 
FUL EXPLOSIVE HELD IN THE FORM OF A "SHAPED CHARGE." THE ACTION OF THE 
"SHAPED CHARGE" ENABLES THE ROUND TO PENETRATE ANY ARMORED VEHICLE 


GUN EMPLACEMENTS AND VARIOUS OTHER TYPES OF ENEMY WEAPONS 


OF THE 2436=-INCH ROCKET LAUNCHER. 


B64KX (Q) ? 

SIGHTING OF THE NEW WEAPON IS ACCOMPLISHED BY MEANS OF A REFLECTING 
SIGHT WHICH, WHEN THE GUNNER LOOKS THROUGH, SUPERIMPOSES A SCALE ON THE 
FIELD SIGHT. THIS SCALE ENABLES THE GUNNER TO OBTAIN 

ANGULAR LEADS ON TARGETS MOVING UP TO A SPEED OF 40 MILES AN HOUR. 

ALTHOUGH PRIMARILY DESIGNED AS A CLOSE=IN ANTITANK WEAPON, THE 
3e5@INCH ROCKET LAUNCHER CAN ALSO BE USED AGAINST FORTIFIED POSITIONS 
AND--UP TO ITS MAXIMUM RANGE=-FOR AREA=-TYPE FIRE AGAINST TROOP 
CONCENTRATIONS AND SIMILAR GROUND TARGETS. ITS EFFECT IN AREA=TYPE - 
FIRE IS VERY SIMILAR TO THAT OF AN 81=MM MORTAR ROUND. 

FEW WEAPONS CAN EQUAL THE NEW ROCKET LAUNCHER AS A CLOSE-IN 
ANTITANK WEAPON, ALTHOUGH MUCH LARGER GUNS MAY BE SUPERIOR IN RANGE 
AND EFFECT.

TRUMAN INTERPRETIVE 
BY JOHN MeHIGHTOWER 

WASHINGTON, JULY 20-(AP)-PRESIDENT TRUMAN'S DECISION TO RALLY 
AMERICAN POWER AGAINST EXPANDING COMMUNIST STRENGTH PUTS SQUARELY 
UP TO RUSSIA THE DECISION ON WHETHER THE WORLD IS TO MOVE TOWARD 
ALL-OUT WAR OR A NEW, UNEASY PEACE. 

DIPLOMATIC AUTHORITIES SAID THE NEXT MOVE IN THE GLOBAL CRISIS IS 
CLEARLY UP TO MOSCOW--NOW THAT THE PRESIDENT HAS BACKED UP HIS STOP- 
AGGRESSION POLICY WITH INITIAL PREPARATION TO FIGHT WHERE NECESSARY. 

ADMINISTRATION LEADERS REMAINED HOPEFUL THAT THE MEN IN THE KREMLIN 
WOULD HEED THE PRESIDENT'S WARNING AND CHOOSE A PEACEFUL COURSE. 

THEY DID NOT RULE OUT, HOWEVER, THE POSSIBILITY THAT THE COMMUNIST 
CHIEFTAINS HAVE DECIDED ON WAR AND MAY NOW UNFOLD A POLICY TO THAT 
END. 

IN ANY CASE, RUSSIA HAS THE INITIATIVE AND THE UNITED STATES AND 
ALLIED NATIONS ARE CONFRONTED WITH THE NEED TO MARSHAL MAXIMUM FORCES 
AS RAPIDLY AS POSSIBLE. | " ies

WESTERN POWERS. THIS MIGHT BE ONE uae WHY THE RED LEADERS WOULD

STATES HAS AN EDGE rn ATOMIC WEAPONS AND PROBABLY ALSO IN SOME OTHER

INTO MASS PRODUCTION. THE ATOMIC BOMB MAY BE A POWERFUL INFLUENCE 
AGAINST THE KREMLIN FORCING THE ISSUE ANYTIME SOON. 2

HONG KONG, JULY 20-(AP)-BRITISH SHIPPING CIRCLES SAY THEY ARE 
UNEASY ABOUT WHAT THEY CALL A TIGHTENING OF THE CHINESE NATIONALIST 
BLOCKADE OF THE RED-HELD MAINLAND. 

THIS IS DESPITE THE RELEASE YESTERDAY OF TWO PANAMANIAN- 
REGISTERED VESSELS WHICH ARE RETURNING TO HONG KONG. 

THEY ARE THE PERICO AND THE SHAPUR, WHOSE DETENTION AND RELEASE 
BY THE NATIONALISTS WERE CONFIRMED TODAY BY PANAMANIAN CONSUL- 
GENERAL E.E. LINARES. AT THE SAME TIME LINARES WARNED SHIPS FLYING 
PANAMANIAN FLAGS THAT THEY RUN THE BLOCKADE AT THEIR OWN RISK AND 
CANNOT COUNT ON PROTECTION BY THE PANAMANIAN GOVERNMENT. 

MEANWHILE BRITISH SHIPPING CIRCLES EXPRESSED ALARM OVER THE 
WAY THEY SAY THE NATIONALISTS HAVE TIGHTENED UP SINCE THE AMERICAN 
SEVENTH FLEET WAS DISPATCHED TO PROTECT FORMOSA FROM COMMUNIST 
INVASION. THEY REFER POINTEDLY TO STILL UNCONFIRMED REPORTS THAT 
TWO BRITISH SHIPS WERE SEIZED THIS WEEK AND ARE BEING HELD IN A 
NORTHERN FORMOSAN PORT, PROBABLY KEELUNG. THEY ARE THE EMPIRE 
AND ONE OTHER, 

IT HAS BEEN CONFIRMED THAT ON MONDAY THE NATIONALIST NAVY INTER- 
CEPTED THE 2,500-TON BRITISH SHIP POYANG IN THE FORMOSAN STRAIT

NORTHWARD.

COMMUNIQUE, NO. 115, ISSUED TODAY AT 2350 PeM. (11250 P.M. THURSDAY 
EST): 

Be29S OF THE UsSeAIR FORCE STRUCK AT NORTH KOREAN AIRFIELDS AND 
BRIDGES ON JULY 20 IN SWEEPS ACROSS THE 38TH PARALLEL AS FAR NORTH 
AS PYONGYANG. 

MORE THAN 160 TONS OF HIGH EXPLOSIVES WERE DROPPED IN ATTACKS ON 
FIVE MAJOR TARGETS. PYONGYANG'S HEIJO EAST AIRFIELD AND ONJONG 
AIRFIELD SOUTH OF CHINNAMPO WERE HIT WITH GOOD RESULTS. ONE SPAN WAS 
KNOCKED OUT ON A MAINLINE RAILROAD BRIDGE SOUTH OF PYONGYANG AND 
ATTACKS WERE AGAIN MADE ON A RAILROAD BRIDGE AT SEOUL. DIRECT HITS 
WERE SCORED, DAMAGING THE STRUCTURE. 

NORTH KOREAN AIR OPPOSITION TO THE B-29 STRIKES WAS ENCOUNTERED 
NEAR SEOUL BUT ATTACKING AIRCRAFT WERE DRIVEN OFF BY THE BOMBING 
AIRPLANES GUNNERS. TWO FIGHTERS, ONE A YAK=9 AND THE OTHER NOT 
DEFINITELY IDENTIFIED, WERE OBSERVED TO BE DAVAGED AND SMOKING.

DAMAGED IN THE AIR BATTLE AND ANOTHER WAS DAMAGED BY FLAK IN THE 
SEOUL AREA BUT BOTH RETURNED SAFELY TO BASE.

LONDON, JULY 24-(AP)-TWO BRITISH SCIENTISTS WITH EXTENSIVE 
EXPERIENCE IN THE ORIENT, SUGGESTED TODAY THAT MILLIONS OF ASIANS 
WILL TURN AGAINST AMERICA BECAUSE OF THE AIR RAIDS ON NORTH KOREA 
INDUSTRIES. 

IN A LETTER TO THE TIMES TODAY DR. JOSEPH NEEDHAM AND HIS WIFE 
DOROTHY SAID THE IMPRESSION BEING GIVEN IN MANY EASTERN LANDS 
IS THAT THE MOST HIGHLY INDUSTRIALIZED COUNTRY IN THE WORLD SEEKS TO 
DESTROY THE BEGINNINGS OF INDUSTRALIZATION IN ASIA. 

"WE ARE NOT HERE CONCERNED WITH THE LEGAL RIGHTS AND WRONGS 
OF THE PROCEEDINGS NOW GOING ON IN KOREAN," THEY WROTE. "WHAT WE ARE 
ANXIOUS TO POINT OUT IS THAT THE AMERICANS AND THEIR SUPPORTERS HAVE 
GOT THEMSELVES INTO A POSITION IN WHICH THEY MUST SEEM, TO THE EYES 
OF THE MASSES OF ASIA PEOPLES, IMPLACABLY OPPOSED TO THE RELIEF OF 
THEIR POVERTY AND THE ADVANCE OF THEIR SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY. 

" X X X WE FEAR THAT THE WHOLE PRESENT POLICY OF THE OCCIDENTAL 
POWERS IN EAST ASIA IS SOWING A HARVEST OF HATRED WHICH WILL 
RIPEN IN YEARS TO COME 

NEEDHAM IS SCIENTIFIC ADVISER TO UNESCO, AND WAS A MEMBER OF 
A BRITISH SCIENTIFIC MISSION TO CHINA. IN AMERICA HE HAS LECTURED 
AT STANFORD, YALE, CORNELL AND OBERLINe HIS WIFE HAS CONDUCTED 
RESEARCHES “IN BIOCHEMISTRY IN THE UNITED STATES.

WASHINGTON, JULY 21@(AP)-THE ARMY TODAY BEGAN DIPPING INTO ITS 
932,000 HAN POOL OF NATIONAL GUARD AND RESERVE STRENGTH.

THIS IS A MOVE TO PREVENT LOSING TRAINED MENe : 

THE NUMBER_OF GUARDSMEN AND RESFRUFS THE ARMY TS CALLING TO ACTIVE 


Taerrw 2 wen = 


vuit was NOT STATED. IT IS BRINGING THEM UP IN UNITS SMALLER THAN A

THE SENATE VOTE CAME LITTLE MORE THAN FIVE HOURS AFTER HOUSE AND 
SENATE ARMED SERVICES COMMITTEE HAD STAMPED SPEEDY APPROVAL ON BILLS 
TO TAKE ALL LEGAL LIMITS OFF THE SIZE OF THE ARMED FORCES, AS WELL AS 
PERMITTING THE ONE-YEAR "FREEZE" ON ENLISTMENTS « 

THE SENATE TOOK UP ONLY THE LATTER MEASURE TODAY. IT CAME ON A 
REQUEST BY CHAIRMAN TYDINGS (D-MD) OF THE ARMED SERVICES COMMITTEE 
FOR UNANIMOUS ACTION, HE SAID THAT OTHERWISE THE FIGHTING FORCES 
WOULD LOSE "TRAINED MEN WHO CANNOT BE REPLACED." 

THE EFFECT OF THE TWO PROPOSALS WOULD BE: (1) TO ALLOW EXPANSION 
OF THE ACTIVE FORCES BEYOND THE PRESENT CEILING OF 2,005,882, AND (2) 

TO PREVENT AN ESTIMATED LOSS OF 193,000 MEN THOUGH EXPIRING ENLISTMENTS. 

THE HOUSE HAS YET TO ACT ON EITHER PROPOSAL. 

IN ANOTHER DEVELOPMENT, THE HOUSE ARMED SERVICES COMMITTEE 
CALLED FOR A DETAILED REPORT FROM ALL THREE SERVICES ON HOW THEY HAVE 
SPENT THE BILLIONS HANDED THEM DURING THE LAST THREE YEARS. THE 
INQUIRY BEGINS BEHIND CLOSED DOORS MONDAY WITH THE NAVY FIRST UP. 

THE ARMY ACTED ON AUTHORITY GIVEN IT BY PRESIDENT TRUMAN TO CALL 
UP RESERVES AND GUARDSMEN JUST A DAY AFTER THE NAVY AND MARINE CORPS 
HAD ISSUED CALLS FOR 86,000 OF THEIR RESERVES TO JOIN THE COLORS. 

THE AIR FORCE HAS INDICATED IT WON'T ORDER UP ANY RESERVES FOR A 
WEEK OR SO, BUT COLeHARLAND PARKS TOLD THE HOUSE ARMED SERVICES 
COMMITTEE THAT THE AIR FORCE WOULD LIKE AUTHORITY TO DRAFT WORLD WAR II 
VETERANS IF IT FAILS TO FILL ITS MANPOWER NEEDS THROUGH VOLUNTEERS AND 

a 

COLePARKS SAID THE SERVICE BELIEVES USE OF SUCH AUTHORITY WOULD 
NOT BE NECESSARY.

TO ACTIVE DUTY AS THE NEED ARISES AND FACILITIES FOR THEIR RECEPTION 
AND TRAINING CAN BE PROVIDED.

LONDON, JULY 24-(AP)=THE NEW CHINA NEWS AGENCY SAID TONIGHT

COMPANIES TO SURRENDER THEIR STOCKS OF UeS. ECONOMIC COOPERATION 
ADMINISTRATION (ECA) PETROLEUM PRODUCTS. 

THE AGENCY, IN A BROADCAST FROM SHANGHAI HEARD HERE, SAID THE 
ORDER WAS ISSUED TO THE OIL COMPANIES LAST MONDAY. IT DID NOT

COMPANY.

REFUSE TO COMPLY WITH THE ORDER OR CONCEAL GOODS," THE AGENCY SAID.

WASHINCTON.JULY 21-CAP)-THE UNITED STATES AND BRITAIN SIGNED A 
O5&lt;YEAR AGREEMENT HERE TODAY FOR JOINT USE OF SECRET INSTALLATIONS ON 
THE BAHAMA ISLANDS FOR TRACKING AND GUIDING AMERICAN GUIDED MISSILES. 

BRITISH AMBASSADOR SIR OLIVER FRANKS AND SECRETARY OF STATE ACHESON 
SIGNED THE ACCORD IN A BRIEF CEREMONY AT THE STATE DEPARTMENT. 

THE UNITED STATES HAS ALREADY SET UP LAUNCHING FACILITIES ON THE 
EAST COAST OF FLORIDA NEAR CAPE CANAVERAL. 

UNDER TODAY'S AGREEMENT, THE TWO COUNTRIES WILL OPERATE SUPPORTING 
INSTALLATIONS IN THE BAHAMAS TO CONTROL AND CHECK THE GIANT MISSILES 
SHOT SOUTHEASTWARD OVER THE ATLANTIC OCEAN. 

THE MISSILES TO BE FLIGHT TESTED, THE STATE DEPARTMENT SAID 
WILL BE UNARMED AND WILL CARRY INSTRUMENTS FOR MEASURING PERFORMANCE 
AND CONTROL, IT ADDED THEY CAN BE DESTROYED IN FLIGHT IF NECESSARY

LONDON, JULY 21-(AP)=THE INTERNATIONAL SUGAR COUNCIL HAS DECIDED 
SU2MIT TO MEMBER GOVERNMENTS THE DRAFT OF A PROPOSED NEW 

REEMENT ON INTERNATIONAL TRADING IN SUGAR. 


3 Q 2 r i ‘¢

° ti OY ot. 


TEXT OF A COMMUNIQUE ISSUED BY THE “COUNCIL TODAYS 

"THE INTERNATIONAL SUGAR COUNCIL HELD A MEETING ON JULY 20 AT 
BRETTENHAM HOUSE, LONDON. IT WAS ATTENDED BY REPRESENTATIVES OF 16 
GOVERNMENTS, BY OBSERVERS FROM FIVE OTHER GOVERNMENTS, AND BY AN 
OBSERVER FROM THE UNITED NATIONS AND AN OBSERVER FROM THE FOOD AND 
AGRICULTURAL ORGANIZATION. 

"THE COUNCIL HAD BEFORE IT A DRAFT OF A NEW INTERNATIONAL SUGAR 
AGREEMENT PREPARED BY ITS SPECIAL COMMITTEE. AFTER A FULL DISCUSSION 
IT DECIDED TO ASK ALL ITS DELEGATIONS AND THE OBSERVERS WHO HAD 
ATTENDED ITS MEETING TO SUBMIT THE DRAFT TO THEIR GOVERNMENTS AND 
OBTAIN THEIR GOVERNMENTS* VIEWS, NOT LATER THAN OCTOBER 16. 

"THE SPECIAL COMMITTEE AND THE FULL COUNCIL WILL MEET AGAIN IN 
THE LATE AUTUMN TO PREPARE A MORE FINAL DRAFT AND DECIDE WHETHER IT 
SHOULD ASK THE SECRETARY GENERAL OF THE UNITED NATIONS TO CALL AN 
INTERNATIONAL SUGAR CONFERENCE.

GENEVA, JULY 21-C(AP)-JAIME TORRES BODET, DIRECTOR GENERAL OF 
THE UNITED NATIONS EDUCATIONAL, SCIENTIFIC AND CULTURAL ORGANIZATION, 
TOLD THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COUNCIL TODAY "THERE IS NO REAL PEACE 
JITHOUT ECONOMIC JUSTICE AND SOCIAL PROGRESS." 

ARGUING FOR AN INCREASE IN UNESCO'S BUDGET, TORRES BODET SAID THAT 
"TO EXTEND THE POLITICAL RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE UNITED NATIONS WITHOUT 
INCREASING TO CO A CORRESPONDING OR EVEN GREATER DEGREE THE ECONOMIC 
AND SOCIAL ACTIVITIES OF THE SPECIALIZED AGENCIES WOULD BE TO THROW 
THE WHOLE SYSTEM OUT OF BALANCE AND TO REPUDIATE THE PRINCIPLES 
ON WHICH IT IS BASED." 

*AS THINGS ARE TODAY," THE DIRECTOR GENERAL SAID, "IT WOULD 
BE DEFEATISM." 

TORRES BODET SAID THE SPECIALIZED AGENCIES "WERE NOT CREATED 
TO KNOCK TOGETHER A JERRY=BUILT WORLD OF TOMORROW DURING AN UNEASY 
TRUCE, BUT TO PAVE THE WAY, DESPITE TENSIONS OR EVEN WARS, FOR 
THE DAWN OF THE ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL JUSTICE WITHOUT WHICH 

THERE IS NO TRUE PEACE." 

UNESCO'S BUDGET IN 194% WAS $7,683,000. FOR 1951 IT IS TO BE 
$8,200,000. IF THE ORGANIZATION IS TO MOVE FROM THE STAGE OF "SYMBOLIC 
GESTURES" TO "MAJOR ACHIEVEMENT," A SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE IS 
ESSENTIAL, TORRES BODET SAID.

NORTH OF ASTRA ON THE RUSSO-IRANIAN BORDER HAVE BEEN RECEIVED BY 
IRANIAN GENERAL STAFF, RELIABLE INFORMANTS SAID TODAY. 

ASTRA IS “IN NORTHEAST AZERBAIJAN) PROVINCE.

RANGOON, BURMA, JULY 21-CAP)-AN AMERICAN LABOR REPRESENTATIVE 
SAID TODAY AN INCREASING NUMBER OF EASTERN COUNTRIES ARE TURNING FROM 
THE COMMUNIST INSPIRED WORLD FEDERATION OF TRADE UNIONS (WFTU) TO THE 
WESTERN@SUPPORTED saireurtt o JAL CONFEDERATION OF FREE TRADE UNIONS 
CICFTU). 

THE STATEMENT WAS MADE BY GORDON W.CHAPMAN, REPRESENTING THE 
WISCONSIN STATE AND COUNTY MUNICIPAL EMPLOYES UNION (AFL), AND WHO IS 
WITH AN ICFTU DELEGATION VISITING RANGOON. 

CHAPMAN SAID IT WAS APPARENTLY TRUE THAT THE BURMA TRADE UNION 
CONGRESS WAS AFFILIATED WITH WFTU. ANOTHER MEMBER OF THE 

DELEGATION, ROGER DEKEYZER OF BELGIUM, SAID THE ICFTU WAS FREE OF 
GOVERNMENT CONTROL AND URGED THE BURMESE TO CHANGE THEIR AFFILIATION 
HE SAID IT WAS SIGNIFICANT THAT COUNTRIES LIKE INDIA, CEYLON, THE 
PHILIPPINES, IRAN, LEBANON, AUSTRALIA AND THAILAND SOUGHT OR ARE 
SEEKING TO JOIN ICFTU.

JAPANESE (&amp;50) 
BY JOHN MeHIGHTOWER 

WASHINGTON, JULY 21-(AP)=TOP STATE DEPARTMENT OFFICIALS TODAY 
RESUMED ACTIVE WORK ON PLANS FOR A JAPANESE PEACE SETTLEMENT~-~ 
BUT WITHOUT ANY FIRM DECISION WHETHER TO PRESS FOR A TREATY SOON. 

SECRETARY OF STATE ACHESON, IT WAS LEARNED, TALKED WITH JOHN FOSTER 
DULLES REPUBLICAN ADVISER AND FAR EASTERN EXPERT, OPENING A TOP 
LEVEL STUDY OF JAPANESE POLICY IN THE LIGHT OF THE KOREAN CRISIS. 

JUST BEFORE THE KOREAN OUTBREAK, DULLES, DEFENSE SECRETARY JOHNSON 
AND GEN. OMAR BRADLEY, CHAIRMAN OF THE JOINT CHIEF OF STAFFS, 

CONFERRED WITH GEN. DOUGLAS MACARTHUR IN TOKYO ON THE TREATY 
PROJECT AND RELATED QUESTIONS OF AMERICAN SECURITY INTERESTS IN 

THESE TALKS WERE REPORTED TO HAVE RESULTED IN A GENERAL UNDERSTAND- 
ING THAT A JAPANESE PEACE SETTLEMENT SHOULD BE WORKED OUT AS SOON 
AS POSSIBLE. WITH OR WITHOUT RUSSIAe 

SINCE THEN TOP OFFICIALS HAD BEEN SO OCCUPIED WITH KOREA THAT 
THE URGENT QUESTION OF JAPAN*S FUTURE WAS TEMPORARILY SHOVED ASIDE. 

AFTER PRESIDENT TRUMAN SENT HIS KOREAN MESSAGE TO CONGRESS WEDNESDAY 
ACHESON DIRECTED AIDES TO RESUME FULL SPEED ON JAPAN. 

THE FIRST QUESTION IS WHETHER THE AMERICAN GOVERNMENT SHOULD SEEK A 
TREATY AT THIS TIME OR PERHAPS UNDERTAKE BY OTHER MEANS TO FULFILL 
JAPAN'S ASPIRATIONS FOR SELF-RULE AND AN END TO THE OCCUPATION. 

A PEACE TREATY IS A WAY TO WIND UP ALL THE QUESTIONS GROWING OUT 
OF A WAR. BUT MANY OF THESE QUESTIONS=--PERHAPS ALL THE IMPORTANT 
ONES, SOME OFFICIALS THINK, COULD IF NECESSARY BE HANDLED SEPARATELY. 
THUS IN A SETTLEMENT WITHOUT A TREATY JAPAN MIGHT BE GIVEN FULL | 
REPRESENTATION IN FOREIGN CAPITALS, CONTROL OF ITS FOREIGN AND 
DOMESTIC POLICIES AND AN END, IN FACT, TO THE OCCUPATION. IN ANY 
SUCH ACTIONS THE UNITED STATES WOULD EXPECT TO COOPERATE FULLY WITH 
FRIENDLY GOVERNMENTS. | . 

UNDERLYING ALL AMERICAN THINKING ON THE JAPANESE ISSUE, NOW AS 
IN THE PAST, IT IS UNDERSTOOD, IS A DECISION THAT ANY ARRANGEMENT 
MUST PROVIDE FOR THE CONTINUED PRESENCE OF AMERICAN TROOPS IN JAPAN. 
THEY WOULD REMAIN AS A SECURITY FORCE AGAINST SOVIET COMMUNISM IN 
ASIA RATHER THAN AS AN OCCUPATION FORCE. 

JAPAN ITSELF, UNDER ITS CONSTITUTION, CAN HAVE NO TROOPS. THE 
DANGERS OF ITS EXPOSED POSITION ARE UNDERSTOOD TO HAVE BECOME MUCH 
CLEARER TO THE, JAPANESE THEMSELVES AS A RESULT OF THE COMMUNIST

CR AN ACUTE SHORTAGE OF NON-PERISHABLE FOODSTUFFS IN HAMBURG, 
GERMAN RETAILERS ASSOCIATION OFFICIALS REPORTED TODAY. 

FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE THE 1948 CURRENCY REFORM 
QUEUES FORMED IN FRONT OF SHOPS WHICH STILL HAD SMALL STOCKS OF SUCH

AS A RESERVE AGAINST WARTIME SHORTAGES OR RATIONING. 

SIMILAR BUYING SPREES BY FOOD HOARDERS HAVE BEEN REPORTED FROM MANY 
CITIES IN GERMANY SINCE THE OUTBREAK OF WAR IN KOREA. BUT HAMBURG 
APPEARED TO BE THE FIRST CITY WHERE AN ACUTE SHORTAGE DEVELOPED. 

THE WEST GERMANY GOVERNMENT RECENTLY ISSUED AN OFFICIAL ASSURANCE 
TO THE PEOPLE THAT FOOD STOCKS ARE ADEQUATE AND THERE IS NO NEED 


OF HOARDING.

THE MUSIC. A FEW HANDSHAKES FROM GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS, AND THE 
SALUTES OF THE MEN ASSIGNED TO GUARD HIM, WERE ALL THE WELCOME 
LEOPOLD GOT AFTER HIS SIX YEARS ABSENCE FROM HIS HOMELAND. 

THE NAZIS TOOK LEOPOLD TO GERMANY IN 194d WHEN BRUSSELS WAS 
ABOUT TO FALL TO ADVANCING ALLIED TROOPS, UNDER HEAVY GUARD. 

MANY BELGIANS CHARGED THAT HE WAS MORE "GUEST" OF THE NAZIS THAN 
A PRISONER OF WAR. THIS, ADDED TO THE FACT THAT HE HAD SURRENDERED 
TO THE INVADERS IN 1940 INSTEAD OF FLEEING TO ENGLAND WITH HIS 
MINISTERS TO CONTINUE THE FIGHT, LED TO HIS BEING EXILED IN 1945. 

A LONG AND BITTER STRUGGLE FOLLOWED BETWEEN THE SOCIAL CHRISTIANS, 
WHO WANTED THE KING BACK, AND THE SOCIALISTS, COMMUNISTS AND 
LIBERALS WHO DIDN*T. 

IT ENDED THURSDAY WHEN THE SOCIAL CHRISTIAN MAJORITY IN 
PARLIAMENT VOTED TO ASK THE KING TO RETURN. THE SOCIALISTS HAVE 
THREATENED TO DISRUPT BELGIUM WITH STRIKES IN PROTEST. 

LEOPOLD SPED FROM THE AIRPORT TO HIS COUNTRY PALACE AT SUBURBAN 
LAEKEN IN A WILD RACE LIKE A SCENE FROM A HOLLYWOOD GANGSTER MOVIE.’ 

THE KING*S CAR, FLYING THE ROYAL STANDARD, WAS IN THE MIDST OF AN 
ARMED CAVALCADE INCLUDING FOUR ARMORED CARS AND 17 TRUCKLOADS OF 
HEAVILY ARMED GENDARMFS.

AGAINST THIS COUNTRY. PRESSURE CAMPAIGN 
THIS CAMPAIGN OBVIOUSLY HAS THREE MAJOR OBJECTIVES: 
1--TO KEEP YUGOSLAV DEFENSES SPREAD AS THINLY AS POSSIBLF. 
2=-TO SOUND OUT BEST POSSIBLE SPOTS FOR INVASION, SHOULD THE 
KREMLIN DECIDE UPON SUCH A STEP. 

3-=-TO FORCE YUGOSLAVIA TO MAINTAIN A LARGE STANDING ARMY 
DRAINING OFF MANPOWER NEEDED FOR DOMESTIC RECONSTRUCTION AND 
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. 

BY BELT TIGHTENING AT HOME AND THROUGH TRADE AGREEMENTS WITH THE 
WEST, TITO HAS MANAGED THUS FAR TO OFFSET THE COMINFORM PRESSURE AND-- 
IN SOME WAYS--TO USE IT TO PROMOTE YUGOSLAV UNITY. 

DIVIDED BY RACE AND RELIGION, BY CUSTOMS PARTLY WESTERN AND 
PARTLY EASTERN, THERE IS ONE COMMON CHARACTERISTIC IN YUGOSLAVIA-- 
HISTORICAL DETERMINATION FOR INDEPENDENCE.  TITO HAS PLAYED UPON 
IT TO THE UTMOST. 

THIS HAS STRENGTHENED HIS HAND NOW AT A TIME WHEN YUGOSLAV CONCERN 
OVER THE POSSIBILITY OF AN INVASION HAS REACHED ITS HIGHEST POINT-- 
MUCH MORE SO THAN DURING THE SO-CALLED AUGUST CRISIS OF 1949. 

THAT CONCERN HAS BEEN GENERATED BY THE KOREAN WAR AND THE 
POSSIBILITY IT MAY TURN INTO A GENERAL WORLD CONFLICT. PLUS THE

ASHINGTON, -(AP)-STA AND DEFENSE DEPARTMENT OFFICIALS 
WERE REPORTED GIV PROMF ONSIDERATION TODAY TO THE QUESTIONS 
RAISED BY THE REPORTED CHINESE COMMUNIST SHELLING OF THE NATIONALIST 
ISLAND OF QUEMOY. 

FIRST INDICATIONS WERE THAT OFFICIALS DO NOT REGARD AMERICAN 
REQUESTS TO THE CHINESE NATIONALISTS TO WITHHOLD MILITARY MOVES 
AGAINST THE COMMUNISTS AS PREVENTING PURELY DEFENSIVE OPERATIONS. 

THERE WAS NO INDICATION THAT THE AMERICAN SEVENTH FLEET 
WHICH PRESIDENT TRUMAN HAS ASSIGNED TO PROTECT FORMOSA, WOULD HAVE 
ANY RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PROTECTION OF QUEMOYe THAT SMALL ISLAND, 
THOUGH NATIONALIST“@HELD, LIES JUST OFF THE MAINLAND AND IS FAR 
OVER ON THE COMMUNIST SIDE OF THE LINE OF THE SEVENTH FLEET PATROL. 

A STATEMENT OF THE AMERICAN ATTITUDE IS EXPECTED TO BE SENT TO THE 
CHINESE NATIONALIST GOVERNMENT ON FORMOSA IN A FEW DAYS. MEANWHILE, 
THE STATE DEPARTMENT SAID THAT NO OFFICIAL REPORT ON THE QUEMOY 
INCIDENT HAD BEEN RECEIVED FROM NATIONALIST HEADQUARTERS AT TAIPEI. 

ON JUNE 27, IN HIS STATEMENT ANNOUNCING THAT AMERICAN FORCES HAD BEEN 
ORDERED TO SUPPORT SOUTH KOREA AGAINST COMMUNIST ATTACK, PRESIDENT 
TRUMAN ANNOUNCED ALSO THAT HE HAD ORDERED THE SEVENTH FLEET TO PREVENT 
ANY ATTACK ON FORMOSA AND CALLED ON THE CHINESE NATIONALIST GOVERNMENT 
"TO CEASE ALL AIR AND SEA OPERATIONS AGAINST THE MAINLAND.* 

ABOUT TWO WEEKS LATER, THE CHINESE ASKED THE UNITED STATES FOR 
CLARIFICATION OF THE PRESIDENT'S STAND. DID IT MEAN, FOR EXAMPLE, 
THAT RECONNAISSANCE FLIGHTS TO_OBSERVE THE MOVEMENT GF CHINESE 
COMMUNIST FORCES SHOULD NOT BE MADE?* 

THIS CHINESE NOTE, OFFICIALS MADE CLEAR TODAY, HAS NOT YET BEEN 
ANSWERED BUT AN ANSWER WILL BE SENT SHORTLY. IN RESPONSE TO INQUIRIES 
AS TO WHAT THE UNITED STATES THINKS THE CHINESE NATIONALISTS SHOULD 
DO ABOUT AN ATTACK ON QUEMOY, THE STATE DEPARTMENT WOULD SAY 
ONLY THAT THE PRESIDENT'S STATEMENT SPEAKS FOR ITSELF. 


AUTHORITIES WOULD OFFER NO GUIDANCE ON SUCH QUESTIONS AS WHETHER 
A NATIONALIST SEA=AIR ATTACK ON THE RED CONCENTRATIONS REPORTED BEING 
BUILT UP FOR A DRIVE ON QUEMOY WOULD BE CLASSED AS DEFENSIVE ACTION. 
THE ATTITUDE BEING DEVELOPED HERE WITH RESPECT TO QUEMOY WOULD 
NOT NECESSARILY APPLY TO ALL OTHER NATIONALIST HELD ISLANDS OTHER 
THAN FORMOSA. FOR INSTANCE SMALL ISLANDS AROUND FORMOSA WHOSE 
DEFENSE WOULD BE ESSENTIAL TO THE DEFENSE OF FORMOSA ITSELF EVIDENTLY

A FOREIGN CAPTAIN OF A TRAWLER FISHING OFF THE NEWFOUNDLAND GRAND 
BANKS RECEIVED THE FRIGHT OF HIS LIFE LAST WEEK WHEN A CREW MEMBER 
REPORTED THAT A SUBMARINE HAD SURFACED OFF THE STERN. 

THE CAPTAIN DISCOVERED TO HIS AMAZEMENT THAT THE REPORT WAS 
CORRECT. AND A LARGE BLACK SUBMARINE WITH NO MARKINGS HAD SURFACED 
LESS THAN 100 YARDS FROM THE VESSEL. THE SUB REMAINED ON THE SURFACE 
FOR OVER 10 MINUTES, THEN DIVED. 

THE TRAWLER CAPTAIN GOT THE IMPRESSION THAT FROM THE TYPE OF 
CONSTRUCTION IT WAS A RUSSIAN SUB ALTHOUGH IT IS POSSIBLE FOR JUST 


ABOUT ANY SUBMARINE TO CAMOUFLAGE ITS CONSTRUCTION TO MAKE IT LOOK 


LIKE THAT OF ANOTHER NATIONALITY 

HOWEVER, . NO. BRITISH OR AMERICAN MARKINGS- WERE ON THE SUB. ‘AND AS 
THE TRAWLER HAD NO SHIP-TO-SHORE RADIO, IT WAS IMPOSSIBLE TO REPORT 
THE SUB TO THE AUTHORITIES UNTIL THE SHIP RETURNED TO PORT. 

WHEN THE TRAWLER ARRIVED IN TOWN FIVE DAYS AFTER SEEING THE 
SUBMARINE, THE SUNDAY HERALD UPON LEARNING OF THE INCIDENT REACHED 
THE CAPTAIN AND LEARNED FROM HIM THAT THE SUB APPEARED TO BE SOMETHING 
OF A MYSTERY BECAUSE ALTHOUGH THERE ARE A NUMBER OF BRITISH AND 
AMERICAN SUBMARINES IN THE NORTH ATLANTIC AT THE TIME THE MYSTERY 
CRAFT GHTED, THERE WAS NONE REPORTED IN THE AREA OF THE

THE TANKS THAT GENe MACARTHUR HAD TO SEND TO KOREA WHEN THE 
RUSSIAN-MADE T-34 TANKS BEGAN TO SPEARHEAD THE DRIVE OF THE RED FORCES 
WERE ONLY THE LIGHT TANKS, THE 35-TON JOBS. THEY MOUNTED THE SAME 
CALIBER GUN AS THE REDS* ‘T-34S, 76 MILLIMETERS, BUT THE VELOCITY oF 
THE REDS" GUN WAS MUGH HIGHER AND THE ARMOR MUCH BETTER. 

WHAT WAS NEEDED, IT WAS APPARENT, WERE MEDIUM TANKS--45-TONNERS WITH 
HIGH*-VELOCITY 90 MILLIMETER GUNS, WIDER TREADS TO ENABLE THEM TO 
OPERATE ON BAD ROADS AND IMPROVED TRANSMISSION-STEERING FACILITIES. 

MACARTHUR"S COMMAND HAD A FEW OF THESE MEDIUMS, BUT THEY HADN'T 
BEEN USED AND WEREN'T READY. THE REASON HIS JAPANESE OCCUPATION 
FORCES HAD NOT USED THEM IN JAPAN WAS THAT JAPANESE BRIDGES GENERALLY 
CANNOT CARRY THE WEIGHT.

THE CONGRESSIONAL SCHEDULE FOR THE NEXT FEW DAYS IS A BUSY ONE. 

SENATE AND HOUSE BANKING COMMITTEES WILL OPEN PUBLIC HEARINGS 
MONDAY ON A BROAD=-TERMED SYSTEM OF CONTROLS AND ALLOCATIONS PREPARED 
AT THE WHITE HOUSE AND TITLED "DEFENSE PRODUCTION ACT OF 1950." 

BOTH HOUSE AND SENATE LEADERS WERE CERTAIN OF QUICK FINAL PASSAGE 
THIS WEEK OF TWO MEASURES FOR BUILDING UP STRENGTH OF THE FIGHTING 
FORCES. ONE, ALLOWING THE PRESIDENT TO EXTEND ALL ENLISTMENTS ONE 
YEAR. ALREADY HAS SPED THROUGH THE SENATE WITHOUT OBJECTION. THE 
PRESIDENT NOW HAS AUTHORITY TO CALL AND HOLD OFFICERS IN BOTH REGULAR 
AND RESERVE FORCES. 

THE OTHER WOULD REMOVE THE PRESENT MANPOWER CEILINGS OF JUST ABOVE 
2,000,000 FROM THE ARMY, AIR FORCE NAVY AND MARINES. 

HOUSE LEADERS SCHEDULED QUICK PASSAGE OF BOTH FOR TUESDAY AND 
SENATE LEADERS MAY ACT ON THE EXTRA DUTY BILL BY OR BEFORE THEN. 

THE NEXT MILITARY LEGISLATION ASKED FOR BY CHAIRMAN TYDINGS (D-MD) 
OF THE SENATE ARMED SERVICES COMMITTEE IS A REVIVAL OF THE WARTIME 
"FAMILY SUPPORT ALLOWANCES" FOR ALL SERVICE MEN. 

CONGRESS ORDERED THESE BENEFITS TO TAPER OFF IN 1948 BUT THEY COST 
$250 000.000 FOR THE LAST YEAR EVEN THOUGH THE ARMED FORCES WERE ONLY 
A FRACTION OF WARTIME STRENGTH. REVIVAL OF THE FAMILY SUPPORT 
ALLOWANCES USED DURING THE LAST WAR WOULD COST BILLIONS IF THE ARMED 
FORCES ARE BUILT UP RAPIDLY.

GERMANY'S PLACE IN THE DEFENSE OF THE WEST IS REGARDED BY MANY 
OFFICIALS AS AMONG THE MOST IMPORTANT OF THE GROUP"S PROBLEMS. THE 
INDUSTRIAL WEALTH OF THE RUHR VALLEY AND OTHER FACILITIES WHICH

THE DEFENSE OF THE WHOLE WESTERN WORLD IN A THIRD, THESE AUTHORITIES 

IN ADDITION THERE IS A QUESTION OF GERMAN MANPOWER AND WHETHER IT 
SHOULD BE ARMED. AT THE MOMENT THE AMERICAN GOVERNMENT IS NOT PRE- 
PARED TO PRESS THIS PROBLEM, BEING KEENLY SENSITIVE TO FRENCH FEARS, 
BUT IN TIME IT IS EXPECTED TO COME TO A DECISION. 

ON MILITARY PRODUCTION SECRETARY ACHESON WENT TO LONDON LAST SPRING 
PREPARED TO URGE THE MANUFACTURE OF NON-COMBAT EQUIPMENT IN GERMAN 
FACTORIES BUT FINALLY LET THE POINT RIDE OVER UNTIL HIS NEXT MEETING 
WITH THE FOREIGN MINISTERS OF BRITAIN, FRANCE AND THE OTHER TREATY 
NATIONS IN NEW YORK IN SEPTEMBER. 

THE WORK TO BE DONE BY THE DEPUTIES WILL BE POINTED TOWARD THE 
NEW YORK SESSION AS THE PLACE WHERE MEN WITH THE POWER OF FINAL 
DECISION WILL COME TOGETHER. 

FRANCE AND SOME OF THE OTHER CONTINENTAL COUNTRIES ARE EXTREMELY 
RELUCTANT TO SEE GERMAN RESOURCES PUT TO MILITARY USE AGAIN BECAUSE 
OF THE DANGER OF REVIVING GERMAN MILITARY POWER. 

THE AMERICAN ANSWER TO THIS FRENCH VIEW IN THE LONG RUN PROBABLY 
WILL REST ON THREE POINTS: FIRST, THAT THE ATLANTIC ALLIANCE GIVES 
FRANCE MAXIMUM PROTECTION AGAINST GERMANY$3 SECOND, THAT THE SOVIET 
MENACE IS THE DANGER OF THE MOMENT, NOT THE GERMAN MENACE3 THIRD 
THAT GERMAN ARMIES DO NOT HAVE TQ BE RECREATED IN ORDER TO MAKE USE 
OF GERMAN MANPOWER.» 

NO SERIOUS EFFORT TO REARM GERMAN MEN IS IN PROSPECT UNTIL SUCH 
TIME AS THE ATLANTIC POWERS HAVE ORGANIZED THEIR OWN DEFENSES TO THE 
POINT OF ESTABLISHING SOME KIND OF INTERNATIONAL FORCE OR MILITARY 
COMMAND. WHAT IS NOW GENERALLY SPECULATED ON AMONG OFFICIALS IS THE 
IDEA OF USING SMALL UNITS OF GERMANS AS PARTS OF AN INTERNATIONAL 
MILITARY ORGANIZATION,

IN MANY CASES THE SHIFT TO WAR PRODUCTION WOULD BE EASY. SOME 
COMPANIES ARE MAKING FOR THE CIVILIAN MARKET THE SAME THINGS THAT THEY 
WOULD MAKE FOR THE GOVERNMENT, AND CONVERSION WOULD SIMPLY SEA CHANGE

REQUIRED. JUL Zor

TOKYO, MONDAY, JULY 24-(AP)-NORTH KOREAN FORCES HAVE SWEPT ALMOST 


BY THE ASSOCIATED PRESS ad 
THE LENGTH OF THE KOREAN WEST COAST AND SEIZED A RAIL AND HIGHWAY LINK 
FAR IN THE REAR OF AMERICAN FORCES ON THE TAEJON FRONT, A UeSe 
EIGHTH ARMY SPOKESMAN ANNOUNCED TODAY. 

AT THE SAME TIME GENERAL MACARTHUR REPORTED COMMUNIST TROOPS 
BUILDING UP ON THE SOUTHWESTERN, WESTERN AND CENTRAL FRONTS. HE 
SAID “CONSIDERABLE STRENGTH*® HAD BEEN FUNNELLED INTO THE VITAL TAEJON 
FRONT BY THE REDS. 

WHILE THE REDS WERE MAKING THEIR WIDE SWEEP DOWN THE WEST COAST, 
A STRONG NORTH KOREAN ARMORED THRUST EAST OF TAEJON WAS HALTED 
BY AN AMERICAN COMBINATION OF PLANES, ARTILLERY AND BAZOOKAS. 

THE NORTH KOREAN'S SWIFT DASH SOUTHWARD ALONG THE WEST COAST 
GAVE THEM KWANGJU SUNDAY, THE FIGHTH ARMY SPOKESMAN SAID. 
KWANGJU, ABOUT 40 MILES FROM THE WEST COAST AND THE SAME DISTANCE FRO! 
THE SOUTH COAST, WAS REPORTED CAPTURED BY THE NORTH KOREAN RADIO AT 


PYONGYANG TODAY. 


POSSESSION OF KWANGJU PUT THE REDS ASTRIDE A RAILROAD AND a 
HIGHWAY LEADING TO THE AREA BEHIND THE NEW UeSe 

POSITIONS ON THE FRONT AROUND TAEJON, 75 MILES TO THE NORTHEAST. 

THE COMMUNISTS APPARENTLY TOOK THE CITY WITH FAIRLY SMALL FORCES WHICH 
HAD LITTLE OPPOSITION ON THE WAY. 

ASSOCIATED PRESS CORRESPONDENT LEIF ERICKSON AT EIGHTH ARMY 
HEADQUARTERS SAID THE RED SWEEP COULD DEVELOP INTO A WIDE FLANKING 
MOVEMENT AGAINST THE AMERICAN SUPPLY LINES RUNNING TO THE TAEJON 
FRONT FROM THE MAIN PORT OF PUSAN AT THE SOUTHEAST TIP OF KOPEA. 

"BUT IT IS APPARENT THE AMERICAN COMMAND HERE IS NOT YET 
CONCERNED THAT_THE REDS CAN MAKE A SERIOUS THREAT FROM THIS DIRECTION 
WHTILE HITTING IN STRENGTH ON OTHER SECTORS."

du IN HISTORY TO THE LIFE INSURANCE AGENCIES

INSURANCE HOME OFFICES AND AGENCIES REPORTED AN UNPRECEDENTED 
DEMAND FOR LIFE INSURANCE, WITH YOUNG MEN AND THOSE OF LOWER MIDDLE 
AGE DOING MOST OF THE APPLYING. 

THE CALL OF MANY MILITARY RESERVISTS TO ACTIVE DUTY WAS ALMOST 
ENTIRELY RESPONSIBLE FOR DEMAND, INSURANCE MEN SAID. 

NATIONAL SERVICE LIFE INSURANCE UP TO $10,000 STILL IS PROVIDED 
AT LOW COST TO MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AND VETERANS BY THE 
VETERANS ADMINISTRATION. MANY MEN EVIDENTLY FEEL, HOWEVER, THEIR 
PROTECTIVE DUTY TO FAMILIES EXTENDS BEYOND $10,006. HENCE THEY ARE 
HURRYING TO BUY ADDITIONAL INSURANCE FROM THE PRIVATE COMPANIES. 

WHILE NO FIGURES AS TO THE NUMBER OF APPLICATIONS OR THE 
AGGREGATE FACE VALUE OF INSURANCE SOUGHT WERE AVAILABLE, COMPANY 
SPOKESMEN SAID THE AGENCIES WERE MUCH BUSIER WITH NEW APPLICATIONS 
LAST WEEK THAN THEY WERE IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO WORLD WAR Ile 

THE INTERNATIONAL SITUATION LEFT THE INSURANCE INDUSTRY WITH A 
BIG PROBLEM=--WHAT TO DO ABOUT WAR RISK CLAUSES. 

THESE CLAUSES AS GENERALLY APPLIED DURING THE LAST WAR 
EXEMPTED DEATH IN ACTION OF MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AS A CAUSE 
FOR PAYMENT OF THE FACE AMOUNT OF POLICIES. UPON DEATH UNDER SUCH 
CIRCUMSTANCES, THE COMPANIES ONLY REFUNDED THE PREMIUMS PAID IN PLUS 
ACCRUED DIVIDENDS. 

THE COMPANIES, AS A MATTER OF BUSINESS RELATIONS, DO NOT LIKE TO 
APPLY A WAR RISK’CLAUSE EXCEPT IN CASE OF ABSOLUTE NECESSITY. IT IS 
WELL UNDERSTOOD, HOWEVER, THAT WITHOUT CERTAIN RESTRICTIONS ON 
POLICY UNDERWRITING, THE INSURANCE BUSINESS WOULD FACE FINANCIAL 
DISASTER IN CASE OF A GENERAL WARe 

IT WAS REPORTED WITHOUT CONFIRMATION THAT SOME COMPANIES HAD 
SUBMITTED SUCH CLAUSES TO STATE INSURANCE OFFICIALS FOR APPROVAL. 

TO DATE, HOWEVER, WAR CLAUSES HAVE FAILED TO APPEAR EXCEPT FOR 
LIMITED APPLICATION. .

BRUSSELS, BELGIUM, JULY 23-CAP)-KING LEOPOLD III APPEARED TODAY TO 
HAVE CONS TO STAY, AND HIS OPPONENTS CONCEDED IT MIGHT BE A LONG, 
IARD FIGHT TO DISLODGE HIM FROM HIS REGAINED THRONE, 

HOPES OF SOME BELGIANS THAT THE KING MIGHT RETURN FROM EXILE 
ONLY TO HAND OVER POWER TO HIS SON AND HEIR, THE 19-YEAR-OLD CROWN 
PRINCE BAUDOUIN, WERE BEGINNING TO WANE FOLLOWING HIS HOMECOMING 

SO FAR, NOTHING THAT LEOPOLD HAS SAID OR DONE HAS GIVEN THE SLIGHTEST 
INDICATION THAT HE WILL RELINQUISH HIS THRONE. WITHIN A FEW HOURS OF 
NOT WANT TO HEAR OF ABDICATION. 

SUMMONED TO A MEETING OF THE CROWN 
COUNCIL AT LAEKEN PALACE, WERE NEATLY FRUSTRATED IN THEIR ANNOUNCED 
INTENTION OF URGING IMMEBIATE ABDICATION. THEY WITHDREW IN PROTEST 
WHEN TOLD TH KING WOULD ONLY READ THEM AN ADDRESS AND THEY WOULD HAVE 
NO CHANCE To EXPRESS THEIR OPINIONS. 

SINCE THE STRONGLY ANTI-LEOPOLD SOCIALIST STATE MINISTERS HAD 
ALREADY SENT IN THEIR RESIGNATIONS, THE KING FOUND HIS COUNCIL REDUCED 
FROM 28 TO 10=-ALL MEMBERS OF THE GATHOLIC SOCIAL CHRISTIAN PARTY 
WHICH VOTED TO RECALL HIM FROM SWITZERLAND. 

THE CROWN PRINCE WAS NOT MENTIONED IN LEOPOLD'S BROADCAST TO THE 
NATION. THE PRINCE'S IMMEDIATE FUTURE WAS INDICATED CLEARLY IN THE 
KING'S MESSAGE TO PARLIAMENT, WHEN LEOPOLD REFERRED TO HIM ONLY IN 
HIS PLANS FOR BAUDOUIN'S FURTHER EDUCATION. 

THE PROUD LANGUAGE OF BOTH DECLARATIONS HINTED AT ROYAL 
CONCILIATION, A PROMISE TO FORGET THE PAST, BUT NOWHERE SUGGESTED THAT 
THE KING ADMITTED ANY PAST MISTAKES. THE KING'S SURRENDER TO THE 
GERMAN ARMIES IN WORLD WAR TWO AND HIS SUBSEQUENT MARRIAGE TO A 
COMMONER HAVE EMBITTERED MANY BELGIANS TOWARD HIM. 


A2i 
BELGIANS, WHO HAD HOPED THE SIX-YEAR=OLD CONSTITUTIONAL CRISIS 


WOULD BE ENDED, SAW AN UNPROMISING START TO THE RESUMED REIGN. 

THE SOCIALISTS, WHO HAVE BEEN THE MOST BITTERLY OPPOSED TO LEOPOLD'S 
RETURN. TOOK A SYMBOLIC OATH IN BRUSSELS LAST NIGHT THAT THEY WOULD 
NEVER CEASE THEIR STRUGGLE UNTIL "HE PACKS HIS BAGS FOR GOOD." 

BUT THE NATIONAL HOLIDAY WEEKEND -- FRIDAY WAS BELGIUM'S INDEPENDENCE 
DAY -- THREW THEM OFF BALANCE. MOST OBSERVERS PREDICTED IT MIGHT

THE SOCIALISTS ARE KNOWN TO BE PREPARING FOR GENERAL STKIKES 
THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY, STREET DEMONSTRATIONS AND AN UNRELENTING NEWS- 
PAPER CAMPAIGN. 

THE KING IS SECLUDED IN THE TREE-SHROUDED PARK OF LAEDEN, PROTECTED 
BY GENDARMERIE AND TROOPS. HE CAN PLAY A WAITING GAME IF HE WANTS. 

HE CAN CALL OUT TO LAEKEN THOSE HE WANTS TO SEE. AND RULE WITHOUT 
BEING SEEN IN PUBLIC UNTIL THE PRESENT TENSION EASES. 

AN INDICATION THAT HE MAY INTEND FOLLOWING SUCH A COURSE WAS SEEN 
IN THE FACT THAT HE SENT A MESSAGE TO BE READ IN PARLIAMENT TUESDAY, 
INSTEAD OF APPEARING IN PERSON TO READ HIS SPEECH FROM THE THRONE 
AS MANY EXPECTED HIM TO DOs SOCIALISTS HAD THREATENED THAT, IF HE 
DID. HE WOULD NOT BE HEARD BEYOND HIS OPENING "MESSIEURS, MESDAMES." 


LEOPOLD REMAINED QUIETLY AT LAEKEN TODAY. IN THE MORNING HE 
ATTENDED MASS IN THE PALACE CHAPEL WITH QUEEN-MOTHER ELISABETH AND 
OTHER MEMBERS OF HIS FAMILY. 

A CROWD OF ABOUT 1,000 STOOD AROUND ALL DAY OUTSIDE LAEKEN PALACE, 
CALLING FOR LEOPOLDe HE DID NOT APPEAR. WOMEN DID A BRISK TRADE 
IN PICTURES OF THE KING. 

LAEKEN LOOKED MORE LIKE A JAIL THAN A PALACE. CENDARMES 
CARRYING RIFLES OR SUBMACHINE=-GUNS STOOD AT INTERVALS OF 25 
YARDS AROUND THE WALLS OF THE PARKe A TROOP OF 30 MOUNTED 
GENDARMES WAS DRAWN UP BY THE MAIN GATE. POLICEMEN ON BICYCLES 
PATROLLED THE FOOTPATHS OF THE PARK INSIDE. 

COMMUNISTS HELD AN ANTI“LEOPOLD DEMONSTRATION IN THE CENTER OF 
BRUSSELSe POLICE BROKE IT UPe AT LIEGE SEVERAL THOUSAND DEMONSTRATORS 
TURNED OUT TO PROTEST THE KING*"S RETURN. 

CHARLEROI, A STRONGLY ANTI-LEOPOLD CENTER, REPORTED THREE SMALL 
BOMB EXPLOSIONS DURING THE NIGHT. ONE WAS At AN ELECTRIC SUBSTATION 
BUT LITTLE DAMAGE WAS DONE. ;

TOKYO ,TUESDAY JULY 25-C(AP)=THE FOLLOWING IS THE TEXT OF KOREAN

1 PeMe TODAY (10 P2Me MONDAY E.SeTe)e IT COVERS AN OPERATIONAL

(9 AeMe SUNDAY TO 9 AcMe MONDAY, EeSete)$ 

STRIKES BY USeSe AIR FORCE B-29S CONTINUED TO TEAR HOLES IN THE 
BATTERED NORTH KOREAN COMMUNICATIONS AND TRANSPORTATION NETWORK 
BEHIND THE BATTLE LINES ON JULY 24. 

A PRELIMINARY ANALYSIS INDICATED THAT FROM 12 TO 15 BRIDGES WERE 
SERIOUSLY HIT IN BOMBER ATTACKS AND OTHER BRIDGES WERE DAMAGED. 

PRIMARY TARGETS FOR THE MEDIUM BOMBER ASSAULTS WERE RAILROAD AND 
HIGHWAY BRIDGES IN OR NEAR KONGJU, ICHON, PYONGTAEK, CHOEHIWON 
SEOUL, CHONGJU AND HONGSONG WHICH THE NORTH KOREANS ARE USING To MOVE 
MEN AND MATERIEL SOUTH TO THE BATTLEFRONTS. 

VISIBILITY WAS GENERALLY EXCELLENT IN ALL TARGET AREAS HIT BY THE 
SUPERFORTRESSES AND THE RESULTS OF NEARLY ALL MISSIONS WERE REPORTED 
AS FROM GOOD TO EXCELLENTe SPANS WERE CONFIRMS AS OUT BY VISUAL 
RECONNAISSANCE ON BRIDGES AT KONGJU, ICHON, PYONGTAEK, SEOUL AND 


CHONG JU. 

FINAL APPRAISAL OF THIS NEW DAMAGE TO THE NORTH KOREAN SUPPLY 
SYSTEM WILL DEPEND ON RECONNAISSANCE PHOTOGRAPHY. 

THE SUPERFORTS ALSO STRUCK AT A RAILROAD MARSHALLING YARD IN 
THE CHONGJU AREA. 

B-26S OF THE FIFTH AIRFORCE TOOK AN ACTIVE PART IN THE INTER- 
DICTION OF THE NORTH KOREAN FORCES BY AIR ASSAULT. THE LIGHT BOMBERS 
DAMAGED A BRIDGE AT TAECHON ON THE KOREAN WEST COAST AND PROBABLY 
DESTROYED ANOTHER NEAR ICHONe DIRECT HITS WERE SCORED ON THE 
CHECHON MARSHALLING YARD AND OTHER GROUND TARGETS WERE PINPOINTED 
IN THE WESTERN BATTLE SECTOR. 

FIFTH AIRFORCE F-80S CONTINUED ARMED RECONNAISSANCE AND GROUND 
SUPPORT MISSINS ALONG THE BATTLEFRONT AND NORTHWARDS AS FAR AS 
SEOUL. ONE NORTH KOREAN CRAFT WAS DESTROYED ON THE GROUND AND 
ANOTHER DAMAGED IN AN ATTACK ON KIMPO AIRFIELD.

COURSE, SUBJECT TO BEING (A) WITHHELD BY OFFICERS IN THE FIELD 
(B) EMBARCOED AT BRIEFING SESSIONS OR BY SPECIFIC ORDER, AS IN THE 
CASE OF A PARTICULAR OPERATION, OR (C) DELAYED UNTIL RELEASED BY A 
HEADQUARTERS SPOKESMAN OR COMMUNIQUE. CORRESPONDENTS FAILING TO 
ADHERE TO THE SPECIFIED OR IMPLIED GROUND RULES, UNDER EXISTING 
CONDITIONS, ARE SUBJECT TO (A) DENIAL OF ACCESS TO ARMY COMMUNICATIONS 
BETWEEN KOREA AND TOKYO OR THE MAINLAND OF THE UNITED STATES, OR (B)

TOKYO, TUESDAY, JULY 25-CAP)-KOREANS AND AMERICANS CLASHED IN 
FIERCE STREET FIGHTING ON THE STREETS OF YONGDONG TODAY AS OTHER RED 
FORCES COMPLETED THEIR SWEEP DOWN THE WEST COAST AND SEIZED CONTROL OF 
ALL KEY RAILWAYS AND HIGHWAYS IN SOUTHWESTERN KOREA. 

DISPATCHES FROM UeSe EIGHTH ARMY HEADQUARTERS SAID TROOPS 
OF THE FIRST CAVALRY DIVISION MET RED INFANTRYMEN IN CLOSE COMBAT 
INSIDE YONGDONG. 20 AIR MILES SOUTH OF COMMUNIST-HELD TAEJON. 

THE NORTH KOREANS APPARENTLY WERE STRIKING WITH FULL POWER IN 
AN ATTEMPT TO MAINTAIN A STEADY PUSH SOUTHEASTWARD ALONG THE DOUBLE- 
TRACK RAIL LINE FROM THE MAIN UeSe SUPPLY PORT AT PUSAN ON KOREA'S 
SOUTHEASTERN TIP. 

AT EIGHTH ARMY HEADQUARTERS THE FIRST CAVALRY WAS DESCRIBED AS 
HOLDING FIRMLY A LINE WEST OF YONGDONG AGAINST REDS ATTACKING FROM 
THE FRONT AND THE FLANKS. THE COMMUNISTS ALSO WERE TRYING TO 
SET UP ROAD BLOCKS IN THE AMERICAN REAR. 

THE YONGDONG PUSH WAS THE HEAVY BLOW OF THE MOMENT ALTHOUGH 
THE ENTIRE 150&lt;MILE AMERICAN-SOUTH KOREAN FRONT WAS UNDER HEAVY RED

OF REDS SWARMING TOWARD THEM. 

SOUTH KOREAN POLICE, ALMOST AS BADLY DISORGANIZED AS THE SOUTH 
KOREAN ARMY AFTER THE SURPRISE INVASION BY THE REDS, PROVED UNABLE TO 
COPE WITH THE SITUATION. THEY TRIED TO SCREEN REFUCEES BUT FAILED. 

MILITARY LEADERS DECIDED TO CLEAR CIVILIANS FROM THE FIGHTING 
AREAS TO SAVE LIVES. 

THOUSANDS STREAMED SOUTH ALL DAY SUNDAY. TO KEEP THE HIGHWAYS 
OPEN TO MILITARY TRAFFIC THEY WERE ROUTED OVER RAILROAD TRACKS WHER- 
EVER POSSIBLE. AT RAIL TERMINALS THEY WERE PUT ABOARD TRAINS.

THERE WAS A COMPLETE ABSENCE OF NORTH KOREAN AIR OPPOSITION.

COMMAND UNLOADED APPROXIMATELY 150 TONS OF HIGH EXPLOSIVES ON

ROUTES IN THE CENTRAL SECTOR.

NIGHT LEAD BRITISH 
BY ARTHUR GAVSHON 
orte Y 25-C(AP)-BRITAIN WAS REPORTED.TOMNIGHT READY TO 


A SMALL GROUND FORCE TO HELP_AMERICAN GIS IN SHE HAS 
ALREADY THROWN SOME NAVAL AND AIR FORCES INTO THE FIGHT. | 
QUALIFIED SOURCES SAID AN IMPORTANT, POSSIBLY DECISIVE FACTOR 
WAS THAT BRITAIN DID NOT WANT AMERICANS TO FEEL THEY WERE FIGHTING 
THE UNITED NATIONS* KOREAN BATTLE SINGLE-HANDED,. 
THE GOVERNMENT'S OFFER MAY BE ANNOUNCED IN THE HOUSE OF COMMONS 
TOMORROW IN A DEBATE ON THE STATE OF THE NATION'S DEFENSES. 
PRIME MINISTER ATTLEE AND CONSERVATIVE LEADER WINSTON CHURCHILL 
WILL JOIN IN THE DEBATE. 
ATTLEE PRESUMABLY WILL TELL THE COMMONS JUST HOW THE BRITISH 
PROPOSE TO MEET U.N. SECRETARY@GENERAL TRYGVE LIE*S PLEA FOR A 
GROUND FORCE TO HELP OUT THE HARD@-PRESSED U.S. TROOPS, 
THESE ARE SOME OF THE QUESTIONS HE MAY HAVE TO ANSWER: 
HOW MANY BRITISH TROOPS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE? 
WHERE WILL THEY COME FROM? 
WHEN WILL THEY GO? 
QUALIFIED OFFICIALS IN THE PAST TWO WEEKS HAVE SUGGESTED THAT 
IF A BRITISH GROUND FORCE IS OKAYED BY THE GOVERNMENT, IF MIGHT RANGE 
FROM A BATTALION TO A BRIGADE IN STRENGTH. 
ONE BATTALION--AVERAGING ABOUT 1,000 MEN--WOULD BE A TOKEN FORCE. 
A BRIGADE FORMATION WOULD RUN TO ABOUT 5,000 MEN. 
SUPPORTING AND SPECIALIST TROOPS WOULD SWELL THESE FIGURES. 
BRITAIN HAS BUDGETED TO SPEND BETWEEN 20 AND 25 PER CENT OF HER 
TOTAL NATIONAL REVENUE THIS YEAR FOR DEFENSE. ECONOMIES WILL HAVE 
TO BE MADE IN OTHER GOVERNMENT SERVICES IF THE COST OF A REARMAMENT 
PROGRAM--IN KEEPING WITH HER ATLANTIC PACT COMMITTMENTS--IS TO 
BE MET. AS _A RESULT THE NATION'S CAPITAL INVESTMENT PROGRAM, ITS 
SOCIAL SERVICES, POSSIBLY ITS FOOD SUBSIDIES MAY HAVE TO BE SLICED. 
THE CABINET DEVOTED MOST OF ITS SESSION TODAY TO SUCH QUESTIONS AND 
TO OTHER ISSUES WHICH HAVE ARISEN AS A RESULT OF THE KOREAN WARe 
ONE THING DISCUSSED, FOR INSTANCE, WAS WHETHER TO LENGTHEN THE 
18-MONTH TERM WHICH THE NATION'S CONSCRIPT ARMY NOW SERVES, TO 
TWO YEARS. THIS WOULD INVOLVE NEW LEGISLATION. THE GOVERNOENT 
PRESUMABLY DECIDED TO DROP THE IDEA FOR THE PRESENT AT LEAST, SINCE 
PARE JANERT RECESSES AT THE END OF THE WEEK.

LONDON, JULY 25-(AP)=-THE UNITED STATES URGED LIS-SELLOW MEMBERS OF 
THE NORTH_ATLANTIC PACT TODAY TO REARM SPEEDILY AS A MEANS OF PREVENT- 
ING ANOTHER COMMUNIST ATTACK ON. N PATTERN. 

THE CALL WAS VOICED BY CHARLFS M.S D. A NEW YORK LAWYER 
WHO IS DEPUTY TO UeS. SECRETARY OF STATE ACHESON, AT THE OPENING 
SESSION OF THE ATLANTIC PACT COUNCIL. A CIVILIAN’ HIGH COMMAND. 

SPOFFORD WAS ELECTED CHAIRMAN, THE MEETING WAS SECRET, BUT HERE Is 
THE GIST OF HIS SPEECH TeOPT BECAME KNOWN 

EVENTS IN KOREA HAVE SHOWN COMMUNISM DOES NOT HESITATE TO PASS 
FROM SUBVERSION TO ARMED AGGRESSION, THE 12 PACT NATIONS MUST BE 
VIGILANT SO AS NOT TO BE CAUGHT NAPPING BY COMMUNIST AGGRESSION 
ELSEWHERE IN THE WORLD. THE COUNCIL'S BASIC TASK IS TO SAFECUARD 
PEACE AND FREEDOM IN THE WESTERN WORLD. THE PACT NATIONS HAVE OVER- 
HWLEMING SUPERIORITY IN MORAL STRENGTH-- 


WHELMING SUPERIORITY IN MORAL STRENGTH==AND POTENTIALLY IN MILITARY 
STRENGTH=~OVER THE COMMUNIST WORLD. INCREASING THE MILITARY STRENGTH 
OF THE PACT NATIONS IS NOW NECESSARY, THOUGH NONE HAD WANTED TO DO IT. 

THE PACT NATIONS ARE THE UNITED STATES, CANADA, BRITAIN, FRANCE, 
BELGIUM, THE NETHERLANDS, LUXEMBOURG, NORWAY, DENMARK, PORTUGAL, 
ICELAND’ AND ITALY.

LONG—BEACH, CALIFe, JULY 25-(AP)=SEVEN HUNDRED BALES LABELED "RAGS" 
FOR EXPORT TO GENGA ITALY, ARE HELD BY THE GOVERNMENT TODAY AFTER 
CUSTOMS INS °EC OUND THEY CONTAINED CLOTHING WORTH PERHAPS $350,000 
AT RETAIL AoROAD~ | | ! 

INSPECTORS ~*TD THAT INSIDE OUTER LININGS OF RAGS THE BALES, WEIGH- 
ING 240 TONS I ALL, CONTAINED THOUSANDS OF MEN'S SUITS, WOMEN'S 
DRESSES AND ARMY CLOTHING. | 

A WARRANT OF DETENTION WAS ISSUED UNDER THE EXPORT CONTROL ACT 
WHEREBY THE MERCHANDISE IS IMPOUNDED UNTIL FEDERAL COURT DISPOSITION. 
ASSISTANT UeSe ATTY. MAX DEUTZ EXPLAINED THAT THE ACTION IS AGAINST THE 
MERCHANDISE ITSELF. : 

FOUR COMPANIES WHO WERE LISTED AS THE EXPORTERS ARE INVOLVED AS 
CLAIMANTS, DEUTZ SAID, AND HAVE THE RIGHT TO COME INTO COURT WITHIN 30 
DAYS WITH?A CLAIM AND’PETITION FOR RESTORATION OF THEIR GOODS. IF 
THAT IS DENIED, THE GOVERNMENT WOULD PROCEED WITH LIBEL OR LEGAL 
SEIZURE ACTION’ UNDER WHICH THE.GOODS COULD BE CONFISCATED AND SOLD. 

DEUTZ SAID THERE IS NO PROHIBITION AGAINST SHIPPING CLOTHING BUT 
THERE IS AGAINST MIS-LABELING MERCHANDISE, OR OBTAINING AN EXPORT 
LICENSE FOR RAGS WHEN THE GOODS ACTUALLY {S$ CLOTHING.s THE CASE PROBABLS 
WILL REQUIRE A FEDERAL JUDGE TO DECIDE WHETHER THIS MERCHANDISE ACTU- 
ALLY IS RAGS UNDER TRADE DEFINITIONS, OR CLOTHING, NEW OR USED. 

DEUTZ SAID THE GOODS WERE VALUED AT $35,000 AS RAGS BUT CUSTOMS 
MEN FIGURED THERE WOULD BE A PROFIT OF AROUND 1,000 PER CENT IN SALE 
OF IT AS CLOTHING AT RETAIL IN EUROPE, BOOSTING THE POTENTIAL VALUE 
TO AT LEAST $350,000. 

THE COMPANIES INVOLVED ARE ETRURIA EXPORT CO«, NEW YORK, AND THREE 
LOS ANGELES FIRMS, PHILIP FENEGRAM COs, CALIFORNIA MILL SUPPLY CORPe, 
AND JAKE GOLMAND 0
